The classic Kelly gambling problem maximizes the long-term wealth growth rate but risks substantial drawdown; adding a constraint that limits the probability of a wealth drawdown to a given undesirable level is intractable directly, so the paper derives a bound on the drawdown probability whose use in place of the constraint yields a tractable convex optimization problem that guarantees the drawdown risk constraint holds.

The risk-constrained Kelly method is parametrized by a single parameter with a natural interpretation as a risk-aversion parameter that systematically trades off asymptotic growth rate against drawdown risk; simulations show it outperforms fractional-Kelly bets at the same drawdown risk level or the same growth rate.
A natural quadratic approximation of the risk-constrained Kelly convex problem is closely connected to the classical mean-variance Markowitz portfolio selection problem.

In the Kelly gambling setup, fractions b of total wealth are placed on n bets with b >= 0 and the budget constraint 1^T b = 1, where 1 is the all-ones vector; the wealth changes by the random factor r^T b with r the vector of nonnegative payoffs, and one bet with certain return of one represents cash held (not wagered).

An objective machine-learning framework using statistics related to offensive lineman performance evaluates individual NFL offensive linemen and identifies specific players overvalued or undervalued relative to their salary; eight such players were identified across the 2013-2014 and 2014-2015 NFL seasons and corroborated with subjective film-based metrics.

Portfolio selection for contests with top-heavy payoff structures (daily fantasy sports, venture capital, drug development) is modeled as combinatorial optimization with a submodular objective: the probability that at least one entry wins; this probability can be approximated using only pairwise marginal probabilities of entries winning when the joint distribution has a certain structure.

Under a jointly Gaussian model of entry scores with a closed-form approximation, entries are constructed by integer programming: maximize the expected score of an entry subject to a lower bound on its variance and an upper bound on its correlation with previously constructed entries; applied to daily fantasy sports this ranked in the top ten multiple times in hockey and baseball contests with thousands of competing entries.

Point-differential metrics inflate low-leverage performance: a home-team lead dropping from 5 to 0 points in the last minute of the first half dropped the home team's win chance from 72% to 56%, while a lead dropping from 30 to 25 points in the last minute of the second half kept win chance constant at 100%, yet both are a -5 point differential treated identically by traditional metrics.

Each NBA player's partial effect on his team's chance of winning is estimated by regressing the change in the home team's win probability during each substitution shift onto signed player indicators: E[y_i | h_i, a_i] = mu_i + theta_{h_i1} + ... + theta_{h_i5} - theta_{a_i1} - ... - theta_{a_i5}, where y_i is the win-probability change in shift i, theta (488 players in the 2013-2014 season) are player partial effects, and regularization shrinks estimates toward zero to handle collinearity from players frequently sharing the court.

Real-time EPL betting odds are represented with a two-parameter Skellam process (difference of Poisson processes for the discrete goal difference); given a matrix of market odds on all possible final scores, expected scoring rates for each team are estimated by a non-linear objective function, and those rates define the game's implied volatility, which is re-estimated as goals, red cards, and corner kicks occur; the model calibrates well on 1520 EPL games from 2012-2016.

A typical market vig is 5-8% in the win/lose/draw market, and the final-score odds matrix contains extra information about win odds beyond the moneyline; the Skellam-process approach extracts that information for more accurate win-probability estimates.

There exist deterministic knockout tournaments where one optimal draw is much more robust than another, and general tournaments with slightly suboptimal draws that are more robust than all optimal draws, motivating robust draws that guarantee a specified winning probability under small errors in the pairwise winning probabilities.

The robustness of a draw can be approximated in polynomial time for sufficiently small errors in pairwise winning probabilities, but the computational problem of finding robust draws is NP-complete; two natural deterministic cases that admit polynomial-time optimal draws also admit polynomial-time robust optimal draws.

The robust (epsilon-perturbed) winning probability of a distinguished player i* under draw sigma is the worst-case winning probability over all pairwise-win-probability matrices within epsilon of the nominal one: wp_epsilon(i*, P, sigma) = inf_{P' in P(P,epsilon)} { wp(i*, P', sigma) }.

The winning probability under a perturbed pairwise matrix expands to first order as wp(1,P',sigma) = wp(1,P,sigma) - epsilon sum_{ij} e_{ij} alpha_{ij} + epsilon^2 Q(epsilon), where e_{ij} is +1/-1 according to the sign of P'_{ij} - P_{ij} and alpha_{ij} are sensitivity coefficients.

New data-dependent margin guarantees for structured prediction hold for a wide family of loss functions and hypothesis sets with arbitrary factor-graph decomposition; these are the tightest margin bounds known for multi-class and structured prediction, expressed in terms of factor-graph complexity, which is estimable from data and bounded via familiar quantities plus a sparsity measure on features and graphs.

The Voted Risk Minimization (VRM) principle extends structured-prediction theory to show learning is possible even with complex factor graphs, yielding two new algorithms, Voted Conditional Random Field (VCRF) and Voted Structured Boosting (StructBoost), that use complex features and factor graphs while keeping favorable learning guarantees; VCRF experiments on POS tagging validate the theory.

The free-energy surrogate for structured prediction with loss L and weight vector w is F_i(w) = (1/m) log(sum_{y in Y} exp(L(y,y_i) - w . delta-Psi(x_i,y_i,y))) = (1/m) log(sum_{y in Y} exp(L(y,y_i) + w . Psi(x_i,y))) - (w . Psi(x_i,y_i))/m, where delta-Psi is the feature difference between the true label y_i and candidate y.

Approximate nonparametric maximum likelihood (Kiefer-Wolfowitz) estimation of multivariate mixing distributions is made scalable by reducing it to a simple convex optimization problem; empirically, multivariate mixing distributions substantially improve performance, e.g., in high-dimensional microarray classification the multivariate NPMLE substantially outperforms the 1-dimensional NPMLE, and interior-point methods are faster than EM at this scale.

For the baseball empirical-Bayes application, the posterior mean of player j's hit probability given A_j at-bats and H_j hits under the estimated mixing distribution G-hat_Lambda is pi-hat_j = E_{G-hat_Lambda}(pi_j | A_j, H_j) = [int pi_j f_0(A_j,H_j | lambda_j, pi_j) d G-hat_Lambda(lambda_j, pi_j)] / [int f_0(A_j,H_j | lambda_j, pi_j) d G-hat_Lambda(lambda_j, pi_j)].

The baseball at-bat/hit likelihood decomposes as f_0(A_j,H_j | lambda_j, pi_j) = [lambda_j^{A_j} e^{-lambda_j} / A_j!] x C(A_j, H_j) pi_j^{H_j} (1 - pi_j)^{A_j - H_j}, i.e., Poisson at-bats with rate lambda_j times Binomial hits with success probability pi_j.

The Frank-Wolfe Market Maker (FWMM), which uses an integer-programming solver as an oracle for arbitrage removal in combinatorial prediction markets, achieves superior accuracy to LCMM (e.g., on the NCAA 2010 market with securities on Duke wins); incorporating partial outcomes into the cost function improves over LCMM even without the arbitrage-removal step.

The controlled-growth example for LMSR uses the negative-entropy extension over the non-negative orthant R-bar(mu) = I{mu >= 0} + sum_i mu_i log mu_i, whose Hessian is diagonal with entries 1/mu_i, giving operator norm max 1/mu_i and Lipschitz bound L_epsilon = O(1/epsilon) with p = 1.

The bid-ask spread forms from the interplay of order liquidity and order impact: when trading volume is small, adding liquidity improves price accuracy and reduces spread, but past some point additional liquidity begins to deteriorate price; the model connects bid-ask spread and high-low bars to measurable microstructural parameters, expressing their dependence on trading volume, volatility, and time horizon, and is used to optimize the operating spread for maximum market-making profit.

Recurrent neural networks trained on raw sequential positional tracking data (over 20,000 three-pointers from NBA SportVu) outperform a static feature-rich gradient-boosted-machine model (angle, velocity, and other engineered features) at predicting whether a three-point shot is successful; the RNN learns the ball's trajectory with no knowledge of physics, with impressive AUC at 6-8 feet distances, showing deep sequence models can reduce reliance on feature engineering for tracking data.

Zermelo's 1928 skill model for paired comparisons (later rediscovered as Bradley-Terry, and as the Elo rating system with an online update rule) can be cast as Gaussian process classification, bringing Bayesian uncertainty handling and kernel-function modeling perspectives to game-outcome prediction.

A player kernel relating any two football matches through the players lined up on the field lets abundant club-match data improve predictive models for national-team matches, which suffer data sparsity (national teams play at most ~10 matches per year) and data staleness (rosters constantly evolve); evaluated on the Euro 2008, 2012, and 2016 final tournaments.

In Zermelo's paired-comparison model, each object u has a positive strength parameter w_u and the probability that u beats v is P(u > v) = w_u / (w_u + w_v), reparametrized as w_u = e^{s_u} with s_u the log-strength.

In binary prediction markets organized as a limit order book (no market makers), there is little empirical evidence for convergence of trader beliefs to a consensus; interval estimates of mean beliefs from order-submission decisions cannot exclude aggregate beliefs equal to 0.5.

Execution prices in a limit-order prediction market can be systematically misleading: when informed traders agree state 1 will occur but noise traders are willing to pay above 0.75 for state 0, all execution prices fall in (0, 0.25], falsely suggesting state 1 is unlikely; later entrants observing only execution prices cannot tell whether 0.25 carries information beyond their private signals and will rely only on private information.

Bayesian survival analysis of Test cricket batting ability shows most players begin their innings playing with between only a quarter and half of their potential batting ability ('getting your eye in'); the model quantifies each player's initial and equilibrium batting abilities and the rate of transition between them, and a hierarchical version for New Zealand openers predicts the batting abilities of the next debutant and identifies players who excel at opening, informing batting-order and selection policy.

A batsman's effective batting ability after scoring x runs transitions exponentially from initial ability mu_1 to equilibrium ability mu_2: mu(x; mu_1, mu_2, L) = mu_2 + (mu_1 - mu_2) exp(-x/L), where L is the e-folding transition scale.

The alternative eye-in parametrization writes effective ability as mu(x; C, mu_2, D) = mu_2 + mu_2 (C - 1) exp(-x / (D mu_2)), where C is the ratio of initial to equilibrium ability and D is a transition scale normalized by equilibrium ability.

The log-likelihood for batsman dismissal (hazard H) with completed scores x_i and not-out scores y_i is log[L(theta)] = sum_{i} log H(x_i) + sum_i sum_{a=0}^{x_i-1} log[1 - H(a)] + sum_i sum_{a=0}^{y_i-1} log[1 - H(a)], combining dismissal events and censored (not-out) runs.

Statistically validated lead-lag networks of traders' actions in the foreign exchange market are remarkably persistent, which explains why and how order-flow prediction is possible from trader-resolved data; using random forests, both the sign of order flow and the direction of the average transaction price are strongly predictable for retail investors at an hourly time scale, relevant to brokers and order-matching engines managing inventory.

The existence of persistent trader lead-lag networks explains in a self-referential way why a given trader becomes active, consistent with the finding that most trading activity has an endogenous origin, i.e., is triggered by past activity rather than exogenous news.

A UCL PhD thesis in collaboration with Tottenham Hotspur FC investigates predictive modeling of football injuries in three studies: predicting recovery time from UEFA injury recordings using machine learning improved by correlation-based subset feature selection and random forests; predicting injury incidence from exposure records (training and match hours) as the number of days a player can train before getting injured; and predicting intrinsic injury incidence in a week from in-training GPS measurements as indicators of fatigue and overtraining.

Sports metrics are evaluated with meta-metrics on three criteria: stability (does the metric measure the same thing over time), discrimination (does the metric differentiate between players), and independence (does the metric provide new information); demonstrated on NBA and NHL metrics to identify the most reliable metrics and guide construction of new ones.

Each player metric is decomposed into three sources of variation: intrinsic player skill, context (e.g., influence of teammates), and chance (sampling variability); the classification of variation into signal vs. noise depends on the decision task, e.g., attribution (year-end awards, where repeatability does not matter) versus acquisition (signing/retention, where repeatability does).

Integrating lexicon embeddings and an attention mechanism into convolutional neural networks for sentiment analysis achieves comparative or better results against existing state-of-the-art systems on both SemEval'16 Task 4 and the Stanford Sentiment Treebank; lexicon embeddings allow high-performing models with much smaller word embeddings, and the attention mechanism effectively dims out noisy words.

Vector quantile regression (VQR) models the dependence of a multivariate random vector Y on explanatory variables X as an optimal transport problem subject to the mean-independence condition E(X|U) = E(X); even under misspecification the VQR problem has a solution giving a general representation of conditional dependence, and in the univariate case VQR is equivalent to classical Koenker-Bassett quantile regression with an additional monotonicity constraint.

Brenier's theorem characterizes the vector quantile: the optimal coupling U, uniform on [0,1]^d and maximally correlated with Y, satisfies Y = nabla-phi(U) for a convex function phi, generalizing the univariate quantile map's monotonicity to higher dimensions.

The quantile-regression coefficients for the affine conditional quantile Q(x,u) = alpha(u) + beta(u) x are dual to the linear program sup_{(U_t)} { E(U_t Y) : U_t in [0,1], E(U_t) = (1-t), E(X U_t) = E(X) }, where the constraints fix the mean of the rank variable and its covariance with the explanatory variables.

Using Word2vec and N-gram textual representations with supervised machine learning to analyze tweet sentiment about a company shows a strong correlation between rises and falls in the company's stock price and public sentiment expressed in tweets; prior work (Bollen et al.) found aggregate public mood from Twitter correlated with the Dow Jones Industrial Average.

Kelly-optimizing portfolio managers (fixed leverage ratio = risk premium / volatility) combined with power-law price impact produce deterministic price dynamics with three phases depending on parameters: (1) price changes gradually decay to zero, (2) the sign of the price change switches at each step, (3) price changes grow at each step in a run-away effect; meta-CTA strategies exploit this predictability by avoiding critical areas of the phase diagram or taking contrarian positions at opportune times.

The CTA (Commodity Trading Advisor) space grew from $300 million in 1980 to more than $300 billion in 2014, with around $275 billion controlled by systematic traders whose overlapping trend/momentum models create crowded trades and slippage.

For the universal ranking problem with arbitrary preference intensities, incomplete and multiple comparisons, no ranking method can simultaneously satisfy independence of irrelevant matches (IIM) and self-consistency; the impossibility holds under various domain restrictions but does not emerge for round-robin tournaments, and possibility is recovered by restricting the IIM domain via the macrovertex concept.

Row-sum (Borda/score) ranking has favorable properties in round-robin tournaments but is a poor choice when players face different opponents, as in Swiss-system tournaments, where players with weaker opponents can score the same number of points more easily.

Multi-object tracking in sports videos uses a probabilistic Attributed Relational Graph (ARG) initialized from the first frame and incrementally updated; structural relations (distance, angle between objects) generate new tracking hypotheses to recover lost objects after long-term occlusion or abrupt motion (camera cuts), outperforming state-of-the-art methods on table tennis, volleyball, and the ACASVA dataset; a color-based particle filter serves as the single-object tracker.

The Russian Regional Efficiency of Football Development model evaluates regional football federations on 5 dimensions with scoring based on the three-sigma rule of distribution, adjusting for population density and climate as support factors; findings: no region achieved the maximum 5-star rating, and regions set to host the 2018 FIFA World Cup did not score better than others.

The Discrete Adiabatic Monte Carlo sorting algorithm sorts with unreliable human comparisons (large, constant, independent error rate) by tracking a set of plausible hypotheses updated after each comparison and requesting the most informative next comparison; since one human judgment costs far more than computation, the objective is to minimize comparisons, and the cost is reduced from O(N L^3 ln L) to O(N L) by only considering pairs adjacent in a current candidate ordering.

The posterior probability that the hypothesized true ordering is correct given comparison data is P_n(true|data) ~ P_n(data|true) / [P_n(data|true) + L x P_n(data|atypical)], contrasting the true ordering's likelihood against L atypical-hypothesis likelihoods.

The human error rate can be marginalized out under a uniform prior as int_0^1 dp p^{n_match} (1-p)^{n - n_match}, where p is the probability a judgment matches the hypothesized ordering, n_match the number of matching comparisons, and n the total comparisons.

The Spatial Dirichlet Hawkes Process (SDHP) clusters streaming spatiotemporal data (e.g., geolocated tweets) to uncover collective social activity patterns (concerts, sporting events, rallies); online inference via Sequential Monte Carlo scales to millions of geolocated posts, SDHP surpasses the plain DHP in normalized mutual information, and the model can be used to estimate the location from which a tweet was posted.

Spatial goodness of fit is measured as spatial g.o.f. = (1/2000) sum_{n=501}^{2500} log p(r_n | t_{<=n}, s_{<n}, d_{<=n}, r_{<n}), the average log marginal likelihood of each location r_n given inferred patterns and parameters from prior samples, with an analogous perplexity measure for content.

Replacing true outcome probabilities with estimates in the Kelly criterion leads to overbetting (MacLean et al. 1992): outcomes with overestimated values consistently look more favorable and attract oversized wagers, producing higher risk with lower returns; the fractional Kelly strategy (e.g., half-Kelly, used by Benter and Thorp) mitigates this, and Baker and McHale 2013 derived an optimal shrinkage fraction for two-outcome settings; this paper extends uncertainty-aware Kelly betting to many-outcome settings such as horse races and achieves superior returns in simulation by accounting for estimation error.

The Kelly multi-outcome investment problem maximizes expected log wealth: max sum_{h=1}^n pi_h log(x_h O_h + w - sum_{i=1}^n x_i) subject to sum_h x_h <= w and x_h >= 0, where pi_h is horse h's win probability, O_h the decimal payout odds, x_h the stake, and w current wealth.

Horse win probabilities are estimated by multinomial logistic regression as pi_h = e^{beta' v_h} / sum_{i=1}^n e^{beta' v_i}, where v_h is the factor-value vector for horse h and beta the regression coefficients; the log-likelihood ln L(beta) = sum_r beta' v_{w^r} - ln sum_i e^{beta' v_{i^r}} is concave, so the MLE is found by standard unconstrained optimization.

Massey's sports rating method is reinterpreted as a network centrality measure: each game k between teams i and j contributes r_i - r_j = y_k (margin of victory), forming the least-squares system X r = y; the Massey system M r = p with M = X^T X and p = X^T y decomposes as M = D - A, where D is the diagonal matrix of games played and A the match adjacency matrix.

The Massey rating of team i equals the mean rating of its opponents plus its mean point spread: r_i = (1/D_{ii}) sum_j A_{ij} r_j + p_i/D_{ii}, where p_i is the signed sum of point spreads; since M is singular, a solution is obtained by replacing one row of M with all ones (fixing the ratings' sum).

High prediction accuracy does not equal high payout in sports betting: across NCAAB, NBA, and NFL, models with similar accuracies produced strongly diverging monetary payoffs; Naïve Bayes was 1.5 percentage points less accurate than the KP model yet showed solid gains, while the more accurate KP model lost money, because payout depends on which match-ups (favorites vs. pick'ems vs. underdogs) are predicted correctly.

Measured Vegas baselines show the accuracy-profit gap: NBA regular-season accuracy 0.7096 accrued a -1502 payout and NFL regular-season accuracy 0.6441 a -1215.69 payout, so following moneyline favorites loses money in aggregate despite high accuracy; models that correctly pick underdogs or pick'ems are the more attractive predictive tools even with lower straight-up accuracy.

Prediction-market forecast error decomposes into three components analogous to bias-variance: sampling error (finite traders with noisy estimates of ground truth), market-maker bias (from the choice of cost function providing liquidity), and convergence error (prices not yet at equilibrium); sampling error vanishes as the number of traders grows, but there is a tradeoff between market-maker bias and convergence error controlled by the liquidity parameter.

Under a tractable model of exponential-utility traders with exponential-family beliefs, the paper gives upper and lower bounds on market-maker bias and convergence error that are tight in numerical simulations, yielding guidance on setting the market's liquidity parameter and on the forecasting benefits of enforcing coherent prices across securities.

For any task loss in structured prediction, a convex surrogate can be constructed that is optimizable via stochastic gradient descent with tight bounds on the calibration function relating excess surrogate risk to actual risk; the analysis shows some task losses make learning harder than others and that the classical 0-1 loss is ill-suited for structured prediction.

The quadratic surrogate excess at label distribution q is delta-phi_quad(F theta, q) := phi_quad(F theta, q) - inf_{theta'} phi_quad(F theta', q) = (1/(2k)) ||F theta + L q||_2^2, where L is the task-loss matrix and F the feature map.

The task risk and surrogate risk are defined as R_L(f) = E_{x ~ D_X} l(f(x), P(.|x)) and R_Phi(f) = E_{x ~ D_X} phi(f(x), P(.|x)), respectively, where l is the task loss, phi the surrogate, and P(.|x) the conditional label distribution.

A PageRank model rates individual basketball/soccer/hockey players: nodes for each player plus a goal node, arcs between players indicate passes in reverse order (plus sport-specific handling of turnovers, fouls, missed shots), with extra arcs ensuring primitivity so a unique PageRank vector exists; applied to nine NBA games from 2014-2016, top-ranked players mostly matched impressive traditional stat lines but with surprises in both directions, reflecting game flow more than traditional statistics.

The PageRank vector v is the unique stationary vector satisfying T^t v = v with v^t 1 = 1 (nonnegative eigenvector of the transposed transition matrix with eigenvalue 1 whose entries sum to 1), where T_{i,j} = n_{i,j}/n_i for a directed graph with n_{i,j} arcs from node i to node j.

Split Linearized Bregman Iteration (Split LBI) recovers beta* from noisy linear measurements y = X beta* + epsilon under structural sparsity where gamma* := D beta* has mostly zero entries; with proper early stopping it achieves model-selection consistency under irrepresentable conditions weaker than those necessary and sufficient for the generalized Lasso, and l2 error bounds at minimax optimal rates, outperforming generalized Lasso in theory and experiments (applications include partial-order ranking of sports teams).
The structural-sparsity measurement model is y = X beta* + epsilon with gamma* = D beta* (S = supp(gamma*), s = |S|), where X is the design matrix, D a fixed linear transform, and gamma* is s-sparse.

Two Bayesian multinomial-Dirichlet models for football match outcomes that use only each team's counts of wins, draws, and losses as inputs are competitive with standard approaches on 1710 matches of the Brazilian first division (2006-2014), are well calibrated under the Brier, logarithmic, and spherical proper scoring rules, and show reasonable goodness of fit, outperforming an extended Bradley-Terry baseline and matching the Arruda and Lee benchmark models.

The benchmark goal models assume home/away goals (Y_1, Y_2) follow a bivariate Poisson (Holgate) with P(Y_1=y_1, Y_2=y_2 | lambda_1, lambda_2, lambda_3) = exp(-(lambda_1+lambda_2+lambda_3)) sum_{k=0}^{min(y_1,y_2)} lambda_1^{y_1-k} lambda_2^{y_2-k} lambda_3^k / ((y_1-k)! (y_2-k)! k!), where lambda_3 >= 0 is the dependence parameter (lambda_3 = 0 gives independent Poissons as in the Lee model; lambda_3 > 0 gives positive correlation as in the Arruda model).

Minimum Rényi entropy portfolios minimize the exponential of the Rényi entropy of the portfolio return distribution (estimated with a robust m-spacings estimator), accounting for non-normality and all higher-order moments; they outperform state-of-the-art minimum variance portfolios in terms of risk-return-turnover trade-off, and a Gram-Charlier expansion shows the Rényi parameter alpha controls the relative contributions of the central (variance) and tail (kurtosis) parts of the distribution.

Variance is an adequate risk measure only for Gaussian distributions and is largely unaffected by increasing tail concentration, so the minimum variance portfolio does not account for the non-normality of asset returns; the minimum-variance portfolio usually performs better out of sample than any other mean-variance portfolio (DeMiguel and Nogales 2009).

The official ATP ranking points predict tennis match results through the ranking-point ratio between players: the logistic model p-hat_{i,j} = pi_{i,j}^alpha / (1 + pi_{i,j}^alpha) with pi_{i,j} = r_i/r_j (ratio of ranking points) fits over 24,000 matches from 2009 with alpha = 0.8722, and explains match results across a wide range of ranking-point ratios.

Prediction error for tennis match outcomes is measured as E^2 = (1/number of matches) sum_{all matches} (w_{i,j} - p-hat_{i,j})^2, where w_{i,j} is the actual outcome and p-hat_{i,j} the predicted win probability.

A game is fair when the bookmaker's expected revenue E(R_b) = -r p + (1-p) = 0, giving r = 1/p - 1 where 1/p is the decimal odds; for the fair game the variance of the revenue scheme Var(R_b) = E(R_b^2) - [E(R_b)]^2 = r, so the fractional odds r double as the measure of the game's risk.

Bookmakers earn a long-run profit by paying less than the fair amount, r - epsilon instead of r: with win probability 0.606 and fair payout 0.65, paying only 0.6 yields expected revenue -0.6 x 0.606 + 0.394 = 0.0304, i.e., about 3 cents per dollar staked in the long run.

Training-load monitoring (GPS, accelerometers, perceived exertion; rolling averages, EWMA, acute:chronic workload ratio, monotony, strain) predicts elite Australian-football injuries only marginally better than chance for non-contact and non-contact time-loss injuries (AUC << 0.65) on unseen third-season data from 75 unique athletes over 3 seasons; the best model was multivariate logistic regression for hamstring injuries (best AUC = 0.76), suggesting load models from a single club are limited as daily decision tools and that focusing on specific injury types with more data may improve them.

Modern neural networks, unlike those from a decade ago, are poorly calibrated: a 110-layer ResNet's average confidence substantially exceeds its accuracy on CIFAR-100 while a 5-layer LeNet's confidence closely matches its accuracy; depth, width, weight decay, and Batch Normalization are important factors influencing calibration, and temperature scaling (a single-parameter variant of Platt scaling) is surprisingly effective at calibrating predictions on most datasets.

Soccer plus-minus ratings are adapted from basketball/hockey with two variants: an expected-goals plus-minus and an expected-points plus-minus using in-play match-outcome probabilities; the model suggests the English Premier League is the strongest league with the German Bundesliga a close runner-up, and player ratings' evolution over time is tracked.

The regularized plus-minus ratings are estimated by ridge regression beta-hat = (X^T X + lambda^2 I)^{-1} X^T y, where y is the target (goal differential, expected goals, or expected points change per segment) and X holds signed player-indicator columns.

Forecast skill is measured by the Brier score BS = (1/N) sum_{t=1}^N sum_{r=1}^R (p_{tr} - o_{tr})^2 over N matches and R outcomes, and expected points for the home team at time t are xP^H_t = 3 x P^{HW}_t + 1 x P^D_t, i.e., three points for a home win plus one for a draw weighted by in-play probabilities.

The Labouchère gambling system has the player create an arbitrary series of consecutive integers summing to a desired profit; simulations of millions of rounds show the system produces psychologically appealing consistent linear returns over time, but there is eventually a critical moment at which required stakes exceed available capital and the player loses everything, and as the number of bets increases the outcome of applying the sequence approaches zero.

On the meso-scale of limit order books (volume-bucketed aggregation of tick data from six large-tick Nasdaq assets), the relationship between trade imbalance and price change is nonlinear but becomes linear when using a weighted average of market and limit order flows; there is a hockey-stick dependence between trade imbalance and one-sided limit order flows, and limit order flows (plus relative addition/cancellation rates) carry the most predictive power, with deeper LOB shape more relevant than simple book imbalance.

For log-optimal (Kelly-style) portfolios with weighted logarithmic returns and cautious risk-averse policies that never exceed current capital (covering worst possible losses): under certain conditions the logarithmic growth rate is a supermartingale, and the optimal investment strategy is proportional betting — invest a proportion of current capital that is independent of the capital level but depends on the return process's current state (often zero, i.e., no bet).

A physical (Boltzmann) model for ranking in networks assigns rank probabilities P(s) = Z^{-1}(beta, alpha) e^{-beta H(s)} with temperature beta; imposing the prior P_ij = gamma_i/(gamma_i + gamma_j) and setting k = 2 beta recovers the Bradley-Terry model; cross-validation over the temperature beta-hat optimizes edge-direction prediction accuracy, and the method outperforms alternatives in speed and accuracy at recovering hidden ranks and predicting unobserved edges in networks and sports tournaments, with a natural statistical-significance test via randomized edge directions.

An interpretable Bayesian Poisson model fit by variational inference infers per-player event abilities (e.g., scoring a goal) and extends the Baio and Blangiardo (2010) hierarchical team scoring-rate model; player abilities inferred over the 2013/2014 English Premier League season were used to predict over/under 2.5 goals per game in the 2014/2015 season, expert football analysts agreed with the inferred rankings, and including time dependence improves prediction while latent player abilities reduce the variance of attack and defense parameters.

Variational inference maximizes the evidence lower bound ELBO{q(nu)} = E_{q(nu)}[log{pi(nu, x)}] - E_{q(nu)}[log{q(nu)}], the expected joint log-density minus the entropy of the approximating density.

Kelly's criterion is incorporated into standard portfolio optimization models via a single objective function combining risk and return with a risk parameter; the model is solved for a 10-stock portfolio using a differential evolution algorithm with Monte Carlo verification, showing evolutionary algorithms can successfully solve Kelly-based portfolio optimization.

Kelly betting can be too conservative rather than too aggressive: the Restricted Betting Theorem states that if X_min < 0 and X_max > 0 are the infimum and supremum of the return support, the optimal Kelly fraction must lie between -1/X_max and -1/X_min; when the support is unbounded both above and below, the optimal fraction K* = 0, i.e., the theory prescribes no betting at all, while a data-based practitioner using an empirically derived distribution can identify 'golden' opportunities the theoretical model rejects.

The classical Kelly problem maximizes expected logarithmic growth g(K) = E[log(1 + K^T X)] over admissible fractions K with K_i >= 0 and sum K_i <= 1, under the wealth recursion V(k+1) = (1 + K^T X(k)) V(k) and the survival constraint min_{X in X} K^T X >= -1; for a biased coin with win probability p > 1/2 the optimal fraction is K* = 2p - 1.

Kelly's expected log-growth is g(K) = E[log(1 + K^T X)] = int_X log(1 + K^T x) f_X(x) dx, a concave program in K; Taylor-style approximations of this objective and neglect of wealth drawdowns are identified as ways the theory can go wrong in practice.

Fine-grained retrieval of multi-agent sports plays uses a tree-based hierarchical method to align trajectories coarse-to-fine, solving the permutation/alignment problem caused by frequent player position swaps; validated with domain-expert user studies, it boosts retrieval of similar basketball plays (especially for user-selected trajectory subsets) over state-of-the-art methods, reducing exemplar-based play search from days to seconds.

A strategy exploiting the probability information implicit in publicly available odds (rather than competing with bookmaker forecasting models) to find mispriced bets was profitable across a 10-year historical simulation with closing odds, a 6-month simulation with minute-by-minute odds, and a 5-month period staking real money with bookmakers; the authors conclude the football betting market is inefficient and document discriminatory industry practices against successful clients.

For binary-state forecast aggregation by an ignorant aggregator (who sees only experts' forecasts, not the information structure), low-regret aggregation schemes exist when there are two experts who are either Blackwell-ordered or receive conditionally i.i.d. signals; in contrast, with many experts receiving conditionally i.i.d. signals, no scheme performs asymptotically better than a constant (0.5, 0.5) forecast; regret is measured against a hypothetical omniscient expert via proper scoring rules.

Maximum regularized likelihood estimators (MRLEs) are broadly consistent in prediction under Kullback-Leibler divergence assuming only convex parametrization of densities and definite positive-homogeneous regularization, with no need for restricted-eigenvalue or similar conditions; the bounds are optimal for lasso-type regression and the theory covers tensor regression and graphical models with convex and non-convex regularization.

Restricted-eigenvalue conditions limit correlations among covariates, but for prediction even perfectly collinear covariates need not hurt and collinearity can be beneficial; MRLE prediction theory avoids such identifiability-oriented assumptions entirely.

Portfolio tail-risk estimation (99.5% VaR under Solvency II, TVaR under Basel III) in a nested-simulation framework is accelerated by Gaussian-process emulation: the portfolio value f(z) = E[Y((Z_t)_{t >= T}) | Z_T = z] is learned nonparametrically from inner simulations, sequential algorithms adaptively allocate inner-simulation budget to the quantile region, and the GP framework yields better uncertainty quantification with reduced bias and variance versus existing methods.

Multivariate generalized linear mixed models jointly model margin of victory or win/loss together with a second game-level response (penalty yards, shots on goal, turnover margin) using non-nested correlated team random effects b_j = (b_j^o, b_j^d, b_j^w)' ~ N_3(0, G*) for offensive, defensive, and win-propensity effects; fit by first-order and fully exponential Laplace approximations (R package mvglmmRank), higher correlation between the win/loss response and the game-level response improves cross-validated predictions for college football and basketball.
Game-outcome predictions are scored with log-loss_i = -y_i log(y-hat_i) - (1 - y_i) log(1 - y-hat_i), where y_i = 1 for a home-team victory; smaller log-loss means a more accurate prediction.

Sequential rank aggregation (choosing which pair of K items to compare, when to stop, and the final ranking) is solved under a Bayesian decision framework with asymptotically optimal procedures that balance exploration and exploitation by comparing the most indistinguishable pair; decision accuracy is measured by a Kendall's tau distance loss, and a mirror-descent algorithm computes the procedures.

Oddsmaker bias can be exploited to improve NFL outcome prediction: decisions that are strongly biased correspond to minimum-entropy spreads, and spreads exceeding a 0.95 entropy threshold are identified as biased; the Min-Entropy model achieved mean 71.85% (SEM 0.82) and the k-Lowest Entropy model 66% (SEM 0.99), outperforming the non-bias Max-Probability baseline at mean 58.15% (SEM 1.13) across valid spreads.

Posterior predictive treatment assignment (PPTA) estimates causal effects under limited propensity-score overlap by marginalizing over uncertainty about whether each observation belongs to an unknown subset for which treatment assignment can be assumed unconfounded; it is a stochastic version of propensity-score pruning or IPTW truncation, related to the overlap weights of Li et al. 2016, with advantages in uncertainty quantification and finite-sample performance; illustrated on evaluating pollution-emission-reduction technologies at US power plants.

Optimal crowdsourced M-ary classification with a reject option and spammers uses weighted majority voting with optimized weights and no prior information about individual workers; workers may skip binary microtasks (answer lambda) when unsure, spammers submit random guesses, and the M-ary task decomposes into N = ceil(log2 M) independent binary microtasks of equal difficulty, with simulation results showing significant performance improvement.

A multilayer perceptron trained on data for more than 15,000 football players from FIFA 2017 (tuning activation functions, neurons, layers, learning rate and decay, Nesterov-momentum SGD, L2 regularization, early stopping) predicts player prices with top-5 accuracy of 87.2% among 119 pricing categories and places any footballer within 6.32% of his actual price on average.

TenisRank is a PageRank-based tennis ranking built on a history of 40,000 matches that uses tournament characteristics to estimate each player's real chances of victory before a tournament, evaluated against the official ATP ranking which is criticized for poor win prediction and rewarding single good tournaments.

A hierarchical Bayesian Bradley-Terry model for paired comparisons outperforms maximum-likelihood analogues by integrating over uncertainty (preventing overfitting), especially when data is scarce: on MLB 2017 data the Bayesian approach performs significantly better during the first half of the season and continues to outperform into July, after which the two methods converge.

In the Bradley-Terry model, team i defeats team j with probability P = pi_i/(pi_i + pi_j) with strengths pi_i > 0, and an entire season has probability mass function p(V | pi) = prod_{i<j} C(n_ij, V_ij) (pi_i/(pi_i+pi_j))^{V_ij} (pi_j/(pi_i+pi_j))^{V_ji}, where V_ij is the number of i-wins and n_ij games between i and j.

For a Kelly bettor who selects fraction K and waits n steps between bet-size updates (proceeds at risk between updates, 'buy and hold'), the first conjecture is that absent transaction costs the optimal log-growth g_n* is non-increasing in n (high-frequency betting is best); with transaction costs a low-frequency bettor may do better; a 'sufficient attractiveness inequality' is proved sufficient and conjectured necessary for the low-frequency bettor to match high-frequency performance.

Narrow field-of-view soccer PTZ cameras are calibrated with a two-point method requiring only two point correspondences given prior knowledge of the camera's base location and orientation; a fast random forest predicts pan-tilt angles without image-to-image feature matching, achieving superior performance over the state of the art on synthetic data and two real soccer datasets.

The PTZ camera projection matrix decomposes as P = K Q_phi Q_theta S[I | -C], where K is the intrinsic matrix, Q_phi and Q_theta are pan and tilt rotations, and S[I | -C] encodes the fixed camera center C prior.

The angle alpha between two back-projected rays satisfies cos alpha = (d_1^T d_2)/(sqrt(d_1^T d_1) sqrt(d_2^T d_2)) = (x_1^T omega x_2)/(sqrt(x_1^T omega x_1) sqrt(x_2^T omega x_2)), where omega is the image of the absolute conic and x_i the image points.

The footballer most resembling Lionel Messi was found by statistical analysis of WhoScored data: 17 attacking parameters (goals, assists, shots, passes, dribbles, fouls, etc.) for 28 candidate players from the WS Top 100 list, after data normalization and application of a proper metric function.

For photovoltaic power prediction, the most influential weather parameters are solar radiation, duration of sunlight, and altitude of the sun (highest CART variable importance in both winter and summer), with humidity and temperature also important in summer; common approaches are multilayer perceptrons, extreme learning machines, and similar-day selection using historical power plus weather data.

Neural Relational Inference (NRI) is an unsupervised variational auto-encoder in which the latent code represents the underlying interaction graph and the reconstruction is based on graph neural networks; it recovers ground-truth interactions in simulated physical systems (springs, charged particles) with high accuracy in a completely unsupervised way, and on real motion-capture and NBA basketball tracking data it learns a small number of interpretable edge types (e.g., pick-and-roll phases) enabling future-state prediction.

The NRI model is trained by maximizing the variational lower bound L = E_{q_phi(z|x)}[log p_theta(x|z)] - KL[q_phi(z|x) || p_theta(z)], where z is the latent interaction graph and x the observed trajectories.

PlayeRank is a data-driven, multi-dimensional, role-aware framework for soccer player performance evaluation built on millions of match events across four seasons of 18 competitions; compared against known evaluation algorithms and professional soccer scouts' ratings, it significantly outperforms competitors, and its flexibility supports player search and player-versatility applications.

A general abstention (selective classification) framework optimizes any metric of interest (e.g., sensitivity at a target specificity, auROC, weighted Cohen's kappa), adapts to label shift at test time, and works out-of-the-box with any calibrated classifier by using calibrated probability estimates as a proxy for true labels to estimate the metric change from abstaining on an example; a novel strong baseline based on JS divergence from prior class probabilities is introduced, validated on synthetic, biological, and clinical data.

Basketball players in the Spanish ACB league are ranked by a multicriteria outranking methodology that summarizes multiple efficiency indices (points, playing time, attempts, etc.) into a ranking for agents negotiating contracts and coaches designing lineups; a novel automatic parameter-tuning approach lets non-mathematical decision-makers design templates and strategies.

In repeated forecast aggregation where each expert observes a different subset of conditionally independent signals (partial-evidence information structures), an ignorant aggregator who sees only experts' forecasts and the realized states can learn the optimal Bayesian aggregation in polynomial time in a wide range of instances, with a tight characterization of where learning is possible vs. impossible; this contrasts with one-shot aggregation, which is impossible in a strong sense when the number of experts is large.

Model trees for NHL draft prospect evaluation partition the feature space (discrete features or learned continuous thresholds) so each leaf defines an interpretable group of comparable players with its own group regression model; the single interpretable tree's predictions are competitive with state-of-the-art methods and the ranking correlates with future success (NHL games played after 7 years) about as well as the generalized additive model, adding information beyond the NHL Central Scouting Service rank; out-of-sample Pearson correlations of 0.69 and 0.72 (training on 1998-2000, predicting 2001/2002 draft years) beat draft-order baselines of 0.43 and 0.45.

A hierarchical Bayesian Poisson model for football scores makes team scoring rates convex combinations of parameters estimated from historical data and parameters implied by bookmakers' betting odds; applied to a nine-year dataset of the most popular European leagues to predict match outcomes in their tenth seasons, improving fit and predictive accuracy over history-only models.

The goal difference follows a Skellam (Poisson-difference) distribution Y_{m1} - Y_{m2} ~ PD(gamma-hat_{m1}, gamma-hat_{m2}) with blended rates gamma-hat_{m1} = p-hat_{m1} theta-hat_{m1} + (1 - p-hat_{m1}) lambda-hat_{m1}, i.e., a convex combination of the odds-implied rate theta-hat and the historically estimated rate lambda-hat with weight p-hat.

Deep reinforcement learning on player-trajectory data from over 643,000 NBA possessions quantifies the double-teaming trade-off: the learned policy's value estimates are predictive of points per possession and win percentage and correlate with possession outcomes; doubling the ball handler yields significantly lower field-goal percentage but a significantly greater likelihood of the possession ending in a foul, the observed and learned policies differ significantly, and all teams could improve their defense under optimal play.

AURORA audits PageRank on large graphs by identifying the set of key graph elements (edges, nodes, subgraphs) with highest influence on the ranking results; influence is measured via gradients over the ranking results and elements are selected incrementally with greedy algorithms exploiting the diminishing-returns property, achieving intuitive explanations with linear scalability and outperforming baselines on all datasets.

The influence of the adjacency matrix on a ranking objective f(r) is measured by the gradient df(r)/dA = 2c(1-c) Q' r e' Q' = 2c(Q'r) r' (directed case), where c is the damping factor, Q' the resolvent-like matrix, r the ranking vector, and e the all-ones vector.

Spatial risk measures for extreme environmental events (e.g., Hurricane Irma, 134+ deaths, $64.8B+ damage) satisfy asymptotic spatial homogeneity of order 0 for expectation, -2 for variance, -1 for Value-at-Risk, and -1 for expected shortfall, quantifying the rate of spatial diversification as the region grows; for cost fields that are functions of max-stable random fields (the natural extension of multivariate extreme-value theory to random fields), sufficient conditions on the function and field ensure these homogeneity orders.

Structured Output Learning with Abstention (SOLA) learns a pair of predictors — one for structured abstention and one for structured output prediction — under a wide class of asymmetric abstention-aware losses; learning is by surrogate least-squares regression in a feature space followed by a new pre-image problem, with statistical guarantees on excess risk, and it achieves state-of-the-art results on fine-grained opinion mining with a hierarchical abstention-aware loss.

The MLB-YouTube dataset enables fine-grained activity detection in baseball broadcast videos (segmented classification and continuous detection); learning temporal structure matters — temporal convolution outperforms mean/max pooling, fixed temporal pyramids, and LSTMs (which overfit small pitch-type differences); combining convolutional sub-event and super-event representations gives the best performance; pitch-type prediction from broadcast video reaches 68% for fastballs, 45% for sliders, and only 12% for sinkers.

The sub-event activity score is S_c = sum_{m=1}^M A_{c,m} * sum_{t=1}^T F_m[t] * v_t, where F_m[t] are learned temporal sub-event filters, v_t the frame features, and A_{c,m} the attention weights for class c.

Predicting cricket batsmen's runs and bowlers' wickets (as classification into ranges) with Naïve Bayes, decision trees, multiclass SVM, and random forests: random forest was most accurate for both (90.74% for runs, 92.25% for wickets with 90% training data), while Naïve Bayes was least accurate (42.5% for runs, 57.05% for wickets); accuracy generally increased with training-set size.

twAwler, a lightweight language-targeted Twitter crawler using multiple API endpoints while respecting rate limits, generated a dataset of close to all Greek-speaking Twitter accounts (about 330,000) between August 2016 and March 2018: 750 million tweets (424 million in Greek), 750 million follow relations, 119 million list-member relations, 705 thousand trending topics, and information on 52 million users total (292 thousand later suspended, 141 thousand deleted, 3.5 million protected); retweet, quote, reply, and mention graphs are mined from the tweets.

The NFL's 2011 collective bargaining agreement cut OTAs from 14 to 10 days, the voluntary offseason workout program from 14 to 9 weeks, and eliminated twice-daily padded practices; a 2007-2016 interrupted time-series of regular-season game-loss injuries found no sustained increase in conditioning-dependent or non-conditioning-dependent injuries associated with the CBA, and games missed due to injury actually fell post-CBA (post-vs-pre CBA rate ratios: 0.85 for all injuries, 0.85 for conditioning injuries, 0.77 for non-conditioning injuries).

Injury counts are modeled as ln(Y_ij) = ln(G_ij) + beta_0 + beta_1 * t_ij + beta_2 * CBA_ij + beta_3 * PostCBA_ij + beta_4 * Age_ij + b_0i + e_ij, where Y_ij is the injury count, G_ij the athlete-exposure offset, t the time trend, CBA the level change, PostCBA the post-CBA trend change, and b_0i a player random effect; when exponentiated, beta_1 + beta_3 represents the percent change per year in the post-CBA era.
equation: ln(Yi j ) = ln(Gi j ) + \beta0 + \beta1 \ast ti j + \beta2 \astCBAi j + \beta3 \ast PostCBAi j + \beta4 \ast Agei j + b0i + ei j

claim: Cluster analysis and multidimensional scaling of GPS-tracked basketball player movements (segmenting matches into phases by clustering time instants) consistently finds that defensive clusters have players close together while transition clusters show large spacing among players; the approach identifies the player-positioning patterns that produce the best team shooting performance.

A wrist-worn wearable fusing IMU data (100 Hz accelerometer/gyroscope) with audio (8 kHz microphone) detects table-tennis shots with 95.6% accuracy by synchronizing the two sensor streams via shot-likelihood sequences and then fusing them; it is the first audio-IMU fusion solution for sports analysis on wearables, extending to badminton and other racquet sports, where racquet-impact pressure waves last only 10-20 ms.

Football table prediction quality is measured by MAE = (1/n) sum_{i=1}^n |P(i) - i|, the average misplacement of teams, rather than MSE; for a random table permutation MAE_MIN = 0, MAE_MAX = n/2, and E[MAE] = (1/3)(n^2-1)/n; pundit Paul Merson's 2016/2017 Premier League prediction scored MAE = 2.8 (two perfect hits, eight off-by-one).
The expected mean absolute error of a random league-table permutation is E[MAE] = (1/3) (n^2 - 1)/n, providing a baseline against which expert table predictions can be judged.

Neural networks for post-processing ensemble weather forecasts (2-meter temperature at German surface stations) significantly outperform benchmark distributional-regression methods (EMOS, BMA) while being computationally cheaper; key ingredients are auxiliary predictor variables and station-specific information via embeddings, and the trained network yields meteorological variable-importance insights, challenging the black-box notion.

Poisson regression models with Elo points as covariates (plus team-specific attack/defense effects), fit on all neutral-ground games of participating teams since 2010, are combined with Monte Carlo simulation to estimate FIFA World Cup 2018 stage-reaching probabilities; all models favored Germany (then Brazil) as champion, were validated on the 2010 and 2014 World Cups with goodness-of-fit tests, residual analysis, AIC, and two new ordinal score functions alongside Brier score and rank probability score, with all tournament paths visualized in a single Sankey diagram.

A cumulative ordinal score function for tournament outcomes is error_4(T) = (1/5) sum_{i=1}^5 (sum_{j=1}^i p_j(T) - 1_{[result(T)=j]})^2, where p_j(T) is the predicted probability team T finishes in stage category j (1 = winner through 6 = group-stage exit) and the indicator marks the realized category.
Team-level goodness of fit is assessed with the chi-square statistic chi_T = sum_{i=1}^{n_T} (x_i - mu-hat_i)^2 / mu-hat_i, comparing observed and expected goal counts across team T's matches.

A generalized framework for applying the Kelly criterion to stock markets computes the Kelly investment fraction for each stock from an arbitrary probability distribution of future price movements by inverting a matrix involving only first and second moments; for a single stock under geometric Brownian motion this gives f = mu/sigma^2 (mu the growth rate, sigma the relative volatility), agreeing with existing results, and the framework extends to Gaussian and correlated multivariate portfolios.

SMOGS models basketball passes as directed dynamic relational links with multiplicative latent factors distinguishing wins from losses; parameters are estimated by MCMC, and applied to the first high-resolution optical tracking dataset in college basketball, the learned latent factors show significant differences in players' passing and receiving tendencies between wins and losses.

The log-intensity of passes from player i to player j at time t is modeled as log(theta_{i,j}(t)) = W_{i,j}(t)^T eta_{i,j} + xi_{i,j}(s_i(t)) + xi-tilde_{i,j}(s_j(t)) + z_{i,j,g}(t), combining covariates, spatial effects of the passer's and receiver's court positions, and a game-outcome latent factor.

Uncoupled isotonic regression — estimating a nondecreasing regression function f from only the unordered sets {x_i} and {y_i} with y_i = f(x_i) + xi_i, without knowing which x pairs with which y — admits consistent estimators via minimum Wasserstein deconvolution using optimal-transport tools, with minimax rates derived under weak moment conditions and an efficient algorithm achieving optimal rates via moment-matching arguments.
The empirical L^p norm used for isotonic-regression error is ||g||_p^p := (1/n) sum_{i=1}^n |g(x_i)|^p, the average absolute value over the fixed design points.

Causal discovery (Generalized Correlations, CAM, FGES, GFCI, Hill-Climbing, Tabu Search) on ECG and impedance-pneumography signals from 100 elite athletes at rest finds, for supine position, the best-supported causal path: tidal volume causes heart activity variation, which causes average heart activity, which causes respiratory timing; for standing position: normalized respiratory activity variation causes average heart activity; one can expect to influence heart rate and its variability by changing the depth, not the frequency, of breathing.

Breathing regularity is quantified as BR = (100 - 20 * (tanh(sigma_{iRR}/iRR-bar) + tanh(sigma_{InsT}/InsT-bar) + tanh(sigma_{ExpT}/ExpT-bar) + tanh(sigma_{InsV}/InsV-bar) + tanh(sigma_{ExpV}/ExpV-bar))) [%], combining normalized variability of R-R intervals, inspiratory/expiratory times, and inspiratory/expiratory volumes.

In a control-theoretic Kelly-optimal portfolio framework with rebalancing frequency f = 1/(n Delta-t), high-frequency rebalancing often yields no performance benefit even absent transaction costs; if an asset satisfies a 'dominance' condition, the optimal portfolio consists of that asset alone ('all eggs in one basket') and performance becomes a constant function of rebalancing frequency, rendering the rebalancing problem moot.

Deep contextual multi-armed bandits achieve non-linear context modeling with principled exploration via Thompson sampling, exploiting the connection between inference-time dropout and sampling from the posterior over Bayesian neural network weights; the dropout rate is learned rather than fixed as a hyperparameter, and the approach substantially reduces regret versus non-contextual bandits, epsilon-greedy deep contextual bandits, and fixed-dropout deep contextual bandits on the UCI Mushroom and Casino Parity tasks.

Probability calibration trees, a modification of logistic model trees, identify regions of the input space in which different probability calibration models are learned; they achieve lower root mean squared error on average than the global methods isotonic regression and Platt scaling across a variety of base learners.

In cost-sensitive classification, decisions minimize expected cost sum_{i=1}^m C(y' = i | y = j) P(y = j | x), where C(y' = i | y = j) is the cost of classifying an instance as class i when it belongs to class j; accurate calibrated probability estimates are therefore required.

Thompson sampling is extended to reward-model uncertainty by modeling each arm's reward distribution with independent Bayesian nonparametric Gaussian mixture models that adjust complexity as rewards are observed; the method comes with an asymptotic regret bound from a novel posterior-convergence analysis and outperforms state-of-the-art alternatives in both averaged cumulative regret and regret volatility on non-exponential-family rewards, outliers, and heterogeneous per-arm distributions.

Sequential Monte Carlo methods extend Bayesian multi-armed bandits to non-stationary bandits with nonlinear, stateless- and context-dependent reward distributions: SMC-based sequentially updated random measures of per-arm parameter posteriors handle time-varying rewards (modeled via linear dynamical systems) and achieve good regret performance in previously elusive scenarios.

For training human forecasters ('Calibrate Your Judgment' app), 'practical' scoring rules are designed to be intuitive for right-vs-wrong probabilistic predictions, going beyond properness; two specific rules for prediction intervals — the 'Distance' and 'Order of magnitude' rules — are introduced to satisfy user-tested desirable properties (e.g., good performance rewarded, comprehensible feedback, efficient learning), even at the cost of giving up properness when it conflicts with usability.

In generalized Bradley-Terry models in random environment, the unknown distribution pi of hidden player strengths is estimated by a Bayesian nonparametric approach with posterior contraction rates and an MCMC sampler; the classic BT kernel is K(x, V_i, V_j) = V_i^x V_j^{1-x}/(V_i + V_j), and the MLE of strengths exists only if the directed win-graph connects every pair of players.

In Bradley-Terry models in random environment, the winner of a championship is the player with maximal strength if and only if the tail of the strength distribution pi is sufficiently convex, so tournament-outcome predictions can be inferred from the estimated pi even when each player has been involved in as few as 2 contests.

A simple quantile-regression forecaster for GEFCom2017 probabilistic load forecasting (log-transformed hourly load split into a long-term trend stabilized by temperature plus a remainder modeled with weekly/annual seasonalities and interactions, ignoring public holidays) placed second in the open-data track and fourth in the definite-data track among ~100 teams and consistently beats the Vanilla benchmark.

The pinball (quantile) loss at level tau is S_tau(y, q) = 1_{y >= q} tau (y - q) + 1_{q > y} (1 - tau) (q - y) = (y - q)(tau - 1_{y - q < 0}), where q is the quantile forecast and y the observed load.

SplineCalib calibrates classifier probabilities with a robust non-parametric smoothing-spline calibration function, improving on sigmoid (Platt scaling) and piecewise-constant (isotonic regression) fits especially for overconfident deep-learning scores; it extends to multi-class problems, improves both log-loss and accuracy by resolving uncertain cases, and uses a cross-validated approach that conserves data (implemented in the ml-insights Python package).

A pre-trained CaffeNet CNN regresses marker-based motion-capture input to 3D knee joint moments for three sports movements; the strongest mean correlation to lab-grade inverse-dynamics modeling was 0.8895 over the initial 33% of stance phase for sidestepping, and a double-cascade transfer-learning technique improved nearly all correlations, demonstrating feasibility of on-field ACL knee-injury-risk monitoring via deep learning without laboratory force plates.

Augmented APM recasts soccer adjusted plus-minus in a Bayesian framework with FIFA video-game ratings (subjective evaluations from 9000+ scouts, coaches, and season-ticket holders covering 18,000+ players) as the prior; it predicts better than both standard APM and FIFA-only models in 10-fold cross-validation and decorrelates highly collinear players.
The ridge-regression APM objective is beta-hat = argmin_beta ||y - X beta||_2^2 + lambda ||beta||_2^2, with player effects given the prior N(alpha x rating, tau^2) centered on the scaled FIFA rating.

A systematic review of sports data mining literature (ACM Digital Library, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, Semantic Scholar; boolean search over sports + data mining/machine learning/deep learning/AI terms) finds data mining techniques reduce manual workload and errors and can improve fairness and development of sports, with applications guiding athletes on performance improvement and error elimination.

Neural networks trained on 2006-2017 data predict NHL skaters' points per game from physical characteristics, shooting percentage, and game usage, outperforming other regression methods and matching TSN.ca/NHL.com projections; a novel Player Availability Rating (PAR) quantifies a player's availability from current performance versus prediction, normalized by season and recent scoring context.

The Player Availability Rating is PAR = (PPG_predicted - PPG_actual)/PPCG_season + w_o * (PPG_predicted - PPG_actual)/PPCG_recent, where PPCG is the points-per-game context of the season/recent period and w_o weights the recent component.

A risk-neutral valuation framework prices and hedges in-play football bets by modeling scores as independent Poisson processes with constant intensities; the Fundamental Theorems of Asset Pricing yield novel arbitrage-free valuation formulas for traded contracts (e.g., half-time/full-time bets), with calibration to market data and replication/hedging strategies described.

The self-financing hedging portfolio for in-play football bets has value V_t^phi = phi_{0t} B_t + phi_{1t} S_t^1 + phi_{2t} S_t^2 = V_0^phi + int phi_{1s} dS_s^1 + int phi_{2s} dS_s^2, where B is the bank account and S^1, S^2 are the underlying score-contingent assets.

Analogical proportions ('A relates to B as C relates to D') are connected to kernel functions on pairs of objects via generalized fuzzy equivalence relations, yielding the analogy kernel k_A(a,b,c,d) = (1/d) sum_{i=1}^d k(a_i,b_i,c_i,d_i), which is positive semi-definite; SVMs trained with it for object ranking are competitive with state-of-the-art (RankSVM, able2rank) on sports, education, and tourism datasets.

Ranking disagreement is measured by the normalized Kendall tau distance d_RL(pi, pi') = [sum_{i,j} [pi(i) < pi(j)] [pi'(i) > pi'(j)]] / [n(n-1)/2], the fraction of pairwise orderings on which two rankings disagree.

The population intervention effect defined through stochastic interventions on exposure decomposes into direct and indirect effects with identification requiring weaker assumptions than the average-treatment-effect decomposition (assuming no mediator-outcome confounders affected by exposure); direct effects are identified in experiments randomizing both exposure and mediator, and the efficient estimator is asymptotically linear under n^{1/4}-consistency of the regression functions; illustrated by estimating the effect of children's sports-team participation on BMI with mediators exercise habits, snack consumption, and overweight status.

The cross-fitted efficient estimator is theta-hat(delta) = (1/n) sum_{i=1}^n D_{eta-hat_{j(i)}, delta}(O_i) = (1/n) sum_i {D^Y_{eta-hat,delta}(O_i) + D^A_{eta-hat,delta}(O_i) + D^{Z,W}_{eta-hat,delta}(O_i)}, decomposing the influence function into outcome, exposure, and mediator/covariate components.

A novel openly available multimodal sensor dataset for human activity recognition covers nine indoor activities performed by 16 participants captured by four sensor types (RGB-D, LiDAR, and others common in indoor applications and autonomous vehicles); a deep neural network reached mean accuracy of up to 96.8% for classification across all stationary and dynamic activities using the RGB-D data, with a novel context-dependent feature-extraction preprocessing algorithm proposed.

UK bookmakers' betting odds and free coupons are evaluated as a set of desirable gambles: the Choquet integral (via natural extension / linear programming) checks whether the set avoids sure loss for the bookmaker; without free coupons the market odds avoid sure loss, but with free coupons some combinations of bets give customers a guaranteed gain, and complementary slackness determines the combination achieving the best possible sure gain.

For the Colonel Blotto game under both objectives — (i) maximizing guaranteed expected payoff and (ii) maximizing the probability of obtaining a minimum payoff u (election-style) — (almost) optimal strategies with few strategies in their support are found by partitioning the non-convex solution space into polynomially many disjoint convex polytopes considered independently, yielding polynomial-time approximation schemes for both; the paper also gives the first complexity result for computing the maximin of a generalized Colonel Blotto game.

SelectiveNet is a three-headed deep neural network with an integrated reject option trained end-to-end to optimize classification/regression and rejection simultaneously via a selective loss (a variant of interior-point optimization) for a user-specified target coverage; it consistently improves the risk-coverage trade-off over MC-dropout and softmax-response baselines, reaching new state-of-the-art results for deep selective classification on four datasets and providing the first practical alternative to MC-dropout/ensembles for selective regression.

The true risk of a prediction function is R(f) = E_{P(X,Y)}[l(f(x), y)] and its empirical risk on a sample S_m is r-hat(f|S_m) = (1/m) sum_{i=1}^m l(f(x_i), y_i), where l is the loss (0/1 error or squared loss).

The first comprehensive study of pace of play in ice hockey (from spatio-temporal data) finds pace varies across rink zones, periods, manpower situations, leagues, and seasons; the negative correlation between attacking speed and shots/goals is explained by a large decline in attacking speed in the offensive zone; pace is positively correlated with high-danger zone entries (odd-man rushes) and higher shot quality, but failed pass receptions occur at higher speeds than successful ones — increased pace is beneficial up to a point, creating defensive breakdowns but also more turnovers.

Range Value at Risk (RVaR_{alpha,beta}) is the average of all VaR_gamma for gamma between alpha and beta, a natural interpolation with RVaR_{beta,beta} = VaR_beta and RVaR_{0,beta} = ES_beta; it has breakdown point min{alpha, 1-beta}, placing it between the robust VaR (breakdown min{beta,1-beta}) and the entirely non-robust ES (breakdown 0).

Like expected shortfall, RVaR alone is not elicitable (admits no strictly consistent scoring function), but a triplet of RVaR with two VaR components at different levels is elicitable; the paper characterizes the class of strictly consistent scoring functions for this triplet, examines their properties including Murphy diagrams, and illustrates with a simulation study.

A dynamic paired-comparison model using a Gaussian process prior for skill time-dynamics (instead of the usual Markovian dynamics), fit by efficient approximate Bayesian inference via the Laplace approximation with sparse linear algebra and hyperparameters selected by maximizing marginal likelihood with Bayesian optimization, outperforms Elo and Glicko on 2018 ATP tennis matches in log loss (0.631 for GP with surface covariates vs. 0.639 for Elo started in 2016), particularly when surface covariates are included.
The Bradley-Terry win likelihood is P(y=1 | theta_i, theta_j) = 1/(1 + e^{theta_j - theta_i}) = logit^{-1}(theta_i - theta_j), where theta_i, theta_j are the latent abilities.

The GP uses an ARD squared-exponential kernel k(x, x' | alpha, rho) = alpha^2 exp(-sum_{k=1}^{n_c} (x_k - x'_k)^2/(2 rho_k^2)) with per-covariate lengthscales rho_k, and model comparison uses log loss(y, p) = -(1/n) sum_i [y_i log(p_i) + (1-y_i) log(1-p_i)], the negative mean log-likelihood.

Machine-learning risk models (explicit algorithm + source code) produce covariance matrices that are not factor models; when the number of assets N greatly exceeds observations T the sample covariance is singular (rank at most T-1) and sample correlations are unstable out of sample; heterotic risk models based on granular fundamental industry classifications sizeably outperform statistical (PCA-based) risk models, while style factors are poor proxies for modeling correlations and add little to no value, and Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage is just a special type of statistical risk model.

A Bayesian parametric Gaussian-process model of cricketers' long-term batting ability between innings, fit by nested sampling, quantifies career trajectories more accurately than the traditional batting average: young players start with raw ability, improve with coaching and experience to a peak, then decline; the model rejects recent form ('being in form') as a significant predictor of near-future innings, while finding overwhelming evidence that players bat worse early in an innings and improve as they score runs ('getting your eye in'); it identifies which players are improving or deteriorating for talent identification and selection.

Long-term equilibrium batting ability over a career follows log(mu_{2t}) ~ Gaussian process(m, K(X_i, X_j; sigma, l)), with priors m ~ Lognormal(log(25), 0.75^2) and sigma ~ Exponential(10); the full parameter vector is theta = {mu_1, {mu_{2t}}, L, m, sigma, l}.

Pairwise-comparison models with flexible time dynamics replace static skill parameters with continuous-time Gaussian processes whose covariance functions enable expressive dynamics; an efficient approximate-Bayesian inference algorithm needs only a few linear-time iterations over the data and exploits multiprocessors, outperforms competing approaches on historical sports databases (including data with strong intransitivities), scales to millions of observations, and generates interpretable skill-trajectory visualizations.

The approximate posterior over skill trajectories factorizes as p(s_1, ..., s_M | D) ~= q(s_1, ..., s_M) = prod_{m=1}^M N(s_m | mu_m, Sigma_m), with the Gaussian update Sigma_m = (K_m^{-1} + Sigma-tilde_m^{-1})^{-1} and mu_m = Sigma_m Sigma-tilde_m^{-1} mu-tilde_m combining the GP prior precision K_m^{-1} with the likelihood site precision Sigma-tilde_m^{-1}.

Teams spend millions of dollars every year on players who are hurt and unable to play, resulting in lost games, decreased fan interest and additional wages for replacement players. Modern convolutional neural networks have been successfully applied to many video recognition tasks. In this paper, we introduce the problem of injury detection/prediction in MLB pitchers and experimentally evaluate the ability of such convolutional models to detect and predict injuries in pitches only from video data. Paper overview — 'Reliable Multilabel Classification: Prediction with'. Abstract: In contrast to conventional (single-label) classification, the setting of multilabel classification (MLC) allows an instance to belong to several classes simultaneously. Thus, instead of selectinga single class label, predictions take the form ofa subset of all labels. In this paper, we study an extension of the setting of MLC, in which the learner is allowed to partially abstain froma prediction, that is, to deliver predictions on some but not necessarily all class labels. We proposea formalization of MLC with abstention in terms ofa generalized loss minimization problem and present first results for the case of the Hamming loss, rank loss, and F-measure, both theoretical and experimental.

This article is devoted to the forecast of the Africa Cup of Nations 2019 football tournament. It is based ona Poisson regression model that includes the Elo points of the participating teams as covariates and incorporates differences of team-specific skills. The proposed model allows predictions in terms of probabilities in order to quantify the chances for each team to reacha certain stage of the tournament. Monte Carlo simulations are used to estimate the outcome of each single match of the tournament and hence to simulate the whole tournament itself. The model is fitted on all football games on neutral ground of the participating teams since 2010. 1.

claim: From the abstract of 'Conformal Prediction': We discuss the concept of Conformal Prediction (CP) in the context of short-term electricity price forecasting.

From the abstract of 'Conformal Prediction': Therefore, we elaborate the aspects that render Conformal Prediction worthwhile to know and explain why this simple yet very effective idea has worked in other fields of application and why its characteristics are promising for short-term power applications as well.

From the abstract of 'Conformal Prediction': Its performance is compared with different state-of-the-art electricity price forecasting models, such as quantile regression averaging (QRA), in an empirical out-of-sample study for three short-term electricity time series.
From the abstract of 'Conformal Prediction': We combine Conformal Prediction with various underlying point forecast models to demonstrate its versatility and behavior under changing conditions.
From the abstract of 'Conformal Prediction': Our findings suggest that Conformal Prediction yields sharp and reliable prediction intervals in short-term power markets.
From the abstract of 'Conformal Prediction': We further inspect the effect each of the model components has and providea path-based guideline on how to find the best CP model for each market.
From the abstract of 'Conformal Prediction': Keywords: Energy forecasting, Prediction intervals, Electricity price forecasting, Probability forecasting, Quantile regression, Linear models1

claim: From the abstract of 'Combating Label Noise in': We introducea novel method to combat label noise when training deep neural networks for classification.

From the abstract of 'Combating Label Noise in': We proposea loss function that permits abstention during training thereby allowing the DNN to abstain on confusing samples while continuing to learn and improve classification performance on the non-abstained samples.
From the abstract of 'Combating Label Noise in': We show how sucha deep abstaining classifier (DAC) can be used for robust learning in the presence of different types of label noise.

From the abstract of 'Combating Label Noise in': In the case of structured or systematic label noise– where noisy training labels or confusing examples are correlated with underlying features of the data– training with abstention enables representation learning for features that are associated with unreliable labels.

From the abstract of 'Combating Label Noise in': In the case of unstructured (arbitrary) label noise, abstention during training enables the DAC to be used as an effective data cleaner by identifying samples that are likely to have label noise.

From the abstract of 'Combating Label Noise in': We provide analytical results on the loss function behavior that enable dynamic adaption of abstention rates based on learning progress during training.

From the abstract of 'Combating Label Noise in': We demonstrate the utility of the deep abstaining classifier for various image classification tasks under different types of label noise; in the case of arbitrary label noise, we show significant improvements over previously published results on multiple image benchmarks.

From the abstract of 'next-gen-scraPy: Extracting NFL Tracking Data from Images to': Our work aims to partially close the gap between what data is available privately (to NFL teams) and publicly, and our contribution is twofold.
