Used August 2016–March 2018 to build a near-complete dataset of Greek-speaking Twitter: about 330 thousand accounts, 750 million tweets (424 million in Greek), 750 million follow relations, 300 thousand lists (119 million memberships), 705 thousand trending topics, and information on 52 million users total (292 thousand since suspended, 141 thousand deleted, 3.5 million protected). The mined retweet, quote, reply, and mention graphs plus the follow relation offer broad research opportunities.

An interrupted-time-series study of NFL injuries before and after the 2011 Collective Bargaining Agreement (player-seasons 2007–2016, regular-season non-illness non-head game-loss injuries from Football Outsiders/NFL injury reports) found NO statistically significant detrimental changes associated with the CBA: it did not observe a sustained increase in conditioning-dependent or non-conditioning-dependent injuries or games missed. The CBA reduced off-game physical burdens (OTAs 14→10 days, voluntary offseason program 14→9 weeks, elimination of twice-daily padded practices in camp). Fitted model: ln(Y_ij) = ln(G_ij) + beta_0 + beta_1 t_ij + beta_2 CBA_ij + beta_3 PostCBA_ij + beta_4 Age_ij + b_0i + e_ij, where beta_1 + beta_3 exponentiated gives the percent change in injuries year-to-year in the post-CBA era.

Metulini's 'Players Movements and Team Shooting Performance' applies cluster analysis and multidimensional scaling to GPS-tracked time instants of player movements in professional basketball (three games at the Italian Basketball Cup Final Eight): consistently across case studies, defensive clusters show players close together while transition clusters are characterized by large spacing, and the analysis identifies the player-positioning patterns that produce the best team shooting performance.

Sharma et al.'s 'Wearable Audio and IMU Based Shot Detection in Racquet Sports' is the first fusion-based wearable solution for sports analysis: a wrist-worn system combining microphone audio (8 kHz) and IMU (100 Hz accelerometer + gyroscope) for shot detection in table tennis and badminton, with a synchronization block aligning the two sensor streams in time via computed signal offset. Each modality produces a shot-likelihood sequence at 100 Hz; the audio detector uses an energy-peak-detection plus MFCC-refinement cascade. It achieves 95.6% shot-detection accuracy in table tennis, a sport difficult for IMU or audio alone.

Haugen and Owren's 'Predicting football tables by a maximally parsimonious model' analyzes football-table prediction quality via mean absolute error of position permutations: MAE = (1/n) sum_{i=1}^n |P(i) - i| and MSE = (1/n) sum_{i=1}^n (P(i) - i)^2. Under a random guess, MAE_MIN = 0, MAE_MAX = n/2, and E[MAE] = (1/3)(n^2 - 1)/n. Applied to Paul Merson's 2016/17 Premier League table prediction: MAE = 2.8 (two perfect hits — Chelsea 1st, Swansea 15th — eight off-by-one, worst miss Bournemouth predicted 18th finished 9th).

Rasp and Lerch's 'Neural networks for post-processing ensemble weather forecasts' replaces distributional-regression post-processing (EMOS/BMA) with neural networks that map arbitrary predictor variables to forecast-distribution parameters, learning nonlinear relationships data-driven rather than via pre-specified link functions. In a 2-meter-temperature case study at German surface stations, the NN approach significantly outperformed benchmark post-processing methods while being computationally more affordable; key ingredients were auxiliary predictor variables and station-specific information via embeddings. The trained networks also yield meteorological variable-importance insights, challenging the black-box view of NNs.

'On Elo based prediction models for the FIFA World Cup 2018' fits four Poisson regression models of increasing complexity using Elo points as covariates with team-specific effect differences, trained on neutral-ground matches of participating teams since 2010; Monte Carlo simulations estimate each team's stage-reaching probabilities and a Sankey diagram visualizes all tournament courses. The paper proposes two new score functions for ordinal random variables, validated with the rank probability score and Brier score on the 2010 and 2014 World Cups: e.g. error_4(T) = (1/5) sum_{i=1}^{5} (sum_{j=1}^{i} p_j(T) - 1_{[result(T)=j]})^2, where result(T) = 1 for the winner, 2 final loser, 3 semifinal exit, 4 quarterfinal exit, 5 round-of-16 exit, 6 round-robin exit. All models favor Germany (followed by Brazil) as 2018 champion; inflated-model probabilities are near zero and the inflation model is judged not to improve forecasts.

Byrnes and Barnett's 'Generalized framework for applying the Kelly criterion to stock markets' takes an arbitrary probability distribution modeling future price movements of a set of stocks and computes the Kelly fraction for each stock by inverting a matrix involving only first and second moments — covering one stock or a whole portfolio, efficiently. For geometric Brownian motion of a single stock the framework reproduces the known Kelly fraction f = mu/sigma^2 (mu = growth rate, sigma = relative volatility), and it is demonstrated for Gaussian distributions and correlated multivariate assets.

SMOGS (Social Network Metrics of Game Success) models basketball passes as directed dynamic relational links on a network within a multi-resolution stochastic process, adding multiplicative latent factors to capture higher-order player-interaction patterns that distinguish wins from losses; parameters are estimated with an MCMC sampler. Applied to the first high-resolution optical tracking dataset collected in college basketball games, the learned latent factors show significant differences between players' passing and receiving tendencies in losses versus wins. The model generalizes to other team sports and time-varying network observations. The latent log-rate is log(theta_{i,j}(t)) = W_{i,j}(t)^T eta_{i,j} + xi_{i,j}(s_i(t)) + tilde-xi_{i,j}(s_j(t)) + z_{i,j,g}(t).

Rigollet and Weed's 'Uncoupled isotonic regression via minimum Wasserstein deconvolution' tackles estimating a nondecreasing regression function f on [0,1] from only the UNORDERED sets {x_1,...,x_n} and {y_1,...,y_n} (no pairing info), where y_i = f(x_i) + xi_i with known noise distribution D. Using optimal transport tools they derive minimax rates under weak moment conditions on y_i and give an efficient algorithm achieving optimal rates, with upper and lower bounds via moment-matching arguments. The noiseless case is trivial (sort both sets and match order statistics), but with noise naive order-matching is inconsistent. Implications: relationships can be learned across datasets with no coupled pairs (e.g. wage data from a government agency vs housing prices from a bank), with privacy benefits and huge effective sample sizes.

'Discovery of causal paths in cardiorespiratory parameters' applies causal-discovery frameworks (Generalized Correlations, CAM, FGES, GFCI, Hill-Climbing, Tabu Search Bayesian-network learners) to ECG and impedance pneumography signals from 100 elite athletes in supine and standing rest positions, seeking time-independent causal paths without prior knowledge. The discovery is ambiguous but the mildest best-supported rules are: supine — tidal volume causes heart activity variation, which causes average heart activity, which causes respiratory timing; standing — normalized respiratory activity variation causes average heart activity. All parameters differ significantly between body positions (HR higher standing; RMSSD and respiratory parameters lower standing), and the results are consistent with medical background knowledge, suggesting breathing depth (not frequency) as the lever to influence heart rate variability. Generalized correlation: r*_{y|x} = sign(r_{xy}) . sqrt(1 - E{(Y-E(Y|X))}^2/var(Y)).

Hsieh, Gubner and Barmish's 'Rebalancing Frequency Considerations for Kelly-Optimal Stock Portfolios in a Control-Theoretic Framework' studies expected logarithmic growth g*_n as a function of rebalancing interval n (frequency f = 1/(n Delta t)) for Kelly-optimal portfolios of multiple risky assets. Answer to 'does high-frequency trading always win without transaction costs': often there are NO performance benefits to high-frequency trading. Key result: a new 'dominance' condition — if one asset satisfies dominance, the optimal portfolio consists of that asset alone ('all eggs in one basket') and performance becomes a constant function of rebalancing frequency, rendering rebalancing moot. Simulations confirm the dominant-asset condition on real stock prices.

Collier and Urdiales Llorens' 'Deep Contextual Multi-armed Bandits' gives a deep-learning contextual bandit framework that is both nonlinear and supports principled exploration: Thompson sampling is done via inference-time dropout as sampling from an approximate posterior over Bayesian neural network weights, and the dropout rate is LEARNED (not a hyperparameter) so exploration adjusts automatically as data accumulate. It substantially reduced regret versus non-contextual bandits, epsilon-greedy deep contextual bandits, and fixed-dropout deep contextual bandits on the UCI Mushroom and Casino Parity tasks; the method is applied to marketing optimization at HubSpot (e.g. optimizing email send time where context includes sender timezone and only the chosen send time's conversion is observed).

Leathart et al.'s 'Probability Calibration Trees' modify logistic model trees to identify regions of the input space in which different local probability-calibration models are learned, instead of applying one global calibration (Platt scaling or isotonic regression). The method achieved lower root mean squared error on average than both isotonic regression and Platt scaling for probability estimates from a variety of base learners. Motivation: well-calibrated probabilities are needed for cost-sensitive decisions minimizing total expected cost sum_{i=1}^m C(y' = i | y = j) P(y = j | x), for use as inputs to other models, and for unbalanced classes.

Urteaga and Wiggins' 'Nonparametric Gaussian Mixture Models for the Multi-Armed Bandit' extends Thompson sampling to reward-model uncertainty using independent Bayesian nonparametric Gaussian mixture models per arm: each arm's reward density is estimated flexibly, its complexity adjusting as bandit rewards are observed, guiding subsequent arm selection. The paper derives an asymptotic regret bound via a novel posterior-convergence analysis and empirically outperforms state-of-the-art alternatives in both average cumulative regret and regret volatility in previously elusive environments — rewards outside the exponential family, outliers, and different per-arm reward distributions.

Urteaga and Wiggins' 'Sequential Monte Carlo Bandits' extends Bayesian multi-armed bandit algorithms beyond stationary exponential-family settings by using sequential Monte Carlo to estimate the sufficient statistics Bayesian MAB agents need: SMC-updated random measures of per-arm parameter posteriors yield flexible policies for bandits with nonlinear, stateless- and context-dependent reward distributions that evolve over time. They demonstrate good regret performance on non-stationary bandits (time dynamics modeled via linear dynamical systems) with nonlinear rewards — scenarios where classic closed-form MAB statistics are analytically intractable.

Greenberg's 'Calibration Scoring Rules for Practical Prediction Training' argues that proper scoring rules, while incentive-compatible, are neither broad enough nor narrow enough for real calibration training: for the 'Calibrate Your Judgment' app (thousands of practice questions with immediate scores and calibration curves), he proposes 'Practical' scoring rules designed to be intuitive for 'right' vs 'wrong' probabilistic predictions, plus two specific scoring rules for prediction intervals — the 'Distance' and 'Order of magnitude' rules — chosen from user testing to satisfy properties like rewarding good prediction performance, fast learning, and a comprehensible, enjoyable user experience.

Le Corff, Lerasle and Vernet's 'A Bayesian nonparametric approach for generalized Bradley-Terry models in random environment' estimates the unknown distribution pi of hidden player-strength variables V_i (i.i.d. on (0, +inf)) from observed pairwise comparisons: each contest between i and j yields outcome x with known probability K(x, V_i, V_j), the classic case being K(x, V_i, V_j) = V_i^x V_j^{1-x}/(V_i + V_j) for x in {0,1}. Three contributions: contraction rates of the posterior distribution, an MCMC algorithm to sample from it inspired by Bayesian nonparametric methods for hidden Markov models, and championship-prediction comparisons against actual team values. Key background results: the MLE exists only if the win-graph connects all player pairs; the MLE of the strength distribution pi is still defined when each player has only 2 contests; and the championship winner is the maximal-strength player iff the tail of pi is sufficiently convex.

Ziel's 'Quantile Regression for Qualifying Match of GEFCom2017 Probabilistic Load Forecasting' (team 'simple_but_good') forecasts ISO New England electricity load with a deliberately simple method: hourly load is log-transformed and split into a long-term trend plus a remainder; the key element is quantile regression on the remainder capturing weekly and annual seasonalities and their interactions, with temperature used only to stabilize the trend forecast and public holidays ignored. Despite its simplicity it placed 2nd in the open-data track and 4th in the definite-data track among about 100 teams and consistently beat the Vanilla benchmark. Evaluation used the pinball score S_tau(y, q) = 1_{y>=q} tau(y - q) + 1_{q>y} (1 - tau)(q - y) = (y - q)(tau - 1_{y-q<0}) for quantile levels {0.1, ..., 0.9}.

Lucena's 'Spline-Based Probability Calibration' proposes SplineCalib, a robust non-parametric probability-calibration method using smoothing splines to learn the calibration function; applying certain transformations within calibration improves performance on overconfident deep-learning scores. It adapts to multi-class problems, and better calibration improved both log-loss AND accuracy by resolving uncertain cases; a cross-validated approach conserves data. Significant improvements on several problems; implemented in the ml-insights Python package.

'On-field player workload exposure and knee injury risk monitoring via deep learning' replaces laboratory force plates with deep learning: using a pre-trained CaffeNet CNN, multivariate regression maps marker-based motion-capture input (flattened to color images) to 3D knee joint moments (KJM) for three sports-related movement types, with output dimensionality reduced by deinterlacing the six component waveforms and PCA (threshold 0.999). The strongest mean correlation to source biomechanical modeling was 0.8895 over the initial 33% of stance phase for sidestepping; the double-cascade technique (initializing from an earlier CaffeNet GRF/M model) improved all but one correlation and reordered the result league table. The accuracy on the three critical KJM associated with ACL injury demonstrates feasibility of on-field knee-injury risk assessment for community and professional athletes.

Szymanski-style 'Augmenting Adjusted Plus-Minus in Soccer with FIFA Ratings': recasts APM into a Bayesian framework where FIFA ratings (subjective evaluations of 9000+ scouts, coaches, season-ticket holders over 18,000+ players) enter as the prior distribution N(alpha x rating, tau^2) on player coefficients. Augmented APM predicted better than both standard APM and a FIFA-ratings-only model (10-fold CV, MSE of predicted game segments vs actual results) and decorrelates highly collinear players. Built on ridge-regression APM: beta-hat = argmin_beta ||y - X beta||_2^2 + lambda ||beta||_2^2; APM works in basketball/hockey but struggles in soccer due to low scoring and few substitutions.

A systematic review of sports data-mining literature (published in Advances in Human-Computer Interaction, 2018) searched ACM Digital Library, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect and Semantic Scholar with the Boolean string ((sports OR sport OR sports science) AND (data mining OR mining OR computational intelligence OR machine learning OR deep learning OR artificial intelligence)), following a planning–conducting–analysis protocol to summarize evidence on sports data-mining techniques (only review-level content was recoverable from this document).

The Player Availability Rating (PAR) project predicts NHL offensive production as points per game (PPG = goals + assists per game) from physical characteristics (height, weight), expected shooting percentage and usage (expected time on ice), trained on 2006–2017 data; neural networks produced the closest estimates to the established baselines (comparable to TSN.ca and NHL.com projections, which the paper uses as the top reference for player projections). The novel PAR metric PAR = (PPG_predicted - PPG_actual)/(PPCG_season) + w_o (PPG_predicted - PPG_actual)/(PPCG_recent) quantifies a player's availability from current individual performance and team performance. The algorithm was deployed on gmaiplaybook.com.

Football HEAD develops a risk-neutral valuation framework for pricing and hedging in-play football bets: scores are modeled by independent Poisson processes with constant intensities, and the Fundamental Theorems of Asset Pricing are applied to derive arbitrage-free valuation formulas for contracts traded in the market, with calibration to market data and demonstration of replication performance. Portfolios evolve self-financing as V_t^phi = V_0^phi + integral phi_1s dS_s^1 + integral phi_2s dS_s^2, and explicit valuations are given for exotic categories such as Half-Time/Full-Time bets (9 combinations of the 3 outcomes per half).

Hullermeier et al.'s 'Analogy-Based Preference Learning with Kernels' connects analogical reasoning with kernel-based machine learning: analogical proportions of the form 'A relates to B as C relates to D' define kernel functions on pairs of objects (via generalized fuzzy equivalence relations), yielding the analogy kernel k_A(a,b,c,d) = (1/d) sum_{i=1}^d k(a_i,b_i,c_i,d_i) measuring how strongly four objects stand in analogical relationship. Applied to object ranking in preference learning, an SVM trained with the analogy kernel was competitive with state-of-the-art (on par with able2rank and Ranking SVM, better than ERR and RankNet) on datasets from sports, education, tourism and other domains.

Diaz and van der Laan's 'Causal mediation analysis for stochastic interventions' decomposes the population intervention effect — defined through stochastic (rather than deterministic/binary) interventions on the exposure — into direct and indirect effects, covering continuous and categorical exposures. Identification of direct and indirect effects requires WEAKER assumptions than the average-treatment-effect counterpart, under no mediator-outcome confounders affected by exposure; in particular, direct-effect identification is guaranteed in experiments randomizing both exposure and mediator. They discuss substitution, re-weighted, and efficient estimators allowing multivariate mediators with flexible regression; the efficient estimator is asymptotically linear under n^{1/4}-consistency of certain regression functions. Simulations assess finite-sample properties, and an illustrative study estimates the effect of sports-team participation on children's BMI via exercise habits, snack consumption, and overweight-status mediators.

'Adaptive Feature Processing for Robust Human Activity Recognition' presents a novel open multimodal sensor dataset for human activity recognition: nine indoor activities performed by 16 participants captured by four sensor types (RGB-D depth/color, LiDAR, and others common in indoor applications and autonomous vehicles) — the first dataset of its kind openly available, usable for sports analytics, healthcare, and indoor mobility. It proposes a novel preprocessing algorithm for context-dependent feature extraction and reviews ML approaches to posture recognition: a deep neural network reached up to 96.8% mean accuracy across stationary and dynamic activities on the RGB-D data.

Nakharutai, Caiado and Troffaes' 'Evaluating betting odds and free coupons using desirability' models UK bookmaker odds and free coupons as a set of desirable gambles (mathematically equivalent to a set of probability distributions via duality): the Choquet integral checks whether the bookmaker's set incurs sure loss — i.e., whether a customer can make a guaranteed gain — and complementary slackness determines the combination of bets giving the best possible sure gain. Checking 'avoids sure loss' is a linear programming problem. On actual market odds, without free coupons the desirable gambles derived from odds avoid sure loss, but WITH free coupons the authors identified bet combinations yielding a guaranteed gain. The analysis also frames greater odds and free coupons as bookmaker tools to entice new customers.

'Optimal Strategies of Blotto Games: Beyond Convexity' studies the Colonel Blotto game (Borel 1921): two colonels simultaneously divide troop pools among battlefields, winning each battlefield with more troops, utility = sum of weights of won battlefields. For both objectives — (i) maximizing guaranteed expected payoff and (ii) maximizing the probability of attaining a minimum payoff u (the election-style objective) — the paper obtains (almost) optimal solutions with few strategies in support: the non-convex bounded-support solution space is partitioned via structural results into polynomially many disjoint convex polytopes considered independently, yielding polynomial-time approximation schemes for both objectives. It also gives the first complexity result for computing the maximin of a generalized Colonel Blotto game.

Geifman and El-Yaniv's SelectiveNet (ICML) is a deep neural architecture with an integrated reject option: unlike post-hoc confidence thresholds on pre-trained networks, its three-headed network is trained end-to-end to optimize classification (or regression) and rejection simultaneously for a user-specified coverage slice, via a selective loss optimized with an interior-point method. It achieved consistently improved risk–coverage trade-offs on several classification and regression datasets — new state-of-the-art for deep selective classification and the first alternative to costly MC-dropout/ensemble techniques for selective regression.

The first comprehensive study of pace of play in hockey (2019 Sloan Sports Analytics Conference) measures team-level pace from spatio-temporal data across rink zones, periods, manpower situations, leagues, and seasons. Findings: the reported negative correlation between attacking speed and shots/goals is likely explained by a large decline in attacking speed in the offensive zone; pace is positively correlated with high-danger zone entries (e.g., odd-man rushes) and higher shot quality, but passes with failed receptions occur at higher speeds than successful ones. Conclusion: increased pace is beneficial up to a point — it creates breakdowns in defensive structure and better scoring chances but also more turnovers — with considerable team/player variability in attacking and defending pace.

Fissler and Ziegel's 'Evaluating Range Value at Risk Forecasts' studies RVaR_{alpha,beta}, defined as the average of all VaR_gamma with gamma between alpha and beta — a natural interpolation between VaR_beta = RVaR_{beta,beta} (robust quantile) and ES_beta = RVaR_{0,beta} (sensitive, coherent tail expectation), with breakdown point min{alpha, 1 - beta} placing it between VaR and ES (breakdown 0). Key result: like Expected Shortfall, RVaR admits NO strictly consistent scoring function (it is not elicitable), but a triplet of RVaR with two VaR components at different levels IS elicitable; the paper characterizes the class of strictly consistent scoring functions for this triplet and examines Murphy diagrams as a diagnostic tool, with a simulation study and connections to trimmed least squares in robust regression.

'Gaussian Process Priors for Dynamic Paired Comparison Modelling' replaces the Markovian time dynamics of Elo/Glicko with a Gaussian process prior over players' latent abilities, easily incorporating covariates like playing surface, with efficient approximate Bayesian inference via the Laplace approximation and sparse linear algebra and hyperparameters selected by Bayesian optimization of the marginal likelihood. The Bradley-Terry likelihood is P(y=1 | theta_i, theta_j) = logit^{-1}(theta_i - theta_j). On the 2018 ATP tennis season it outperformed Elo and Glicko on log loss — particularly with surface covariates (log loss 0.631 vs 0.639 for Elo started 2016) — though Elo kept a slight accuracy edge (64.4% vs 63.7% for the best GP); starting Elo/Glicko in 2002 (more history) improved both their metrics.

Kakushadze and Yu's 'Machine Learning Risk Models' gives an explicit algorithm plus source code for building risk models via machine-learning clustering rather than factor models: when the number of stocks N exceeds observations T, the sample covariance is badly singular (rank at most T-1) with unstable out-of-sample correlations. Statistical risk models (first K principal components) are limited since components beyond the first are unstable out-of-sample and Ledoit-Wolf 'shrinkage' is just a special statistical risk model; heterotic risk models built on granular fundamental industry classifications (BICS/GICS/ICB/SIC) sizably outperform statistical ones, and replacing fundamental classifications with multilevel statistical industry classifications from clustering return time series is the paper's ML approach. Style factors are judged poor proxies for correlations, adding little to no value.

'Modelling Career Trajectories of Cricket Players Using Gaussian Processes' derives a Bayesian parametric model with a Gaussian process for long-term batting-ability variation between innings, fitted via nested sampling: log(mu_{2_t}) ~ Gaussian process(m, K(X_i, X_j; sigma, ell)), with career shape mu(x) = mu_2 + (mu_1 - mu_2) exp(-x/L). Results support the anecdotal career arc (raw ability rising with coaching/experience to a peak, then declining) and are more accurate than batting average for current and future ability, identifying improving vs deteriorating players for talent ID and selection. It rejects batting 'form' — recent performances have no significant impact on near-future innings — but finds strong evidence for 'getting your eye in': decreased batting ability early in an innings improving as runs are scored.

'Pairwise Comparisons with Flexible Time-Dynamics' replaces the static parameters of popular pairwise-comparison models with continuous-time Gaussian processes whose covariance functions encode expressive skill dynamics (generalizing beyond Brownian motion), plus an efficient approximate Bayesian inference algorithm needing only a few linear-time passes over the data and exploiting multiprocessor architectures. The posterior is approximated as p(s_1,...,s_M | D) ~= q(s_1,...,s_M) = prod_{m=1}^M N(s_m | mu_m, Sigma_m) with Sigma_m = (K_m^{-1} + Sigma-tilde_m^{-1})^{-1} and mu_m = Sigma_m Sigma-tilde_m^{-1} mu-tilde_m. On historical sports outcome databases it outperformed competing approaches in predictive performance (even under strong intransitivities), scaled to millions of observations, and produced compelling visualizations for interpreting the data.

For Bitcoin price-movement prediction from social-media sentiment, one interpretable NLP sentiment model outperformed more than 20 other public models and could be fine-tuned efficiently because of its interpretable nature; the authors conclude interpretable AI/NLP methods may be more valuable practically than non-explainable, non-interpretable ones.

The authors tested many methods for computing sentiment metrics from text and found most of them not very accurate for the cryptocurrency price-prediction task, before analyzing potential causal connections between sentiment metrics and Bitcoin price movements.

A forecaster that outputs a deterministic short interval of probabilities of length at most 2*epsilon (instead of a point forecast) achieves epsilon-calibration for binary events against a fully adaptive adversary at the faster rate O(1/T), versus Theta(1/sqrt(T)) for randomized point forecasts (Foster and Vohra 1998 upper bound) and Theta(1) for deterministic point forecasts; such narrow intervals are as practically interpretable as point forecasts.

The O(1/sqrt(T)) calibration rate achieved by randomized point-forecast algorithms is tight: a forecaster playing Calibration-Game-I against an adversarial nature cannot achieve epsilon-calibration faster than Omega(1/sqrt(T)), proved via the equivalence between calibration and Blackwell approachability theorem (Blackwell 1956); the paper connects online calibration, the power of two choices, and imprecise probability.
equation: \Omega(1/\sqrt{T})\text{ lower bound on } \epsilon\text{-calibration rate in Calibration-Game-I}

claim: Hierarchical Multimodal Attention (HMA) for soccer video summarization learns, in a first stage, the importance of each modality (event data vs audio) at the event level and, in a second stage, the importance of each event inside the action; HMA outperforms state-of-the-art multimodal attention methods by 7% and "soccer baselines" by 15%.

The paper proposes an LSTM-Multiple Instance Learning schema for sequential data to generate action proposals for soccer summaries, based on variability among similar actions and similarity between actions that belong to the summary and those that do not, and a first-of-kind method for generating multiple summaries of a match by sampling from a ranking distribution.

Measured results: the soccer summarization method beats the state of the art by 6% in F-score and by 9% in generalization (predicting without fine-tuning to a different competition); audio features are exploited because commentator/crowd excitement identifies the most relevant actions.

The paper proposes a marketplace for aggregate forecast elicitation using a wagering mechanism aimed at improving the client utility through better forecasts: after players submit reports and wagers, the market operator creates a collective forecast \hat{r} using an aggregation operator, and the payoff function has a penalizing property named "stimulant".

As aggregation operators the paper compares the linear opinion pool (LOP) with quantile averaging / Wasserstein barycenter (with equal wager weights), and formalizes definitions for strictly proper scoring rules, non-local scoring, sensitivity to distance, the aggregation operator, the linear opinion pool, and quantile averaging.

A novel multi-target active object tracking method for sports cameras predicts the future positions of targets, selects the optimal camera action via Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS), and prunes the MCTS search tree using actions from a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) network, which greatly reduces the search space; experiments in three 2D environments validate it with ablation studies and comparison to HiT-MAC.

For multi-target active tracking, performance is measured by overall target coverage (e.g., cameras around a football field should cover as many players as possible); the team-reward weight \lambda in the MARL reward was found to affect target coverage.

The paper presents a nested zero-inflated generalized Poisson (ZIGP) regression model for estimating probabilities of exact football match scores; with \omega=0 and \varphi=1 it reduces to the classical Poisson distribution, while its flexible variance function handles overdispersion and underdispersion, unlike independent Poisson (one parameter fixing mean=variance) or bivariate Poisson (one extra correlation parameter).

Estimating exact scores (not just win/loss/draw) is necessary because goal difference is a crucial tiebreaker deciding group winner, runner-up, or elimination in World Cup group stages; the model was applied to FIFA World Cup 2022 forecasting with team-specific dispersion estimates, e.g. \varphi_{France}=1+e^{-11.846181}=1.000007 and \psi_{Denmark}=1+e^{-13.407282}=1.000002.

From soccer tracking data the authors show the player arrival region is circular and its initial-speed dependence satisfies the Fujimura-Sugihara model solution: the region center coordinate y_c is independent of initial speed v_0 (y_c \simeq 0) while x_c is proportional to v_0, and they propose a method to estimate the kinetic parameters of the Fujimura-Sugihara model from the \tau-dependence of mean squared displacement (MSD) averaged over all outfield players.

Measured kinetic parameters of the Fujimura-Sugihara model: proportionality coefficients 0.58 and 0.84 from the heat-map regression for arrival times \Delta t = 1 s and 2 s yield \alpha = 1.23 and 1.04 1/s respectively.

Home field advantage in sports is quantified at roughly 55-60% home-win rate (50% = no advantage), with 57.3% for American football versus 69% for soccer; the effect is most pronounced in indoor sports (ice hockey, basketball), and season length correlates negatively with home advantage: sports with 100+ games per season show significantly less advantage than sports with fewer than 50.

In basketball, visiting teams scored 2.8 points less, attempted 2 fewer free throws, and made 1 fewer free throw than their season averages (Calleja-Gonzalez et al. 2018), cited as evidence of home court advantage.

The paper models team outcomes across n teams with N = n(n-1) pairwise matches, using independent baseline effects \alpha_{i,j} for any pair on a hypothetical neutral field and random noise \epsilon_{i,j} ~ N(0,\sigma_0^2), under standard causal-inference assumptions that rule out correlation between different matches involving the same team.

The paper introduces a unified multivariate utility (MU)-based mechanism that incorporates several market-making mechanisms (Hanson 2003/2007, Chen-Pennock 2007, Agrawal et al. 2011) into one framework, and a method for establishing market convergence that subsumes Frongillo et al. 2015 and Sethi-Vaughan 2016; the limiting wealth distribution is Pareto optimal with respect to each trader utility.

For an exponential utility-based prediction market the authors derive the analytical price dynamics: the limiting price is the geometric mean of agents beliefs and is independent of trading sequences; for a wide range of convex risk measures the limiting price emerges as a weighted power mean of agent beliefs, and the impact of trading sequences on the limiting price diminishes to insignificance as the trader population increases.
equation: \lim p = \text{geometric mean of agents\u2019 beliefs (exponential utility)}

claim: A Bayesian dynamic linear model (DLM) with a monotone spline outcome transformation (Ramsay 1988) rates athletes in head-to-head and multi-competitor sports with score outcomes; using observed scores rather than rankings provides additional information that generally improves predictions, and the model fits via MCMC or MAP exploiting the Kalman filter, with latent abilities following a normal random walk.

For the DLM athlete-rating model with normal priors on the spline parameters \lambda_b, the Nelder-Mead algorithm gives the most stable optimization results although L-BFGS is much faster in practice; results are robust to the choice of rating period, and the procedure is implemented in the dlmt R package using US Olympic/Paralympic Committee data.

The paper tests five state-of-the-art deep tracking algorithms (including deep SORT) on tracking and identifying ice hockey players in broadcast NHL videos, noting a lack of publicly available deep-learning hockey-tracking research; the primary error sources found are pan-identity switches and extremely cluttered scenes.

The paper introduces a highly-scalable solver for vector quantile regression (VQR) using custom stochastic-gradient-based solvers with constant memory footprint regardless of problem size, scaling to millions of samples and thousands of quantile levels with GPU acceleration.

Nonlinear vector quantile regression (NL-VQR) is proposed to address the linear-specification limitation; synthetic and real-data experiments show it models complex conditional quantile functions substantially better than linear VQR and separable QR approaches, and the VMR procedure resolves co-monotonicity violations in estimated CVQFs (strictly improving estimation quality with zero violations).

A survey of sports action recognition finds research volume growing in the last five years with attention spreading to less-covered sports (diving, figure skating); it presents 4 types of deep models (2D, 3D, two-stream, skeleton-based) and covers both individual action recognition and team activity recognition, with action recognition improving highlight localization in sports TV programs.

The paper proposes C-OBSO (Creating Off-Ball Scoring Opportunity), an evaluation index for players who create scoring opportunities while off the ball, computed by comparing actual player movements to predicted movements from a trajectory-prediction model and scoring via a potential-score model that reflects the angle to goal and multiple defender positions in a mixed Gaussian distribution.

In a consensus protocol among n agents, if all agents private information were known the information obtainable about the event W is I(X_1,...,X_n;W), while after t rounds of the protocol it is I(H^t;W); both the Standard and Discretized Consensus Protocols quickly reach epsilon-MI consensus, and the paper proves the n-agent extension of the Alice-and-Bob results including Convergence-implies-Aggregation (Theorem 3.8).

For prediction markets related to the Standard Consensus Protocol, the paper shows the expected payment to an agent equals a function of the conditional mutual information of the random variables he reveals, with agents playing myopically to optimize payment at each step.

The expected-goal (xG) model is formalized with a d-dimensional feature vector X in R^d (predictors like shot type, distance to goal, angle to goal) and a binary label Y in {0,1}; the training data is highly imbalanced, causing poor minority-class prediction in prior work, and the paper proposes an xG model accurate on both classes plus an XAI application of aggregated CP profiles (semi-global explainers) for team/player performance evaluation.

Prior xG research cited shows five seasons of data are needed to train a complex xG model, the data does not go out of date, and league-based xG models do not significantly increase accuracy; xG models are used for performance evaluation instead of match outcomes (which are randomness-influenced short-term), e.g. plotting league-table rank against xG-based rank and computing offensive/defensive ratios.

Rigorous experiments in selective classification show the superior performance of SOTA methods comes from training a more generalizable classifier rather than their external head/logit selection mechanisms; future work should learn a more generalizable classifier and base the selection mechanism on the classifier itself rather than architecture modifications for an external head.

Entropy-minimization regularization (a common semi-supervised technique) significantly improves SOTA selective classification, and a selective classifier trained with the entropy-regularized loss plus Softmax-Response selection achieves new state-of-the-art results by a significant margin (up to 80% relative improvement).

The paper explores LSTM deep learning for predicting MLB players home runs from past statistics, comparing 5 LSTM variants plus GRU, BiLSTM, and attention-based LSTM against other ML models and the widely used ZiPS projection system (2018: 9,828 training / 184 test points; 2019: 10,006 training / 191 test points); LSTM models achieved low MAE and RMSE in 2018 and 2019, presented as a new baseline.

Findings: players hitting under 19 HRs are more predictable than high-HR hitters, and predicting performance for players who can hit at least 20 HRs remains a problem; model performance dropped when training only on pre-2019 data, so 2018 data points were added when predicting 2019.

For heterogeneous treatment effect (HTE) estimation in observational studies with random forests (mob), the empirical results identify treatment-effect centering, mob(\hat{W}) (local centering of the treatment variable W), as the most relevant ingredient; it significantly improved performance under confounding (setups A, C), motivating a novel "blended" HTE random forest for PPH combining the instrumental elements.

SoccerCPD is a change-point detection framework that distinguishes tactically intended formation and role changes from temporary switches in soccer matches using spatiotemporal tracking data; for a pair of formation graphs it finds the optimal permutation of role labels of one graph relative to the other and computes the Manhattan distance (Eq. 5) between the adjacency matrices, with applications to switching-pattern discovery and set-piece detection.

RPLIB is a searchable Rankability Problem Library of hundreds of ranking/linear-ordering instances (real and artificial data) with algorithms, code, and an interactive notebook; the paper expands rankability from three to four measures, proposing a fourth measure \beta that uses the number and location of fractional entries of the X^* matrix from the linear ordering model to penalize fractional entries farther from the diagonal and lower in the ranking.

In prior work the authors tied rankability to the presence, number, and properties of multiple optimal solutions to quantify a dataset inherent ability to produce a meaningful ranking; they found 98% of the 50 instances in the LOLIB IO folder share a property that motivated the new library.

The paper proposes a doubly-online changepoint detection model for smartwatch running data that combines the classical changepoint model of Yildirim et al. 2013 (enabling an SMC approach with constant complexity in a between-online framework) with a linear Gaussian state-space model (Durbin-Koopman 2012; Shumway-Stoffer 2017) whose Kalman filter routines update activity information as new observations arrive, for early detection of distributional changes from physical discomfort, de-training, or sensor malfunction.

For predicting young runners performances, missing-data patterns were found to be informative and a structural part of the signal explaining observed variability; the analysis used a matrix-variate state-space model with two processes describing the temporal dynamics of missing-data patterns (when a runner starts/stops competing), augmenting the likelihood with states \mathcal{A}, missing observations \widetilde{\mathcal{Y}}, and selection matrix S.
The paper reports that predicting the studied event with ML sequence models has limited applicability (abs-level finding; the fulltext scrape carries only this conclusion).

The paper solves ranking from multiple types of pairwise comparisons (e.g., animal dominance behaviors like rushing attacks, nod/broadside threats; sports moves with varying success) without knowing in advance either the ranking or what each interaction type conveys, using an efficient method combining expectation-maximization with a Bradley-Terry variant; different interaction modes contribute more or less to establishing dominance, and subordinate actions (following, copying, watching) are also informative once classified.

The multimodal ranking method was validated on synthetic data and three real-world datasets (an animal dominance hierarchy, a human hierarchy, and a competitive team-sports example), significantly outperforming standard unimodal approaches in the reported tests.

The paper presents a comprehensive set of baseline methods and Python modules for a proposed hybrid approach to tabular data, noting that finding the optimal cocktail with tuned modern regularization can boost performance comparable to SOTA end-to-end deep-learning models, and proposing baseline experiments splitting variables into Pres-type (manipulated) and Unis-type (control) groups.

For competitive online shooter games, engineered behavioral ratings outperform popular rating systems (e.g., Elo-like systems) in rank prediction, especially when combined with rating-system outputs using optimal weights in a weighted hybrid; the approach creates accurate, interpretable representations of player behavior from gameplay features across game modes.
The paper reports that advanced deep learning models may be helpful for boosting performance on the studied task (abs-level finding; the fulltext scrape carries only this conclusion).

A scoring rule f is incentive-compatible under a performativity model \phi iff for any reported \hat{p} != p, r_{\phi}(p) > r_{\phi}(\hat{p}); under two classes of performativity models, the paper shows strictly proper scoring rules FAIL to be incentive-compatible, and numerical results show the expert optimal forecast varies widely with the scoring rule, the performativity model, and the true probability.

A derived optimality condition for the performative binary-prediction scoring rule: [2p-1] f\u2032(p) (-4(p-0.5)^2/(2(1-p))) = 8(p-0.5)^2 (f(p)-f(1-p)), used to characterize when a scoring rule remains incentive-compatible under performativity.

When combining individuals judgments in forecasting contests, the median is superior to the mean, but both yield about 20% error on average; relative collective error shows essentially no correlation with judgment skewness (Pearson r = 0.03), with many contests showing high asymmetry yet low collective error.

The mean individual error \epsilon = (1/n)\sum|g_i - G| is interpreted as the expected error of a randomly selected expert; the ARIMA model is more accurate than a randomly selected expert in only 35% of the forecasting contests studied.

Two new Bayesian methods estimate in-game home-team win probability for Division-I FBS college football, extending the Maddox et al. basketball methods: (1) a "dynamic Bayesian estimator" using expected score differential and expected possessions remaining (modeled from the data) with a prior from 14 college football field experts; (2) an "adjusted dynamic Bayesian estimator" that adjusts the first by TeamRankings.com pregame win probabilities, with the adjustment optimized over time and score differential so the pregame prior fades as the game progresses. Applied to the 2021 Big XII Championship (Baylor vs Oklahoma State).

RASIPAM (RAcket-SPorts Interactive PAttern Mining) is a human-in-the-loop system for adjusting sports tactics: a constraint-based pattern mining algorithm plus an interactive visual interface with comparative visual design, introducing the metric L^*(S,T) (Eq. 2) to fit global constraints, and a new generator/optimizer for fine-tuning; two quantitative experiments demonstrate effectiveness, efficiency, and necessity.

Conformal risk control is tight up to a factor 2B/(n+1) that cannot be improved in general for monotone loss functions: for any epsilon>0 there exists a loss and alpha in (0,1) with E[L_{n+1}(\hat{\lambda})] <= alpha - 2B*epsilon/(n+1); conformal prediction reduces to risk control as the special case of controlling the expectation of an indicator loss, and the algorithms are shown equivalent.

The miscoverage-loss specialization: the condition on the distribution of discontinuities P(J(L_i^{Cvg},\lambda)>0)=0 is equivalent to continuity of the score function P(s(X_i,Y_i)=\lambda)=0; an appendix algorithm picks \lambda with an asymptotic risk-control guarantee for non-monotone loss functions.

NSVA is a new identity-aware NBA dataset for sports video analysis built on web data, filling the vacancy left by prior datasets that were neither identity-aware nor publicly available; a data-quality finding is that the NBA website reuses the same video clip for different play-by-play events occurring close together in time.

On NSVA, video captioning was benchmarked against MP-LSTM, TA, Transformer, and UniVL on CIDEr, BLEU, METEOR, and ROUGE-L; fusing S3D features with the proposed module features improved all metrics, suggesting TimeSformer features suit video captioning and the proposed features fuse well with other video-understanding features.

The paper analyzes whether the NFL franchise tag is fair to players using Spotrac contract data (tabulated contract extensions for free agents, one-year and multi-year franchise-tag players, 2020-2022 offseasons), box-and-whisker plots of guaranteed vs maximum money, and game-theoretic modeling of tag player vs team pre/post solution; it argues the tag is a one-sided tool rather than a synergistic nomination, noting NFL players prime is only ~25-29 years old, and proposes two reform suggestions.

NETS (Neural Embeddings for Team Sports) is a transformer architecture that creates context-aware embeddings for each player pooled through a team-wise pooling layer to classify basketball group activities (e.g., distinguishing pick-and-roll from handoff, whose setups are very similar); self-supervised pretraining on a trajectory-prediction task significantly improved downstream performance, and shallow models (logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting) had relatively low F1 scores on this difficult classification problem.

Manually labeled pick-and-roll datasets contain only roughly 1,000 play sequences because labeling requires focused multi-player watching with ambiguous edge cases; NBA SportVU tracking data (25 Hz player/ball positions, mandated league-wide) provides the raw material.

First study of target attacks on ranking aggregation from pairwise comparisons: the attack with a specified purpose is formulated as the fixed point of a continuous operator, with a game-theoretic adversary-vs-victim framework; the attack on HodgeRank is modeled as a least-squares problem with a constraint derived from HodgeRank optimality conditions (target ranking is a fixed point in the complete game), and attacks on the spectral RankCentrality are analyzed for reversible and irreversible stochastic transition matrices.
equation: \mathcal{T}:\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{X},\ L\in[0,1)\ \text{(Lipschitz operator whose fixed point is the target ranking)}

claim: Ranking aggregation differs from standard learning: there are no separate train/test phases (all comparisons are combined one-shot into a global ranking) and the data object is a binary pairwise partial order rather than features plus supervisory output; security is thus a new perspective since attackers have strong economic incentives to manipulate aggregated rankings.

The paper studies predicting Twenty20 cricket match outcomes (11 players per side, one innings each, max 20 overs) by determining player/team features that decide the outcome, using clustering approaches to derive player ratings compared against ICC ratings.

For Dream11 fantasy cricket score prediction, the paper concludes regressor models (not classification models) must be used to predict a player prospective-game performance; their regression approach matched the R2 score of the PyCaret library model on the unseen 50% of the dataset.

Grid WAR estimates a starting pitcher context-neutral win probability added above replacement game-by-game at the point he exits, rather than averaging season performance; it is convex in runs allowed, capturing that you can only lose a game once. Averaging lets one blow-up game dilute great ones, so standard WAR tends to undervalue mediocre and highly variable pitchers.

Measured: pitcher rankings built from past Grid WAR predict future pitcher rankings (by GWAR) better than rankings built from past FanGraphs WAR (2010-2019); the paper identifies the six most undervalued/overvalued pitchers by GWAR vs FWAR (RA/9) and uses a Poisson model as a powerful approximation yielding reasonable grids per league, season, and ballpark without overfitting.

A survey of data science and analytics applications in organized sports covers football, hockey, basketball, soccer, tennis, and cricket datasets and methods, including Bayesian posterior computation P(A|B) as a foundational technique.

The paper proposes a novel method to detect price-sensitive traders in prediction markets, motivated by experiments showing that better pricing depends on having more individual traders who are either better informed or better at analyzing homogeneous information (an edge over other traders).

The paper reports methods that detect multiple athletes in video and associate them across frames, with results indicating the method may transfer directly to basketball videos rather than soccer videos.

The paper modifies motion-based observation-centric SORT (OC-SORT) with an extra central-distance recovery stage, improving multi-object tracking under non-linear movement while staying online and cheap, plus a sport-specific ReID post-processing stage for basketball, football, and volleyball; final performance 73.968 HOTA, ranking 3rd in the 2022 ECCV DeeperAction Challenge SportsMOT multi-actor tracking track.

Appearance-based tracking cues often fail under occlusion, crowded scenes, or when targets share similar appearances (common in team sports), motivating the observation-centric motion approach with tracklet-association post-processing.

Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) are proposed as a plausible alternative to post-hoc calibration methods (Platt scaling, isotonic regression, beta calibration) for obtaining well-calibrated probabilities on tabular datasets, and the results show the proposed method works provably well for tabular datasets with small sample size.

For consistent pairwise comparison matrices (PCMs), where a_{ik}=a_{ij}a_{jk} for all i,j,k, the Logarithmic Least Squares Method (LLSM), the Eigenvector Method (EM), and the Bradley-Terry model all produce the same priority vector; the paper establishes a direct relation between these methods via consistency, with BT consistency expressed through a connected graph I.

Using English Premier League data (2020-2022) with two independent models (home goals, away goals) and six approaches (three naive heuristics, three ML feature combinations), Support Vector Regression outperformed other techniques for predicting final scores, and adding player-lineup statistics did NOT improve predictions; goalkeeper stats were found more important than attacker stats for predicting goals scored.

Lineup features were more impactful on home-prediction accuracy than away; for relegated teams, machine learning significantly improved predictions; the evaluation framework assessed model fitness, real-world scenarios, and simulated betting.

The paper proposes an AI-based, strategyproof chess tiebreak mechanism replacing rapid/blitz/Armageddon: the winner is decided by Total Pawn Loss Value (TPLV), the sum over positions of (engine evaluation of best move minus engine evaluation of the move played) using a ~3600-Elo engine; for small thresholds nearly every game yields a winner, essentially eliminating the tie problem and increasing viewership.

Empirical illustration: in the 1972 Fischer-Spassky "Match of the Century," Fischer had cumulative TPLV 28.96 in decisive games vs Spassky 84.56, demonstrating TPLV separates player quality where average centipawn loss does not.

flexBART re-implements Bayesian additive regression trees so decision nodes can assign multiple levels of a categorical variable to both left and right children, instead of one-hot encoding each level as a binary indicator; one-hot encoding places zero prior probability on most partitions of levels, limiting partial pooling, while the flexible trees borrow strength across categories and usually yield more accurate predictions.

Measured: flexBART partitioning is preferable to one-hot or target encoding except when one level has a substantially different outlying response surface; flexBART can substantially improve an already-good one-hot BART model but cannot rescue an extremely poorly performing one.

GOAL is a new dataset for grounded football commentaries enabling study of knowledge and visual grounding in sports; results show models trained on GOAL require both multimodal fusion and history (unlike VisDial or VQA), require grounding in both language and vision, and that generation can be supported by a knowledge base.

SportsTrack is a multi-object tracker for sports scenes using YOLOX for detection, introducing "crowded tracks" (when tracks get too close by IOU distance, one detection bbox may correspond to many crowded tracks) and "Sports Matching," a three-stage matching strategy; it reached 76.264 HOTA on SportMOT.

Two novel ROC-analysis approaches for paired-comparison data are proposed: WL-ROC/SW-ROC curves with convergence results via the ROC metric in (3.9) (Theorem 3.1), and WL-c/SW-c statistics summarizing discrimination ability of paired-comparison models; AUWLC is shown equivalent to the WL-c-statistic and the Mann-Whitney U-statistic between estimated win-probability vectors, demonstrated on professional sports regular-season game outcomes.

Comparing state-of-the-art neural-network ensemble methods for soccer predictions, the paper demonstrates the efficacy of the Kelly Index in reducing uncertainty in the predictive problem and thereby increasing overall predictive accuracy; the best-performing models efficacy dropped significantly for Type 3 matches but still marginally beat baselines.

CopulaCPTS is a copula-based conformal prediction algorithm for multi-step time-series forecasting; Bonferroni correction is shown to produce inefficient confidence regions for multidimensional data or long horizons, and per-step confidence regions are built as {y_j in R^d : nonconformity score < s_j^*}, with thresholds from inverse marginal CDFs \hat{F}_j^{-1}(u_j^*); its advantage grows with prediction horizon (validated with LaneGCN as the base trajectory model).

Methodological paper: a publicly documented method (with an online tool) converts college-football point-spread differentials plus the bettor projected spread into the probability of winning a specific bet, combining and modifying existing spread-to-probability techniques (Stern 1991; Huggins et al. 2020; adjusted Pythagorean) to determine whether a projected margin implies positive expected value at posted odds; calibrated on the 2021 season with caveats about COVID effects and sixth-year seniors.

A novel Bayesian Mixture Model for expected possession value (EPV) in rugby league places a set of centres across the pitch and aggregates data by proximity to centres, producing a smooth pitch surface of individual possession-outcome probabilities and improving on zonal Markov Reward Process approaches (whose smallest zone of 100 m^2 covered almost a quarter of a basketball court, too coarse for rugby league large pitch); used to compare teams attacking/defending and evaluate players.

Lasso and random-forest methodology for evaluating football (soccer) player quality achieves up to 60% explained variance, empirically shown to hold more value in player-quality evaluation than present market value, and can successfully rank young players by quality.

The paper derives analytical expressions characterizing the behavior/evolution of skill parameters \boldsymbol{\theta}_k throughout a tournament for paired-comparison rating systems, defining variables: M teams/players, K matches, scheduling vector x_k, skill difference z_k, outcome y_k, step-size \beta, home-field advantage \eta, logistic function \sigma, negative log-likelihood \ell_k(\boldsymbol{\theta}), mean-square skill deviation \bar{d}_k.

ECET is a holistic ensemble-classification methodology using evidence theory that quantifies uncertainty of individual classifiers after training AND of the ensemble during inference, selects the classifier pool by performance/diversity/expert-area criteria, provides binary and multiclass ensembles with a likeliness degree, and includes a novel anomaly-detection procedure via uncertainty tracking on out-of-distribution data.

The bivariate Poisson conditionals distribution of Arnold et al. (1999) / Obrechkoff (1963) always has negative correlation (except the independent case), filling the gap in negatively-correlated bivariate Poisson models; the paper gives classical (iterative MLE needing no optimizing/root-finding subroutines) and Bayesian estimation of its parameters with approximate asymptotic variance-covariance.

Hopaas (Hyperparameter OPtimization As A Service) coordinates hyperparameter-optimization campaigns across multiple compute providers (INFN, CERN, CINECA) via a thin client layer querying a central service over HTTPS with minimal REST APIs; hyperparameter tuning and Bayesian gradient-less optimization effectively exploit opportunistic compute despite environment variability and provider constraints.

The top-k list functional T_k is elicitable: a consistent scoring function yields a proper scoring rule when predictive distributions are first reduced by the functional (Gneiting 2011, Theorem 3); invalid top-k lists are ruled out a priori and all true top lists of a given length have the same expected score (comparability property).

The entropy function of any symmetric proper scoring rule is Schur-concave (via the Schur-Ostrowski condition for concave functions), and under a moderately predictable distribution the top-2 list prediction is much more informative than top-1, with a score not far from optimal.

A second-order scoring rule S_2 based on loss L_2: P_2(Y)xY -> R is (strictly) proper if and only if it is (strictly) order sensitive; the deep evidential regression loss L_2^DER fulfills the Theorem 5.2(ii) conditions, with one case incentivizing flatter predicted distributions and the other incentivizing peaked distributions.

Methods are presented for fusing multiple views (e.g., model-generated views) assuming zero or non-zero inter-view correlation, plus a conservative fusion for mutually inconsistent views; the Bayesian update is p(theta|q) proportional to p(q|theta)p(theta), and the predictive distribution integrates over parameters: p(r,f|q) = integral p(r,f|theta) p(theta|q) d theta; fusion-based methods statistically significantly beat the mean/median of the three view-generating models, and optimal portfolio allocation follows from p(r|q).

The Agent Imputer is a multi-agent time-series imputation model (LSTM + GNN components) that learns spatiotemporal inter-agent interactions to estimate player positions from sparse football event data (only the ball-carrier location and on-ball actions like passes/shots observed), beating naive baselines and XGBoost on mean Euclidean distance error and enabling heatmaps, physical metrics, and pitch-dominance analysis for lower-league clubs without tracking data.

The Transformer-based Neural Marked Spatio-Temporal Point Process (NMSTPP) models football event data interevent time, location, and action type simultaneously and dependently under the neural temporal point process framework, outperforming baselines; the derived HPUS (Holistic Possession Utilization Score) possession-effectiveness metric reflected a team final league ranking, average goals scored, and average xG over a Bundesliga season.

Each football player averages only about 3 minutes of ball possession per match, so on-ball action effectiveness and efficiency are critical to evaluate; the 2022 FIFA World Cup entertained over 5 billion viewers per FIFA estimates, underscoring the scale of football data analysis.

Wasserstein-Kelly portfolios apply Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization to the Kelly portfolio growth criterion; experiments on S&P500 data (out-of-sample 2020/01/01-2023/02/20) show Wasserstein-Kelly portfolios diversify Kelly portfolios and exhibit more stable portfolio-value evolution than the standard Kelly portfolio. The type-p Wasserstein metric is defined by d_p(F1,F2) = inf_Pi (E[||xi1-xi2||^p])^{1/p} over couplings Pi with the given marginals.
A trading algorithm significantly reduced the number of transactions to roughly one-third, and the classification score improved significantly under stricter classification conditions.

Six ML algorithms were evaluated on NFL Scouting Combine data: combine data predicts whether a prospect plays a single NFL snap (matriculation) with 83% accuracy, but cannot predict long-term success (best model RMSE = 1,210 snaps, R^2 = 0.17); the Scouting Combine may predict matriculation but is not a reliable predictor of long-term player success.

Methodology finding on model selection: for a moneyline-style probabilistic prediction task over an NBA season (2014/15-2018/19 training data, 2018/19 Westgate closing odds), the authors hypothesize and test that calibration is a more appropriate model-selection metric than accuracy; the calibration-selected system identified value wagers (predicted win probability > bookmaker implied probability) and in their simulation the best-performing system increased wealth by more than a third over the single season.

A common approach of averaging season-to-date box-score statistics for NBA game-outcome prediction was shown to be matched by averaging the differences in box-score statistics versus opponents; decimal odds display total return per unit stake, and the inverse of the odds gives the bookmaker implied probability.

The Leapfrog Diffusion model (LED) for stochastic trajectory prediction replaces the long denoising sequence with a leapfrog initializer that directly estimates the denoised distribution (with reparameterization), achieving SOTA on four real-world datasets and ~20x inference speedup over standard diffusion, satisfying real-time needs; on the NBA dataset standard diffusion needs ~100 denoising steps taking ~886 ms while the next frame arrives every 200 ms.

Range queries on the CMT search structure with Kendall-Tau distance retrieve objects within distance r of a query in practical time: it scales sublinearly with population size N, superlinearly with query distance r, but poorly with rank-list length (list length must be chosen carefully); controlled found-set size restores sublinear scaling in the number of objects found.

The Indeterminate Probability Neural Network (IPNN) theory is derived from three conditional mutual-independency assumptions the authors say can neither be proved nor falsified; IPNN converges to a global minimum only when P(y_l | a^1_{i1},...,a^N_{iN}) = 1 for all products of alpha weights > 0; the indeterminate probability theory extends classical probability as a special case.

An algorithm computes each football team optimal lineup against an opponent assumed to field its best players, maximizing win probability; reported effects include Tottenham increasing win probability and Stoke City decreasing loss probability with a better goalkeeper, and the Phil Jagielka-Sylvain Distin defensive combination significantly reducing Everton loss probability; team-wise individual analysis outperformed generic SOTA for some teams.

A generalized Glicko rating system represents each player strength as a discretized density rho_A over 1001 points (new players initialized as N(0, 0.7^2)), updating rho_A and rho_B after observed outcome A>B via a logistic win-probability kernel 0.1 + 0.8/(1+exp((x_k - x))); it generalizes Glicko by avoiding the known-chances approximation that overestimates strong players win chances and misbehaves in luck-heavy games, and it outperformed Glicko2 in the online card game Duelyst II.

Research finding: a recipe determines the number of TOTO 13er Wette lottery tips required to achieve a target number of strikes at a given safety level, based on home wins being the most frequent soccer result; the analysis derives a hypergeometric approximation for large numbers and argues the positive expected profits reveal a market-inefficiency anomaly in that lottery, partly eroded by transaction procedures and betting regulations.

GATv2-TCN predicts player performance from a dynamic player-interaction graph using a graph attention network (attention each player pays to others) plus a temporal convolution layer over multivariate player statistics, outperforming models that rely only on player historical performance; spectral GNNs (GCN, ChebyConv) are shown expressively limited on player-interaction graphs due to their high automorphism order. An open-sourced sports dataset with dynamic graph structure and temporal node attributes is released.

Table tennis match prediction (OSAI data, men and women professional singles) using sklearn classifiers with 5-fold CV and hyperparameter tuning achieves accuracy comparable to SOTA tennis models; ablation found the non-linear rank difference the most salient feature, and aggregating features with/without the target match performs comparably (no overfitting signal). Table tennis has no draws and pro singles are best-of-seven sets.

A Bayesian latent hidden Markov model (BLHMM) analysis of a Miami Heat season found cold streaks more frequent than hot streaks (more like a cold hand than a hot hand), with the two states clearly differentiated by the posterior distribution of transition probabilities; the BLHMM can compare teams/players and analyze opponent performance during a match, with a third intermediate state proposed for future work.

CUQR defines conformity scores over a sequence of bands rather than intervals to build adaptive predictive intervals retaining conformal marginal coverage, with PAC-style coverage holding per relevance subgroup g with slack lambda/sqrt(n_g) (n_g calibration points in subgroup S^g_hat), proved via the Dvoretzky-Kiefer-Wolfowitz inequality applied to the empirical CDF of conformity scores; weighting by localized density G_x gives a first-order approximation of the marginal quantile functional.

Survey conclusion: deep-learning approaches outperform traditional ML for wearable IMU-based human activity recognition via automatic feature extraction and knowledge transfer, but perform poorly under training/test distribution heterogeneity; domain adaptation (a transfer-learning technique) alleviates this, with adversarial and GAN-based approaches prominent in the literature; a domain is defined by (feature space, marginal distribution) and a task by (label space, predictor function).

RolFor is a graph-based encoder-decoder for robust NBA player-trajectory prediction that learns roles to model player interactions (using a TCN encoder); trained on 95,002 12-second NBA SportVU trajectory sequences from 1,247 games, it demonstrates that roles exist (via player-permutation tests) and that learning role interactions yields state-of-the-art forecasting.

For UEFA Champions League seeding, an Elo variant (Football Club Elo Rating, fixed at season start) provides higher accuracy/explanatory power than the official UEFA club coefficient in logistic-regression models, because the coefficient ignores national-league games; the authors urge UEFA to reform the coefficient calculation for the 2024/25 36-team league format (8 matches each) where balanced opponent strength is crucial.

A hybrid simulation model adds agent-based logic (four agent classes: team, player, etc.) to sports prediction, generalizing discrete-event logic: stochastic models (statistical distributions), play-by-play Markov-chain models, and ML models can each serve as subroutines whose parameters/strategies/data are modified by agent interactions; case study on NBA regular-season games compares a "basic" model without team rational thinking against an "extended" one, finding more data is not always better.
Including quantiles significantly improved the studied models by enabling prediction of quantiles for uncertainty quantification (comparing studies finding).

Probability predictions are assessed on calibration (events occur at forecasted rates), accuracy, and boldness (spread/std of predictions); a forecaster predicting the 0.53 base rate for every NHL game is calibrated but not bold/actionable, while bold-but-uncalibrated predictions show misplaced confidence. Boldness-recalibration maximizes boldness while maintaining a high posterior probability of calibration, subject to classification accuracy.
equation: P(M_c|\mathbf{y})\ \text{= posterior model probability as the measure of calibration}

claim: Simulation evidence: the Bayesian calibration assessment P(M_c|y) correctly identifies miscalibration and appropriately emboldens nearly all forecaster types at reasonable sample sizes, even under calibration misspecification; the method suits anyone willing to sacrifice a little posterior probability of calibration to gain boldness for riskier decision-making predictions.

STST (Spatiotemporal Transformer for Stocks) is a transformer-LSTM model correlating spatiotemporal patterns for stock movement prediction, evaluated on the ACL18 and KDD17 datasets against StockNet and other baselines with higher accuracy/MCC reported.

An Azure Lambda-architecture big-data pipeline (batch + speed layers via Azure Data Factory) was built for high-throughput cotton phenotyping: image compression for data reduction, a separately trained YOLOv5 object-detection model for cotton bloom detection/counting/visualization, validated on 9,000 images.

For transfer-learning-based CATE estimation, the paper proposes ell_1-TCL and a Partition-then-Transfer approach (ParT); the source-sample-size condition for consistency relaxes to n_s >> s^2 d^2 log d (s-sparse transfer vector, d dimensions), improving on the rough n_s >> n d^2 bound, under unconfoundedness (Y0,Y1) indep Z | X.

The win-martingale closest to Brownian motion (natural model for prediction markets) is unique and given by the SDE dM_t = sin(pi M_t)/(pi sqrt(1-t)) dB_t with M_0 = x_0, minimizing relative entropy h(Q|W^{x_0}) over continuous win-martingales; the paper also derives a new first-order condition for continuous-time martingale transport.

For any strictly proper scoring rule S(q,q) >= S(p,q), there exist prediction-to-belief functions f such that performatively optimal reports are NOT fixed points, even when a fixed point exists and is unique; under reasonable distributions over such functions, optimal reports are almost never fixed points. However, performatively stable (Perdomo et al. 2020) predictions ARE fixed points, with tight bounds in some cases.

For any strictly proper scoring rule S(q,q) >= S(p,q), there exist prediction-to-belief functions f such that performatively optimal reports are NOT fixed points, even when a fixed point exists and is unique; under reasonable distributions over such functions, optimal reports are almost never fixed points. However, performatively stable (Perdomo et al. 2020) predictions ARE fixed points, with tight bounds in some cases.

An exact replication (new Python code vs original Stata) of Ramirez, Reade and Singleton "Wikipedia Relative Buzz Factor" tennis study confirmed their backtested results and that WikiBuzz/RankDist coefficients are significantly non-zero; BUT a large share of the best models profits came from a single erroneous "Hercog" entry caused by an odds-data inconsistency in tennis-data.co.uk, and after cleaning, only one Bet365-based strategy remained significantly profitable (p_bs = 0.002 via 100,000 simulation trials). All code and cleaned datasets released open source.

ShuttleSet is presented as the largest public stroke-level badminton dataset for turn-based sports analytics, annotated by domain experts with the S2-labeling tool in BLSR format; the ShuttleScorer model (shot encoder + pattern extractor + Transformer rally encoder) outperforms Bi-GRU by 26.8% in AUC, 11.6% in accuracy, and 27.1% in Brier score, reaching AUC 0.8371 with remaining headroom.

The first unsupervised statistical feature-guided diffusion model generates wearable sensor data for human activity recognition without labels, directly on raw sensor data; it improves HAR performance over conventional oversampling and GAN-based methods and produces more diverse synthetic data, addressing the costly annotation bottleneck (sensor annotation is far more expensive than image/video annotation and sensor data lacks rich semantics).

A video modernization pipeline combines Stable Diffusion with ML-extracted static background regions for temporally coherent outpainting; Stable Diffusion dominates compute at up to 40 seconds per frame (far slower than all other stages, including Mask-RCNN), and the modular pipeline could swap it for a faster algorithm or use foreground detection instead of object detection.

A framework infers ball trajectories from player trajectories (instead of tracking the ball directly) with a reality-loss term and postprocessing ensuring trajectories only change direction when carried/kicked by a player; it achieves mean ball position error below 3.7 m and 64.7% player-possession accuracy, and a hierarchical Bi-LSTM architecture outperforms Transformers on this task (with reasons analyzed).
equation: s_{t}^{p}=\hat{g}_{t}^{p}/\|\hat{\mathbf{y}}_{t}-\mathbf{x}_{t}^{p}\|\ \text{(possession score: probability over distance to predicted ball)}

claim: UACQR (Uncertainty-Aware Conformalized Quantile Regression) separates aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty to adjust quantile regressors differentially across feature space; experiments over 150 trials show good conditional coverage P(Y_{n+1} in C_hat_n(X_{n+1}) | X_{n+1}=x) and competitive interval widths, UACQR-P is preferred over UACQR-S with the epoch heuristic, and adding a squared-error-loss output dimension improves finite-sample quantile-regression performance.

Bagged-PCMCI+ combines bootstrap aggregation and link-confidence measures with the PCMCI+ constraint-based time-series causal discovery method (Runge 2020); numerical experiments show it outperforms standard PCMCI+, and the confidence measure for links is effective (also tested with the adapted PC algorithm and LPCMCI for contemporaneous edges and hidden confounders, B=1000).

GrAMMI (Graph-based Adversarial Modeling with Mutual Information) predicts current and future states of an adversarial agent under partial observability via multi-agent graph communication and a mutual-information maximization objective that disentangles latent embeddings across multimodal hypotheses; it achieves 40.54% and 18.39% higher average log-likelihood than all baselines on the new Prison Escape and Narco Traffic Interdiction domains (two contributed open-source continuous-action adversarial domains).

A scalable approach estimates multi-dimensional conditional quantile functions on manifolds (sphere, torus) via a relaxed dual optimal-transport problem, adding a penalty to the VQR loss for deviations of learned c-concave potentials from the involution property; it is substantially more scalable than Hallin et al. 2022 discrete-OT linear programming, achieving 93.72% ESS and mean KDE-L1 (14.38 +/- 5.03)x10^-4.
