A novel framework of ranking with abstention lets the learner abstain from a prediction at a limited cost c in both general pairwise and bipartite ranking; the paper derives H-consistency bounds for pairwise and bipartite abstention losses (hinge, exponential, sigmoid surrogates) for linear hypothesis sets and one-hidden-layer networks, and proves a negative result: for equicontinuous hypothesis sets any H-consistency bound is vacuous (with f non-decreasing continuous at zero).

The Dixon and Coles (1997) football score model is a special case of the Sarmanov family of bivariate distributions; exploiting this connection lets probabilities be shifted between scores beyond 0-0/1-0/0-1/1-1, accommodates non-Poisson discrete marginals (negative binomial), and handles wider correlation ranges. In women football leagues (four leagues tested) fewer 0-0s occur than under independence (opposite of men), and the ANS model variant performed most promisingly.
The paper analyzes a G-score metric broken down per category (abs-level finding; the fulltext scrape carries only this fragment).

Three reject-option models are proposed for out-of-distribution (OOD) selective classification: cost-based, bounded TPR-FPR, and bounded precision-recall models; despite different formulations they share a common class of optimal strategies (the Bayes ID classifier h_B is optimal for the bounded TPR-FPR model). Motivated by this, double-score OOD methods combining two OOD detectors (one for OOD/ID discrimination, one for misclassification detection) consistently outperform SOTA experimentally.
equation: \min_{h,c}R(h,c)\ \text{(cost-based optimal OOD selective classifier)};\quad r(x)=\sum_{y\in\mathcal{Y}}p_I(y\mid x)\ell(y,h(x))

claim: Bayesian Taut Splines (BTS) estimate the number of modes in a univariate density (modes = subpopulations/model complexity) by combining KDEs with compositional splines in a divide-and-conquer Bayesian framework: an MCMC exploration phase enforces regularity (penalizing curvature and multimodality), SFPCA summarizes candidate splines, and global model selection plus local testing give a holistic view of modality; applied to the Hidalgo test-bed with per-mode probabilities (0.63, 0.99, 0.83, 0.96, 0.91, 0.51, 0.75).

Tournament winning probabilities can be computed EXACTLY (not simulated) by exploiting limited mixing of team trajectories in sports brackets: the computation is independent of the single-match model, two orders of magnitude faster than any reasonably accurate tournament simulation for FIFA World Cup schedules, supports live updates on partial tournaments (known outcomes set to probability 1), and yields 1 - sum_j(G_ij + G_ji) as the probability team i exits after the group stage.
equation: 1-\sum_{j}G_{ij}+G_{ji}\ \text{= probability team } i \text{ exits after group stage}

claim: CAMP (Context-Aware Metric of player Performance) rates all 22 players in a cricket match by measuring contributions conditional on game context and opposition strength, tracking the evolving match situation with context-aware ratings; its top-rated players substantially agree with expert Man-of-the-Match awards, and the framework extends to any cricket format (future extensions: fielding, extras, power plays, captaincy, wicket-keeping).

Methodology study: Von Neumann-Morgenstern expected-utility framework with deep-learning outcome forecasts, comparing Sharpe Ratio vs Kelly criterion portfolio construction on the second half of the 2020-21 English Premier League season; contributions include a matrix-based formulation of the multivariate Kelly criterion and the optimization problem for multiple simultaneous Kelly stakes; the utility functional is U(F) = integral u dF = E_F[u(X)], with log or quadratic utilities, and multinomial-regression odds models lost 19.3% accuracy vs the deep model.

Kernel Rank Centrality (KRC) is a spectral dynamic ranker for the time-varying Bradley-Terry model, integrating Rank Centrality with kernel smoothing over time; its estimates converge to the dynamic BT score with ell_2 error bound O_p(sqrt(1/(nMh)) + h^2), and it is the first spectral method with an established asymptotic normal distribution, validated on NBA statistics with computational efficiency over Bayesian/MCMC and time-weighted MLE alternatives.

A hierarchical generative model for soccer shot coordinates (mixture of truncated bivariate Gaussians, fit by variational inference in RStan) yields player shooting-habit parameters plus two novel shooting metrics that extract signal from OFF-TARGET shot trajectories; the new metrics are significantly more stable than GAX (goals above expected, which is poorly predictive year-to-year) and better predict second-half performance from first-half shots, valuable for recruitment and player valuation.

The abile package formalizes skill rating as state-space models separating model definition from inference, with novel SMC and finite-space inference schemes suffering fewer bias sources than previous model-based approaches; principled Bayesian model-based skill ratings offer interpretable and predictive advantages over Elo and Glicko, significantly outperforming them on football and chess (sports with draws), and model-based methods with uncertainty quantification are preferable.

A modified three-team group tournament format where the match order is NOT predefined in advance (dynamic match order) reduces collusion risk; Monte Carlo simulations show the dynamic-order three-team format is comparable in collusion risk to the four-team group system of past World Cups, making a 16x3-team 48-team World Cup feasible (vs FIFA adopted 12x4 with 104 matches over 39 days).

The forecast combination puzzle: the standard two-step approach to forecast combinations yields accuracy tests with no power against a large class of alternatives (fixed, random, drifting weights), because the scaled test statistic converges to a generalized chi-squared distribution rather than the standard normal; for two forecast combinations to differ meaningfully the weights must be surprisingly disparate. The puzzle is entirely resolved by building forecast combinations in a single step (shown on the Geweke-Amisano S&P500 density-prediction example).

The player count in a football team possession is effectively approximated by a mixture of two geometric distributions (composed of location-dependent geometric distributions), with MLE estimates beta = 2.29 and tau = 1.09 s; team possession-time density relates to player possession-time density via f_team(t) = sum_{n=1}^inf P(n) f_player^{*n}(t), for which a closed form is derived under approximations.

The f-GBT family generalizes the Bradley-Terry model (binary comparisons) to a natural family of probabilistic comparison-to-score models; with a Gaussian Bayesian prior on alternatives scores, all GBT models guarantee: MAP scores vary monotonically with comparisons and are Lipschitz-resilient to each new comparison (outliers have limited impact), and the negative log-posterior L(.|R) is (1/sigma^2)-strongly convex with a unique minimizer, making the MAP well-defined and fast to compute.

ROBART/ARROBART are nonparametric Thurstone models for rank-order data using a BART specification for the regression of latent evaluation scores (allowing nonlinear dependence on lagged scores and covariates); the dynamic ARROBART outperformed linear and static competitors in forecasting simulations and on out-of-sample 2022 NCAA weekly American-football team rankings, supporting temporal persistence and nonlinearity. The consistency set is A_t = {z in R^N : z_{j,t} < z_{i,t} iff tau_{j,t} < tau_{i,t}}.

Encoding volleyball round data as a graph (contact-by-contact context) for GNNs yields large improvements on prediction tasks that depend on that context, without extra data collection; but graph encodings are specialized tools that may not help tasks that do not need the context, and simpler architectures can noticeably outperform complex ones on some sports-analysis tasks.

A real-time end-to-end pipeline analyzes badminton broadcast videos (singles and doubles): player-movement heatmaps, distance covered, and average speed; processing every third frame is empirically sufficient, with each component optimized for accuracy vs latency. Two new datasets (singles, doubles) cover diverse tournaments, camera angles, lighting, and players, more diverse than prior recorded-only datasets.

Increasing the diversity of a forecast ensemble positively impacts accuracy: on six years of hourly German EPEX day-ahead electricity prices, introducing diversity to the pool of probabilistic forecasts was highly beneficial for CRPS accuracy and for profits of a trading strategy in the day-ahead power market; the DDNN_JSU_CRPS_LEAR ensemble was significantly better than all competitors, though naive weighting beat CRPS weighting on the lowest percentiles (advantage during the early COVID-19 period).

Glocal XAI explanations of xG models (aggregated SHAP values + aggregated profiles) bridge local (per-shot) and global (model-level) explanation: decomposing xG predictions into variable contributions lets analysts assess player/team scoring potential over a period and compare players strengths/weaknesses (demonstrated on Lille OSC 2020/21 vs 2021/22), because end-of-match statistics like possession percentage and penalty-area shots often do not reflect match outcomes.

A neural network estimates a basketball's 3D location by predicting the pixel distance between the ball and its ground projection in image space; the 3D ball coordinates are then recovered geometrically using the camera calibration projection matrix, with player gaze and context cues informing the height guess.

For context-aware 3D ball localization, MAPE decreases as the input image crop size increases but plateaus beyond a certain crop size; the method reaches MAPE as low as 1.1 meters and is robust to image resolution, so low-resolution images can be used with the same crop size while preserving context and inference speed.

Rank aggregation via the spectral method models pairwise observations as latent score differences plus noise, H_ij = r_i - r_j + noise for observed pairs (i,j) in E; the paper proves improved sample-complexity guarantees over the prior state of the art, with numerical experiments confirming the theory.

Under a corruption model where each observation equals the true score difference r_i - r_j with probability eta*p and is i.i.d. uniform noise on [-M,M] with probability (1-eta)*p, the normalized spectral ranking estimate theta-hat is computed from the leading eigenvector phi_1 via the arctangent of the ratio of its real and imaginary inner products with the all-ones vector.
equation: H_{ij}=\begin{cases}r_{i}-r_{j},&\text{with probability }\eta p,\\ Z_{ij}\overset{\text{i.i.d.}}{\sim}{\cal U}[-M,M],&\text{with probability }(1-\eta)p,\end{cases}\qquad \widehat{\theta}=\arctan\left(\frac{\langle\Re\bm{\phi}_1,\bm{1}_n\rangle}{\langle\Im\bm{\phi}_1,\bm{1}_n\rangle}\right)\ \text{(piecewise on the sign of }\langle\Im\bm{\phi}_1,\bm{1}_n\rangle\text{)}

claim: The approximation error in the spectral ranking analysis is controlled with the leave-one-out technique: auxiliary matrices H^(k) = H + Delta^(k) are formed so that the perturbation Delta^(k) is zeroed out on the k-th row and column, decoupling the dependence between the eigenvector and the k-th observation.

The paper proposes the Balance score, a scoring-function-based evaluation metric for probability estimation models (motivated by esports win-probability data) that satisfies six desirable properties of probability metrics and remedies shortcomings of accuracy, Brier score, and bin-based calibration metrics; it is the average of a per-sample scoring function over the n samples.

The Balance score's per-sample scoring function f_ba gives +1-p_hat for a correct confident prediction (p_hat>=0.5, y=1), +p_hat for a correct unconfident prediction (p_hat<0.5, y=0), -p_hat for an incorrect confident prediction (p_hat>=0.5, y=0), and -1+p_hat for an incorrect unconfident prediction (p_hat<0.5, y=1): gains are large when uncertain-but-correct and losses are large when confident-but-wrong.

The expected score of a probability-estimation model decomposes as the double integral over true probability p and predicted probability p-hat of the expected scoring function, with the optimal-score function G(p) = p*f_ba(p,1) + (1-p)*f_ba(p,0) giving the expected score of a perfectly calibrated predictor.

On esports game-snapshot data the optimal achievable accuracy ranges from 68.92% to 81.88% and the optimal Brier score from 0.1995 to 0.1241 depending on the true-probability distribution (0.75 accuracy / 0.166 Brier in the baseline analysis), so a trained logistic regression at 65.56% accuracy and 0.2159 Brier is limited by irreducible data uncertainty rather than by model capacity or a learning problem.

Table-tennis motor-skill recognition from wearable signals uses time-domain statistics as features, including the signal mean x-bar = (1/n)*sum x_i (eq. 14) and the variance sigma_x^2 = (1/n)*sum (x_i - x-bar)^2 (eq. 15), alongside mean-square and RMS statistics, with PCA for dimensionality reduction before classification.

For the six table-tennis action-skill states the paper uses a directed-acyclic-graph support vector machine to classify the PCA-reduced features, and maps acceleration/velocity information through a logistic function into the [0,1] interval as normalized evaluation scores.

Market-GAN targets financial market data generation controllable by semantic context; the paper pinpoints two blockers: (i) current financial datasets do not contain context labels, and (ii) current generative techniques are not designed for generation with context as control, which demands greater precision than other modalities.

For constant-product automated market makers with concentrated liquidity, the paper characterizes the continuous-time wealth dynamics of strategic liquidity providers, deriving predictable loss and optimal liquidity provision (forthcoming in the SIAM Journal on Financial Mathematics).

UBET AMM (UAMM) prices sports-betting conditional tokens with a swap-rate function using a base rate alpha and a target rate rho: it applies the target-balance-adjusted rate alpha*Delta_tau_Out + (rho-alpha)*(R_tau_Out - TB) when the post-trade target balance TB lies within [R_tau_Out - Delta_tau_Out, R_tau_Out], and the flat rate Delta_tau_Out when TB <= R_tau_Out.

Controlled and uncontrolled experiments with repeated trials and sensitivity analysis show UAMM maintains the total investment balance of LP funds and incurs permanent gain on average while Uniswap incurs permanent loss on average, with relatively low vigorish; the paper also gives a formal on-chain methodology for defining, minting, merging, and redeeming conditional tokens (payouts, reporting, redemption) plus a collateral liquidity pool so bettors can wager base currency like USDC.

Early churn prediction trains a model y = g(theta; x) on user activity sequences with churn labels, and builds per-user statistical feature sets G_i = {mu_i,1, sigma_i,1, ..., mu_i,N, sigma_i,N} from the per-feature means mu and variances sigma across each user's sequence.

Transformer-based churn models using limited features outperform traditional churn prediction and reduce the need for extensive feature engineering; reported results include F1 of 81.16%, DL1/DL2 holdout AUC of 0.706 and 0.743, 10-fold cross-validation AUC of 86.57% with holdout AUC 88.11% on one dataset, and 73.90%/79.38% on the Cell2Cell dataset.

The latent shrinkage position cluster model (LSPCM) embeds network nodes as z_i drawn from a multivariate normal with zero mean and diagonal precision Omega = diag(omega_1^{-1}, ..., omega_p^{-1}), jointly inferring the node clustering structure and automatically selecting the latent space dimension through shrinkage of the precision parameters.

For clustering, node latent positions follow a sparse finite mixture z_i ~ sum_g tau_g * MVN(mu_g, Omega^{-1}) with cluster weights tau_g and cluster means mu_g, and edge probabilities are logistic in the latent positions: q_ij = exp(eta_ij)/(1+exp(eta_ij)).

The LSPCM reduces the latent dimension by 1 whenever the cumulative proportion of latent-position variance explained by the dimensions falls below the threshold, and clustering decisions use posterior similarity criteria.

FENCE detects multiple accounts on the Dream11 fantasy sports platform (over 190 million users) with a two-step formulation: first build a graph whose edges e = {x, y} connect users x, y in V, then run multiple-ID account detection assigning each node a score in [0,1], where scores above 0.95 count as high-confidence matches.

FENCE's detection algorithm is reported to achieve convergence; the system trades recall against precision as it scales, and batch-processed labels act as ground truth for updating and improving the existing detection models.

Elo player-skill variances are updated via the Laplace approximation of the posterior, combined with a random-walk model for strength dynamics and a lower bound B on each player's standard deviation: the updated variance (sigma_i')^2 = max(B^2, sigma_i^2*(1-L_i) + eta^2), where L_i is the information-gain factor from the match and eta^2 the random-walk noise variance.

The random-walk noise variance can be parameterized as eta_i^2 = alpha*sigma_i^2; new-player prediction experiments with lower bound B=75, initial sigma=130 and alpha^(2)=0.03 achieved the smallest negative log-likelihood with an accuracy of 0.6369.

TacticAI, built by Google DeepMind with Liverpool FC, is an AI assistant for football tactics that algorithmically identifies key patterns in rival teams' tactics and develops effective responses, addressing an open research challenge at the heart of modern football.

European and South American football league ratings use the Glicko-2 algorithm tailored for football: promoted teams are re-anchored toward an initial rating r(mu_init+mu_new, phi, sigma), and teams changing leagues receive shifted ratings r(mu+mu_l, phi+phi_s, sigma), with the initial league rating penalized for teams arriving from lower-ranked leagues so they start below the average league rating.
equation: r(\mu,\phi,\sigma)=\begin{cases}r(\mu_{init}+\mu_{new},\phi,\sigma)&\text{if team was promoted}\\ r(\mu+\mu_{l},\phi+\phi_{s},\sigma)&\text{if team changed league}\end{cases}

claim: A transition parameter captures each league's propensity to strengthen or weaken after league changes: for example, promotion to the Premier League (or relegation to a second league) triggers slight rating adjustments reflecting active transfer campaigns that follow league transitions.

The MOBA ELO variant weights rating updates by performance share: on a win, ELO_new = ELO_old + (PS/PS_T)*K*(S_A - E_A) where PS/PS_T is the player's score share of the team total, K the K-factor, S_A the actual and E_A the expected score; ladder points update as Ladder_new = Ladder_old + (PS/PS_T)*20 on wins.

The paper argues MOBA ELO systems are tuned so every player's win rate stays only slightly above or below 50% regardless of true skill (strong players are matched with weaker teammates or stronger opponents and vice versa), creating the paradox that the better you play, the harder it becomes to win.

For score-based multi-class learning with abstention (Mao, Mohri, Zhong), H-consistency bounds for surrogate losses can be strictly stronger than excess-error bounds because the minimizability gap M_L(H) can be strictly smaller than the approximation error A_L(H); in the deterministic scenario the discrepancy equals e^{-Lambda} exactly.

The H-consistency bounds yield finite-sample estimation guarantees for surrogate-loss minimizers that are more favorable than those derivable from excess-error bounds; for zero-one and deferral losses the minimizability gap equals the approximation error, while for general surrogate losses it is less than or equal to it.

The predictor-rejector framework for multi-class learning with abstention lets the learner abstain from predicting at a pre-defined cost; the paper presents new theoretical and algorithmic results for this setting (companion to the score-based abstention analysis).

The hybrid graph network for complex activity detection in video achieves the highest average mAP of 69.3 on the activity-detection benchmarks using both optical-flow and RGB modalities, outperforming all RGB-only models and attaining the best mAP at every IoU threshold; state of the art on Thumos-14 improved by about 19% over four years.

Video frame interpolation is disambiguated by replacing time indexing with distance indexing: an iterative reference-based estimation strategy breaks long-range interpolation into short-range steps so per-step uncertainty is minimized, yielding sharper frames and enabling independent per-object temporal manipulation for video re-timing.

A continuous indexing-map estimator computes pixel-wise dense distance maps from four input frames using cubic B-splines and neural ordinary differential equations, and multi-frame refinement fuses nearby frames; both are plug-and-play with existing VFI models without architectural changes, and uniform distance maps add no extra computation.

Infinite forecast combination uses a Dirichlet-process deep-learning ensemble: the learning rate is sampled with three basis distributions as hyperparameters to convert the infinite mixture into a finite one, all training checkpoints are collected into a sub-model pool, and weight-adjustment plus diversity strategies drive the combination; on the M4 weekly dataset the ensemble substantially improves prediction accuracy and stability over a single benchmark model.

Classifier calibration via ROC-regularized isotonic regression: isotonic regression calibrates binary classifiers by minimizing cross-entropy on a calibration set through monotone transformations, acting as an adaptive binning procedure that can achieve zero calibration error, with ROC-based regularization added to control the ranking behavior.

Bayes-xG builds Bayesian hierarchical logistic regressions on roughly 10,000 English Premier League shots from StatsBomb data to quantify how player- and position-level factors shift the probability of a shot becoming a goal beyond the baseline expected-goals metric.

Continuous football player tracking can be reconstructed from discrete broadcast data, bridging the gap for professional teams whose video feeds are not high enough quality for computer-vision tracking technologies.

Football match events (goals and other events) are modeled as Cox processes, i.e. doubly stochastic Poisson processes whose intensities may depend on all modeled events plus external factors; the parameterization yields a strictly concave log-likelihood, so fitting is a convex optimization with globally optimal and (under linearly independent regressors) unique maximum-likelihood estimates.

Fitted on eight seasons of Campeonato Brasileiro Serie A, the Cox model finds the home team has 51.40% higher goal intensity than the away team all else equal, and the goal rate rises 20.62% in the second half for both teams; the home/away indicator psi^j_{k,h} equals 1 when k is the home team and 0 otherwise, with a home-advantage parameter set to zero for the away process.

Dynamic in-game regressors significantly improve predictive power: a red card cuts the team's goal intensity by more than 30%, a team losing by one goal raises its rate by 10% (20% when losing by two), a team leading by one goal has its rate multiplied by 0.9082 (leading teams' intensity falls while trailing teams' rises), and stoppage time averages more than one minute longer when the second-half goal difference is one or less.

The 1-0 home win is the most common football scoreline at 14.9% of matches in the Brazilian Serie A sample, with the 'Other' scoreline category at 17.0%; models with more covariates better estimate the number of draws.

Estimated Performance Rating (PR_e) for chess, tennis and other games is defined as the rating that solves an optimization problem related to scoring probability and applies at any performance level; unlike the Tournament Performance Rating (TPR), which is undefined for zero or perfect scores, PR_e remains well-defined, and the paper shows TPR's predictive value can vary and drop as low as 0.25.

Rink-agnostic hockey rink registration generalizes to unseen rink types using only an overhead rink template plus the video frame: a three-module pipeline (semantic segmentation, homography estimation, iterative refinement) warps broadcast frames onto the overhead template, trained with unsupervised domain adaptation on labeled NHL and unlabeled non-NHL data, semi-supervised synthetic data, and logo/copy-paste augmentations.

Sports-QA is introduced as the first large-scale video question-answering benchmark designed for complex, professional sports reasoning, covering fine-grained motion and professional action understanding that general daily-life VideoQA datasets do not address.

Constrained Max Drawdown is an alternative linearization of the classical Markowitz quadratic portfolio optimization that minimizes maximum portfolio drawdown instead of variance, appealing in financial distress such as the COVID-19 pandemic; its mixed-integer linear programming variation delivered more profitable and robust out-of-sample results with sensitivity analysis.

OpenSkill is a concrete implementation of a faster asymmetric multi-team, multiplayer rating system: it improves rating-update accuracy by accounting for players affecting each other during updates and weighting by individual contributions, with speedups from dropping into SciPy's faster C code.

In the Bristol Betting Exchange agent-based model, an XGBoost bettor agent trained only on the profitable activity of minimally simple betting strategies learns a wagering policy that outperforms even the best of those simple strategies, showing XGBoost generalizes beyond its training behaviors; the work is a proof-of-concept that in-play horse-race market time series can in principle feed an ML system to learn an automated wagering system.

A classification component in the XGBoost in-play study reports F1 of 0.93 for class 0 and 0.56 for class 1, with 88% overall prediction accuracy, and the authors note parameter tuning further improves XGBoost performance.

Whole-body inter-personal dynamics between two players (pitcher-batter) are analyzed with neural Granger causality (NGC), which identifies nonlinear Granger-causal relations among multiple time series from the weights of a neural network trained to predict them; NGC values are non-negative (ngc >= 0 for all i,j) with the significance threshold set at the mean NGC value, achieving prediction R above 0.9 with under 2 minutes training per pair.

In the pitcher-batter study, a movement feature is significantly correlated with batter performance outcomes at R^2 = 0.69, joints show a large effect on performance (eta^2 = 0.69) despite accounting for only a small share of variance, and hitting performance improves when the batter shows the opposite pattern to the pitcher's motion.

Tennis players' career trajectories are characterized by early-career wins and tournament prestige: success in tennis is modeled as a complex phenomenon where the timing of early wins and the prestige of tournaments won shape long-run trajectory patterns.

Least-squares estimators for graphical models of cardinal paired-comparison data (with and without covariates) are rigorously analyzed, yielding novel graph-based necessary and sufficient conditions guaranteeing their existence.

The Expected Booking (xB) model estimates the likelihood that a foul in football results in a yellow card; it was developed through three iterative experiments and is proposed as a metric for fouling efficiency.

Goals above expected is defined as GAX = sum_i (G_i - xG_i), the cumulative gap between actual goals and expected goals; the paper shows the standard xG model is biased in estimating finishing skill because 'average player' is ill-defined, e.g. Pogba accumulated 20.85 xG but scored only 17 goals.

To mitigate xG bias, the paper proposes learning the xG model with multi-calibration from the AI-fairness literature: calibrate predictions for subpopulations defined by complex intersections of player attributes, which explicitly represents multiple alternative 'average players' and lets the GAX metric state the group characteristics it was derived from; training reached AUROC 0.7990 and Brier score 0.0793 with calibration-error tolerance 0.01 per group using 10 log-spaced bins.

Individual and team performance in cricket is studied with newly available large-scale fine-grained data, providing a first data-driven characterization of how individual performance aggregates into team outcomes in the sport.

A comprehensive survey of the home advantage in American football (co-authored with NFL researchers) consolidates the cross-league, long-horizon evidence on the existence and magnitude of the benefit teams receive when playing at home, beyond the short-window single-league studies that dominate the literature.

Algorithmic robust forecast aggregation addresses combining multiple forecasters' predictions when their information structure is unknown; the paper develops aggregation algorithms with robustness guarantees for this setting.

Applying RLFN super-resolution as preprocessing markedly improves football object detection on low-resolution video: 4x upscaling of 320x240 images raises Faster R-CNN mAP@IoU=0.50:0.95 by about 12% (12.3% in the size sweep), while mAP@IoU=0.50 slightly declines; gains shrink with input size (3.3% at 640x480, 3.7% at 1280x720).

Detection quality scales strongly with input resolution: enlarging inputs sixfold from 320x240 to 1920x1080 improves mAP@IoU=0.50:0.95 by over 21% and mAP@IoU=0.50 by about 20%; 640x480 super-resolved images move mAP@IoU=0.50:0.95 from 27.6 to 28.5 and 1280x720 from 29.5 to 30.6.

Training the RLFN super-resolution network on football-specific SoccerNet data yields higher PSNR on the SoccerNet test set than training on disparate datasets; PSNR above 30 is considered good and above 35 high quality, while a sixfold downscale drops reconstruction PSNR to 25.58.

Predicting batter-vs-pitcher specific batting averages uses generalized linked matrix factorization: regression approaches that add pitcher/batter averages are too inflexible for high-dimensional predictors, so dimension-reduction finds a lower-dimensional representation that can absorb many additional parameters.

UK horse-racing markets on Betfair show a paradox of high informational efficiency: short-tailed return distributions, rapidly decaying autocorrelations, no long-term memory, no gain-loss asymmetry, and a Hurst exponent indicating mean reversion, in sharp contrast to financial assets with heavy tails and volatility clustering; the generalized Gaussian unconditional distribution has a light tail, pointing to knowledge being quickly assimilated into prices.

The Strain of Success model is a sequential team-selection framework that uses Monte Carlo Tree Search over states S and actions A with transition function P = Pr(s'|s,a) to optimize lineups while minimizing injury risk; unavailability length L = {l_1,...,l_n} is defined per game and decrements by one each game for injured players, and squad-selection constraints are 3-5 defenders, 3-5 midfielders, and 1-3 attackers.

The player-level injury-risk model achieves log-loss 0.1676 +/- 0.0005, outperforming logistic regression and random-forest baselines, while the team-level model scores 0.910 +/- 0.018, similar within error bounds to an established benchmark; acute workload is the most contributory feature with mean SHAP value 0.0033.

Optimized team selection under the injury-risk model consistently beats the greedy strategy across all risk multipliers and cuts money inefficiently spent on injured players by 11% on average across clubs, improving long-term wage efficiency and player welfare.

In robust forecast aggregation with peer expectations (each forecaster is also asked for their expectation of the average of others' forecasts), the paper takes an adversarial approach in the Arieli-Babichenko-Smorodinsky robust framework and characterizes when the extra second-order information makes aggregation possible versus impossible.

Self-calibrating conformal prediction combines Venn-Abers calibration with conformal prediction to deliver calibrated point predictions together with prediction intervals that have finite-sample validity conditional on those predictions, extending the original Venn-Abers procedure.

Regression trees are used to build fast, adaptive prediction intervals under conformal inference, providing a tree-based method for quantifying predictive uncertainty with statistically valid coverage.

Under quasi-symmetry, defined by the cycle condition p_ij*p_jk*p_ki = p_ji*p_kj*p_ik on pairwise win probabilities, the Bradley-Terry model is equivalent to a scaled version of PageRank; PageRank-based scores can be asymptotically efficient estimators of Bradley-Terry strengths, giving Bradley-Terry scores a novel interpretation as scaled PageRanks and vice versa.

Multiple-output composite quantile regression is derived through an optimal-transport lens: the paper reveals an intrinsic link between the composite quantile regression loss and the Wasserstein distance from the residuals to the set of quantiles, generalizes CQR to multiple-output settings, and proves theoretical convergence rates of the estimator.

SportsMetrics benchmarks LLMs on sports analytics tasks blending text and numerical data: long-context LLMs significantly outperform standard LLMs across all tasks, GPT-3.5-Turbo-1106 leads in every task except one, and the best model GPT-4-1106-Preview still shows a 34.77-yard discrepancy when predicting NFL passing yards while open-source Llama-2-13B-Chat lags far behind.

On filling missing key statistics from basketball game recaps (points, assists, rebounds, team scores), Claude-2.1 shows strong performance and Mistral-7B-Instruct achieves the highest accuracy among standard LLMs; on adapting to new game rules, Claude-2.1, Gemini-Pro, and GPT-3.5-Turbo-1106 are the top performers.

A tennis momentum study uses PCA dimensionality reduction, gradient-boosting frameworks, and stacking of SVM/RF models with 10-fold cross-validation to predict match outcomes, with feature-importance rankings differing across methods (e.g. running distance, ball speed in mph, and rally count among the examined features).

Focused-portfolio bet sizing is modeled with a generalized Kelly criterion that computes optimal capital allocation across investment candidates from the investor's outcome probabilities, with constraints enforcing no shorting, limited leverage, a maximum limit on permanent-loss-of-capital risk, and maximum individual allocation.

Conformalized selective regression asks whether prediction models should always deliver a prediction, arguing that the pursuit of maximum predictive performance overshadows reliability considerations and proposing a conformal approach to selective prediction.

In a dynamic prediction-market model where agents forecast sequences of random vectors, the main theorem shows that if some agents make correct (or asymptotically correct) next-period forecasts, the aggregated market forecasts converge to the next-period conditional expectations of the random vectors.

Analyzing Florida State's 2023 exclusion as the first undefeated Power 5 team to miss the College Football Playoff, the paper uses a ratings model with sensitivity constant 25: teams with high expected win probability gain little rating from wins while upsets boost ratings noticeably; it concludes committee subjectivity best serves viewer/media attention whereas a ratings model is the only path to transparency.

League of Legends player skill measurement: the paper develops analytical measures of individual player skill and performance for a game whose complexity has stymied such metrics, demonstrates the method's advantages, and finds stability-focused adjustments give only modest improvement.

For human action recognition in video, two-stream ConvNets and LSTM networks with reduced units are compared; one reported model reaches 88% accuracy and another 93.30% accuracy, while plain RNNs struggle to achieve high accuracy, pointing to the importance of temporal modeling choices.

The multi-concept multivariate Elo rating system is adapted to medical students' training data to estimate question difficulty and predict student performance, optimizing educational instruction and learning outcomes on digital learning platforms.

MambaMOT replaces the Kalman filter with a state-space model (Mamba) as the motion predictor for multi-object tracking, addressing the Kalman filter's limitations on the complex nonlinear motions and occlusions common in dynamic environments like sports and dance.

Comprehensive out-of-sample evaluation should use statistical decision theory and replace K-fold and Common Task Framework validation: the statistical decision function chooses d(psi) = argmin_{c in C} L[c, f(psi)], and minimax regret is the most appealing decision criterion among those studied.

In the statistical-decision-theory evaluation framework, squared-error loss is L[c,P(y|x)] = E[(y-c)^2|x] (eq. 7) and zero-one loss is L[c,P(y|x)] = P(y!=c|x) (eq. 8); the indicator 1[y!=c] equals (y-c)^2 when the choice set is {0,1}, linking classification and regression loss.
equation: L[c,P(y\mid x)]=\mathbb{E}[(y-c)^{2}\mid x],\qquad L[c,P(y\mid x)]=P(y\neq c\mid x)=\int\mathbf{1}[y\neq c]\,dP(y\mid x)

claim: Under partial identification, outcome probabilities are bounded by P_s(y=1|x') + lambda_-(x,x') <= P_s(y=1|x) <= P_s(y=1|x') + lambda_+(x,x') for all states s, with a minimax-regret decision function using symmetric bound kappa; prediction-error intervals are found to be far too small, with intervals targeting 10% miscoverage actually giving 31% miscoverage.
equation: P_{s}(y=1\mid x')+\lambda_{-}(x,x')\leq P_{s}(y=1\mid x)\leq P_{s}(y=1\mid x')+\lambda_{+}(x,x'),\ \forall s\in\mathcal{S}

claim: SportsNGEN is a transformer-decoder sports simulation engine trained on professional tennis player-and-ball tracking sequences that generates sustained, realistic gameplay; output sampling parameters are crucial to realism, the same approach transfers to football, and a generic model can be fine-tuned to mimic a specific tennis player from their match data.

SportsNGEN ablations show three enhancements significantly improve convergence and simulation quality: (a) extending representations with relative velocity, distance to the ball, and time into the game/sequence; (b) adding small perturbations to ball positions during training so the model learns error correction; (c) context tokens letting the model adapt to playing surfaces, correctly capturing that clay has the slowest and hard courts the fastest bounces.

SportsNGEN defines statistical metrics to evaluate generated tennis data quality and optimizes simulation hyperparameters against them; training on noise-free ball trajectories yields unstable simulations because prediction errors create out-of-distribution next-step inputs, and sequences longer than 6 seconds are computationally impractical without accuracy gain, suggesting tennis decisions are not strongly affected by information more than 6 seconds old.

Machine-learning match-outcome prediction for football reports: random forest accuracy 64.95% on a two-season split, 67.33% on one season, and 47.73% on recent matches; recursive feature elimination lifts accuracy marginally to 69% from 68% on available features; SVM reaches 67% on two seasons (strong on away wins) and 72.67% on one season but struggles with draws; KNN scores 61.52% on two-season data.

Concluding a suspended sports league is formulated as selecting a subset of already-scheduled games whose final rankings match what full-season play would have produced; the paper gives an exact deterministic reformulation with a tailored Frank-Wolfe algorithm plus a min-max-regret robust counterpart, and NBA 2004-2019 simulations show computational efficiency and wins over a greedy non-rankings benchmark.
equation: X=\left\{\sum_{g\in G^{h}_{i}}x_{g}=m^{h}_{i}\ \forall i\in T,\quad \sum_{g\in G^{a}_{i}}x_{g}=m^{a}_{i}\ \forall i\in T\right\}

claim: Across 76 completed NBA seasons (1946-2021), over 75% of playoff series were won by the team with home-court advantage; the paper proves its PW objective effectively minimizes the expected Euclidean distance between rankings, and its best game-prediction models (Logit, ELM, SVM, MLP) exceed 75% accuracy with Logit best overall on log-loss, accuracy, and AUC.

LLMs used as recommender backbones lag conventional methods on retrieval because of a mismatch between LLM knowledge and recommendation knowledge (complex user-item interactions); the paper bridges the gap by fine-tuning with data samples encoding item correlations, e.g. random masking of purchase sequences [i1,i2,i3,i4,i5] into [i1,[mask]1,i3,[mask]2,i5].

Fine-tuning FLAN-T5-XL with recommendation-knowledge data samples significantly outperforms the base model on retrieval, ranking, and rating prediction; a unified model (UT+AT) handles all three tasks with little per-task sacrifice, ranking-task samples help most while BPR contrastive samples help least, and a sliding window accommodates long sequences.

A temporal graph model captures basketball team collective behavior from player-interaction networks, integrating the time dimension to study the dynamics of collective behavior and performance in team sports.

Isotonic distributional regression postprocesses point predictions into probabilistic forecasts of day-ahead electricity prices; operational decisions based on predictive distributions can yield significantly higher profits than those based on point forecasts alone.

ActNetFormer is a cross-architecture pseudo-labeling framework for semi-supervised video action recognition combining 3D CNNs (local spatiotemporal features) with vision transformers (long-range dependencies); it uses SGD with momentum 0.9 and weight decay 0.001, sampling five clips per video with three 224-resolution crops, and reports state-of-the-art results on standard action-recognition datasets.

X-VARS investigates multi-modal large language models for explaining football refereeing decisions, trading off the performance gains of automated decision-making against explainability and transparency.

Across 12 popular team ball sports (basketball, cricket, field hockey, futsal, handball, ice hockey, lacrosse, roller hockey, rugby, soccer, volleyball, water polo), the paper examines how inherent randomness factors drive underdog achievement, i.e. the likelihood of weaker teams beating stronger ones, using match scores and computed team rankings from major international competitions.

Assumption-lean quantile regression addresses two major limitations of standard quantile regression when the goal is detecting exposure-outcome associations across the outcome distribution rather than pure prediction.

Bayesian learning is calibrated via regularization, confidence minimization, and selective inference, addressing the difficulty of quantifying the reliability of AI decisions in engineering applications where a well-calibrated model must match its confidence to actual outcomes.

Novel measures for aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty are proposed using proper scoring rules, providing uncertainty representation and quantification as a prerequisite for safety-critical machine-learning applications.

Conformal predictive systems, which construct predictive distributions for calibrated inference, are extended to handle covariate shift, broadening their applicability when training and deployment distributions differ.

Market making in spot precious metals centers on navigating liquidity provided mainly by futures contracts, where the Exchange for Physical (EFP) spread, the price difference between futures and spot, plays the pivotal role.

An online multi-player tracking method fuses multiview LiDAR and cameras, claimed as the first to take multiview RGB plus point clouds as input; the PointVoxel 3D pose-estimation pipeline unifies modalities in volumetric space preserving each modality's geometry, pretrained on synthetic data then adapted with unsupervised domain adaptation to avoid costly manual annotation.

Bayesian predictive decision synthesis (BPDS) provides a foundational framework for portfolio analysis under model uncertainty, with a set of candidate models for financial time series driving sequential learning, forecasting, and recursive reinvestment decisions.

CNNs forecasting English Premier League player performance outperform Ridge regression, LightGBM, and prior deep-learning models, achieving strong Spearman correlations with true player rankings; Spearman correlation is proposed as a proxy for expected fantasy ranking performance, and cross-validation splits are stratified by player skill (mean FPL points/week) and variance to prevent leakage.

On the small EPL dataset, cross-validation favored aggressively regularized LightGBM hyperparameters: 50 trees, depth 3, L2 strength 10, 7 leaves with minimum 70 observations per leaf; transfer learning from a news corpus with a longformer showed no predictive signal, with the FWD model unable to beat even training MSE.

The EPL forecasting paper notes as a research direction that aggregating player-level performance predictions into team features for a win/loss logistic regression could yield win probabilities competitive with sportsbook odds, while stressing this is untested speculation.
Tennis momentum and game-fluctuation dynamics are analyzed with Lasso/Ridge-regularized XGBoost and Deep LSTM models to predict match outcomes and understand performance swings.

Expected Points Above Average (EPAA) is a novel NBA player metric based on Bayesian hierarchical modeling, alongside an 'expected points' team metric; both target team and player evaluation where identifying and retaining elite shooters has major financial implications.

Australian Football League team strengths from 2015-2023 are analyzed with time-variant Bradley-Terry models, giving interpretable factors behind team performance where complex black-box match-outcome models lack interpretability.

Ice-hockey multi-object tracking is formulated as bipartite graph matching infused with homography: player foot keypoints from broadcast frames are projected to an overhead rink template via p_i = s*[P_x',P_y',1]^T = H*[P_fx,P_fy,1]^T with a 3x3 homography H (bottom row [h31,h32,1]), disentangling occluded/overlapping players into a pseudo top-view for consistent tracklets.

The hockey tracker uses a message-passing network to aggregate player features and model temporal relations, prunes association edges below threshold xi via Pruned(y_hat) = y_hat if y_hat > xi, and matches identities across frames; trained 30 epochs (batch 16, LR 0.01 with 10-epoch warmup and cosine annealing to 0.001) on a single RTX 4090, it reports state-of-the-art results on all sequences of the 7-game VIP-HTD test set.

Jersey number recognition is reframed as scene text recognition: instead of a dedicated classifier restricted to training-set numbers, a general pretrained STR model (PARSeq) detects, localizes, and recognizes numbers, adapting to new scenarios with little fine-tuning and handling all possible jersey numbers; tracklet-level prediction aggregates frame posteriors as p(d_j=k|{I_n}) = sum_n (log p(I_n|d_j=k) + ...).

A new hockey jersey-number dataset accompanies the framework: the binary legibility classifier (trained balanced despite only 5% legible images, 20 epochs, LR 0.001, momentum 0.9, Sharpness-Aware Minimization) reaches 94.5% accuracy with F1 71.7%; image-level number recognition hits 91.4% (85.4% for the STR model without fine-tuning); tracklet-level accuracy is 87.45% on the SoccerNet test set and 79.31% on the challenge set with heuristic consolidation.

Baseball pitch trajectories are reconstructed in 3D from single-view 2D video: OpenCV's CSRT tracker follows the ball and fixed reference points, and a custom neural network maps the tracked 2D pixel coordinates to 3D space after training on labeled trajectories, offering a low-cost alternative to multi-camera systems like MLB Statcast (12 cameras) and Hawk-Eye; accuracy is limited by timestamp and pixel-tracking errors.

Elite athletic performance shows strong within-season peaking on top of career improvement-decline curves: Swimmer 1 improves from ~57s at age 15 to ~53s at 25 with ~2s within-season gains, Swimmer 4 gains ~3s within seasons, Swimmer 3 gains ~3.5s from ages 15 to 21; errors are non-Gaussian, positively skewed with heavy right tails, the horseshoe prior destabilizes MCMC, and parameters without known full conditionals use adaptive Metropolis-Hastings random-walk updates.

Sports-Traj is a unified trajectory-generation model for multi-agent movement in sports that jointly handles trajectory prediction, imputation, and spatiotemporal recovery, overcoming single-task methods and the limitation that public datasets focus on casual pedestrian motion with weak interactions.

Heterogeneous treatment effect estimation fuses randomized-trial data (strong internal validity) with observational data (external validity) using multi-task Gaussian processes to bridge the internal-external validity gap.

Extensions to expected possession value (EPV) for soccer skill estimation weight events immediately before a shot more heavily than earlier events (decay effect), model possession risk more accurately via the decay effect and effective playing time, and address the selection problem in skill estimation.

A neural network produces probabilistic temperature forecasts from deterministic Global Deterministic Prediction System outputs up to ten-day lead times targeting METAR observations in Canada and the US; training a single model across multiple lead times improves postprocessing, with several lead-time conditioning strategies (supplementary predictor and embedding variants) compared.
Relaxed quantile regression constructs prediction intervals under asymmetric noise, extending quantile-based uncertainty quantification beyond symmetric-noise assumptions.

Bayesian predictive decision synthesis (BPDS) for monetary policy starts from an initial model mixture based on past performance and admits small perturbations of model probabilities by expected performance to improve scores; the VAR(p) companion form stacks lagged states in c = [a + sum_j A_j y_{T+1-j}, ...]^T with block-Toeplitz H, and BPDS mixture effective sample sizes stay higher and less volatile than individual models' ESS even when one model suffers low ESS.

Online learning in betting markets contrasts two binary-market types, profit-seeking (sports gambling) and information-seeking (prediction markets), articulating the interplay between bettors' beliefs in the two settings.

Analyzed via Markov-chain techniques under the Bradley-Terry-Luce model, the Elo rating system learns the model parameters at a rate competitive with the state of the art in the online ranking setting.

Generative-model selection is cast as a multi-armed bandit problem: instead of offline evaluation on large batches, the framework identifies the model maximizing a standard assessment score with the fewest generated samples, minimizing the cost of querying suboptimal models.

Paired-comparison models (Bradley-Terry, Thurstone-Mosteller) with a ridge penalty are estimated via a new empirical-Bayes plus composite-likelihood approach that selects the ridge tuning parameter without refitting the model, as a convenient alternative to cross-validation; simulations show much better predictive accuracy than ordinary maximum likelihood.

Cyclicality and intransitivity in cardinal paired-comparison data are handled within graphical linear models, with a detailed study of the parameter space linking the reduced completely-transitive model to the full not-necessarily-transitive model.

Prediction intervals for time-series forecasting from point forecasters are improved with heteroscedastic quantile regression and width-adaptive conformal inference, enhancing reliability where prior work focused only on widening intervals.

In random-walk football simulations, the field position evolves as X_{g,t+1} = X_{gt} + xi_{gt} when the step stays inside (0,L), the score S increments on touchdowns at the boundaries, the game outcome is y=1 if final score S>0 (0 if <0), and the true win probability satisfies WP(T+1,x,s) = 1/0/1/2 for s>0/s<0/s=0 with backward recursion WP(t-1,x,s) = (1/2)WP(t,L/2,s+1) + (1/2)WP(t,x+1,s) at x=1.

The dependence structure of observational play-by-play data inflates both bias and variance of win-probability estimators; naive bootstrapped confidence intervals are too narrow with dismally low marginal coverage, the randomized cluster bootstrap still undercovers, and only a tuned fractional bootstrap producing extremely wide intervals achieves approximately valid coverage in the simulation.

A parallel corpus of NFL game-thread comments from both teams' fans supports studying intergroup bias in sports fandom language; few-shot GPT-4o tagging improves with linguistic descriptions of win probability, fine-tuned Llama-3 models perform better, and both approach or exceed the human ceiling (crowd annotator agreement 0.69), with 100,000 comments tagged at scale.

Six alternative competitive-balance indices (ex ante Elo-based and ex post benchmark-based) find no evidence of any trend in UEFA Champions League group-stage competitive balance between 2003/04 and 2023/24, contradicting prior studies; ex ante balance declined until 2014/15 then improved through 2023/24.

Proper scoring rules for multivariate probabilistic forecasts are constructed via aggregation and transformation, since propriety alone does not guarantee an informative characterization of predictive performance.

Rank aggregation from pairwise comparisons is vulnerable to sequential manipulation: an adversary with incomplete knowledge (lacking victims' preference scores) maximizes the victims' objectives while globally modifying comparison-graph weights; observed outcomes follow the Bradley-Terry-Luce model y*_ij = 1 with probability theta*_i/(theta*_i+theta*_j), reported signs y^u_ij = +/-1 encode the manipulated ranking, and the aggregation map R(G(C)) = theta returns the estimated strengths.

Bernoulli and reservoir sampling become accomplices of the online rank-manipulation adversary, generating stable comparison sequences that favor the attacker; the proposed adversarial policy is the only one shown able to designate the winner of the aggregation results turn by turn.
Indian stock-market price prediction combines five machine-learning models with superforecaster predictions to enhance investment decisions.

A survey of data synthesis categorizes approaches into four types and model-based augmentation into three strategies (direct training, pre-train and fine-tune, foundation models without fine-tuning); it documents diminishing returns to data volume, motivating the trend toward smaller high-quality datasets, and stresses post-processing to filter synthetic data for task benefit.

A tennis dynamic-analysis and prediction model using a momentum score as output reports model accuracies of 0.913, 0.932, 0.931, 0.919, 0.919, and 0.931 across tests, finding that more recent rounds have greater impact on momentum and that serving-later win probability weakens as other factors improve.

PEP (prevention of expected points) values American-football tackles by comparing the real end-of-play yard line with the predicted yard line under the hypothetical that the tackle had been missed, using high-resolution tracking data, instead of counting tackles without context.

A spatio-temporal graph-analytics framework for field sports targets GPS-wearable tracking data; the global sports-analytics industry is valued at USD 3.78 billion in 2023, with traditional analysis focused on individual athletes rather than collective structures.

Multi-tier tournaments are a novel chess tournament matching and scoring system: players are divided into skill-based tiers, and the tournament score depends on wins, draws, and losses with chess-specific tie-breaking rules.

Conformal Thresholded Intervals (CTI) produce the smallest possible prediction sets with guaranteed coverage by estimating, with off-the-shelf multi-output quantile regression, the conditional probability density of a new response falling in each interquantile interval, then thresholding that density using the inverse relationship between interval length and probability density.

Probabilistic forecasts of extreme wind speeds from numerical weather prediction ensembles are improved by training statistical post-processing models with weighted scoring rules that emphasize the extreme tail of the distribution.

PlayerTV automates soccer player tracking and identification for highlight clips by integrating object detection, SORT-based tracking, team labeling, and OCR kit-number reading; CIELAB color space improves team labeling by 3.9% over weighted RGB (perfect vs 76.2% in challenging light), post-processing adds 2%, and PaddleOCR beats EasyOCR threefold, ranking the correct kit number in the top 5 for 107 of 300 tracklets (top-1 in 92 of those 107).

In the PlayerTV pipeline the OCR kit-number module is the binding constraint at just over 30% association accuracy, so overall pipeline performance tracks OCR accuracy nearly one-for-one and improving OCR would proportionally lift the whole system.

Local level dynamic random partition models treat the evolution of data partitions over time as latent states in a state-space model with a Markov structure linking consecutive partitions, motivated by biomechanics, motion analysis, and sports-science time series; co-clustering probabilities such as P(c_{1,t1}=c_{2,t1}, c_{1,t2}=c_{2,t2}) factor through the marginal at t1, and posterior inference uses Gibbs sampling with an auxiliary MCMC run fitting independent Chinese-restaurant-process models per time point for initialization.

Across varying data dimensions, the local level dynamic partition model consistently outperforms all competing models on every metric, while all models degrade as sample size grows because subjects switch clusters more often; the GMDDP variant is most robust on changepoint-detection metrics.

Kairosis aggregates probability forecasts made over time for a single end-of-period outcome: informed by Bayesian change-point detection, it builds at each time point the posterior probability that forecasts before and after differ, then integrates the resulting posterior mass function into a cumulative mass function for dynamical aggregation.

A tennis momentum capture-and-prediction system reports swing-prediction accuracy of 0.999013 over multiple matches and 0.992738 for finals, with generalization accuracies of 0.9651, 0.8620, 0.9112, and 0.9467 across scenarios; it selects XGBoost regression over other ML algorithms, adds a serve-advantage factor, validates with Mann-Whitney U and Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests, and accepts the hypothesis that players with momentum significantly outperform those without.

The FIVB volleyball ranking (in use since 2020) is recast in a statistical framework: the weighting of match results is shown to be counterproductive, the algorithm's implicit scale parameter is too small so increasing it three- to four-fold improves performance, new numerical-score parameters are derived in closed form, and the ranking penalizes inactive teams by reducing their score 50 points per idle year.

Using Bayesian state-space models on NFL game outcomes and betting-market data (2002-2023), the bye-week rest advantage was +2.2 points per game before the 2011 Collective Bargaining Agreement but is mitigated to about +0.3 points per game since 2011, when the CBA guaranteed four days off and removed bye-week practices; neither the bye nor the mini-bye currently shows significant evidence of a competitive edge.

The NFL rest-differential state-space model writes expected point differential as E[Y_{s,ij}] = theta_{s,i} - theta_{s,j} + mu_{HA,s} with team strengths theta evolving as theta_{(s,i)} ~ N(gamma*theta_{(s-1,i)}, sigma_teamstrength^2), home advantage modeled as a linear trend, and rest effects via signed indicators I(MNF), I(Mini), I(Bye) equal to +1/-1/0 depending on which side holds the advantage.
Multi-agent sports trajectory imputation uses a derivative-accumulating self-ensemble method to fill missing values in player tracking data, where gaps arise from occlusions and sensor limits.

Upselling effects on the Dream11 online fantasy sports platform are studied by modeling users' deposit behavior and building an experimental framework to evaluate how upselling changes user engagement.

Strategic shrouding of digital sin taxes by profit-maximizing firms impairs corrective-tax effectiveness: there is no pure-strategy equilibrium where all firms unshroud taxes (and no symmetric pure-strategy equilibrium), but a segmented-market equilibrium exists; betting agencies' cash bonuses, loyalty free bets, and odds boosts mostly do not affect single-event prices, and the average tax pass-through is 0.038 (SE 0.004), rising to 82% excluding cross leagues.

GST predicts precise 3D human bodies from a single image with Gaussian Splatting Transformers: Gaussians are loosely tied to SMPL mesh vertices by an offset for good density/pose initialization including back faces, joint pose-appearance optimization improves SMPL prediction, and a Gaussian tightness regularization keeps splats close to SMPL parameters; trained on 2D data only it nearly matches HMR2 trained on 3D data, with PSNR 18.68 on 256x256 HuMMan crops.

CS:GO player ratings are built from Plus/Minus values within the match structure of 30 rounds (first to 16 wins; 15-15 ties go to 6-round overtimes won by the first to 4 round wins), five-player teams, and asymmetric attack/defense win conditions (bomb plant/defuse or elimination).

Bellwether trades, the trades most informative for future price movements, are identified with nonlinear machine-learning methods: an optimized neural-network predictor first demonstrates accurate prediction of future market movements, then trade characteristics carrying the information are extracted from it.

Men's ice-hockey World (Junior) Championship success is forecast with a dynamic ranking model combining separate regression and dynamic components that handles non-participating teams and missing tournament years by reverting strengths toward long-term values; penalized log-likelihood estimation improves forecasting accuracy over the static model despite biased estimates.

Inverse constrained reinforcement learning infers the implicit constraints expert agents follow from demonstration data within a Constrained Markov Decision Process framework; the survey distinguishes ICRL from inverse reinforcement learning and inverse optimal control, and shows via example that reward-function and constraint-function generalization differ in new environments.

A Bayesian forensic framework evaluates alleged illegal signaling in sports (bridge, baseball) by comparing two hypotheses: H_C (a specified illegal code was used) versus H_R/H_B (it was not). The core identity is Bayes' rule: posterior odds equal the likelihood ratio times the prior odds.

In the bridge cheating case (alleged orientation code C for lead cards, O_i in {0,1} per board, O=(O_1,...,O_n), h=sum O_i matches m=sum M_i), the likelihood ratio of the observed orientations under the cheating hypothesis versus random orientation is LR(O)=P(O|H_C)/P(O|H_R) approx 4x10^19, i.e. the data are ~4e19 times more likely if the alleged code was used.

The prior odds in the cheating framework incorporate a code-space penalty: with psi the prior probability of cheating and M the number of conceivable codes, P(H_C)/P(H_R) = (psi x 1/M)/(1-psi), so posterior odds approx (4x10^19/M) x psi/(1-psi); even huge likelihood ratios are discounted when many codes could have been dreamed up.

In the baseball case (trash-can bangs signaling pitch type, S_i in {0,1}, b=sum S_i), modeling the random-hypothesis bang rate q with an upper bound of 0.1 via P(S|H_R)=integral_0^0.1 q^b (1-q)^{n-b} dq gives a likelihood ratio LR(S)=P(S|H_B)/P(S|H_R) of about 3.4x10^30 in favor of the cheating hypothesis.

Frequentist p-values answer how unlikely the data are under innocence, which the paper calls the wrong question; the right question is which hypothesis best explains the data, requiring at least two candidate hypotheses and a likelihood-ratio (Bayesian) comparison, standard in forensic statistics.

In Glicko-2, the rating variance for a player with rating mu facing opponents with ratings mu_j and rating deviations phi_j is the inverse of the sum over games of g(phi_j)^2 E(mu,mu_j,phi_j)(1-E(mu,mu_j,phi_j)), where E is the expected score.
Glicko-2 uses the deviation-shrinkage function g(phi)=1/sqrt(1+3 phi^2/pi^2) and the expected-score function E(mu,mu_j,phi_j)=1/(1+exp(-g(phi_j)(mu-mu_j))).

Glicko-2 rating update: Delta = v sum_j g(phi_j)(s_j - E(mu,mu_j,phi_j)) is the rating change scaled by variance v; the new rating is mu' = mu + phi'^2 sum_j g(phi_j)(s_j - E(...)) with phi' = 1/sqrt(1/phi*^2 + 1/v) and phi* = sqrt(phi^2 + sigma'^2) folding in rating volatility sigma'.

A CNN-LSTM that reads chess move sequences and clock times (CNN for positional features feeding a bidirectional LSTM) estimates player ratings directly from games with no hand-crafted features, outputting a rating after each move; trained on 1M+ Lichess games it reached MAE of 182 rating points on test data, and its puzzle-rating predictions were competitive on the 2024 IEEE Big Data Cup chess puzzle difficulty dataset.

The Lamperti transform phi(y)=integral_{y0}^{y} dx/sigma(x) converts a diffusion dY_t=b(Y_t)dt+sigma(Y_t)dW_t into unit-diffusion form dX_t=L(X_t)dt+dW_t with L(x)=(b/sigma - sigma'/2)(phi^{-1}(x)), which the paper uses to move financial diffusion models from the risk-neutral to the real-world measure.

A Girsanov change of measure creates the real-world measure P^phi from the risk-neutral measure Q with density dP^phi/dQ|_{F_T}=exp(-integral_0^T phi_u dW_u - 1/2 integral_0^T phi_u^2 du), under which W*_t=W_t+integral_0^t phi_u du is a Brownian motion.

The paper's market-price-of-risk process is phi_t=(1/zeta)[-(L(X*_t)-L(X_t)) - vartheta(X*_t - X_t - alpha_t)], with a deterministic mean-reversion target alpha_t and reversion speed vartheta, steering the risk-neutral diffusion toward a real-world trajectory.

The CIR++ credit intensity is lambda(t)=y(t)+psi(t) with dy(t)=kappa(theta-y_t)dt+sigma sqrt(y_t) dW_t, kappa,theta,sigma>0, under the Feller condition 2 kappa theta >= sigma^2; global calibration gave kappa=5.138e-1, theta=1.497e-2, sigma=8.904e-2, y0=4.348e-2.

The risk-neutral-to-real-world framework was validated against Goldman Sachs' 2024 global credit outlook forecasts and the EBA 2023 stress tests; under stress (Eurozone sovereign debt crisis, 2012-2013) the Credit Agricole credit spread term structure inverts versus normal conditions (2022-2023).

Passing-network node importance measures used for soccer match prediction: degree centrality C_D(v)=deg(v)/(n-1); closeness C_C(v)=(n-1)/sum_u d(u,v); betweenness C_B(v)=sum_{s!=v!=t} sigma_st(v)/sigma_st (fraction of shortest paths through v); eigenvector centrality C_E(v)=x(v) where Ax=lambda_max x; clustering C_tr(v)=2T(v)/(deg(v)(deg(v)-1)); average path length l=sum_{s,t} d(s,t)/(n(n-1)).

Combining complex-network structural analysis of team passing networks with match statistical data provides deeper insight into team game patterns and strategies, and serves as an alternative tool for predicting soccer match outcomes.

For contextual multi-armed bandits, the Heterogeneous Winning Treatment Effect (HWTE) feature importance is the sample-weighted gap between the best arm's success rate within each feature bin b and the global best arm: FI_HIE(x)=sum_{b=1}^{m_x} (N_b/N)(P_{w_b}(Y=1)-P_{w*}(Y=1)), with w_b the winning arm in bin b and w* the global winning arm.

The Heterogeneous Distribution Divergence (HDD) feature score is the sample-weighted contextual divergence of the arm reward distributions minus the non-contextual divergence: FI_HDD(x)=sum_b (N_b/N) D_b(P_{b_1},...,P_{b_k}) - D(P_1,...,P_k), and the combined score FI(x) is a weighted sum alpha_1*FI_... of the two normalized scores.

The HDD score expands into pairwise KL divergences: the contextual term is sum_b (N_b/N) sum_{i,j} (N_{b_i}N_{b_j}/N_b^2) sum_{v=0}^{1} P_{b_i}(Y=v) log(P_{b_i}(Y=v)/P_{b_j}(Y=v)), minus the analogous non-contextual term over arm pairs.

Conventional feature selection picks features correlated with the outcome, but contextual MAB needs features that cause heterogeneous treatment effects across arms; model-free causal selection (HIE/HDD) evaluated 10 features on 50000 samples in 2.7s per trial versus 647.3s (LinUCB), 665.5s (nonlinear LinUCB), 82.5s (CohortMAB).

TrackNetV4 builds a motion attention map H_t = sigma(A_t circledcirc V_t) where sigma is the sigmoid, A_t is a learnable motion prompt modulation of frame-differencing maps, and V_t are visual features, so the moving ball's location is emphasized before tracking.

The motion-enhanced visual representation is A_tau odot V_{tau+1} (elementwise product of the motion attention at tau with visual features at tau+1), fusing high-level visual features with motion information to handle occlusion and motion blur in fast sports-ball tracking.

TrackNetV4 fuses high-level visual features with learnable motion attention maps from frame differencing through a motion-aware fusion mechanism, improving tracking of high-speed small objects (tennis balls, shuttlecocks) under partial occlusion and low visibility where visual-only TrackNet v1-v3 struggle.

Monte Carlo experiments on weather parametric insurance show portfolio basis risk and volatility decrease as the number of contracts increases, i.e. basis risk (mismatch between actual loss and payout) can be managed through diversification like other risks.

Spatial relationships significantly impact weather parametric insurance basis risk: risk levels correlate with the ratio between the insured location, the weather station, and the disaster footprint radius.
Event severity does not significantly impact weather parametric insurance basis risk, suggesting catastrophic disaster severity should not hinder parametric insurance development.

Dream11 spending-propensity prediction is formalized as P-hat_i = f(U_i, R_i, C_i) for each user i from user, round and contest features, minimizing total prediction loss L-hat = min sum_i L(P_i, P-hat_i).

The proposed transformer tokenizes each tabular feature as T_j = b_j + f_j(x_j) in R^d with a learnable feature tokenizer f_j, stacking numerical and categorical tokens into T=stack[...], to capture rich feature interactions for spend prediction.
The new transformer for user spending propensity on Dream11 (200M+ users) surpasses the FT-Transformer baseline, improving MAE by 2.5% and MSE by 21.8%.

Easy2Hard-Bench assigns numerical difficulty to problems with the 3-parameter logistic IRT model (1PL-with-guessing): P(X_ui=1|theta_u,b_i,c_i)=c_i+(1-c_i)/(1+e^{-(theta_u-b_i)}), where theta_u is solver ability, b_i item difficulty, c_i guessing floor.

The IRT ladder used for difficulty labels: 1PL P=1/(1+e^{-(theta_u-b_i)}); 2PL adds discrimination a_i as P=1/(1+e^{-a_i(theta_u-b_i)}); 4PL adds an upper asymptote d_i as P=c_i+(d_i-c_i)/(1+e^{-a_i(theta_u-b_i)}).

The easy-to-hard discrepancy for problem pair i is delta^{(i)}=|s_h^{(i)}-s_e^{(i)}| x 1{s_h^{(i)}<s_e^{(i)}}, nonzero only when the human difficulty score is below the estimated (LLM) difficulty; mean and std of delta over pairs summarize average discrepancy.

Easy2Hard-Bench is a consistently formatted collection of 6 benchmark datasets (AMC math, Codeforces, Lichess chess puzzles, reasoning) with IRT- and Glicko-2-derived numerical difficulty scores; splits include E2H-AMC 1000/2975, E2H-Codeforces 3663/4000, E2H-Lichess 71763/5000 (train/eval), with a higher share of challenging problems than prior collections; data at huggingface.co/datasets/furonghuang-lab/Easy2Hard-Bench.

Glicko-2 update: r' = r + q/(1/r_d^2+1/d^2) sum_j g((r_d)_j)(s_j - E(s_j|r,r_j)); new volatility sigma'=exp(x0/2) where x0 solves f(x)=0 with f(x)=e^x(Delta^2-phi^2-v-e^x)/(2(phi^2+v+e^x)^2)-(x-2 ln sigma)/tau^2; phi'=1/sqrt(1/(phi^2+sigma'^2)+1/v); mu'=mu+phi'^2 sum_j g(phi_j)(s_j-E(s_j|mu,mu_j,phi_j)).

Code-generation average accuracy in Easy2Hard-Bench is (1/P) sum_{p=1}^{P} (1/C_p) sum_{c=1}^{C_p} 1{eval(<code_p>, x_{p,c}) = y_{p,c}}, the mean over problems of the per-problem pass rate across test cases.

RisingBALLER is the first publicly available transformer approach that treats each football match as a sequence with players as tokens, learning match-contextual player embeddings via masked player prediction (MPP) pre-training, like masked language modeling for text.

RisingBALLER's downstream next-match-statistics-prediction (NMSP) model surpasses a strong community baseline for player performance forecasting, and its embeddings support positional-role features beyond rigid x,y coordinates, team cohesion estimation, and similar-player retrieval for data-driven scouting.

Ablation on RisingBALLER embeddings: with team-affiliation embeddings, same-team players form low-dissimilarity blocks (model leans on team identity); without them, embeddings cluster by individual profile across teams (Benzema~Suarez, Neymar~Ronaldo, Messi~Bale as forwards; Iniesta/Kroos/Modric as midfielders; Varane~Pique as defenders), measured by cosine-similarity dissimilarity heatmaps.
Action spotting maps continuous time to frame index j=floor(t/T+1/2)+1 with T the inter-frame time, and maps a predicted frame back to milliseconds as t-hat=(j-hat-1)xT.
A spotted action counts as correct within tolerance delta if |t-hat - t| <= 0.5 x delta, defining the TP/FP/FN sets TP^c_{delta,tau} etc. used for precision-recall.

Average precision for action class c at tolerance delta is the 11-point interpolated area under the precision-recall curve: AP^c_delta=(1/11) sum_{r'=0}^{10} max_{(p,r) in Phi(r')} p with Phi(r')={(p,r) in PR^c_delta | r >= r'/10}.

Mean average precision mAP@delta=(1/C) sum_{c=1}^{C} AP^c_delta averages AP over C action classes; the averaged a-mAP=(1/Delta) sum_{d=1}^{Delta} [mAP@(delta_l+(d-1)(delta_h-delta_l)/Delta)+mAP@(delta_l+d(delta_h-delta_l)/Delta)]/2 trapezoids across tolerances, with a loose variant (Delta=11, 5s steps, 5s to 60s) and a tight variant (Delta=4, 1s steps, 1s to 5s).

SoccerNet is the largest public sports-video action-spotting resource: 550+ complete annotated broadcast games, yearly challenges, and 60+ methods developed over five years, making automatic action spotting viable for sports analytics, coaching, and broadcast fan engagement.

FanCric is a multi-agent LLM framework with orchestration for crafting Dream11 fantasy cricket (IPL) teams, fusing structured and unstructured data; it was evaluated on about 12.7 million unique entries from a Dream11 contest against crowd wisdom and a simpler prompt-engineering approach, with ablations on the number of teams generated.

The Elo expected score for player A against B with ratings R_A, R_B is E[A|B]=1/(1+10^{(R_B-R_A)/400}), the classic 400-point logistic scaling used as the win-probability emulator in the CS:GO skill-rating study.

The surrogate-modeling evaluation framework treats each rating system as an emulator E whose ratings feed a matchmaking acquisition function AF: Emulator x Team x Team -> R; the weighted variant is AF_weighted(E,T1,T2)=alpha*draw_factor+beta*seen_factor and the exploration variant is AF_unseen=-sum_T log c(T) over teams in the match.

For the entropy-based acquisition theta=H(R|M=m)=-p log p-(1-p) log(1-p) with p=p(w_T1|m), the derivative d theta/dp=log(1-p)-log(p) equals zero exactly at p=0.5, so predictive entropy (matchmaking information gain) is maximized for evenly matched teams.

TrueSkill parameters are mu (default rating 25), sigma (skill volatility), beta (skill class width: a beta rating gap means an 80% win chance), and tau (additive dynamics factor added to variance each step); sensitivity analysis on CS:GO data finds beta and sigma the most important parameters, tau less so, with optimal ratio beta=sigma/0.5 and beta=sigma/1.6 for the two emulators versus the default beta=sigma/2.

The CS:GO study's Gaussian-process surrogate for emulator performance uses kernel k(x,x')=(1/1000)exp(-||x-x'||^2/0.5) with a mean performance prior of 60%, and the acquisition function parameterized with alpha=1, beta=1 produced the best matchmaking-driven rating evaluation.
Soccer camera calibration quality is scored as Score = Acc@5 x Completeness Ratio, the product of keypoint accuracy within 5 pixels and the completeness ratio of detected pitch features.

Heatmap regression for soccer keypoint detection places Gaussian peaks with sigma=3px at keypoint locations and sigma=4px at extremity locations; the calibration pipeline runs keypoint and line detection on video frames, feeds line-intersection points (including beyond-frame intersections) through an iterative keypoint selection algorithm, and calibrates against a predefined pitch model (evaluated on SoccerNet-v3).

The Gaussian log-score loss for multivariate probabilistic forecasting is L=sum_t log p(z_t|theta(h_t)) proportional to sum_t -1/2[ln|Sigma_t|+eta_t^T Sigma_t^{-1} eta_t], which is sensitive to outliers and motivates the robust MVG-CRPS alternative.

The closed-form Gaussian CRPS is CRPS(F_{mu,sigma},z)=sigma*CRPS(Phi,(z-mu)/sigma) where Phi is the standard normal CDF; MVG-CRPS extends this to multivariate Gaussian forecasts via the eigendecomposition Sigma_t=U_t S_t U_t^T as L(N(mu_t,Sigma_t),z_t)=sum_i lambda_i ... mimicking the univariate formula, giving a strictly proper scoring rule with a closed form in neural network outputs.

The energy score ES(F,z)=E_{Z~F}||Z-z||^beta - 1/2 E_{Z,Z'~F}||Z-Z'||^beta (beta=1 standard) is a multivariate extension of CRPS growing linearly with outliers; its sample form is (1/n)sum_i||Z_i-z||^beta - 1/(2n^2)sum_{i,j}||Z_i-Z_j||^beta.

MVG-CRPS is a strictly proper scoring rule for multivariate Gaussian distributions that is robust to outliers where the log-score fails; on real datasets it improves robustness, accuracy and uncertainty quantification, e.g. univariate Seq2Seq energy scores: exchange_rate 0.1240+-0.0022 (MVG-CRPS) vs 0.2876+-0.0055 (log-score), traffic 2.2200+-0.0022 vs 3.6810+-0.0136.

The Elo rating process for N players with random pairings is a Markov chain on the zero-sum hyperplane Z_N={x in R^N: sum_i x_i=0}; it has a unique stationary distribution pi to which it converges almost surely and in Wasserstein metrics: lim_t W_p(L(X_t),pi)=0 for p>=1.

The Elo stationary distribution concentrates on true skills rho as the K-factor vanishes: E[(1/N)|X-rho|_1]<=C sqrt(K), so lim_{K->0} E[(1/N)|X-rho|_1]=0 and pi converges to the Dirac mass at rho; pi has a finite exponential moment and full support supp(pi)=Z_N.
