A novel 2D-to-3D uplifting model directly estimates 3D human poses including joint rotations in a single forward pass, investigating multiple rotation representations, loss functions and training strategies with and without ground-truth rotations; it reaches state-of-the-art rotation accuracy, is 150 times faster than the IK-based approach, and surpasses Human Mesh Recovery models in joint localization precision.

SoccerNet-v3D and ISSIA-3D extend SoccerNet-v3 and ISSIA with field-line-based camera calibration and multi-view synchronization, enabling 3D object localization by triangulation; the paper introduces a monocular 3D ball localization task built on triangulated 2D ball annotations, calibration and reprojection metrics for on-demand annotation quality, a single-image 3D ball localization baseline using camera calibration and ball-size priors, and a bounding-box optimization technique aligning 2D annotations with the 3D scene; code and generation pipelines are public.

TextArena is an open-source collection of 57+ competitive text-based games (single, two-player and multi-player) for training and evaluating agentic LLM behavior in dynamic social skills such as negotiation, theory of mind and deception, with online play against humans and other models and real-time TrueSkill ratings; documentation, environments, leaderboard and examples are on GitHub and textarena.ai.

Action anticipation in football broadcast videos is formalized as predicting future actions in unobserved frames within a five- or ten-second anticipation window; the paper releases the SoccerNet Ball Action Anticipation dataset (based on SoccerNet Ball Action Spotting) and proposes FAANTRA, a Football Action ANticipation TRAnsformer baseline adapting the state-of-the-art FUTR model to ball-related action prediction.

Generalized visual relation detection with diffusion models moves beyond predefined relation categories: visual relations have subtle appearance describable by multiple phrases, so the method handles the semantic ambiguity characteristic of visual relations instead of restricting to a fixed label set.

A novel bottom-up geometric method derives a set of points and lines from circle correspondences so that sparse circular field markings (the only features visible in close-up central-area broadcast views) can be exploited in the linear equations of single-frame sports field registration, complementing top-performing line-based detectors and enabling registration and image annotation in otherwise difficult scenarios.

Research Power Ranking (RPR) adapts the Elo rating system to scientist evaluation: scientific productivity is scored through three components (fundamental, applied, commercial activity), each a separate rating updated on probabilistic 'scientific games' analogous to chess matches, and the researcher's scientific rating is a weighted sum of the components reflecting current position plus career trajectory including phase transitions.

The preference metric (PM) of a distribution Q with distortion function h:[0,1]->[0,1], h(0)=0, is the signed Choquet integral U_h(Q)=int_{-inf}^0 (h(1-Q(x))-h(1)) dx+int_0^inf h(1-Q(x)) dx; setting h(u)=u recovers the expected value, so PM-centric bandits subsume conventional mean-based bandits while capturing tail behavior and decision risk.

The paper proves optimality of mixture policies under preference metrics and provides two regret-efficient algorithm classes for horizon-dependent and infinite-horizon (anytime) settings that estimate optimal mixtures and track arm-selection fractions toward them; for measures such as mean and CVaR, the ETC-based algorithm matches existing regret bounds under sub-Gaussian bandit models (unlike bounded-distribution UCB analyses that assume gap knowledge).

An 'ARIMA - Stepwise Regression - Neural Network' pipeline predicts gold prices in international financial markets: ARIMA estimates price and technical-analysis variables capturing trader psychological behavior, stepwise regression selects the best influencing variables, and the selected variables feed an artificial neural network; the approach is presented as transferable to stocks, commodities, currency pairs and financial market indicators.

A machine-learning framework for FIFA World Cup match-winner prediction integrates team-level historical data with player-specific performance metrics (goals, assists, passing accuracy, tackles), building year-specific team profiles that account for evolving rosters and player development; classification techniques with dimensionality reduction and hyperparameter optimization achieve superior accuracy over baseline methods on FIFA 2022 World Cup data, with findings emphasizing player synergy and strategic match-ups.

Novel deterministic and robust integer programming models select the optimal fantasy football starting eleven and captain under a fixed budget, realistically encoding FPL constraints; a hybrid scoring metric built with interpretable AI on match-performance data defines the cost vectors, and on 2023/24 Premier League data the hybrid method achieved the highest total score with consistent performance, with Monte Carlo simulation confirming the effectiveness of the averaging-based cost estimation out of sample; formations and players chosen by the models are analyzed in depth.

A survey of video event detection in sports analytics distinguishes three key tasks - Temporal Action Localization (TAL), Action Spotting (AS) and Precise Event Spotting (PES) - reviewing their definitions, applications and methodological evolution, categorizing sports-specific datasets and evaluation metrics with strengths and limitations, analyzing SOTA techniques (CNNs/Transformers, audio-visual multimodal fusion, self-supervised learning, knowledge distillation, cross-sport generalization), and outlining open challenges and research directions for generalized, efficient, robust event detection.

Multidimensional space of events (MDSE) theory extends Bayesian probability to model mutual influences between events and hypothesis sets instead of assuming conditional independence; validated by analytical proofs, computational simulations and domain case studies, it reports 15-20% improved prediction accuracy over standard Bayesian methods on high-interdimensionality datasets and polynomial (vs exponential) computational scaling for systems with over 50 interrelated variables.

Crossing in soccer (Shandong Taishan Luneng 2017 season): distinct matching strategies estimate the overall Average Treatment Effect (ATE) and the Average Treatment Effect on the Treated (ATT) of crossing on shot creation; crossing yields a 1.6% additive increase in shot probability overall (ATE) versus not crossing, and 5.0% among plays where crossing was actually attempted (ATT), illustrating how the estimand choice changes interpretation.

The case study demonstrates that ATE and ATT require distinct matching strategies even when both aim to eliminate spurious crossing-shot relationships, and that framing analytics questions causally determines which estimand is appropriate in sports tactic analysis.

SoccerChat is a multimodal conversational AI framework for soccer video understanding integrating visual and textual data, fine-tuned on a structured video instruction dataset built on SoccerNet enriched with jersey-color annotations and automatic speech recognition transcripts; benchmarked on action classification and referee decision-making, it shows strong general soccer event comprehension with competitive referee-decision accuracy; code at github.com/simula/SoccerChat.

Distributional forecasting of e-commerce order fulfillment time uses Conformal Predictive Systems and Cross Venn-Abers Predictors (model-agnostic, with rigorous coverage/validity guarantees), integrating granular spatiotemporal features of fulfillment location and carrier performance, plus a cost-sensitive decision rule converting probabilistic forecasts to point predictions; on a large-scale industrial dataset, ML-based point predictions beat the rule-based system by up to 14% higher accuracy and up to 75% improvement in identifying late deliveries.

Modified fitness-fatigue performance equation with training-dose-dependent time constants: P(n)=P_0+sum_{i=1}^{n-1} k_1 w(i) exp(-(n-i)/tau_1(w(i)))-k_2 w(i) exp(-(n-1)/tau_2(w(i))), where w=(w(1),...,w(n-1)) are daily training impulses; the dose-dependent tau's make impulse responses transcendental and resist analytic optimization.

Mathematical optimization of training load to maximize performance is carried out for the Banister et al. 1975 Fitness-Fatigue Impulse Response Model and the Busso 2003 Variable Dose-Response Model; the authors note discrepancies between optimized load trends and recommended practices (tapering, periodization), and propose interpretable nonlinear modifications to the magnitude and time response of the fitness-fatigue model so optimized loads exhibit those trends.

Using 1 Hz bookmaker odds and betting-stake data from a leading European bookmaker over a full German top-flight season, regression and state-space models (accounting for an underlying market activity level) test whether the market anticipates the first goal: results indicate neither the bookmaker (via odds adjustments) nor bettors (via stakes on the scoring team) significantly anticipate goals before the first goal is scored.

The paper proposes the first betting-based algorithm computing fixed-horizon confidence intervals for the mean of a bounded random variable with the optimal O(sqrt(sigma^2 log(1/delta)/n)) width guarantee, empirically outperforming competitors.

The key innovation is using the optimal betting strategy at every step (in a certain sense) rather than choosing a constant strategy in advance as standard betting-based confidence-sequence methods do, which yields strict improvements and finite-time guarantees for the fixed-horizon setting.

Total, aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty are defined from the known decomposition of (strictly) proper scoring rules into a divergence and an entropy component, giving a flexible uncertainty-quantification framework instantiable with different losses: for selective prediction the scoring rule should ideally match the task loss, mutual information performs best for out-of-distribution detection, and an epistemic uncertainty measure based on the zero-one loss consistently outperforms others in active learning.

A novel method for abstention in pairwise learning-to-rank abstains when the ranker's conditional risk exceeds a predefined threshold, with three contributions: theoretical characterization of the optimal abstention strategy, a model-agnostic plug-in algorithm for constructing abstaining ranking models, and comprehensive empirical evaluation across multiple datasets demonstrating effectiveness (motivated by high-stakes domains like health, education, employment).

Conf-OT addresses domain drift in split conformal prediction for foundation models (e.g. CLIP, pretrained once on an inaccessible source domain) by operating transductively over the combined calibration and query sets: solving an optimal transport problem bridges the pre-training-to-adaptation domain gap without extra data splits while maintaining coverage guarantees; evaluated across 15 datasets and three non-conformity scores.

Glickman (Harvard, 2026) proposes a paired-comparison model in which both the tie probability and the order effect depend on the average strength of the two competitors: draws are more likely between stronger pairs, and order effects are more pronounced for stronger competitors. Demonstrated on US Chess Open game outcomes from 2006 to 2019. The baseline Bradley-Terry win probability is given by logit P(Y_ij=1)=theta_i - theta_j, where Y_ij=1 indicates a win for player i and theta_i, theta_j are latent strength parameters.

Davidson's 1970 tie-extended Bradley-Terry model (preserving Luce's choice axiom / IIA) gives win, loss and tie probabilities with a shared tie term: P(Y_ij=1)=exp(theta_i)/D, P(Y_ij=0)=exp(theta_j)/D, P(Y_ij=1/2)=nu*exp((theta_i+theta_j)/2)/D, where the denominator D=exp(theta_i)+exp(theta_j)+nu*exp((theta_i+theta_j)/2) and nu>0 controls the overall tie likelihood. The odds of a win versus a loss are independent of the tie probability.

Glickman's strength-dependent order effect replaces the constant order-effect parameter alpha by alpha_0 + alpha_1*(theta_i+theta_j)/2, so that for alpha_1=0 the model reduces to David (1988), while alpha_1>0 means the probability that White wins increases with the average strength of the two competitors, controlling for strength difference.

Strength-dependent tie probability: with beta_0=log(nu), the tie term nu*exp((theta_i+theta_j)/2) is replaced by nu*exp((1+beta_1)*(theta_i+theta_j)/2)=exp(beta_0+(1+beta_1)*(theta_i+theta_j)/2). For beta_1=0 the draw probability does not depend on average player strength; beta_1>0 makes stronger evenly-matched pairs draw more often. With beta_1=1 the draw probability dominates win/loss probabilities for strong pairs.

Bayesian fit to US Chess Open 2006-2019 gives posterior means alpha_0=0.363 (95% CI 0.289, 0.434), alpha_1=0.037 (0.000, 0.074), beta_0=-0.471 (-0.505, -0.437), beta_1=0.120 (0.103, 0.138). For two average players, alpha_0=0.363 implies White win-to-loss odds of exp(0.363/2)=1.2; for two strong players (theta_i=theta_j=2) the odds rise to exp((0.363+2*0.037)/2)=1.244. Draw probability for average players is exp(-0.471)/(1+1+exp(-0.471))=0.238, versus 0.489 for two strong players with beta_1=0.120.

The multinomial log-likelihood for the full strength-dependent model over K games is l(alpha_0,alpha_1,beta_0,beta_1,theta_1,...,theta_n|y)=sum_{k=1}^{K} I[y_{k.ij}=1]*log(p_{ij1}) + I[y_{k.ij}=0]*log(p_{ij0}) + I[y_{k.ij}=0.5]*log(p_{ijd}), where y_{k.ij} is game k's outcome between i and j and p_{ij1}, p_{ij0}, p_{ijd} are the win/loss/draw probabilities. MLE proceeds by alternating conditional maximization (Newton-Raphson on the non-strength parameters, then on strengths with identifiability constraint sum_k theta_k=0).

Bradley-Terry strength parameters convert to the FIDE/Elo rating scale by R_i = 1500 + (400/log 10)*hat(theta_i), where hat(theta_i) is the estimated Bradley-Terry parameter for player i and R_i is the rating on the Elo scale.

MOVDA (Margin of Victory Differential Analysis, Rimble Inc.) enhances Elo by using the deviation between the true margin of victory and a learned expected margin. On 13,619 professional NBA games (2013-2023), MOVDA reduced Brier score prediction error by 1.54% compared to TrueSkill, increased outcome accuracy by 0.58%, and accelerated rating convergence by 13.5%, while keeping the computational efficiency of the original Elo updates (only a few extra arithmetic operations per update).

MOVDA models expected margin of victory as a scaled and shifted hyperbolic tangent incorporating home advantage: E_MOV(Delta R, I_HA) = alpha*tanh(beta*Delta R) + gamma + delta*I_HA, where Delta R = R_A - R_B is the rating differential; alpha>0 scales the asymptotic expected margin from skill difference (approaches +-alpha as |Delta R|->infinity); beta>0 controls steepness around Delta R=0; gamma is a baseline offset; delta quantifies home advantage in margin points; I_HA is the home-advantage indicator. The tanh form captures saturation effects (blowouts stop scaling linearly).

The MOVDA rating update augments Elo's outcome-based error term (S_A - E_A) with a second term reflecting the margin-expectation deviation: R'_A = R_A + K*(S_A - E_A) + lambda*Delta_MOV, and R'_B = R_B - (K*(S_A - E_A) + lambda*Delta_MOV), where Delta_MOV = T_MOV - E_MOV(Delta R, I_HA) is the true margin minus the expected margin, and lambda>=0 controls the margin-differential influence. Setting lambda=0 recovers standard Elo. Ablation confirms removing the differential term (lambda=0) reverts performance to standard Elo.

MOVDA assumes true margins are approximately normally distributed around the expectation, T_MOV,i ~ N(E_MOV(Delta R_i, I_HA,i), sigma^2), and estimates the parameters (alpha, beta, gamma, delta) by nonlinear least squares: (hat alpha, hat beta, hat gamma, hat delta) = argmin over (alpha,beta,gamma,delta) of sum_{i=1}^{n}(T_MOV,i - E_MOV(Delta R_i, I_HA,i; alpha,beta,gamma,delta))^2, solved with Adam or quasi-Newton methods (implemented via SciPy curve_fit on chronologically-ordered training data).

MOVDA NBA results table: MOVDA outcome accuracy 63.32%, Brier 0.2258, convergence 166 games vs standard Elo 62.77%/0.2274/193 games, linear-MOV-scaled Elo 63.18%/0.2282/199, Glicko-2 63.18%/0.2264/189, TrueSkill 62.66%/0.2294/192. Ablation: MOVDA full model 63.24%/0.2259/166 vs standard Elo 62.77%/0.2274/193. All hyperparameters (including lambda in [0.1, 3.0]) were grid-search tuned optimizing Brier score on the same dataset.

McByte is a tracking-by-detection multi-object tracking framework for sports analytics that integrates temporally propagated segmentation masks as an association cue without per-video tuning and without training (relying only on pre-trained models and community detectors). It computes two pixel-count ratios between the tracklet's propagated mask and a detection bounding box: the bounding-box coverage of the mask mc^{i,j} = |mask(tracklet_i) cap bbox_j| / |mask(tracklet_i)| and the mask fill ratio mf^{i,j} = |mask(tracklet_i) cap bbox_j| / |bbox_j|, with mc, mf in [0,1].

McByte's association cost update: when ambiguity/isolation conditions are satisfied, the final association cost between tracklet i and detection j becomes costs^{i,j} = costs^{i,j}_{IoU} - mf^{i,j}; otherwise it stays the plain IoU cost costs^{i,j}_{IoU}. The enriched cost matrix is solved with the Hungarian matching algorithm. McByte outperforms the baseline on SportsMOT val (HOTA 83.9 vs 69.0, IDF1 83.6 vs 77.9, MOTA 98.9 vs 97.5), DanceTrack val (HOTA 62.3 vs 47.1), SoccerNet-tracking 2022 test (HOTA 85.0 vs 72.1), and MOT17 val (HOTA 69.9 vs 68.4).

DIAMOND is an LLM-driven agent for context-aware baseball highlight summarization combining sabermetric features (Win Expectancy, WPA, Leverage Index) with LLM narrative reasoning. Evaluated on five Korean Baseball Organization League games, DIAMOND improved F1-score from 42.9% (WPA-only / NAVER AI Highlights) to 84.8% (DIAMOND'), with DIAMOND full at 79.3% F1 and ablation without the reflection stage at 76.5%. Top-ranked plays where LI far exceeds WPA get up to 20 extra ranking points, decreasing 1 point per rank.

DIAMOND's sabermetric foundations: Win Expectancy WE(s) = W_s / N_s where W_s is games won from state s and N_s total games observed in state s (precomputed from historical data); Win Probability Added WPA = WE_after - WE_before (positive means the play improved the team's win probability); Leverage Index LI = |WE_after - WE_before| / Avg(|WE_after - WE_before|) where the denominator is the average absolute WE change across all historical plays - higher LI marks higher-stakes moments. Scoring bands: high-impact 40-60 points for |WPA| >= 0.15 in crucial moments; moderate 20-39 for 0.05 <= WPA < 0.15.

Skripnikov & Sivadanam (New College of Florida) model drive-by-drive football scoring with partially regularized ordinal regression on 2014-2020 FBS college and 2009-2017 NFL data. The cumulative-logit model is: log(P(Y_ijkl >= s)/P(Y_ijkl < s)) = mu_s + alpha_i + beta_j + delta*h_ijl + phi^T g_ijkl + xi*I.cmp_ijkl + gamma^T x*_{ji(k-1)l} * I.cmp_ijkl, where Y_ijkl is the scoring outcome of a drive, mu_s cumulative-odds intercepts for league-average opponent, alpha_i the team's offensive margin over league average, beta_j the opponent's defensive margin, delta the home-field effect, g_ijkl game-context variables, and gamma^T x* the centered complementary-football statistics from the previous drive (e.g., turnovers forced by the defense creating easier scoring chances). Constraints sum alpha_i = sum beta_j = 0 anchor intercepts to the league-average opponent.

The Skripnikov football model uses an elastic-net penalty for variable selection on the complementary features gamma while leaving team strength coefficients (alpha, beta) unpenalized to guarantee full strength-of-schedule adjustment, and partially relaxes the proportional-odds assumption (rather than fully relaxing it, which would explode parameters: ~64 team coefficients for NFL, ~260 for college). Complementary statistics are mean-centered (x* = x - x-bar) so intercepts and alpha/beta margins read as projections onto a league-average complementary unit. Residual diagnostics use the surrogate approach extended to non-proportional-odds models.

Real-time egocentric table-tennis trajectory prediction with event cameras and Meta Project Aria glasses: foveated vision using eye-gaze restricts event processing to a w x w window around the gaze reprojection, achieving a 10.81x reduction factor on collected trajectories. The detection pipeline has worst-case total latency 4.5 ms (computation + perception), far below a 30 FPS frame-based system's 66 ms worst-case perception alone. Events considered: E = {e_i | x_i in N(x_ET, w)}_{i=0}^{N-1}, where e_i=(x_i, t_i, p_i) with timestamps in [t, t+Delta t], x_ET the eye-gaze reprojection, and N(x_ET, w) a w-by-w window centered at x_ET.

Event-camera motion compensation uses IMU gyroscope angular velocity: the compensated event coordinates are x_i^{mc} = K [I - [bar omega]_x (t_i - t_0)] K^{-1} x_i, where K is the intrinsic calibration matrix, I the identity, [bar omega]_x the skew-symmetric matrix of mean angular velocity bar omega from the Aria IMU gyroscope, and t_0 the reference time. Moving objects are found via a normalized mean-timestamp image rho(x) with adaptive threshold B(x)=1 if rho(x) > theta_0 + theta_1 ||bar omega|| (theta_0 static threshold, theta_1 scales with angular speed), then DBSCAN clustering on (t_i, x_i, y_i), selecting the cluster whose convex hull circularity gamma_j = P(conv(S_j))^2 / (4 pi A(conv(S_j))) is closest to 1 with perimeter and area in geometry bounds [P_min, P_max], [A_min, A_max] as the ball.

DYNAMO (DYnamic Non-stAtionary local M-estimatOrs) learns time-varying causal structures of home-field advantage without stationarity assumptions, integrating general loss functions for linear/nonlinear structures, with theoretical identifiability and estimation-consistency guarantees. Applied to high-resolution event data from the 2020-2021 and 2021-2022 English Premier League seasons (the former played with no audience), results reveal time-varying, team-specific field advantages influenced by referee bias that differ significantly with and without crowd support; the learned time-varying causal structures improve goal prediction accuracy over existing methods.

DYNAMO's time-varying causal process model: x_t := f(Pa(x_t), epsilon_t; theta(tau_t)) for t=1,...,T, where tau_t = t/T, Pa(x_t) subset of {x_t, x_{t-1}, ..., x_{t-L}} in R^{(L+1) x d} is the parent set (up to L lags), and theta(tau_t) is the time-varying parameter describing the causal structure G_t = (V_t, theta_t), a directed acyclic graph at each time t. The framework uses local M-estimators for inference of linear or nonlinear time-varying causal structures in the non-stationary process {x_t}.

Interpretable low-dimensional modeling of football tactics (Ide et al., Nagoya): interpretable state variables are defined for the ball-holder and potential pass receivers based on options like passing, with key variables representing the game state identified through discussion with a manager. Validated on StatsBomb event data and SkillCorner tracking data from the 2023/24 season, an XGBoost model predicting successful passes selects the top-n players by shortest distance to the ball and by highest values of the other variables; the pass receiver's score considers the space the off-ball player can move into, the distance between ball and off-ball player, and the time for the nearest opponent to reach either the off-ball player or the passing lane. Performance validated by F1 score on test data.

Composite visualization study for marksmanship training (Zerman et al., Mid Sweden University): five composite views built from first-person shooting video with overlaid metrics and graphical summaries were evaluated with 10 participants (5 expert marksmen, 5 novices) via shot-count and aiming interpretation tasks, pairwise preference comparisons, and semi-structured interviews, measuring perceived effectiveness for steadiness, accuracy, consistency, recoil management, timing, pre-shot/post-shot behavior, and aiming trajectory. Dashboard-style composite view results showed significance against chi-square thresholds: D >= chi^2(4, 0.05) approx 9.448 for novice-vs-expert comparisons and D_combined >= chi^2(9, 0.05) = 16.919.

Targeted random-forest tuning for quantile estimation (Berkowitz et al.): QCL (quantile coverage loss) tuning minimizes the estimated bias of the marginal quantile coverage probability based on the out-of-bag sample, rather than default parameters or traditional tuning (MSPE for uncensored data, C-index for censored). QCL tuning produces quantile estimates with more accurate coverage probabilities and narrower valid prediction intervals, including with random survival forests on censored data. The marginal coverage probability of the tau-quantile estimate is tau_tilde = integral_X F_T(hat q_tau(x) | x) dF_X(x), where q_tau(x) = F_T^{-1}(tau|x) is the conditional quantile function.

QCL estimation detail: for fully observed responses, the marginal coverage probability is estimated by hat tau_tilde = (1/n) sum_{i=1}^{n} hat F_{i,T}(hat q_tau(x_i) | x_i), with per-observation CDF estimate hat F_{i,T}(hat q_tau(x_i)|x_i) = 1(t_i <= hat q_tau(x_i)) (the indicator that the observed time falls below the estimated quantile). QCL tuning then minimizes this coverage bias over forest tuning parameters, aligning tuning with the actual quantile-estimation goal.

USAD: unsupervised statistics-guided diffusion + multi-attention spatio-temporal interaction network for human activity recognition. Conditioning vector f = [mu (replicated L times), sigma (replicated L times), gamma (replicated L times), z_1..z_L]^T in R^{4L} with global stats mu=(1/L)sum x_{0,i}, sigma=sqrt((1/L)sum(x_{0,i}-mu)^2), gamma=(1/L)sum((x_{0,i}-mu)/sigma)^3 (skewness) and local z-scores z_i=(x_{0,i}-mu)/sigma. Forward DDPM process x_t = sqrt(bar alpha_t) x_0 + sqrt(1-bar alpha_t) epsilon with cosine schedule bar alpha_t = cos((pi/2)(t/T+s)/(1+s))/cos((pi/2)s/(1+s)), beta_t = clip(1 - bar alpha_t/bar alpha_{t-1}, 0, 0.999), offset s=0.008. Reverse denoising uses label-conditioned AdaGN: AdaGN(h,t,y) = gamma_y(t) . (h-mu_h)/sigma_h + beta_y(t) with MLP-generated gamma_y(t), beta_y(t). Multi-branch network uses parallel residual branches with 3x3, 5x5, 7x7 kernels plus temporal/spatial attention and cross-branch fusion. Accuracies: 98.84% WISDM, 93.81% PAMAP2, 80.92% OPPORTUNITY; deployed on embedded devices.

MLLM tennis video analysis study (Jiang Kan lab project): evaluates multimodal LLMs on classifying tennis actions and identifying sequences of actions in a rally, including training variations and combination with traditional models (pose/object detection). Sequence quality measured by Edit Score = (1 - (event additions, deletions or replacements needed)/(number of events in longer label)) * 100.
equation: \text{Edit Score}=(1-\frac{\text{Event additions, deletions or replacements needed}}{\text{Number of events in longer label}})*100

claim: Tennis doubles video analytics framework (final-year project): standardized annotation methodology for doubles (player positioning, shot types, court formations, outcomes) plus a custom annotation tool; GroundingDINO for player localization via phrase grounding and YOLO-Pose for pose estimation to cut manual labeling. CNN transfer-learning models outperformed pose-based approaches at predicting shot type, positioning, and formations. GCN layer used: H^{(l+1)} = sigma(D^{-1/2} A D^{-1/2} H^{(l)} W^{(l)}), where A is the adjacency matrix, D the degree matrix, H^{(l)} node features at layer l, W^{(l)} learnable parameters. Multi-person pose input restructured from X in R^{T x J x 3} to X_m in R^{T x 4J x 3} for all four players' joints across T frames.

Temporal Conformal Prediction (TCP): ML-based quantile forecaster with an online conformal calibration layer whose thresholds update via a modified Robbins-Monro scheme, adapting to volatility clustering and regime shifts in non-stationary time series without parametric assumptions. Benchmarked against GARCH, Historical Simulation, and static Quantile Regression across financial assets: static Quantile Regression is sharp but poorly calibrated, systematically over-covering the nominal 95% target; TCP actively achieves the correct coverage, handling the coverage-sharpness tradeoff, with confirmed adaptive response during the 2020 market crash and robustness to hyperparameters.

Mallows ranking model generalization (learning the distance metric): the L_alpha Mallows model defines P(pi) = exp(-beta d_alpha(pi, sigma))/Z with d_alpha(pi, sigma) := sum_i |pi(i) - sigma(i)|^alpha, where beta>0 controls dispersion around the central ranking sigma and Z is the partition function. The authors develop an FPTAS to sample epsilon-close (total variation) to the true distribution for any alpha >= 1, beta > 0, generalizing prior results that required vanishing dispersion (beta -> 0) even in L_1/L_2 cases; MLE jointly estimates the central ranking, dispersion parameter, and distance metric, with strong consistency results, validated on sports ranking datasets.

THYME (Temporal Hierarchical Cyclic Scene Graph) for video scene graph generation: hierarchical feature aggregation with cyclic temporal refinement models multi-scale spatial context and enforces temporal consistency across frames; combined with the new AeroEye-v1.0 aerial video dataset (five interactivity types), it outperforms state-of-the-art on ASPIRe and AeroEye-v1.0. Formulation: video scene graph G=(V,E) where each node S_i in V is an object tracked throughout the video with a unified feature and each edge (S_i,S_j) in E carries a predicate p in C_p describing the object relationship; per-frame features come from a DETR detector producing object query embeddings {q_i^{(t)} in R^{d_0}}, with features updated hierarchically by neighborhood aggregation.

Player-Team Heterogeneous Interaction Graph Transformer for soccer outcome prediction (KDD 2025, U. Sydney + Stats Perform): builds per-match player interaction graphs where each player node carries key-event counts X_V^i = [x^i_{v,1}, ..., x^i_{v,|V|}] = [c^i_{v,1}, ..., c^i_{v,|V|}] and each edge between players carries event-type counts X_E^i = [x^i_{e,k,1}, ..., x^i_{e,k,|E|}] = [c^i_{e,k,1}, ..., c^i_{e,k,|E|}], with node types Team Red/Blue via tau(v): V -> A and edge types via phi(e): E -> K; edge features are augmented as X^i_{E,aug} = [X^i_E, P_u - P_v + P_k] encoding directional relationships; outcome hat y^i = f_theta([H_{p^i_n} for n=1..46], H_{R^i}, H_{B^i}) predicts win/draw/lose from player histories and team embeddings.

Posture-based mental-state inference in cricket: a posture-based method discriminates aggressive vs defensive shot intent through motion analysis with over 75% F1 score and over 80% AUC-ROC. Shots labeled high-energy if runs scored on the ball >= 3 and low-energy if runs <= 1. Evaluation uses P(11,2) permutation runs (11 folders, one validation, one test, nine training per iteration). Claim: posture leaks strong signals for intent inference even with data-pipeline noise; data statistics used as weak supervision to overcome labeling limitations.

AthleticsPose: public dataset of authentic sports motions captured from 23 athletes performing athletics events on an athletic field (Nagoya University, 2025). A representative monocular 3D pose estimation model trained on AthleticsPose significantly outperforms a baseline trained on an imitated sports motion dataset, reducing MPJPE (mean per-joint position error) by approximately 75%. The dataset's speed and acceleration distributions are right-shifted relative to existing datasets, covering a wider and higher range of athletic motion speeds.

FST.ai (R3AL.ai): AI framework for sports officiating applied to Taekwondo real-time head-kick detection and scoring, using pose estimation, motion classification, and impact analysis on edge inference, reducing decision time from minutes to seconds. Formalization: pose estimation finds f*_pose: I_t -> P_t maximizing alignment with ground-truth body landmarks under per-joint confidence C_i; action recognition finds f_class: R^{n x 2K} -> {A_1..A_m} mapping a sequence of pose vectors {P_{t-n}..P_t} to an action class maximizing posterior P(A_j|{P}). Joint features: theta_i = angle(p_{i-1}, p_i, p_{i+1}) and v_i = |p_i^{(t)} - p_i^{(t-1)}|/Delta t. Impact rule: a point of interest counts as impact if deceleration a_i = (v_i^{(t-1)} - v_i^{(t)})/Delta t > a_threshold AND IoU(foot bbox, head bbox) > 0.3. Example measured kick: foot decelerates 4.1 m/s to 0.6 m/s over 0.033 s (a approx 106 m/s^2), torso angular velocity 105 deg/s, peak knee extension 172 deg.

InstructPix2Pix adapted for robot future-frame prediction (RoboTWin dataset): fine-tuned to predict the frame I_{t+100} (100 frames = 10 s) from a single current image I_t and a text instruction T, minimizing theta* = argmin_theta E_{(I_t,T,I_{t+Delta t})}[L(f_theta(I_t,T), I_{t+Delta t})] with composite loss L = lambda_1 L_diff + lambda_2 L_perc + lambda_3 L_adv where lambda_1=1.0 (latent diffusion reconstruction), lambda_2=0.1 (VGG perceptual), lambda_3=0.01 (adversarial from lightweight discriminator). Fine-tunes only cross-attention layers, partial self-attention, and the last encoder layers; progressive 64x64 -> 128x128 training. Achieves superior SSIM/PSNR vs state-of-the-art baselines on RoboTWin with single-image + text input instead of multi-frame sequences.

Isotonic Quantile Regression Averaging (iQRA) for probabilistic electricity price forecasting: builds on QRA by adding stochastic order constraints, improving accuracy, reliability and compute cost. On the German day-ahead electricity market it consistently beats state-of-the-art postprocessing methods in reliability and sharpness, producing well-calibrated prediction intervals across confidence levels with superior reliability to coverage-based conformal prediction; isotonic regularization also gives hyperparameter-free variable selection. Variance-stabilizing transform: Y_{d,h} = f((P_{d,h}-a)/b) with robust variant f(p) = sgn(p)*[(|p|+1)^lambda - 1]/lambda for lambda>0, log(|p|+1) for lambda=0, using lambda=0.5 for polynomial damping; forecasts inverted as hat P_{d,h} = b f^{-1}(hat Y_{d,h}) + a.

SV3.3B (Sports Vision, Inc.): sports video understanding model for action recognition aimed at amateur sports, achieving superior performance on basketball datasets vs larger closed-source models including GPT-4o variants while requiring significantly lower compute; produces analytically rich sports descriptions with 29.2% improvement over GPT-4o in ground-truth validation metrics, with gains in information density, action complexity, and measurement precision metrics.

ASIS (ancillarity-sufficiency interweaving strategy) gets its first rigorous theoretical justification for Bayesian hierarchical panel data models: when the product of the prior variance of unobserved heterogeneity and cross-sectional sample size N is sufficiently large, latent individual effects can be sampled almost independently of their global mean, which explains ASIS's rapid mixing in tall panel datasets. By interweaving sufficient augmentation (SA): y_it = alpha_i + epsilon_it, alpha_i ~ N(mu_alpha, sigma_alpha^2), with ancillary augmentation (AA): y_it = mu_alpha + tilde alpha_i + epsilon_it, tilde alpha_i ~ N(0, sigma_alpha^2), ASIS achieves the optimal geometric rate of convergence and renders the global-mean Markov chain asymptotically independent and identically distributed. Simple inequalities predict which of SA vs AA converges faster; Monte Carlo experiments confirm the ordering even for small panels (N=10). Applicable across finance, marketing, and sports.

ASIS precision parameters: lambda_alpha = sigma_epsilon^{-2} T + sigma_alpha^{-2}, lambda_{mu SA} = sigma_alpha^{-2} N + tau_alpha^{-2}, lambda_{mu AA} = sigma_epsilon^{-2} NT + tau_alpha^{-2}, where sigma_epsilon^2 is the idiosyncratic error variance, sigma_alpha^2 the individual-effect variance, N cross-sectional size, T time periods, and mu_alpha has prior N(varphi_alpha, tau_alpha^2). Covariates enter via x_it^T beta absorbed into y_it.

Event-camera domain adaptation for human pose estimation under motion blur (EvSharp2Blur): event-based augmentation generates motion-aware blurred images bridging the sharp/blurred domain gap without paired annotations; a student-teacher framework iteratively refines pseudo-labels with mutual uncertainty masking to drop incorrect labels. Network outputs a center heatmap H_C, offset map O, and keypoint heatmaps H_k, where offsets O = {p_c^i - p_1^i, p_c^i - p_2^i, ..., p_c^i - p_K^i} are displacements of person i's center p_c^i from keypoint locations p_k^i in R^2. Supervised loss L_g = L_H + lambda_g * L_O with MSE on heatmaps, smooth-L1 on offsets, lambda_g = 0.03. Outperforms conventional domain-adaptive pose methods on blurred targets without target annotations.

Generalized Bradley-Terry model with covariates: n-dimensional merit parameter beta and fixed-dimensional regression coefficient gamma for covariates. With n -> infinity and fixed comparisons per pair, the MLE (hat beta, hat gamma) is uniformly consistent; the asymptotic normal distribution of hat gamma is biased while hat beta's is unbiased, attributable to their different convergence rates - claimed as the first asymptotic theory for paired-comparison models with covariates in high dimension, extended to Erdos-Renyi comparison graphs with diverging covariates. Win probability: P(i beats j) = e^{beta_i - beta_j}/(1 + e^{beta_i - beta_j}); home-field model: logit of home i beating away j = (beta_i - beta_j) + gamma, with gamma > 0 indicating home advantage and evenly-matched home teams winning with probability exp(gamma)/(1+exp(gamma)).

Silent Impact (KAIST, UIST 2024): tracks tennis shots from the passive arm using only a smartwatch IMU, avoiding sensors on the racket or dominant arm. IMU data from 20 recreational tennis players trained neural networks that exclusively use passive-arm data to detect and classify six tennis shot types, achieving 88.2% classification accuracy and 86.0% detection F1 score, comparable to dominant-arm performance.

Skripnikov/Cemek/Gillman adjust soccer team offensive production for game context using minute-by-minute event data from 15 seasons across five major European leagues with count-response GAMs. Model: log(Shots) ~ s(Diff.S) + s(Diff.RC) + Home + s(Diff.WP) + s(GM|Half=1) + s(GM|Half=2) + s(Team) + s(season), where s() are smoothing splines for nonlinear effects of score differential, red-card differential, pre-match win probability differential, and game minute modeled separately per half; Home is a dummy. To project onto a tied-game common denominator, multiply shot counts by exp(-(hat eta_s - hat eta_0)) where hat eta_s - hat eta_0 is the linear-predictor difference between score differential s and 0; to adjust away performance to a hypothetical home game, multiply by exp(-hat gamma) with hat gamma the home dummy coefficient. Example motivating case: England's 1-2 loss to France in the 2022 World Cup quarterfinal - England's 16 shots and 5 corners were largely accumulated while France led and conceded initiative. Analysis used ~1,000,000 observations per league with Holm multiple-testing correction over 75 tests (5 leagues x 15 seasons).

Bayesian dynamic football goal models with period-specific commensurate priors: separate time-varying precisions for attacking and defensive abilities in each period, controlled by spike-and-slab hyperpriors, giving adaptive shrinkage that borrows strength when past and current performance align and adapts rapidly after transfer windows or coaching changes. Integrated into six standard goal-based models (including double Poisson and bivariate Poisson) and evaluated on the last five seasons of Bundesliga, Premier League, and La Liga; outperforms other discrete-time dynamic models. Implemented in the free open-source R package footBayes. Base structure: double Poisson X_{i,n}|lambda_{1,n} ~ Poisson(lambda_{1,n}), Y_{j,n}|lambda_{2,n} ~ Poisson(lambda_{2,n}) independent, with log(lambda_{1,n}) = beta_0 + home + beta^{att}_{h_n} + beta^{def}_{a_n} and log(lambda_{2,n}) = beta_0 + beta^{att}_{a_n} + beta^{def}_{h_n}, where beta_0 is a common intercept, 'home' the home-field advantage, and beta^{att}/beta^{def} attacking/defensive abilities.

DTVW (diversity-driven time-varying weights): Bayesian forecast combination embedding forward-looking signals as predictive priors into time-varying weight updating, so weights adapt on both historical forecast performance and anticipated future model behavior. Using model diversity as the forward-looking signal, DTVW embeds diversity-driven predictive priors that penalize redundancy and encourage informative contributions. Simulations (complete model set and complex misspecified environment) and applications to multi-step oil price forecasts and bivariate US inflation/GDP forecasts show superiority over Equal weighting, Bayesian Model Averaging, and standard TVW. Foundation: p(y_t | y_{1:t-1}) = integral_{Y^{K x t}} p(y_t | tilde y_{1:t}, y_{1:t-1}) p(tilde y_{1:t} | y_{1:t-1}) d tilde y_{1:t}, combining K predictors' predictive densities.
equation: p({\bf y}_{t}|{\bf y}_{1:t-1})=\int_{\mathcal{Y}^{K\times t}}p({\bf y}_{t}|\tilde{\bf y}_{1:t},{\bf y}_{1:t-1})p(\tilde{\bf y}_{1:t}|{\bf y}_{1:t-1})d\tilde{\bf y}_{1:t}

claim: Uncertainty-driven selective prediction survey/paper: core selective-prediction pipeline takes input x, model f produces prediction hat y with uncertainty estimate p(y|x), and a selection function returns hat y or rejects (bottom) based on uncertainty. Core uncertainty tools: Bayes posterior p(theta|D) = p(D|theta) p(theta) / p(D) with evidence p(D) = integral p(D|theta) p(theta) d theta; conformal prediction sets Gamma(x) with coverage Pr{Y in Gamma(X)} >= 1 - alpha; deep ensembles aggregated prediction hat y = (1/M) sum_m f_m(x) with uncertainty from empirical variance hat sigma^2(x) = (1/(M-1)) sum_m (f_m(x) - hat y)^2.

Limits of selective AI prediction - clinical user study (259 clinicians, Jabbour et al.): compared to no-AI baseline accuracy of 66% [95% CI: 56%-75%], clinician accuracy declined to 56% [46%-66%] when shown inaccurate AI predictions, but recovered to 64% [54%-73%] under selective prediction (AI abstains on unreliable cases). However, selective prediction shifts error patterns: when informed the AI abstains, clinicians underdiagnose (18% increase in missed diagnoses) and undertreat (35% increase in missed treatments) vs no-AI input. Selective mechanism computes reliability score u_{i,j} = a(x_i, hat y_{i,j}) in [0,1] deciding whether to show prediction hat y_{i,j} in [0,1] for sample x_i, label j. On the accurate subset, baseline clinician accuracy was 80% (75-85), rising to 85% [81-89] with AI and 86% [81-89] with selective prediction.

Symbolic Quantile Regression (SQR): extends symbolic regression to predict conditional quantiles Q_Y(tau | X=x) := inf{q in R : P(Y <= q | X=x) >= tau} for tau in (0,1) with interpretable closed-form expressions. In extensive evaluation SQR outperforms transparent baselines and performs comparably to strong black-box baselines without sacrificing transparency; used to explain distributional differences by comparing models at extreme vs central quantiles in an airline fuel-usage case study. Expression token complexity: +/-/x/feature/constant = 1, division/square = 2, sin/cos = 3, exp/log/sqrt = 4. Example recovered quantile family: tau=.01 -> y ~ x - 2.33 x^{2.5}, tau=.5 -> y ~ x, tau=.75 -> y ~ x + 0.67 x^{2.5}, tau=.99 -> y ~ x + 2.33 x^{2.5}.

ELASTIC (Event-Location-AgnoSTIC synchronizer): aligns soccer event and tracking data using only tracking-derived features (not annotated event locations, which carry spatial errors). Detects end times of pass-like events and separates major vs minor event detection to improve completeness and reduce error cascade. Ground truth: 2,134 annotated events from three Eredivisie matches; outperforms existing synchronizers by a large margin. Scoring uses f(x; x0, x1) = 0 if x<=x0, 1 if x>=x1, (x-x0)/(x1-x0) if x0<x<x1; event candidate score components: s1(t_k)=lambda_1*(1-f(d(t_k);0,3m)) (player-ball distance), s2(t_k)=lambda_2*f(a(t_k);0,20 m/s^2) (ball acceleration), s3/s4 from max player-ball distance before/after over 0-5m, s5 from time-since-anchor over 0-5s, with lambda_1..lambda_5 >= 0 summing to 100. Preprocessing in [0,105]x[0,68] IFAB coordinates.

TOTNet (Temporal Occlusion Tracking Network): robust ball tracking under occlusion using 3D convolutions, visibility-weighted loss, and occlusion augmentation; developed with Paralympics Australia. New TTA dataset: occlusion-rich table tennis from professional Paralympic matches, 9,159 samples with 1,996 occlusion cases. Evaluated across tennis, badminton, table tennis: reduces RMSE from 37.30 to 7.19 and improves accuracy on fully occluded frames from 0.63 to 0.80. Loss: L = w_v * (BCE(P_x, T_{x,map}) + BCE(P_y, T_{y,map})), where P_x in R^W, P_y in R^H are predicted 1D heatmaps, targets are Gaussian heatmaps T_{x,map}[j] = (1/Z_x) exp(-(j-T_x)^2/(2 sigma^2)) for visible/partially occluded levels 1-2, and w_v is the weight for visibility level v in {0,1,2,3} (0 out-of-frame, 1 visible, 2 partially visible, 3 fully occluded). Frames resized to 288x512.

OpenFPL (Daniel Groos, Groos Analytics): open-source Fantasy Premier League forecasting from public data only (FPL + Understat, seasons 2020-21 to 2023-24), using position-specific ensemble models optimized for RMSE with K-Best Search (population K=10). Tested prospectively on 2024-25: accuracy comparable to a leading commercial service; surpasses the commercial benchmark for high-return players (>2 points) that drive rank gains; holds across 1-, 2-, and 3-gameweek horizons. Category breakdown: commercial FPL Review has lowest RMSE/MAE on low-return categories (Zeros = non-playing, Blanks <= 2 points), while OpenFPL is most accurate on high-return categories (Tickers 3-4 points, Haulers >= 5 points). More than 11 million people play FPL. Code at github.com/daniegr/OpenFPL.

Figure-skating jump recognition (VIFSS): view-invariant pose representation via contrastive pre-training on FS-Jump3D (first public 3D pose dataset for figure-skating jumps), plus fine-grained annotation of 'entry (preparation)' and 'landing' phases for temporal action segmentation (TAS). Embedding z = [z_pose; z_view] split: pose loss L_pose = BarlowTwins(z_pose, z'_pose) (redundancy reduction, no negative samples); view loss L_view = MSE(cossim(z_view, z'_view), cossim(v_c, v'_c)) aligning embedding similarity with virtual-camera direction similarity; regularization L_R = VarianceLoss(z)+VarianceLoss(z')+KLUniformLoss(z)+KLUniformLoss(z') with VarianceLoss(z) = (1/d) sum_i (sigma_i^2(z) - sigma_target^2)^2. Achieves over 92% F1@50 on element-level TAS (jump type + rotation level); view-invariant pre-training especially helps with limited fine-tuning data.

BOLFI (Bayesian Optimization Likelihood-Free Inference) applied to influenza A virus dynamics ODE models: infers six parameters - virion entry rate beta, infection probability gamma, total RNA production rate P_RNA, infectious virion production rate P, eclipse phase duration tau_E, infectious phase duration tau_I - without any likelihood knowledge, with uncertainty measures; improvements include a Gaussian-process classifier for extreme values and discrepancy design combining data from different experiment processes (single-cycle with rinse at t=0h, MOI 3 inoculation at t=-1h; multiple-cycle from t=0h). RNA measurement noise log-normal: sigma_MCRNA=0.226 (multiple-cycle total virus), sigma_SCRNA=0.145 (single-cycle total virus).

TrajSV (Huawei): trajectory-based sports video representation with three components: data preprocessing (extracts player/ball trajectories from broadcast video), CRNet (trajectory-enhanced Transformer for clip representations), VRNet (encoder-decoder aggregating clip representations + visual features into video representations), optimized by a triple contrastive loss in an unsupervised manner (no supervision labels needed). Trajectories tokenized via segment matrices M: sports field partitioned into a grid, cells set to 1 if traversed by trajectories, 0 otherwise, mapped to tokens T; clip representation c = t (trajectory Transformer encoding) concatenated (oplus) with visual representation y.

Adaptive conformal prediction intervals over trajectory ensembles (Li/Menacho/Rodriguez): turns sampled trajectory ensembles (from probabilistic models or autoregressive predictors, e.g., hurricane forecasts, epidemic models, autonomous driving) into calibrated prediction intervals via conformal prediction with a novel online update step plus an optimization step capturing inter-step dependencies, producing discontinuous intervals around each trajectory with theoretical coverage guarantees and sharper adaptive uncertainty. Dual objective: (1) min |(1/T) sum_t 1(y_t^h not in C_t^h) - alpha| + (1/T) sum_t |C_t^h| for each horizon h in [1,H] (miscoverage converges to alpha while intervals stay tight); (2) min |(1/H) sum_h 1(y_t^h not in C_t^h) - alpha| for each t (marginal miscoverage across horizon).

Badminton doubles pose-based shot recognition: transfers singles-trained models (ViT-Pose keypoints on ShuttleSet, ST-GCN contrastive embeddings) to doubles analysis, with a custom multi-object tracking post-process that resolves ID switches from fast overlapping movements by predicting player positions during temporary disappearances and reassigning identities via velocity-based extrapolation; a Transformer classifier detects shot occurrences. Pose-based models show 2x better cross-format (singles-to-doubles) transferability than vision-only methods.

Personalized contest recommendation in daily fantasy sports (Dream11 production system): Wide and Deep Interaction Ranker (WiDIR) predicts ranking of contests a player will join given contest transaction history; contests vary in entry fee, number of spots, prize pool distribution. Training at player-match level: ordered contest list O_{it} = (c_{it}^{(1)}, ..., c_{it}^{(L_{it})}) of player i's most-to-least frequently joined contests in match t (fixed to 100 entries, padded with random non-joined contests); pairwise preference set Theta_{it} = {(c, c') in O_{it} x O_{it} | c succ c'}; hinge ranking loss l_{it}(c,c') = max{0, 1 - hat s_i(c) + hat s_i(c')}, where hat s_{ic} is WiDIR's affinity score. Data: ~1 billion train contest joins, ~100k players, ~1.5M total contests; behavior window k=3 for current behavior, k in (7,30) for historical preferences; train ~12 months, val ~2 months, test ~6 months. Online experiments show marked improvement in recall and business metrics over candidate models.

BasketLiDAR (Keio University + AISIN): first LiDAR-camera multimodal dataset for professional basketball multi-object tracking - three calibrated camera-LiDAR units with no blind spots, fully synchronized IDs across LiDAR point clouds, multi-view camera images, and per-player 3D bounding boxes. Specs: 10 FPS hardware-synced, cameras 4K 3840x2160 FOV 95x78 deg F2.6, LiDAR 0.18x0.23 deg angular resolution, 144 lines, 452,000 pts/s, FOV 125x25 deg, 150m range. Occlusion-Session-Extractor: N_t = |T_t| track-ID count at frame t; occlusion interval I_k=[t_s(k), t_e(k)] is the shortest contiguous segment with N_{t_s(k)-1} = N_{t_e(k)} =: N_ref and N_t < N_ref for t in [t_s(k), t_e(k)-1]; first difference Delta N_t = N_t - N_{t-1} (negative = lost IDs, positive = gained).

Dynamic graph-based tennis odds forecasting: forecasts bookmaker odds for any match on any surface to enable pre-tournament prediction, matching bookmaker and literature accuracy while beating rankings-based predictions (on 2024-2025 majors; model-vs-bookmaker forecast correlation approx 0.88, best-fit line y=0.88x+0.08). Bookmaker-implied probabilities normalized as p = d/||d||_1; Elo-style base with surface-dependent ratings: P(a beats b) = 1/(1+10^{(r_b - r_a)}) =: p_ab. Log-transformed odds x_ab := log((1-p_ab)/p_ab) = r_a - r_b satisfy additivity x_ab = x_ac + x_cb, enabling a directed weighted complete graph over players with edge weight w_ab(M) = rho^{t_M} tau_s for match M played t_M days ago on surface s (geometric temporal decay = Markovian ability assumption), aggregated edge E_ab = sum_M w_ab(M) x_ab(M)/W_ab with W_ab = sum_M w_ab(M). Set-win probability xi imputed for 5-set matches via P(Bin(N_s, xi) > N_s/2) = p_ab.

Systematic S&P 500 put-writing with position sizing (0-5 DTE SPXW options): compares Kelly criterion, VIX-based volatility-regime scaling, and a hybrid of both; ultra-short-dated far-OTM options deliver superior risk-adjusted returns; hybrid sizing balances return with drawdown control, especially in low-volatility regimes like 2024. Kelly derivations: expected log-growth G(f) = p ln(1+bf) + (1-p) ln(1-f) gives optimal fraction f* = (bp-(1-p))/b = (p(b+1)-1)/b; Rotando-Thorp generalization f* = p/a - (1-p)/b with a odds of negative outcome, b odds of positive outcome. Moneyness for strike selection: M_put = K e^{-r tau} - S. GBM discretization: log(S_{t+Delta t}/S_t) = (r - q - sigma^2/2) Delta t + sigma sqrt(Delta t) Z, Z~N(0,1); simulated path S_{t+n Delta t} = S_0 exp(sum_i ((r-q-sigma^2/2)Delta t + sigma sqrt(Delta t) Z_i)); per-path short-put return r_i = (P - V_T^{(i)})/P with premium P and terminal value V_T^{(i)}.

Robust growth-optimal portfolios via Kelly + European options under estimation risk: in a binomial model (X_t = u with prob p, d with prob 1-p; S_t = S_{t-1} X_t), adding a European option to the Kelly framework yields growth-optimal portfolios robust to estimation risk. Growth rate G_n = (1/n) log(W_n/W_0); closed-form optimal fraction f* = [p(R-u)R + (1-p)(R-d)R]/[(u-R)(d-R)] with R the risk-free gross return. Portfolio allocation: N_0^{(s)} = (W_0/S_0) f shares, N_0^{(b)} = (W_0/B_0)(1-f-g) bonds, N_0^{(o)} = (W_0/P_0) g options; one-period relative payoff W_1/W_0 = g[u S_0/P_0 - (S_0/P_0) R] + (1-g) R + c(u-R) if X_1=u and = g[K_0/P_0 - (S_0/P_0) R] + (1-g) R + c(d-R) if X_1=d, where c := f - (S_0/P_0) g and P_0 = (1/R)((u-R)/(u-d))(K_0 - d S_0).

UTAL-GNN: unsupervised temporal action localization with graph neural networks on skeleton data for untrimmed sports videos. On the DSV Diving dataset (2D coordinates of 16 body joints per clip, 5 action demarcations: start, m1, m2, m3, end), achieves 82.66% mean average precision (mAP) and 29.09 ms average localization latency, matching state-of-the-art supervised performance while maintaining computational efficiency.

Athlete competition networks (tennis, fencing): nodes are contestants, edges directed winner->loser; matches form a time-evolving hierarchy with top players at the apex. Elimination tournaments produce networks with smaller hierarchy level and thus increased probability of circular win-loss cycles vs round-robin networks. Position in hierarchy plus other network metrics predicts match outcomes comparably to official ranking points or Elo. Network built on sliding window of previous t_nb = 1 year of matches (matching official ranking periods). Generalized win-probability (Jerdee-Newman): Pr(i wins over j) = (1/2) alpha + (1-alpha)/(1+e^{beta(s_j - s_i)}), where alpha quantifies extreme-upset probability and beta the depth of competition; fitted per year per score for predicting next-year matches. Two-reach centrality 2RC(i) = (1/(N-1)) * #{reachable nodes from i in 2 steps}, N the weakly connected component size.

Tennis momentum framework (2023 Wimbledon men's singles): chi-squared independence tests on point-contingency tables give significant evidence of momentum; momentum metric built via the entropy weight method; CUSUM control chart detects change points in the momentum series with a relative-distance measure for momentum-shift intensity; prediction via Back Propagation neural network optimized by Particle Swarm Optimization (BP+PSO) beats Random Forest, SVM, and logistic regression at point-outcome prediction; SHAP identifies the four most critical features as unforced errors, winning shots, the momentum metric, and momentum shift intensity. Streak analysis: P(Extension|W_i) = n_{i1}/n_{i.} with example estimates P(Extension|W_1)=4/5=0.8 (5 streaks of single wins, 4 extended), P(Extension|W_2)=1/4=0.25, P(Extension|W_3)=0; under no momentum the point sequence is a first-order Markov chain.

Bayesian stacking via proper scoring rule optimization with a Gibbs posterior (Wadsworth/Niemi): extends forecast stacking into a Bayesian framework where optimal linear-pool weight solutions are influenced by a prior (regularization toward equal weighting) and weight uncertainty is quantified as a probability distribution. Linear pool requires weights w_c >= 0, sum_{c=1}^{C} w_c = 1. Simulations and the 2023-24 CDC FluSight competition (M-open setting where the true model is not among candidates) show the stacked Gibbs posterior often outperforms model averaging and equal-weighted ensembles.

Recht (Berkeley, 2026) gives a decision-theoretic justification of Meehl's Clinical versus Statistical Prediction thesis: statistical rules beat clinical judgment almost by definition once the problem is framed with a small set of outcomes, machine-readable data, and evaluation averaged over individuals - 'metrical determinism', where the evaluation rules implicitly determine the best procedure. The optimal prediction p*(x) = argmin_p q_x S(p,1) + (1-q_x) S(p,0) is a deterministic function of the data-conditional rate q_x under the uniform distribution on {(x_i,y_i)}. Also warns of shortcomings: expertise erosion, decision fatigue, usurpation of discretionary judgment.

Real-time vision-based badminton smash speed estimation on mobile devices (Huang): custom-trained YOLOv5 shuttlecock detector + Kalman filter trajectory tracking, with video-based kinematic speed estimation via spatiotemporal scaling, packaged as a mobile app. YOLOv5 achieved 93% precision, 87% recall, and 91% mAP@0.5 on shuttlecock identification - a cost-effective alternative to radar guns (which struggle to detect shuttlecocks consistently) and professional tracking systems confined to pro venues.

Match Chat (IBM): real-time agent-driven tennis fan assistant integrating generative AI with Generative Computing (GenComp) techniques to synthesize insights during live tennis singles matches; query pre-processing/optimization before GenAI components, GenComp-guided UX for coverage across domains. Reported answer accuracy 92.83% with 6.25 s average response time; over 96.08% of queries guided via interactive prompt design.

AdaSports-Traj (Xu/Fu, Northeastern): role- and domain-aware multi-agent trajectory modeling for sports with a Role- and Domain-Aware Adapter adjusting latent representations by agent identity and domain context, plus a Hierarchical Contrastive Learning objective separately supervising role-sensitive and domain-aware representations to encourage disentangled latents without optimization conflict. Tested on Basketball-U, Football-U, Soccer-U in unified and cross-domain settings. Formal: trajectory X in R^{N x T x D} (N agents, T steps, D=2 for positions), missing-data mask M in R^{N x T} with m_i^t=0 indicating missing; generative model maximizes theta* = argmax_theta sum_{x^{<=T} in Omega} sum_{t=1}^{T} log p_theta(x^t | x^{<t}), optimized via the sequential ELBO: E_{q_phi(z^{<=T}|x^{<=T})}[sum_{t=1}^T log p_theta(x^t | z^{<=t}, x^{<t}) - KL(q_phi(z^t|x^{<=t},z^{<t}) || p_theta(z^t|x^{<t},z^{<t}))].

BlurBall: table-tennis ball detection that explicitly models motion blur. New labeling convention places the ball at the CENTER of the blur streak (classical convention marks the leading edge, introducing asymmetry) and annotates blur attributes including a directional blur label. BlurBall jointly estimates ball position and motion blur attributes using Squeeze-and-Excitation attention over multi-frame inputs with a U-Net backbone and MIMO (multiple-input multiple-output) design; loss combines weighted Dice + binary cross-entropy (replacing focal loss) to handle extreme class imbalance. Consistently improves detection across models and achieves state-of-the-art ball detection; blur cues also enable more reliable trajectory prediction for real-time sports analytics and table-tennis robots.

Rethinking player evaluation (Bajons/Kook, WU Vienna): commonly used 'above-expectation' metrics like GAX (goals above expectation) are directly related to Rao's score test in parametric regression for the expected outcome; ML-based metrics suffer finite-sample bias and slow convergence rates, so they propose residualized (double-machine-learning style) metrics. Empirical GAX: hat GAX_i := sum_{j=1}^{N_i} (Y_{ij} - hat h(Z_{ij})), where Y_{ij} in {0,1} is whether shot j of player i was a goal, Z_{ij} shot circumstances, hat h(Z) the xG estimator of h(Z) := E[Y|Z]. The residualization adds a regression predicting whether the player would take the shot given the features; framework relates metrics to player-specific effects in interpretable semiparametric models to infer directional effects. Applied to soccer GAX, goalkeeper shot-stopping, basketball shooting skill, NFL QB passing skill, and soccer injury-proneness. Statistic form: sum_{j=1}^{N} (Y_j - hat h(Z_j)) X_j with X the player-participation indicator.

Uncertainty-aware knowledge tracing (Eedi): extends KT models with predictive uncertainty; larger predictive uncertainty aligns with incorrect model predictions, and uncertainty is pedagogically useful in low-resource education settings. Multi-class formulation: hat r_{t+1} = F_theta(q_{t+1}, c_{t+1}, {e_i}_{i=1}^t) predicting the categorical response to the next exercise from history H_t = {e_i} of (question id q_i, features c_i, response r_i). Uncertainty quantified via MC-Dropout entropy: H(p(r_{t+1}|q_{t+1}, H_t)) = -sum_k bar p_k log bar p_k with bar p_k = (1/M) sum_{m=1}^M p_k^{(m)}. Data: 11,994 training students (1,199,266 interactions), 1,493 validation students (149,278 interactions), avg 100 responses each.

Latent MMHC for volleyball psychological profiling: hybrid structure learner coupling a latent Gaussian copula (for mixed-type variables: ordinal questionnaire scores, categorical demographics, continuous indicators) with a constraint-based skeleton and constrained score-based refinement returning a single DAG; bootstrap-aggregated variant for stability. Simulations (varying sample size, sparsity, dimension): latent MMHC attains lower structural Hamming distance and higher edge recall than recent copula-based learners with high specificity. On 164 female volleyball players (Italy's C and D leagues), the learned network organizes mental skills around goal setting and self-confidence, with emotional arousal linking motivation and anxiety; Big-Five traits (notably neuroticism, extraversion) sit upstream of skill clusters; scenario analyses quantify how improving specific skills propagates to shift preparation, confidence, and self-esteem. DAG factorization: P(X) = product_{j=1}^{p} P(X_j | X_{pa(j)}), the local Markov property.

3DPCNet: pose canonicalization for view-invariant 3D kinematic analysis from monocular RGB. Pipeline: monocular RGB frame -> 2D keypoint detection + 3D lifting -> camera-centered 3D skeleton -> 3DPCNet predicts a global rotation mapping the skeleton into a fixed body-centered canonical frame, removing camera viewpoint distortion for comparable kinematics (wrist trajectories, joint angles). Hybrid encoder with parallel graph-convolutional and transformer branches fused by gated cross-attention; optional head predicts residual global rotation + joint-position correction. On MM-Fi (synthetically rotated poses): rotation error reduced by 3.4 degrees and MPJPE from 64 mm to 47 mm vs geometric baseline; TotalCapture qualitative evals show accurate acceleration signals from video.

Biomechanical-phase temporal segmentation for javelin throw videos (IIT Gandhinagar): unsupervised framework using structured optimal transport (SOT) to augment an attention-based spatio-temporal graph convolutional network, achieving contextually-aware segmentation into semantically rich phases without expert annotation - outperforming state-of-the-art unsupervised methods with 71.02% mAP and 74.61% F1 on test data. Motivation: conventional throwing-sport analysis needs manual annotation or lab instrumentation (high-speed cameras, motion capture), which are time-consuming, expensive, and fail to generalize across environments and athlete techniques; isolated phase segments enable visualization, cross-session alignment, and real-time feedback.

Aging decline in NBA career trend prediction (National Chengchi University): two-stage framework - stage 1 uses autoencoder + K-means (Silhouette score for optimal K) on complete careers (ages 22-32, at least 5 seasons) to classify NBA player career-trend types by peak period, decline rate, and overall trend; stage 2 uses LSTM to predict career trajectories. Target sequence Y = {y1, y2, y3} where y_i is BPM (box plus-minus); mapping R^{7x48} -> R^3 with reconstruction loss guiding encoder convergence.

Penalty-kick direction prediction (Ranasinghe): real-time multi-modal deep learning predicting left/middle/right BEFORE ball contact. Dual-branch: MobileNetV2 CNN on RGB frames for spatial features + LSTM with attention on 2D pose keypoints; pose keypoints guide visual focus to task-relevant regions; distance-based thresholding segments sequences immediately before ball contact for consistent inputs. Custom dataset of 755 penalty kicks from match videos with frame-level annotations. Achieved 89% accuracy on held-out test set, outperforming visual-only and pose-only baselines by 14-22%; prior work reported 79.05% mean accuracy one second before the kick.

V3 continuous space-time video super-resolution via 3D Video Fourier Field (VFF): encodes video as a continuous spatio-temporally coherent field instead of decoupled spatial/temporal components with explicit frame warping; enables cheap sampling at arbitrary space-time locations, captures fine spatial detail + smooth temporal dynamics, and supports an analytical Gaussian PSF for aliasing-free reconstruction at arbitrary scale. Fourier-like sinusoidal basis coefficients predicted by a neural encoder with large spatio-temporal receptive field conditioned on low-res input. Outperforms prior continuous space-time VSR by up to approx 2 dB PSNR (Adobe240 test set, x4 spatial, x8 temporal) with lower runtime and memory. Formulation: hat V(x,y,t): R^2 x [0,T] -> R^3 continuous video function; observed V^{lr} = D(hat V) with degradation D (discrete space-time sampling); recovering hat V = inverting D via the VFF prior, then sampling at finer grid to get V^{hr} in R^{rT x sH x sW x 3}.

Unified UQ framework for regression via proper scoring rules (CRPS, logarithmic, squared error, quadratic scores): derives closed-form uncertainty measures under practical parametric assumptions, estimable with model ensembles; measures naturally decompose into aleatoric and epistemic components; recovers popular regression UQ measures based on predictive variance and differential entropy. Scoring rule: S: P x Y -> [-inf, +inf]; expected score S(hat P, P) = integral S(hat P, y) dP(y); S is proper relative to P if S(P,P) <= S(hat P, P) for all hat P, P. Broad evaluation on synthetic and real-world regression datasets gives guidance for selecting reliable UQ measures.

ExposureEngine (Forzasys/SimulaMet/OsloMet/UiT): end-to-end oriented logo detection and sponsor visibility analytics for sports broadcasts; replaces axis-aligned Horizontal Bounding Boxes (HBB) - which mis-measure rotated/skewed logos from dynamic camera angles - with oriented detection. A commercial HBB logo solution achieves mAP@0.5 of 0.859; ExposureEngine derives visibility metrics (on-screen position, size, exposure duration) directly from predictions without manual correction, using 1,103 curated frames and Focal Loss (1-p_t)^gamma modulation ablated.

Cricket shot classification baseline study (CricShot10 dataset: 1,894 clips, 10 batting techniques - Cover Drive, Defensive Shot, Flick, Hook, Late Cut, Lofted, Pull, Square Cut, Straight Drive, Sweep - ~180-200 samples per class, 3.2 s avg, 1280x720, stratified split seed 27): standardized re-implementations of prior papers achieve far below their claimed accuracies - Balaji LRCN claimed 96% got 46.0%, IJERCSE claimed 99.2% got 55.6%, Sensors claimed 93% got 57.7%, exposing a gap between literature claims and practical results under standardized evaluation. Modern SOTA: EfficientNet-B0 + GRU temporal model achieves 92.25% accuracy, implemented in PyTorch Lightning.

Bayesian ranking of National Olympic Committees by long-run medals-to-population ratio with shrinkage: mitigates large-population influence and reduces stochastic fluctuation for smaller nations, yielding more stable interpretable national-sporting-performance rankings across games. Modeling: number of athletes M_{i,c} winning exactly i medals modeled as interrelated conditionally-independent Poisson processes linked by country-specific winning-probability effects; unique medal winners U_c = sum_i M_{i,c} follows Poisson, while total medals M_c = 1*M_{1,c}+2*M_{2,c}+... does not (multi-medal athletes break the Poisson limit assumption); in Paris 2024 the max individual medal count was 4 (M_{4,c} counts athletes with >=4 medals). For small countries, Bayesian estimates can diverge significantly from observed ratios due to single-cycle stochastic variation.

Systematic literature review (PRISMA protocol) of 204 journal articles (2002-2024) on AI and analytics in sports, with BERTopic topic modeling on abstracts (transformer embeddings + class-based TF-IDF). Predominant research areas: performance modelling, physical and mental health, social media sentiment analysis, and tactical tracking. Claim: first to introduce BERTopic for latent-structure extraction in sports research literature.

Context-aware conformal prediction for renewable energy forecasting (Moradi et al., Georgia Tech): calibration sets built with a novel context-aware weighting scheme; improves probabilistic forecast reliability at site and fleet levels on large US datasets vs baselines. Weighted alpha-quantile definition: Q^alpha({(z_i, p_i)}_{i=1}^{n}) = Q^alpha(sum_{i=1}^n p_i delta_{z_i}), where delta_x is the Dirac distribution at x and sum p_i = 1; unweighted case Q^alpha(z_1,...,z_n) = Q^alpha({(z_i, 1/n)}). Prediction intervals from trained quantile forecasts: hat C_t^alpha(x_t) = [hat q^{alpha/2}(x_t), hat q^{1-alpha/2}(x_t)].
This file is an extraction artifact (LaTeX macro dump with 'PER-FINAL' glossary repetitions and no readable abstract, body, or results); it contains no substantive extractable claims.

Penalty shootouts in UEFA club competitions (2000-2025, all shootouts) are statistically equivalent to a perfect lottery: no evidence for effects of kicking order, match venue (field), or psychological momentum; stronger teams (by Elo) do NOT perform better than weaker opponents, contradicting prior results. Logistic model P_h = 1/(1+e^{beta_0 + beta_1 Delta}) for home-team shootout win probability with Delta strength difference: Elo-difference model (266 obs) gives beta_0=-0.121 (se 0.123, p=0.326), beta_1=-0.004 (se 0.069, p=0.959); Elo-win-probability model (Delta^{(2)}=1/(1+10^{-(E_i-E_j)/400})) gives beta_0=-0.027 (se 0.307, p=0.930), beta_1=-0.194 (se 0.582, p=0.739) - all coefficients insignificant and negative, robust across estimation windows. Finding holds after UEFA scrapped the away-goals rule in 2021/22.

Uncertainty-aware post-hoc calibration (Mitton et al.): proximity-based conformal prediction stratifies calibration samples by semantic feature-space similarity into putatively correct vs putatively incorrect groups; dual calibration - standard isotonic regression on putatively correct predictions, underconfidence-regularized isotonic regression pulling putatively incorrect confidences toward uniform for identifiability. Isotonic regression: min_f sum_i (y_i - f(p_i))^2 subject to p_i <= p_j => f(p_i) <= f(p_j). On CIFAR-10/100 (BiT, CoAtNet) achieves fewer confidently-incorrect predictions with competitive ECE. Calibration metrics: ECE = (1/N) sum_m |b_m| |acc(b_m) - conf(b_m)| with acc(b_m)=(1/|b_m|) sum 1(hat y_i=y_i), conf(b_m)=(1/|b_m|) sum p_i; MCE = max_m |acc(b_m)-conf(b_m)|. Entropy-based predictive uncertainty PE(x) = -sum_c mu_pred(x,c) log mu_pred(x,c); with log base 2 and entropy threshold tau=0.1, the dominant class needs approx 0.93 probability.

FST.ai 2.0 (explainable AI ecosystem for Olympic/Paralympic Taekwondo officiating): covers head-kick detection, IVR decision support, referee training and big-data analytics with XAI governance/fairness dimensions. Real-time pipeline latency budget: T_latency = T_capture + T_pose + T_classify + T_overlay < 300 ms for live decision workflows. Pilot at 2025 World Cadet Championships reduced Instant Video Replay delays and improved referee consistency; post-event survey of N=27 referees gave mean trust rating Tr = 4.65/5 (93%). Dashboard metrics: scoring latency, head-kick detection accuracy, referee response time, decision consistency across matches.

Signature kernel scoring rule for weather forecasting (rough path theory): reframes weather variables as continuous paths X:[a,b]->R^d and encodes temporal/spatial dependencies through iterated integrals; validated as strictly proper via path augmentations guaranteeing uniqueness. WeatherBench 2 scorecards show high discriminative power and unique capture of path-dependent interactions. Adversarial-free probabilistic training: sliding-window generative networks trained with a predictive-sequential signature-kernel scoring rule on ERA5 reanalysis data; a lightweight model beats climatology for forecast paths up to 15 timesteps. Proper-scoring-rule definitions: E_{Y~Q}[S(Q,Y)] <= E_{Y~Q}[S(P,Y)] for proper S (minimized), strict iff P=Q; empirical score hat S_N(P) = (1/N) sum_{i=1}^N S(P, y_i) converges a.s. to E_{Y~Q}[S(P,Y)].

Policy learning with abstention: policies pi: X -> {0, 1, *} that abstain (defer to safe default/expert) on some units receive a small additive reward on top of random-guess value. Two-stage learner: first identifies near-optimal policies, then builds an abstention class from policy disagreements. Fast O(1/n)-type high-probability regret under abstaining regret with known propensities; O(1/sqrt(n)) worst-case standard regret matching Athey-Wager 2021; extends to unknown propensities via doubly robust objective. Framework also yields improved guarantees under margin conditions without realizability, a hedge for distributionally robust policy learning against small data shifts, and safe policy improvement over a baseline. Setup: Z=(X,D,Y) observational data, D in {0,1}, potential outcomes (Y(1),Y(0)), expected-outcome mapping g_o(d,x) = E[Y(d)|X=x], CATE tau_o(x) = g_o(1,x)-g_o(0,x), propensity p_o(x) = P(D=1|X=x) with unconfoundedness (Y(1),Y(0)) perp D | X and strict overlap p_o(x) in [kappa, 1-kappa].

Intransitive tennis dominance modeling with temporal directed GNNs (players as nodes, historical match outcomes as directed edges): models intransitive A-beats-B, B-beats-C, C-beats-A cycles explicitly. Edge weights use game-win proportion g_k(u,v) in [0,1] with learnable time decay phi_k(u,v) = exp(-lambda (tau_n - tau_k)), where tau_n is the earliest scheduled match timestamp in the predicted tournament round and tau_k the historical match timestamp; matches also scaled by surface-similarity alpha_{s,t_k} (alpha_{s,s}=1 same surface) and tournament-prestige beta_k coefficients. Node features X^V_i in R^{|V| x d} from static player attributes + dynamic graph metrics, l2-normalized. Reports the bookmaker Pinnacle struggles on high-intransitivity-complexity matches; model achieves 65.7% accuracy with 0.215 Brier score on higher-intransitivity matchups, indicating a market inefficiency in handling intransitive matchups.

Conditional forecasts for performative predictions (Boeken/Zoeter/Mooij, U. Amsterdam/Booking.com): performative forecasts influence the outcomes they predict, undermining correct forecasts and standard elicitation. Conditioning forecasts on covariates separating them from the outcome renders the target distribution forecast-invariant, guaranteeing well-posedness; but classical proper scoring rules still fail to elicit correct forecasts - proven as a general impossibility result. Two solutions: (i) in decision-theoretic settings, correct incentive-compatible elicitation is possible if forecasts are separating; (ii) scoring with unbiased estimates of the divergence between forecast and induced target distribution yields correct forecasts. Applied to parameter estimation, conditional forecasts + proper scoring rules enable performatively stable estimation of performatively correct parameters (Perdomo et al. 2020). A forecast F is correct for causal model M if F = P_M(Y | do(F)); self-defeating prophecies (e.g., P_M(Y|do(F))=P_0 if F=P_1 else P_1) have no correct forecasts.

Search diversification as risk minimization (WSDM 2026, Waseda/CMU): shows theoretically and empirically that many well-known diversification algorithms are no more robust than naive non-diversified ranking for minority intents, because existing metrics only model average relevance across intents. Introduces VRisk answering 'how bad is the ranking for the worst beta-fraction of intents'. Framework: query q with intent set C(q)={c_1..c_m}, intent probability Pr(c|q) with sum_c Pr(c|q)=1 (mutually exclusive), per-intent relevance rel(d|q,c) in [0, rel_max], raw relevance rel(d|q) = E_{c~Pr(c|q)}[rel(d|q,c)] = sum_c Pr(c|q) rel(d|q,c); standard top-k metric V_std(R_k|q) = (1/k) sum_{d in R_k} rel(d|q).

Theoretical comparison of weight constraints in forecast combination/model averaging (Zou/Vasnev/Wang/Zhang): combined forecast hat y_t = f_t^T w. Five weight spaces: W^A = {w | w in R^S} (no constraints, arbitrarily large weights); W^B = {w | w^T 1 = 1} (sum-to-unity, search on R^{S-1} hyperplane); W^C = {w | w in [0,1]^S} (non-negativity, weights like probabilities, assumes each candidate contributes positively); W^D = {w | w in [0,1]^S and 1^T w = 1} (both); W^E = {w | w^T w = 1} (norm constraint, allows searching all of R^S per Hsiao and Wan 2014). Study gives practical guidance on choosing constraints from prior information and targets.

Line-break prediction in football (2023 J1 League): XGBoost classifier on 189 features (player positions, velocities, spatial configurations incl. Voronoi regions V(p) = {x in X | forall q in P [d(x,p) <= d(x,q)]}) predicts the probability of attacking teams breaking the defensive line; achieved AUC 0.982 and Brier score 0.015. SHAP analysis: offensive player speed, gaps in the defensive line, and offensive players' spatial distributions are the key contributors.
