Moderate positive correlation between predicted probability of being line-broken and team-level shots/crosses conceded - line breaks are quantitatively linked to scoring-opportunity creation. XGBoost update form: hat y_i = 0.5 (initial) + sum_{k=1}^{K} mu f_k(x_i) with learning rate mu and K boosting iterations.

Hidden scoring dynamics in hockey (Griffiths/Moskow, Syracuse): five-stage pipeline on 541,000 Sportlogiq NHL event records - (1) interpretable momentum weighting of micro-events via logistic regression; (2) nonlinear xG via gradient-boosted decision trees; (3) temporal sequence modeling with LSTM; (4) spatial formation discovery via PCA + K-means on standardized player coordinates; (5) X-Learner causal estimator quantifying the ATE of adopting identified optimal event sequences and formations. ATE of 0.12 (95% CI 0.05-0.17, p < 1e-50), a 15% relative gain in scoring potential - evidence that structured sequences and compact formations causally elevate offensive performance beyond descriptive correlation.

Assessing win strength in MLB win prediction models (Allen/Savala, St. Edward's): common machine learning models show a predictable relationship between predicted win probability and win strength as measured by score differential - the Pythagorean expectation runs-scored^2/(runs-scored^2+runs-allowed^2) is the classical closed-form version of this strength link. Benchmark accuracies on 2005-2014 seasons: ~56% via SVM and two gradient-boosting models, peak 58.92% with an SVM variant, 55.52% with gradient boosting. Logistic regression formulation: beta_0 + beta_1 x_1 + ... + beta_n x_n is the least-squares regression line for ln(p/(1-p)) with p the binary-outcome probability.

Bradley-Terry Stochastic Block Model (Santi/Friel, UCD): embeds the Bradley-Terry model in a stochastic block model so items cluster into tiers sharing tied ranks; fully Bayesian with the number of blocks K, block strengths, and item assignments jointly learned via a fast Gibbs sampler using Thurstonian data augmentation (no reversible-jump or split-merge moves), per-iteration cost O(|E| + nK). BT core: p(i beats j | lambda) = lambda_i/(lambda_i + lambda_j), lambda_i > 0; players in the same block share the same lambda (rank-indifference within clusters). On ATP men's tennis 2000-2022: the top 100 players partition into 3-4 tiers in most seasons; the strongest tier was small from the mid-2000s to 2018 and has grown since - evidence men's tennis has become more competitive recently.

Hawk-Eye-style automated tennis pipeline: YOLOv8 for player detection, custom-trained YOLOv5 for tennis ball tracking, ResNet50-based court keypoint detection, delivering real-time player/ball tracking plus analytics (movement patterns, ball speed, shot accuracy, player reaction times) with annotated video output for coaches and broadcasters. Robust across court conditions; ball-detection datasets suffered annotation inconsistency (imprecise bounding boxes in some frames).

ATSCM (Augmented Time Series Causal Models) for energy markets: extends counterfactual reasoning to multivariate temporal data with learned time-varying causal structure, modeling interpretable factors (weather, generation mix, demand patterns), rich grid dynamics, and observable market variables via neural causal discovery (no ground-truth DAGs). A causal regime change occurs when G_t != G_{t-1} or M(t) != M(t-1) (graph or mechanisms change). Three-level generative hierarchy M^t = <U^t, {W^t, I^t, V^t}, F^t, P(U^t), G^t>: W^t interpretable energy factors; I^t grid dynamics (cross-border flows, merit order, storage); V^t observable market variables; temporal evolution W^t = f_W(W^{t-1}, I^{t-1}, U_W^t, G^t), I^t = f_I(W^t, I^{t-1}, U_I^t, G^t), V^t = f_V(I^t, U_V^t); clear causal pathway Weather -> Renewable Generation -> Net Load -> Price. Enables counterfactuals like 'prices under different renewable scenarios'.

MVU-Eval: first comprehensive benchmark for multi-video understanding in MLLMs - 1,824 curated QA pairs across 4,959 videos spanning diverse domains, assessing eight core competencies (fundamental perception + high-order reasoning) for applications like cross-angle sports analytics and multi-sensor synthesis in autonomous driving. Data via automated MLLM generation with reject sampling + template-based generation, human verification, and distractor options regenerated until no-video accuracy approaches chance. Evaluation of SOTA models: significant discrepancies and limitations revealed; top closed-source Gemini 2.5 Pro only achieves 56.6% accuracy; Qwen2.5VL and InternVL series improve significantly with scale.

Skill-adjusted NHL expected-goals (LightGBM) model using NHL spatiotemporal data: isolates shooter and goaltender skill aspects - overall skill, locational skill (Shuckers-Curro shot binning), situational skill (Gower distance). Talent definitions: Shooter Talent = Cumulative Weighted Goals Scored / Cumulative Weighted xG; Goalie Talent = Cumulative Weighted xG Against / Cumulative Weighted Goals Against. Skill-adjusted model beats baseline on log loss, Brier, and ROC AUC by up to 5%, outperforming prior works that adjusted only for player skill (Sprigings-Toumi saw no log-loss/AUC gain; Shomer only modest AUC gain). Baseline vs skill-adjusted: top-percentile (p>0.75) log loss 0.2982->0.2844, AUC 0.7238->0.7616, Brier 0.0849->0.0816; mid (0.5<p<=0.75): 0.2831->0.2792, 0.7424->0.7519, 0.0809->0.0798; bottom (p<=0.5): 0.2126->0.2100, 0.7531->0.7630, 0.0567->0.0560.
equation: \text{Shooter Talent}=\frac{\text{Cumulative Weighted Goals Scored}}{\text{Cumulative Weighted xG}}

claim: Expected Threat (xT) model flexibility-vs-accuracy tradeoff (Delft/Ajax): finer grids give more flexibility but deteriorate estimate accuracy. xT recursion: xT(s) = P(shot|s)*xG(s) + sum_{s'} T_{s->s'} * xT(s'), where T_{s->s'} is the state-transition probability and P(shot|s)*xG(s) the immediate scoring term; action quality Delta xT(s_before, s_after) = xT(s_after) - xT(s_before). Model error defined as ||xT - hat xT||_inf (maximal difference between true and estimated xT). With g_s = P(shot|s)*xG(s) and transition matrix T with ||T||_inf < 1, a theoretical upper bound holds with probability >= 1-alpha: ||hat xT - xT||_inf <= 1/(1-||T||_inf) * (sqrt(M log(2 M^2/alpha)/(2N)) + sqrt(log(2M/alpha)/(2N))) <= 2/(1-||T||_inf) * sqrt(M log(2 M^2/alpha)/(2N)), where M is the number of grid cells and N samples. Simulations on the Markov chain give a sharper practical characterization; converted into a practitioner rule of thumb for grid choice.

DreamPose3D: diffusion-based 3D human pose estimation combining action-aware reasoning with temporal imagination. Conditions the denoising process on task-relevant action prompts extracted from 2D pose sequences (capturing high-level intent); representation encoder injects kinematic joint affinity into the attention mechanism for joint relationships; hallucinative pose decoder predicts temporally coherent 3D pose sequences during training (simulating mental motion reconstruction). SOTA on Human3.6M and MPI-INF-3DHP across all metrics; robust on a broadcast baseball dataset despite ambiguous/noisy 2D inputs.

Group Activity Recognition benchmark (video vs tracking): first standardized benchmark aligning broadcast video and agent tracking for the same group activities (87,939 group activity instances across 10 football action classes, pairing video with agent positions at event level). The tracking-based baseline (structured agent positions/trajectories) achieves 77.8% balanced accuracy and 57.0% macro F1 vs 60.9% balanced accuracy and 50.1% macro F1 for the strongest video model - while training with 7x less GPU hours and 479x fewer parameters (180K vs video model). Claim: compact agent-centric tracking representations encode spatial interactions explicitly and outperform pixel video for GAR at far lower cost.

UMEG-Net (Unified Multi-Entity Graph Network) for few-shot Precise Event Spotting (PES) in sports videos: integrates human skeletons and sport-specific object keypoints (ball, court corners) into a unified graph, with an efficient spatio-temporal extraction module based on advanced GCN + multi-scale temporal shift; multimodal distillation transfers knowledge from keypoint-based graphs to visual representations (UMEG-Net distill RGB student). Achieves robust few-shot PES performance with limited labeled data, outperforming baselines - a scalable solution for fine-grained exact-moment event recognition (e.g., ball-contacts-racket) despite rapid succession, motion blur, and subtle visual differences.

Amateur darts outcome prediction (Roanoke College dataset, students/faculty/staff): five models evaluated by Brier score and by head-to-head betting-game comparison, both at game start and at each round start - (1) null model from live scores only, (2) logistic regression, (3) basic simulation, (4) time-adjusted simulation, (5) score-dependent Massey variant. The score-dependent Massey model performs best on both evaluation methods, and the framework adapts to other competitive settings. Brier score: B(pi) = (1/n) sum_{t=1}^n (pi_t - sigma_t)^2 with pi_t predicted probability and sigma_t in {0,1} actual outcome. Head-to-head comparison: player A sets odds alpha_t, player B bets for/against when beta_t differs; expected value of B's bet = |alpha_t - beta_t|(p_t - alpha_t), positive iff the true probability p_t exceeds A's estimate alpha_t.

FOOTPASS (Footovision/Mines Paris): first benchmark for play-by-play action spotting over entire soccer matches in a multi-modal, multi-agent tactical context - enabling player-centric action spotting that fuses computer-vision outputs (tracking, identification) with tactical prior knowledge (soccer's tactical regularities over long horizons) to generate reliable play-by-play data streams ('who does what, when, where'). Motivation: current STAD methods jointly detect actions and actors but can't reach the exhaustive coverage soccer analytics needs (high recall => false positives requiring human filtering); tactical models like TacticAI plus trajectory forecasting motivate using tactical priors over raw video. Their DST approach produces coherent tactically-plausible action sequences with significant precision/recall improvements in high-recall regimes vs purely visual baselines, efficient on a single GPU.

RacketVision: unified multi-racket-sports benchmark (badminton, tennis, table tennis) for ball + racket analysis - 1,672 video clips (435,179 frames, 12,755 s) sourced from 942 pro broadcasts; first dataset with large-scale fine-grained racket POSE annotations alongside ball positions. Three tasks: fine-grained ball tracking, articulated racket pose estimation, predictive ball trajectory forecasting. Key insight for multi-modal fusion: naively concatenating racket pose features degrades performance; a Cross-Attention mechanism is essential to unlock their value, beating strong unimodal baselines on trajectory prediction. Table tennis 780 clips/170,027 frames, tennis 431/150,399, badminton 461/114,753; median frame per clip provided for background-aware baselines.

Genetic algorithm for fantasy football trade optimization with playoff biasing (JAIR, Parshall/Ali/Zimmerman): trades exchange subsets P_a subset T_a, P_b subset T_b with |P_a|,|P_b| <= m (default m=3); post-trade rosters T_a' = (T_a \ P_a) U P_b, T_b' = (T_b \ P_b) U P_a. Season projection S(R) = sum_{w=w_c}^{17} L(R,w), optimal weekly lineup over 1 QB, 2 RB, 2 WR, 1 TE, 1 FLEX, 1 K, 1 D/ST. Playoff-weighted gain for team A: g_a^w = sum_{w in W_p} alpha_p l_{a,w} + sum_{w not in W_p} alpha_n l_{a,w} with playoff weight alpha_p default 1.2 (1.5 in high-bias config) and alpha_n = (n_p + n_n - alpha_p n_p)/n_n. Cost function minimized: c = -(alpha g_a^w + beta g_b - gamma |g_a^w - g_b|) subject to g_a>0, g_b>0, trade size limits, where alpha,beta,gamma weight user gain, partner gain, fairness (default 1.0, 1.0, 0.25). Five configurations tested for robustness.

Triathlon overuse-injury prediction via synthetic data generation: framework generates physiologically plausible athlete profiles, individualized periodized training programs, and daily-life factors (sleep quality, stress, recovery). LASSO/Random Forest/XGBoost models reach AUC up to 0.86; sleep disturbances, heart rate variability, and stress identified as critical early injury-risk indicators. Lactate-threshold-HR estimator: LTHR_est = max(160, min(190, HR_max * P_base * M_final * (1+eps))), P_base=0.87, M_final = M_age*M_training*M_VO2max*M_HRR*M_gender. Synthetic distributions: HRV ~ near-normal mean 92.3 ms sd 10.2 ms; RHR right-skewed (gamma1=0.24) mean ~49-50 bpm with 92.5% below 60 bpm bradycardia threshold. Correlations: deep-sleep duration r~=-0.19 strongest protective factor, then REM sleep, HRV, sleep quality; interaction terms Sleep x HRV, Stress x Load; load markers RHR r~=0.06, perceived stress r~=0.04 weaker but directionally consistent.

Baseball matchup models and in-game strategy (thesis): four progressively complex hierarchical Bayesian models predict plate-appearance outcomes from pitcher/batter info, handedness, and recency, plus base-running probabilities calibrated to stealing tendencies; models embedded in a game-theoretic framework approximating subgame-perfect Nash equilibria for bullpen/pinch-hit/intentional-walk decisions. 2024 MLB postseason simulations: better matchup models yield tangible win-probability gains of up to ~1 extra win per 162-game season; playoff-game predictions align with market expectations. Pitcher handedness adjustment: a_i(n,h) = hat a_i(n)^{o_i(n)} if h=0 (opposite-handed) and = hat a_i(n)^{1/o_i(n)} if h=1 (same-handed), with gamma-prior handedness offsets o_i(n) and beta-prior base probabilities hat a_i(n). Log5-style combination: S_i(n,m,h) = P_i ln(a_i(n,h)/(1-a_i(n,h))) + B_i ln(b_i(m,h)/(1-b_i(m,h))) - (P_i+B_i-1) ln(c_i(h)/(1-c_i(h))), weights P_i,B_i ~ Uniform(0.25,1.75) with 1 <= P_i+B_i <= 2; calibrated x_i(n,m,h) = 1/(1+e^{-S_i(n,m,h)}); outcome X(n,m,h) ~ Categorical over 9 plate-appearance outcomes. Stolen-base rate posterior predictive: (alpha+x)/(alpha+beta+n) with beta prior fit on players with >=200 opportunities; GMP = e^{-log loss}.

CausalTraj (multi-agent trajectory forecasting in team sports): critiques per-agent metrics (minADE, minFDE) that score each agent independently on best-of-k trajectories, arguing they allow good per-agent scores while producing incoherent multi-agent futures; instead emphasizes joint metrics (minJADE, minJFDE) measuring joint accuracy across agents within the best generated scenario sample, since each agent's motion depends on the collective configuration of all others. Calls for realistic simulation and strategic gameplay understanding via coherent, interpretable multi-agent scenario generation.

Real-time soccer action forecasting transformer: axial transformer (novel design shown equivalent to a regular sequential transformer) jointly and recurrently predicts expected totals for 13 individual player actions (passes, shots, tackles, fouls, etc.) at multiple timesteps for each player, each team, and the game level - up to 505 predictions per timestep, ~150 prediction times per match, ~75,000 live predictions per game at low latency. Rather than the intractable joint distribution P(Y) over targets Y={Y_{a,p,t}}, trains marginal distributions P(Y_{a,p,t}) = sum_{Y\Y_{a,p,t}} P(Y); the joint space is at least 2^{|A|x|P|x|T|}. Predictions update with game state (goals, red cards shown in live Fulham vs Aston Villa 19 Oct 2024 example).

SkillSight: power-efficient skill assessment from egocentric smart-glasses data; central hypothesis: skill level is evident both in how a person performs (video) and in how they direct attention (gaze). Two-stage: teacher F_v(V,G)->S jointly models egocentric video V and gaze G to predict skill S; student F_g(G)->S distilled to gaze-only, eliminating continuous video processing. Gaze features g_i^t include 3D fixation points, 3D gaze direction relative to eye center, 2D gaze projection g_{2d} on the egoview, gaze depth, glasses translation + quaternion rotation. Gaze-guided attention: A_g^t[m,n] = exp(-d_c^t(m,n)/(2 sigma^2)) / sum exp(...) with Gaussian kernel centered at patch c^t = floor(g_{2d}^t/L); modified attention A_m^t = sigma(A_v^t + lambda_c A_g^t) (softmax, learnable per-scenario lambda_c, e.g., basketball, soccer). Datasets spanning cooking, music, sports: teacher SOTA; gaze-only student maintains high accuracy using 14x-73x less power than competitors.

Skating System Single (SkS) formalized in computational social choice: satisfies nondictatorship, majority criterion, positive responsiveness, monotonicity, citizens' sovereignty; violates Condorcet criterion, strong monotonicity, independence of clones, consistency, participation, resoluteness, strategy-proofness. Constructive coalitional weighted manipulation is NP-complete; destructive manipulation polynomial. Electoral control: constructive/destructive control by deleting candidates and constructive control by adding voters are NP-complete; destructive control by adding voters is polynomial. Bucklin-style scoring: score^i(c) = sum_{v in V} 1(pos_v(c) <= i) counts top-i placements; sum_pos^i(c) = sum pos_v(c)*1(pos_v(c) <= i).

Hierarchical Bayesian xG with player-specific effects + Football Manager expert priors (9,970 StatsBomb 2015-16 shots, FM 2017 z-score-standardized ratings): baseline y_ij ~ Bernoulli(p_ij), p_ij = sigma(eta_ij), eta_ij = alpha + beta^T x_ij (17 engineered features); hierarchical eta_ij = alpha + (beta + gamma_i)^T x_ij with player deviation gamma_i in R^{17}, prior gamma_i ~ N(mu_i, Sigma), Sigma = diag(sigma_1^2..sigma_17^2), mu_i FM-informed. Partial pooling: gamma_i* ~= (tau_i^2/(tau_i^2+sigma^2)) hat gamma_i^{MLE} + (sigma^2/(tau_i^2+sigma^2)) mu_i - shot-rich players data-driven, sparse-history players shrink to FM priors; substantially reduces posterior uncertainty vs weakly informative priors. External validity: hierarchical vs baseline R^2 ~= 0.75; XGBoost benchmark R^2 = 0.833 vs StatsBomb proprietary xG. Skill profiles: one-on-one finishing (Aguero, Suarez, Belotti, Immobile, Martial), distance shooting (Pogba), first-touch (Insigne, Salah, Gameiro); detected latent ability in Immobile/Belotti before their later-season improvement. Counterfactuals: Sansone +2.2 xG from Berardi's opportunities (+1.1 xG from pressure situations), reflected in his €13M Villarreal transfer; Vardy-Giroud swap asymmetry: Leicester -7 xG if Giroud replaced Vardy, Arsenal only -1 xG swapping Giroud for Vardy - tactical fit dominates.

xG+ (possession-level expected goals): remedies standard xG's conditioning-on-shots limitation by jointly modeling shot-taking and shot quality. Per frame t: xG+_t = P_t(Shot) * P_t(Goal|Shot) = xS_t * xG_t; possession aggregation xG+_poss = 1 - prod_{t=1}^{n}(1 - xG+_t) (bounded by 1, captures latent + realized threats); alternatives: max xG+ per possession, at-least-one per possession. Team strength: lme4 metric ~ (1|season) + (1|season:team) + (1|season:opp) + home giving season-specific team attack, opponent defense, season variation, home advantage; second-stage Poisson goals ~ home + season + team_off + opp_def. Over 114 matchdays, xG+ aggregation beats sum-of-xG on 69 (0.605) for at-least-one and 70 (0.614) for max-per-possession (null: Binomial(114, 0.5) wins). Persistence: goals-over-xG correlation ~0.12 (very low), shots-over-xS correlation ~0.63 (highly persistent), xG+ in between - xG+ gives a more persistent player skill signal than standard xG.

Rugby union penalty decision EP framework (2018/19 Premiership: 35,199 phases, 132 matches): expected points of (i) kicking for goal vs (ii) kicking to touch then pursuing a try, as functions of field location (x meters from opposition try line, y lateral distance from pitch center) and game context. Penalty-kick success from an angle-distance model fit on international records; lineout possession EP from phase-level data. Decision quantity: Delta EP(x, y; d_touch) = EP_lineout(x_LO) - EP_kick(x, y), where EP_kick(x,y) includes in-game consequences of made AND missed kicks, and EP_lineout(x_LO) is expected points of the next scoring event from the ensuing lineout at sideline location x_LO. Decision maps (zero-difference contours) show where each option maximizes expected return; the frontier shifts with game context, kicker accuracy, and expected touch gain. First comprehensive EP-based rugby penalty assessment.

Two-stage learning framework (offline learning + online adaptation) for nonlinear stochastic dynamical systems with highly correlated, non-stationary data: offline phase gives a generalization-error upper bound for approximate nonlinear-least-squares under strong correlation and distribution shift, using KL divergence to quantify distributional discrepancy; online phase uses a meta-LMS prediction algorithm to handle uncertain parameter drift on the offline-trained model. The integrated framework outperforms purely offline or purely online methods, with both theoretical guarantees and empirical studies. (NSFC Grant No. 12288201.)

HistoricalML: probabilistic neuro-symbolic framework for sparse historical data (N << 100): (1) Bayesian uncertainty quantification separating epistemic/aleatoric; (2) structural causal models for counterfactuals under confounding; (3) Shapley-value cooperative game theory for fair allocation; (4) attention-based neural architectures for context-dependent factor weighting. Consistency under sparse data when strong domain priors available; posterior mean E[w|y,X] = (X^T X/sigma^2 + Sigma_0^{-1})^{-1} (X^T y/sigma^2 + Sigma_0^{-1} mu_0) converges to mu_0 = w* as prior precision -> infinity, even when n < d. Case studies: 19th-century partition of Africa (N=7 colonial powers) - Germany's +107.9% discrepancy as structural tension preceding WWI, tension factor 36.43, 0.79 naval arms race correlation; Second Punic War (N=2) - Monte Carlo battle sims give Carthage 57.3% win probability at Cannae, Rome 57.8% at Zama, matching historical outcomes; counterfactuals identify Carthaginian political support (score 6.4 vs Napoleon's 7.1), not military capability, as decisive.

COACH (Collaborative Agents for Contextual Highlighting): multi-agent framework for sports video analysis - replaces single-task models with role-based agents coordinated through Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs): an Orchestrator agent acts as strategist with the highest reasoning freedom, planning summary structure then calling a Grounder (often batched) to localize events; designed for interpretable fact-checking, iterative coordination, and composable workflows that construct adaptive pipelines for short-term analytic reasoning. Addresses opaque reasoning in monolithic models by making the decision process inspectable and modular.

Real-time multimodal smartwatch data collection in education (UAM): findings show heart rate alone predicts phone usage with 70% accuracy; combined with other signals in a multimodal model, accuracy improves to 91%, confirming HR as a distraction indicator. Caveats: smartwatch HR sensors often sample at low frequency (~1 reading per 5 s) with intermittent data loss, limiting reliability for precise analysis; multimodal fusion of eye movements, brain activity, posture, facial expressions gives more accurate learning-outcome predictions.

Nonparametric Bayesian probit graphical models for ordinal sports data with heterogeneous subgroups: Mixture of Finite Mixtures (MFM) framework discovers flexible subgroups (e.g., teams with varying styles, players with distinct roles), modeling each subgroup with a probit graphical model and jointly estimating cluster count and configuration via Gibbs sampling with Albert-Chib data augmentation. Ordinal mapping: Pr(X_j = k) = Pr(theta_{k-1}^{(j)} <= Z_j < theta_k^{(j)}) with latent Gaussian Z ~ N(mu, Sigma), precision Omega = Sigma^{-1}; joint density f_{X,Z}(x, z; mu, Omega, Theta) = f(z; mu, Omega) prod_j I(z_j in [theta_{x_j-1}^{(j)}, theta_{x_j}^{(j)})) = (det Omega)^{1/2}/(2pi)^{p/2} exp(-(1/2)(z-mu)' Omega (z-mu)) * I(z in C(x, Theta)). Suited to uncovering latent patterns in player performance metrics.

Robust forecast aggregation via additional queries (Frongillo/Monroe/Neyman/Waggoner): extends robust aggregation beyond the impossibility result that no aggregation of individual expert forecasts can beat following a random expert - by eliciting richer information through structured queries with truthful-reporting incentives. Under independent-but-overlapping expert signals, optimal aggregation is achievable in the worst case with each complexity measure bounded by n agents; tight tradeoffs: aggregation error decreases linearly with number of queries and vanishes when the order of reasoning and agents relevant to a query is omega(sqrt(n)). With query complexity capped at d <= n, best achievable error is 1 - d/n. Example: Y = sum_{j=1}^{n+1} X_j with agent i observing S_i=(X_i, X_{n+1}); query Q := E[Y_2 | S_1] = X_{n+1} reveals the common signal, enabling optimal aggregation A* = sum X_j = Y with zero error.

Long-horizon LSTM for NBA game-outcome forecasting: newly constructed longitudinal dataset of 2004-05 to 2024-25 NBA seasons; LSTM with extended sequence length of 9,840 games (~8 full NBA seasons) captures evolving team dynamics and season-over-season dependencies, addressing concept drift and instability across seasons. LSTM achieves 72.35% accuracy, 73.15% precision, 76.13% AUC-ROC - best across metrics vs Logistic Regression, Random Forest, MLP, CNN baselines. Finding: temporal dependencies improve accuracy beyond what traditional ML captures; accuracy otherwise drops as seasons progress, requiring retraining, but historical seasons still improve robustness.

Free-throw 'command' metric using NBA Hawk-Eye limb tracking (2023 adoption, 60 Hz 3D poses): analyzes 21,964 shot attempts from 72 NBA players (min 200 FT attempts, 2024-25 season). Command measures shot quality via accuracy AND precision near the basket bullseye (defined 2 inches behind rim center, the optimal entry location per Marty 2018) - some makes/misses are better than others. Inaccuracy mu = ball's average end distance from bullseye; variability sigma = shot-to-shot variation in landing distance; command = f(mu, sigma). Key findings: command captures underlying skill better than make-or-miss; early-season command predicts late-season success more reliably than shooting percentage. Launch-based metrics: consistency in release velocity, angle, and 3D position; greater 'touch' (consistent launch dynamics) => stronger command. A physics model identifies launch-condition regions that yield makes and which are most robust to small perturbations ('safe' launch regions).

Multi-class calibration via normalization-aware isotonic techniques (Arad/Rosset, Tel Aviv U): NA-FIR incorporates probability normalization directly into the isotonic optimization; SCIR frames it as cumulative bivariate isotonic regression. Outperforms one-vs-rest isotonic calibration and parametric methods on text and image classification across architectures, improving NLL and ECE. Calibration definitions: classifier hat p(X) in simplex Delta^{k-1} = {p in R^k | p_i >= 0, sum p_i = 1} is calibrated if E[Y | hat p(X)=q] = q; class-wise calibrated if E[Y_j | hat p(X)_j] = hat p(X)_j for all j; confidence-calibrated if E[Y_{argmax hat p(X)} | max hat p(X)] = max hat p(X). NLL and Brier are proper scoring rules: argmin_p E_{Y~q}[S(p,Y)] = q.

Critique of conformal prediction with small calibration sets in medicine: although the marginal coverage guarantee P_{Y,X,D_cal}(Y in C_M(X; D_cal)) >= 1 - alpha holds for calibration sets of arbitrary size, the practical utility of the guarantee depends heavily on calibration-set size - small calibration sets (common in medical domains) yield prediction sets with little practical value even though the nominal guarantee holds. Empirical demonstration on medical image classification. Workflow: split D into D_train (fit model M) and D_cal (calibrate into prediction sets C_M(X; D_cal)).

Basketball rebound anticipation in broadcast video: new task of predicting which team will gain possession after a shot attempt, with a self-curated dataset of 100,000 clips (>300 hours) and 2,000+ manually annotated rebound events. Two setups: offline anticipation - sequence truncated tau_a seconds before the action (temporal context W={t_1..t_W} with t_W = t_A - tau_a), predict the upcoming event; online - decide from a short fixed clip whether a rebound will occur imminently with unknown timestamp. Rebound spotting: predict class hat y_A and timestamp hat t_A; correct if hat y_A = y_A and hat t_A in [t_A - delta/2, t_A + delta/2], measured by mAP@delta. First deep-learning application to basketball rebound prediction with SOTA action-anticipation baselines; dataset to be released publicly pending NBA approval.

Tournament score-set reconstruction: Landau's theorem - non-decreasing S = s_1..s_m is a score sequence of an m-tournament iff sum_{i=1}^{k} s_i >= k(k-1)/2 for all 1<=k<=m, with equality at k=m. Reformulated for degree set D={alpha_i} and exponent set E={x_i} (x_i = multiplicity of score alpha_i): sum_{i=1}^{k} alpha_i x_i >= (sum_{i=1}^k x_i)(sum_{i=1}^k x_i - 1)/2 for all 1<=k<=n, equality at k=n. Based on these conditions the authors give a polynomial-time and a scalable reconstruction algorithm plus a polynomial-time method enumerating all score sequences for a given score set; the reconstruction algorithm can verify Reid's 1978 conjecture (any set of nonnegative integers is some tournament's degree set). Applications: sports analysis, ranking prediction, learning-to-rank, data imputation, recommendation, anomaly detection.

ScoutGPT (Saarland/U. Seoul/DFB): GPT-based framework capturing player impact from team action sequences for transfer evaluation. Each event tokenized as v_t = (h_t, e_t, x_t, y_t, delta_t, o_t, rOBV_t): h_t acting team (home/away), e_t event type, (x_t,y_t) discretized spatial coordinates, delta_t elapsed time since previous event, o_t action success, rOBV_t residual on-ball value of player p_t from t to episode end: rOBV_t = E[sum_{tau=t}^{T_episode} OBV_tau | state at t, player p_t] - reflects how a player's involvement shapes future episode progression rather than immediate action value. Trained autoregressively with teacher forcing: L = -sum_{t=1}^T log P(v_{t+1} | c, p_{1:t} v_{1:t}), jointly supervising event sequencing, player-conditioned action selection, and future value estimation. Transfer simulation: substitute a candidate player's embedding into a team's unchanged event sequence and re-evaluate rOBV_t to quantify transfer impact in the new team's context. Metrics: accuracy for categorical (h_t, e_t, o_t), MAE on original scale for continuous (x_t, y_t, delta_t, rOBV_t).

VAIR: visual analytics system for sports injury risk analysis from 3D human motion reconstructed from video - combines pose estimation, biomechanical simulation, and synchronized visualizations; experts inspect temporally aligned joint angles, angular velocities, and internal forces to detect injury mechanisms. Case studies on Achilles tendon and ACL injuries in basketball: e.g., a reconstructed pose shows left knee with flexion ~74 deg, abduction ~95 deg, internal rotation ~67 deg; an Achilles case shows pronounced plantar flexion (~-32 deg) with knee rotation, known to produce high eccentric loading. Dynamic knee valgus (medial knee collapse during hip/knee flexion) confirmed as a known ACL risk factor. Clips of 3-10 s reconstructed in ~30 s per video; video-based reconstruction less precise than sensor instrumentation but far more broadly applicable. Expert feedback confirms improved diagnostic reasoning and proactive intervention planning.

Data-driven tuning of Elo-type rating systems: learns optimal parameter values by maximizing predictive accuracy of match outcomes rather than relying on convention-based parameters (e.g., K, scale factor); framework generalizes to Glicko, TrueSkill, and multiplayer setups via the parameter space. Validated on real and simulated gameplay. Core equations: expected score E_A = 1/(1+10^{(R_B-R_A)/400}); update R'_A = R_A + K(S_A - E_A), S_A in {0, 0.5, 1}; player-dependent sensitivity rating'_1 = rating_1 + K_1(Actual_1 - Expected_1) with K_1, K_2 depending on games played; generalized scale E_1 = 1/(1+10^{(rating_2 - rating_1)/D}). Bayesian variants: Glicko models skill theta_i ~ N(mu_i, sigma_i^2) with sigma evolving with inactivity/outcomes, plus volatility tau (Glicko-2); TrueSkill p_i ~ N(mu_i, sigma_i^2) with win probability P(i wins) = Phi((mu_i - mu_j)/sqrt(2(sigma_i^2 + beta^2))), Phi the standard normal CDF, beta the per-game performance variance, with approximate Bayesian updates of mu_i and sigma_i after each match.

The paper (Kramov & Bauzha, Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv, 2016) proposes a method for creating an automated hardware-software complex for remote observation and analysis of human heart rate (pulse), enabling remote monitoring of a person's pulse.

The paper proposes a framework for density forecast combination that constructs time-varying combination weights from time-varying features of historical time-series information, estimating the weights via Bayesian log predictive scores, and uses automatic Bayesian variable selection to identify feature importance, giving better interpretability than black-box combination schemes.

Applied to stock market data and M3 competition data, a simple maximum-a-posteriori (MAP) scheme under this framework outperforms benchmark methods, and Bayesian variable selection further enhances accuracy for both point forecasts and density forecasts.

The paper reexamines classical linear regression when covariates may be missing/inaccessible and the measurement-error variance is undetermined and changes by an unknown mechanism, characterizing mean and variance uncertainty in the response by two nonlinear random variables that encompass an infinite family of probability distributions under sublinear expectation theory.
Distribution-uncertain regression model: the response is the sum of the linear predictor, a mean-uncertainty variable eta, and a variance-uncertainty variable epsilon.

Theorem 2.1 (Yang): for a convex loss phi, the upper optimal parameter equals the argmin of expected loss and also equals the argmin over beta of the maximum over the uncertainty set Theta of the theta-indexed expectation; the lower optimal parameter equals the argmin of negative expected negative loss and also the argmin over beta of the minimum over Theta of the indexed expectation.
Corollary 3.1 (Yang): under the square loss phi(z)=z^2, the upper least-squares estimator, the lower least-squares estimator, and the true regression parameter beta all coincide.

Theorem 3.2 (Yang): under the stated data generation process where blockwise minima/maxima of eta_j and sigma_j^2 converge to (underline mu, overline mu, underline sigma^2, overline sigma^2), as K and n both go to infinity the lower variance estimator is strongly consistent (hat underline sigma^2 -> underline sigma^2 with probability 1) and the regression parameter estimator hat beta is strongly consistent (hat beta -> beta).

The paper describes three independent implementations of the Bristol Betting Exchange (BBE), an agent-based model simulating a contemporary sports-betting exchange (like Betfair/Smarkets/Betdaq) as a synthetic data generator for developing and testing betting strategies with data analytics and ML; the implementations are single-threaded Python, multi-threaded Python, and Python driving OpenCL track-race simulations on a 640-core GPU, the GPU version running approximately 1000 times faster.

Betting exchanges act as platforms aggregating and anonymizing orders from multiple participants and showing a real-time market summary, directly comparable to how electronic financial exchanges let traders find counterparties; BBE is aimed first at synthetic in-play (in-race/in-game) betting data for track-race events.
In the BBE model the gap to the nearest competitor ahead of competitor c is defined as the difference between that competitor's distance and c's own distance.

The paper proposes a machine-learning approach to estimate a GraphQL query's cost before executing it, addressing nested query structure, differing API design conventions, and hidden data sources; tested on query-response data from public commercial APIs it is efficient, highly accurate, and consistently outperforms worst-case static query analysis by a large margin (static analysis tends to grossly overestimate cost).
Prediction error for GraphQL query cost is measured as the percentage error between predicted cost hat c and actual cost c.

The paper develops a truncated, mean-parameterised Conway-Maxwell-Poisson model for Test-match bowler wicket counts (data from 1877 onward) to handle under- and overdispersion in small counts and extract innate bowler ability via Bayesian MCMC; it finds the commonly used bowling average is a flawed measure of bowler merit.
Conway-Maxwell-Poisson probability mass function for wicket count x_ijk with rate lambda_ijk and dispersion nu, normalized by G_infinity.
Mean-parameterisation constraint for the truncated (at 10) Conway-Maxwell-Poisson model: the weighted sum of (r - mu_ijk) over r=0..10 must equal zero.

Posterior means (95% HDIs) for innings effects on the multiplicative wicket-taking scale vs the first innings: second innings 1.07 (1.04-1.09), third 1.03 (1.00-1.05), fourth 1.00 (0.97-1.03); playing away reduces the mean number of wickets taken.

6MapNet is a triplet network that represents soccer players from tracking (GPS) data without any soccer-action annotation: player locations and velocities generate two types of heatmaps, subnetworks map heatmap pairs into feature vectors whose similarity corresponds to actual playing-style similarity, and players can be accurately identified from only a small number of matches.

The paper proposes C-LUCB for best-arm identification in the fixed-confidence (1-delta) setting under correlated rewards, using domain knowledge in the form of upper bounds on expected conditional reward of one arm given another arm's realization; its sample complexity sums the O(log(1/delta)) term only over the set C of competitive arms (a subset of all arms K) rather than over all K arms.

The competitive-arm set C can be as small as 2 depending on the problem, so C-LUCB can sharply reduce best-arm-identification sample complexity; theoretical findings are supported by experiments on Movielens and Goodreads recommendation data.

The paper proposes a new soccer state representation plus batch reinforcement learning that trains a policy network to propose the optimal action maximizing expected goal in critical situations; on InStat logs of 104 European matches the optimized policy obtains higher rewards than the behavior policy in all 104 games, and the learned policy matches real-world expectations, e.g. fouls or ball-out actions are sometimes more rewarding than a shot in specific situations.
Reward function used: r(s,a) equals PV(s) if action a is a shot; PV(s')-PV(s) when s and s' belong to the same team; -0.1 otherwise, where PV is possession value.

Importance-sampled policy gradient identity: the gradient of the expected return equals the expectation under the sampling distribution of (p(x)/q(x)) f(x) times the score function grad_theta log p(x).
The shot-outcome classification model in the paper achieves AUC of 80% with 5-fold cross-validation on the shot dataset.

The paper investigates the COVID-19 pandemic's impact on pro and college sports betting markets and finds that during the pandemic the NBA moneyline markets became very inefficient: uniform wagering on underdog teams during that period achieved a 16.7% profit margin (hypothesized to be due to the absence of live audiences), with much of the inefficiency coming from games with moneyline odds in the 233 to 400 range, and cleverly constructed strategies achieved a 26-fold gain on initial investment; no such inefficiency was found for any other sport. (Historical research finding, not a recommendation.)

The paper develops a machine-learning algorithm (random forest) that predicts the frame-by-frame conditional and marginal probability that an NFL pass is completed while the ball is in the air, using 2018 NFL season data with predictors such as receiver separation from the nearest defender, receiver-to-passer distance, and offensive formation; distance measures between players and the ball also let it predict the intended target very accurately via empirical probabilities.

The paper reviews fractional-Kelly portfolios (a fraction of wealth in the growth-optimal portfolio, the remainder at the risk-free rate) in a continuous-parameter time-series framework, showing Kelly's criterion prescribes the same leverage as Markowitz mean-variance optimization, stating a simple distributional relationship between portfolio Sharpe ratio, fractional coefficient, and portfolio log-returns, and demonstrating a method-of-moments calculation that estimates a fund's Sharpe ratio and level of risk deployment from reported returns.

The paper introduces a game-level win probability model for Counter-Strike predicting a team's chance of winning at the start of a round from features including team scores, equipment, money, and spending decisions; using it, the authors identify a pattern of sub-optimal team spending decisions in CS:GO and introduce the Optimal Spending Error (OSE) metric to rank teams by how closely their spending follows the predicted optimal decisions.
The win probability model is trained with the multi-class cross-entropy loss: negative average over N samples and K classes of y_{i,k} log p_{i,k}.
Measured result: winning the first two rounds of a CS:GO game increases a team's chance of winning the game by roughly 15% over the baseline logistic regression model using team scores.

CS:GO in-game economy facts used by the model: teams earn $3,250 per player for winning a round, or $3,500 if they detonate the bomb; a losing team gains a variable loss bonus depending on consecutive losses since its last round win, and the bonus resets after each win.

The paper tackles risk-averse multi-armed bandits with non-stationary losses using conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) as the objective, proposing two CVaR estimation methods (a weighted empirical distribution of losses, and the dual representation of CVaR) that embed into classic arm selection such as epsilon-greedy policies; simulations show these policies outperform naive benchmarks that ignore non-stationarity.

The paper generalizes the Junca-Jabin kinetic Elo model to players/teams of variable strength (variable performance), derives the corresponding formal mean-field model, proves existence and uniqueness of classical solutions (Theorems 1-2), and illustrates the rating dynamics computationally.
Elo-type rating update for players i and j: each rating moves by learning rate gamma times the difference between the observed score S_ij and the expected-score function b of the rating difference.

With variable player strength, the expected game score is the base expected-score function b of the mean-strength difference plus a second-order correction involving b'' and the sum of the players' strength variances sigma_i^2 + sigma_j^2.

Theorem 3 (Düring/Fischer): the energy functional decays exponentially in time, E(t) <= E(0) exp(-2 w_min (L + sigma^2 L_2) t), where L and L_2 depend on b, b'' (hence nu) and the support of the initial datum.

The paper designs a high-frequency market-making strategy using a Deep Hawkes process that creates a feedback loop between order arrival and the limit order book state with self- and cross-excitation effects, accounts for order cancellations and their effect on queue position, spread, and profitability; the trading agent outperforms a baseline using a probability-density estimate of the fundamental price, and the simulation reproduces stylized facts from empirical order-book data.

The paper presents a Bayesian hierarchical model inferring what explains score differences in English Premiership Rugby 2020/2021 matches; its main result is that player effort, measured as the ratio of tries to scoring-kick attempts, is highly relevant to explaining match outcomes, alongside team ability and luck.

Proposition 1 (Manski): for as-if optimization with no sample data, the minimum achievable maximum regret equals the minimum of (1 - p_mx) - U_xB and U_xB - (1 - p_Mx); with no prior knowledge (p_mx=0, p_Mx=1) this simplifies to estimates with U_xB > 1 - phi_x minimizing regret when U_xB >= 1/2.

Proposition 3 (Manski): with one illness observation, as-if optimization using the estimate [phi_x(0)=0, phi_x(1)=1] has maximum regret equal to one quarter of the maximum of (1-U_xB)^2 and U_xB^2, which at U_xB=1/2 gives maximum regret 1/16, substantially better than 1/2 with no data or 1/4 with uninformative data.

The paper develops a Markov reward process / Markov decision process framework to study how execution error (uncertainty in where a tennis shot lands) affects a player's value function and optimal strategy, powered by hundreds of millions of simulated tennis shots with 3D ball and 2D player tracking data.

Findings: optimal shot selection in tennis becomes more conservative as execution error grows; having perfect execution with the empirical shot-selection strategy is roughly equivalent to choosing one or two optimal shots with average execution error; execution error on backhands is more costly than on forehands; and optimal shot selection on the serve return is more valuable than on any other shot across all execution-error levels.

Theorem 1 (Chan): under any fixed policy pi and execution-error level epsilon, the value function V_epsilon^pi(s) equals the probability that Player A wins the point given current state s, because the induced process is a Markov chain and the reward structure makes the value the absorption probability of the win state.

The paper introduces an automated system to track and identify players in broadcast NHL hockey videos with three components: (1) player tracking, (2) team identification, (3) player identification; identification is hard because same-team players look nearly identical except for jersey numbers.

Measured results: player tracking achieves Multi-Object Tracking Accuracy (MOTA) of 94.5%; the team-identification CNN (away jerseys one class, home jerseys grouped by color) reaches 97% test accuracy; a novel temporal one-dimensional convolutional network identifies players from bounding-box sequences and leverages NHL roster data.

The paper models a baseball at-bat as a zero-sum stochastic game between pitcher and batter, where the batter's goal is to get on base (which the pitcher prevents) and the value of the game is the on-base percentage; technical challenges (pitch-location distribution given intent, outcome distribution given a swing, batter patience) are addressed with novel pitcher/batter representations and a deep neural network outcome predictor, evaluated on Kaggle MLB data from the 2015-2018 seasons.

The paper introduces a class of proper scoring rules for evaluating spatial point process forecasts based on summary statistics; they rely on Monte-Carlo approximations of expectations so they can be evaluated for any simulatable point process model (more flexible than the logarithmic score), and they can target calibration of specific aspects such as spatial distribution or clustering tendency; demonstrated on northern California earthquake occurrences and Pacific silver fir spatial distributions.

Using causal inference on League of Legends software patches, the paper finds patches have substantially different impacts by player skill level and break-taking behavior: the gap between good and bad players increases after a patch despite equalization efforts, and longer between-game breaks tend to improve player performance after patches.

Measured heterogeneous effects: Lucian's win rate increases 5% in the analyzed patch; Nami's win rate rises 18% when she is on the team and 23% when Rengar is absent (4.2% unconditioned in patch 4.12); Jhin's buffs plus Fiora on team raise win rate 23% in patch 6.4; Kassadin's nerf cuts his win rate 4.5%; Jinx on team adds 6.4% win rate.

The paper presents a large-scale diverse combinatorial optimization system for ESPN fantasy football trades: each player is valued by an ensemble (Quantum SVC with permutation importance, QSVC with accumulated local effects, variational quantum circuit with PI, hybrid quantum neural net with PI, XGBoost, and subject-matter-expert rules) personalized to league rules and roster; teams pair by cosine dissimilarity to offset strengths/weaknesses; a 0-1 knapsack computes outgoing players; postprocessors score each trade on 6 objectives.

Evaluated by 24 IBM and ESPN experts over 10 Football Error Analysis Tool (FEAT) sessions across the 2020 and 2021 NFL seasons, the system started at 76.9% high-quality trades and was deployed for the 2021 season at 97.3% high-quality trades.

The paper describes an ML pipeline for ESPN fantasy football: trained statistical entity detectors and doc2vec models applied to over 100,000 news sources and 2.3 million articles, videos, and podcasts daily (analogy test accuracy 100%, keyword test accuracy 80%); deep feedforward networks classify players as bust/boom/hidden-injury/meaningful-touches with 72% cumulative accuracy; a multiple regression ensemble over deep-learning output and ESPN projections gives point projections for 500+ players with RMSE 6.78 points.

The paper extends proper scoring rules from scalar/vector forecasts to forecasts of paths and time series, formalized as probability measures on spaces of equivalence classes of paths modulo time-parametrization (capturing the approximate shape of future evolution or order of events), and introduces notions of gradients, entropy, and divergence tailored to that non-Euclidean structure for principled decision-making.

Using MCMC inference under a whole-history dynamic Bradley-Terry rating model on curated ascent data, the paper shows climbing grade scales are logarithmic scales of difficulty (like decibels or stellar magnitude, with links to the Weber-Fechner psychophysical laws); one grade increment multiplies difficulty by 2.1 (Ewbank), 2.09 (French), 2.13 (UIAA), and 3.17 for the Vermin bouldering V-grade scale, assuming a logistic success-probability model.

Climbing send probability model: the probability of sending equals the logistic function of m times climber ability C(t) minus m times route difficulty R, i.e. Pr(y=1)=p_send with p_send = e^{mC(t)}/(e^{mC(t)}+e^{mR}) = 1/(e^{m(R-C(t))}+1) = logit^{-1}(mC(t)-mR), where m is the scale parameter defining the proportional difficulty increase per grade.

Inverse-logit function used in the climbing model: logit^{-1}(x) = 1/(1+e^{-x}); climber ability evolves as a random walk C(t+1) ~ N(C(t), w^2); the expected number of attempts is E[a] = (1-p_send)/p_send.

The paper introduces selective ensembles to fix prediction inconsistency across models trained to the same objective with similar aggregate accuracy: hypothesis testing is applied to predictions of models from randomly selected starting conditions, and the ensemble abstains when no consistent outcome is achievable at a specified confidence level; prediction disagreement is provably bounded, and on benchmark datasets selective ensembles reach zero inconsistently predicted points with abstention rates as low as 1.5%, with consistent feature attributions too.

The paper gives short, simple proofs revealing the probabilistic meaning of classical prediction results for stationary continuous-time stochastic processes, both for prediction using the whole infinite past and using only a finite section of the past.

Spectral representation of a stationary process: X_t is the Fourier integral of e^{2 pi i t mu} against the orthogonal-increment process Y, and its covariance function is the Fourier integral of e^{2 pi i t mu} against the spectral measure G.
equation: X_{t}=\int e^{2\pi it\mu}dY(\mu),\qquad r(t)=\int e^{2\pi it\mu}dG(\mu)

claim: Szego condition for prediction: the integral of log G'(mu)/(1+mu^2) d mu must exceed -infinity; the Fourier pair is f(t)=int e^{2 pi i t s} f*(s) ds and f*(s)=int e^{-2 pi i t s} f(t) dt; the spectral factor satisfies |c(mu)|^2 = G'(mu).

Comparing reinforcement-learning football agents with real players via aggregated statistics and social network analysis, the paper finds (1) strong correlations between an agent's competitiveness and various SNA metrics, and (2) RL agents' play styles become similar to real-world footballers as the agents become more competitive.

DeepSportLab is a unified framework that trains a single model to simultaneously locate the ball, segment player instance masks, and estimate player pose in team sports scenes: part intensity fields give ball/player/joint locations, and spatial embeddings associate player pixels to their player center and group joints into skeletons; on the DeepSport basketball dataset it matches the performance of state-of-the-art models that solve each task separately.

The paper generalizes the Bradley-Terry model to multiple game outcomes (regulation, overtime, shootout wins/losses) for hockey, incorporating the zero-sum point system that values overtime/shootout wins as 2/3 of a win and overtime/shootout losses as 1/3 of a win; posterior strength-parameter distributions are evaluated via Gaussian expansion about MAP estimates and Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, applied to college hockey.
Bradley-Terry win probability: team i beats team j with probability pi_i/(pi_i+pi_j), where pi are team strength parameters.
Davidson-style extension with a tie/nuance parameter nu: the win probability becomes pi_i divided by (pi_i + nu*sqrt(pi_i*pi_j) + pi_j), and the loss probability is theta^L_ij = 1 - theta^W_ij.

From over 75,000 battle-royale matches, the paper engineers behavioral features (goals, strategy, expertise) into player models to predict ranks, and finds simple behavioral models superior to three mainstream rating systems at rank prediction; some features work across all player groups while others are group-specific.

The paper trains generative neural networks for probabilistic forecasting by minimizing a predictive-sequential (prequential) scoring rule on the recorded temporal sequence instead of adversarial training; adversarial-free minimization is possible for some scoring rules, avoiding unstable adversarial training's hyperparameter tuning and uncertainty underestimation, and the authors prove consistency of the minimizer with dependent data (adversarial training assumes independence); on two chaotic dynamical models and global weather observations it outperforms state-of-the-art adversarial approaches, especially in probabilistic calibration.

The paper presents a holistic compound Poisson regression framework (including a Bayesian implementation of the geometric-Poisson distribution) to forecast corner-kick counts in association football, handling serial correlation between matches with a varying shape parameter; cross-market odds information is elicited to improve predictability, and margin-application methods to adjust raw-odds market inefficiency are discussed.
Odds-ratio margin removal: OR = p_i(1-pi_i)/(pi_i(1-p_i)), and the de-biased probability is p_i = pi_i/(OR + pi_i - OR*pi_i), where pi_i is the raw implied probability.

Bivariate Poisson model for match goals: the joint pmf of the two teams' scores factorizes as (lambda1^x1 e^{-lambda1}/x1!) times (lambda2^x2 e^{-lambda2}/x2!), with total goals TG_i = lambda-hat1 + lambda-hat2 and supremacy SUP_i = lambda-hat1 - lambda-hat2.

The paper proposes a multi-modal attention network for stock movement prediction that extracts semantics from social media (estimating post credibility from poster identity and public reputation) and fuses them with numeric historical-record features; it outperforms previous methods by a significant margin with 61.20% prediction accuracy and 9.13% trading profits.

The paper studies mean-risk portfolio choice for log-returns in a continuous-time complete market (growth-optimal with risk control), measuring log-return risk by weighted Value-at-Risk (WVaR, generalizing VaR and Expected Shortfall); it characterizes optimal terminal wealth via the concave envelope of a function, gives analytical optimal wealth and policy under VaR or ES, finds the efficient frontier is a concave curve connecting the minimum-risk and growth-optimal portfolios (unlike the vertical line when WVaR is applied to terminal wealth), and advocates the mean-WVaR-on-log-returns criterion over terminal-wealth WVaR.

The paper tests Bill James's Pythagorean expected-wins model against serial-form and difference-form Tullock contest success functions on MLB team data (2003-2015) with cross-validation; the serial CSF estimator dramatically reduces root mean squared error of wins estimation versus the original model, an optimized Pythagorean, and the optimized difference form, substantially improving team-quality estimates on average.

The paper formulates an adaptive version of Kelly's horse-race model in which the gambler learns win probabilities from past races by Bayesian inference, characterizes the cost of the strategy and the asymptotic scaling of the gambler's regret (growth-rate gap vs the optimal rate), relates it to the universal portfolio strategy, builds improved adaptive strategies exploiting the bookmaker odds distribution, and develops Laplace's rule of succession with prior information (including its limitations) plus an extension to correlated races.

Smart Director (JD AI Research) is an event-driven automated sports-broadcast directing system that mimics the human-in-the-loop broadcasting process to automatically create near-professional multi-camera productions.

Measured results for Smart Director: event detection outperforms state-of-the-art detection by 2.5% mean average precision; the view classifier reaches 93.06% accuracy; the MVEL highlight module achieves 55.8% mAP, a 2.6% absolute improvement over the best competitor CTAP; and the directing-consistency accuracy score over six ground-truth broadcast videos is 92.3%.

The paper proposes an online match-scheduling algorithm for identifying top Elo ratings via a dueling bandits framework tailored to gradient-based Elo updates; it reduces per-step memory and time complexity to constant (vs O(t) for likelihood maximization), carries a regret guarantee of O-tilde(sqrt(T)) sublinear in competition rounds, and extends to multidimensional Elo ratings for intransitive games.

Dueling-bandit cumulative regret for Elo evaluation: R(T) = sum_{t=1}^T [r*_{x*} - (r*_{x_t} + r*_{y_t})/2], the gap between the optimal player's true rating and the average true rating of the two players matched at round t; the Bradley-Terry/Elo link uses the logistic sigma(x)=1/(1+e^{-x}).
Lemma 1 (Yan et al.): the sum of the V_i^{-1}-norms of the selected pair differences from round tau+1 to tau+t is bounded by sqrt(2 n t log((2 tau + t)/n)).
Theorem 1 (Yan et al.): cumulative regret satisfies R(T) <= tau*Delta_max + (2+tau) g_1(T) sqrt(2 n T log((2 tau + T)/n)) + 4 g_2(J) sqrt(tau T), giving the O-tilde(sqrt(T)) regret guarantee.

The paper builds a Market Knowledge Graph with bi-typed entities (listed companies and their executives) and hybrid relations (explicit and implicit) to capture momentum spillover in stock fluctuation, then proposes DanSmp, dual attention networks that learn spillover signals from the graph; experiments against nine state-of-the-art baselines show DanSmp improves stock movement prediction.

The paper systematically evaluates CRPS-Sum for multivariate probabilistic forecasting and shows its discrimination ability depends on the statistical properties of the target data, and that CRPS-Sum calculation overlooks each dimension's individual performance; these flaws can mislead model assessment, demonstrated by a random-noise dummy model achieving a better CRPS-Sum than a state-of-the-art method on real data.

GNNRank is a trainable GNN framework with digraph embedding for recovering global rankings from pairwise comparisons (directed-graph edges), with new objectives encoding ranking upsets/violations and an inductive bias from unfolding the Fiedler-vector computation of a learnable similarity matrix; on 78 digraphs from 10 real-world datasets it is competitive with and often superior to baselines, with promising transfer ability (code at github.com/SherylHYX/GNNRank).
Bradley-Terry pairwise model used in GNNRank: P_ij = w_i/(w_i+w_j), where w is the parameter (strength) vector.
GNNRank ranking-difference matrix: T' = r 1^T - 1 r^T in R^{n x n} with entries T'_{ij} = r_i - r_j, and the symmetrized similarity S' = (1/2)(n 1 1^T + C C^T).
Theorem 3.1 (He et al.): with fixed step size alpha in (0, 1/(4(n-1))) and the Fiedler eigenvector r* a strict local minimizer, Algorithm 1 converges locally uniformly to r*.

The paper introduces a 'latent style allocation' model (latent conditional distributions as mixed members of finite Gaussian mixtures) for return-impact locations, applied in a fully Bayesian implementation to 142,803 return points by 141 top ATP players (2018-2020); it improves predictive performance (ELPD) over finite Gaussian mixture and mixed-membership alternatives and identifies six unique impact styles on both first and second serve returns.

Measured style-allocation results: on first serve returns 80 of 141 players have the majority of posterior style weight in style group 1, and on second serve returns 72 of 141 do, with style group 6 the next-most-common plurality group for both serves; first-serve ELPD improved about 2.8% over mixture-model alternatives.

The paper proposes a deterministic decision-tree algorithm that automatically extracts football events from tracking data in two steps: (1) a possession step determining which player possessed the ball each frame plus distinct player configurations during out-of-play intervals for set-piece detection, and (2) an event detection step combining possession changes with the laws of football; it achieves over 90% detection rate in most event categories versus manual annotations across tournaments and tracking-data providers.

Neural Temporal Logic Programming first learns implicit temporal relations between atomic events, then lifts logic rules for composite events using only composite-event labels as supervision, via an end-to-end differentiable search over the combinatorial rule space; it outperforms baselines for rule discovery on video and healthcare datasets.

Lemma (Samel et al.): in temporal ILP with |X| events, |P| predicates, and n predicates per rule, the rule search space is O((P E^2)^n), tightened to Theta((floor(P/2) E^2 + E(E+1)/2)^n) when P contains symmetric relations (before(u,v)=after(v,u), during(u,v)=during(v,u)).
Temporal logic rule form: r := AND_{i=1}^n p^i(x_u^i, x_v^i) for predicates p^i and event variables x_u^i, x_v^i drawn from predicate(C_j^i).

Ensemble conformalized quantile regression (EnCQR) builds distribution-free, approximately marginally valid prediction intervals for nonstationary heteroscedastic time series: a bootstrap ensemble estimator lets conformal predictors work on time series without requiring data exchangeability, and generic ML quantile-regression learners let PI length adapt to local variability; experiments show EnCQR outperforms quantile-regression-only or conformal-only models with sharper, more informative, valid PIs.

Using state-space models on high-frequency in-play stake data, the paper finds live-betting market stakes are driven both by perceived pre-game team strength and by in-game strength measured via the Valuing Actions by Estimating Probabilities (VAEP) approach, with both effects varying over the course of the match.

This comprehensive review surveys computer vision in sports (player/ball detection and classification, tracking, trajectory prediction, team-strategy recognition, event classification) across soccer, basketball, cricket, badminton and more, catalogs public datasets, discusses AI applications and GPU/embedded platforms, and identifies open issues, challenges, and future research directions.

On the M4 dataset of 100,000 time series, Feature-based Forecast Model Averaging is on average the best late-fusion ensemble with ES-RNN base learners; on the M4 Daily subset (where all base learners perform similarly) stacking is the only successful ensemble; model averaging is more robust than model selection and stacking, gradient boosting is superior for implementing ensemble strategies, and the results are state-of-the-art versus the N-BEATS benchmark.

SuperCone is a unified user-segmentation system over heterogeneous experts via concept meta-learning: a flat concept representation summarizes each user's heterogeneous digital footprints, 'super learning' combines prediction models of incompatible architectures, and an end-to-end meta-approach adaptively attends to the best-suited experts; it significantly outperforms state-of-the-art recommendation and ranking algorithms on predictive-segment tasks and public benchmarks, reaching close to 100% F1 and ROC-AUC without tuning.

Theorem 1 (Li/Hu): Unfolded Concept Learning with Heterogeneous Experts is no less difficult than Learning in Heterogeneous Data, Learning in Relational Databases, Heterogeneous Graph Learning, and First-Order Logic Graph Learning, with efficient linear-time reductions from each to it.

Theorem 2 (Li/Hu): for any prediction model there exists a SuperAug parameter space with the same or less asymptotic generalization error on every data instantiation, and for float-point meta-parameter omega with K=1 the generalization error converges to 0 or to the best prediction model at an O(log n / n) rate.
SuperCone expert training objective: theta*_j(omega;D) is defined as the argmin over theta_j in Theta_j of the empirical risk R^D_j(h_j(.;theta_j)).

Analyzing all 51 UEFA EURO 2020 final-phase matches, the paper finds the Poisson model fits the per-match goal counts and the exponential distribution fits goal waiting times quite well; despite the memoryless property seeming counterintuitive, the authors note homogeneous team abilities, a short time span, no home/away distinction, and total-goals-only data, concluding EURO 2020 is not a 'pure game of chance' but an example of independence's real-world ubiquity in one parsimonious model.

Using a novel Bayesian multilevel rank-ordered logit regression on Formula One hybrid-era data (2014-2021), the paper disentangles driver skill from constructor advantage: Hamilton and Verstappen are the best drivers of the era, Mercedes/Ferrari/Red Bull clearly outperform other constructors, and approximately 88% of the variance in race results is explained by the constructor.

Estimated variance components (log-odds scale): constructor sigma^2_c ~ 2.65, constructor-season sigma^2_cs ~ 0.54, driver sigma^2_d ~ 0.29, driver-season sigma^2_ds ~ 0.12, quantifying that constructor advantage dominates driver skill in F1 results variance.

Head-to-head win probability from the rank-ordered logit: exp(theta_{ham:alfa:2021})/(exp(theta_{ham:alfa:2021}) + exp(theta_{rai:merc:2021})), i.e. the softmax of the driver-constructor latent scores.

The paper asks how high an Elo rating can be pushed with n players and k rigged games starting from 0: there is a phase transition at n = k^{1/3} with a huge increase in the highest possible rating from n=2 to n=k^{1/3} but little-to-no increase beyond; past the transition the maximum is at least Theta(k^{1/3}), and for standard Elo the upper bound is Theta(k^{1/3} log(k)^{1/3}).

Theorem 1.1 (Shah): with any pot function sigma, the two-player maximum rating satisfies (1/2)f^{-1}(2k) <= R(2,k) <= (1/2)f^{-1}(2k-2) + 5/2; and for n = h(k) = Omega(k^{1/3}), constants C_1, C_2 exist with C_1 k^{1/3} <= R(h(k),k) <= C_2 k^{1/3} f^{-1}(k)^{1/3} for large k.

Theorem 3.1 (Shah): the constructed strategy achieves highest rating min(k^{1/3}/2, n/4) from all-zero starts (hence Omega(k^{1/3}) for n = Omega(k^{1/3})), using the invariant that the sum of squared ratings equals j/2 after j games; for real chess the pot-function constant is c = (5/6)*log(10)/400 approx 4.80e-3.

The paper proposes 3D ball localization from a single calibrated image by estimating ball diameter in pixels combined with the known real ball diameter in meters: a small neural network on patches around conventional-detector candidates predicts diameter and a ball-presence confidence; validated on three basketball datasets, it is the first model for single-image 3D ball localization, and confidence filtering improves the detector's detection rate.
Diameter regression loss is Huber-like: L^d(d, d-hat) = (1/2)(d-d-hat)^2 when |d-d-hat| <= delta, else delta*(|d-d-hat| - delta/2).

The paper collects 7,582 real-world elections in 25 datasets (sports competitions, music charts, surveys, indicator rankings), complementing the PrefLib database (701 elections, 36 datasets); using the map-of-elections framework it categorizes them, analyzes structural properties (voter agreement, distance from single-peakedness), and studies Condorcet-paradox frequency and consensus among voting rules.

Kendall tau distance between two votes v, v' in L(C): the number of candidate pairs on which the two orderings disagree, i.e. |{{c,c'} in C-choose-2 : (c >_v c' and c' >_{v'} c) or (c >_{v'} c' and c' >_v c)}|, interpretable as the minimum number of adjacent swaps transforming one ordering into the other.

The paper proposes generic full-game team-sport player tracking with few game-specific annotations: pre-trained detection and re-identification networks auto-generate non-ambiguous tracklets and appearance features, an incremental-learning mechanism trains a Transformer to classify identities from only ~6 few-second tracklets annotated per player via a semi-interactive system, then an association algorithm links tracklets; demonstrated on a challenging rugby sevens dataset which the authors publicly release.
Appearance similarity between tracklet features: Psi_app(F_u, F_v) = 1 - (1/eta_app) * d(F_u, F_v), one minus the normalized feature distance.

Measured results on a full rugby sevens game: up to 67.9% detection-and-identity classification recall when players are sufficiently visible with only 6 annotations per player; after the third annotation round, IDF1 and MOTA average 75% and 66% respectively with the iterative association algorithm.

The paper presents a generic semi-supervised teacher-student method for soccer player/ball detection: the teacher produces surrogate annotations on a large unlabeled broadcast-video dataset to train a same-architecture student, with three training-loss parametrizations letting the student doubt the teacher depending on proposal confidence scores; adding unlabeled data substantially improves over labeled-only training, and it sets the first SoccerNet-v3 detection benchmark at 52.3% mAP.

Student loss weightings: hard version alpha_j = 0 if tau_l <= s_j < tau_h else 1; soft version alpha_j = (s_j - tau_l)/(tau_h - tau_l) if tau_l <= s_j < tau_h else 1, where s_j is the teacher proposal confidence.

The paper (Dream11 authors) applies deep reinforcement learning to optimize fantasy sports team selection, addressing strategic team-building for fantasy cricket based on real-world professional athlete performance.

PandaSkill assesses esports player performance and skill rating: machine learning estimates in-game performance from individual player statistics with each role modeled independently, then OpenSkill's Bayesian framework updates skill ratings in a free-for-all setting from performance scores rather than game outcomes (highlighting individual contributions); a dual-rating system combines regional ratings with a meta-rating of each region's overall skill to fix isolated rating pools and enable cross-regional comparison.

Applied to five years of professional League of Legends matches worldwide, PandaSkill's ratings better predict game outcomes and align more closely with expert opinions than existing methods such as Elo and TrueSkill.

In a limited-selection fantasy cricket contest framework where participants choose from four expert-designed teams and prizes are shared based on highest cumulative score, strategic informed team selection consistently outperforms random choice, per simulation experiments combined with real 2024 IPL performance data (ISI Kolkata study).

The fantasy cricket skill model represents team performances as a multivariate lognormal: (P_1,...,P_n) ~ LogNormal(mu, Sigma), equivalently (log P_1,...,log P_n) ~ N(mu, Sigma), with team i's win probability pi_i = P(P_i >= P_j for all j != i) and participant selections drawn as p ~ Dirichlet(alpha * pi).

Team composition, inter-team correlation, and participant behavior jointly influence fantasy cricket winning probabilities; the study identifies configurations where skill becomes statistically dominant over chance.

The extended OpenTTGames dataset adds frame-accurate table tennis annotations for (i) left/right player and stroke type classes, (ii) player posture at ball-bat contact (body lean and legs), and (iii) point outcome of each rally, enabling supervision beyond event spotting and learning of higher-level tactical patterns; inspection and annotation scripts are openly available.

TimeGAN and VAEs trained on historical S&P 500 daily returns can generate synthetic financial return series whose distributional shapes, volatility patterns, and autocorrelation behavior are close to real returns, enabling portfolio allocation, trading backtesting, and risk modeling with improved data privacy.

For synthetic financial data, TimeGAN-generated sequences closely replicate volatility clustering, autocorrelation structures, and extreme events of real markets, while VAEs produce smoother sequences that are stable but less faithful to market extremes.

A statistical framework for skill-vs-chance in online fantasy cricket compares deterministic and stochastic team selection strategies (recent form, historical statistics, statistical optimization, multi-criteria decision making), evaluated on points, ranks, and payoff under two contest structures: Mega and 4x-or-Nothing.

The fantasy cricket skill study introduces a dynamic tournament model capturing adaptive participant behavior, and notes that integrating richer contextual data (real-time player form, weather, credit points) would further bridge simulation and reality.

In conformal prediction, exact distribution-free conditional coverage is impossible with finite samples; standard quantile regression with pinball loss is identified as a fundamental limitation because the conformalization step fixes coverage bias but variance reduction requires capturing heteroscedasticity.

Colorful Pinball derives, via Taylor expansion, a sharp surrogate objective for quantile regression: a density-weighted pinball loss where the weights are the conditional density of the conformity score evaluated at the true quantile, implemented as a three-headed quantile network that estimates these weights by finite differences to minimize the MSE of conditional coverage probabilities.

A covariate-dependent Hidden Markov Model (CDHMM) for football corner kicks infers time-resolved man-marking and zonal defensive assignments directly from player tracking data with no labels, supporting a defensive credit-attribution framework and a role-conditioned ghosting method for counterfactual analysis of off-ball defense.

The off-ball defense study evaluates learned defensive assignments by normalized observation log-likelihood (per-frame, pooled across teams and random seeds) as a function of training sample size, separately for inswinging and outswinging deliveries, to assess assignment stability.

STIPP (space-time in situ postprocessing) is an ML model that generates spatio-temporally consistent probabilistic weather forecasts for a station network over the French Alps, making hourly ensemble predictions from only a six-hourly deterministic forecast, with increased accuracy for surface temperature, wind, relative humidity, and precipitation versus baselines.

STIPP's fully spatio-temporal strategy outperforms a time-independent equivalent, and multivariate training losses on proper scoring rules improve the physical plausibility of the generated forecasts; it demonstrates temporal interpolation beyond typical postprocessing models.

TASC is a state-space framework for synthetic control-type data with algorithms for model learning and counterfactual inference; by explicitly modeling temporal evolution of latent time-factors it achieves strong long-term predictive performance, remains effective under high observational noise, leverages larger donor pools, is robust to hyperparameter d, and produces narrower confidence intervals than CIM.
TASC's stated limitation is that it models only a single time series, despite multivariate data being available.

Topological portfolios define an estimation error-free risk measure called Topological Risk: each asset's topological risk is the squared error of the asset's time series of Lp norms of persistence landscapes from the norm of the mean persistence landscape, and the portfolio's topological risk combines the asset-level topological dynamics.

The topological portfolio paper compares TDA-based (persistent homology) portfolios against classical portfolios, aiming for robust, reliable, and stable outcomes by combining topological dynamics of each asset.

eSkiTB is the first neuromorphic (event-camera) benchmark for tracking skiers in broadcast footage; event streams are generated under a strict iso-informational constraint to address RGB trackers' failure on motion blur, static overlays, and clutter that obscure fast-moving athletes.

Event cameras isolate the athlete's independent motion from the event stream, letting a tracker focus on the skier; the authors note broader application to autonomous ski-filming drones, where neuromorphic control loops could offer safer following in visually congested alpine terrain.

The Bayesian Intransitive Bradley-Terry model embeds combinatorial Hodge theory into a logistic framework, decomposing pairwise comparisons into a gradient flow representing transitive strength and a curl flow capturing cycle-induced (intransitive) structure, rather than explaining all comparisons solely through subject-specific parameters.

In BIBT experiments, data imbalance accelerates degradation of reliable intransitivity detection: precision begins deteriorating at lower sparsity levels in imbalanced settings than in balanced settings (where comparable decline appears only at sparsity 0.9), underscoring the need to account for heterogeneity in paired comparison data.

BoxMind is a closed-loop AI expert system for boxing that parses match footage into 18 hierarchical technical-tactical indicators from atomic punch events with precise temporal boundaries and spatial/technical attributes, then fuses explicit tactical profiles with learnable time-variant latent embeddings in a graph-based predictive model of matchup dynamics.
