BoxMind models match outcome as a differentiable function of technical-tactical indicators and converts winning-probability gradients into executable tactical adjustments via the tactical gradient G_b = partial y-hat / partial I_{b,ind} = [partial y-hat/partial i_1, ..., partial y-hat/partial i_18].

BoxMind was deployed in the full preparation cycle of the Chinese National Boxing Team for the 2024 Paris Olympics, with its closed-loop interventions providing consistent, quantifiable, opponent-specific tactical guidance.

In a climate-economics model with an ad hoc positive lower bound D on consumption (fear of ruin / value-of-statistical-life parameter), expected value is bounded via E[M] = beta * integral_{-inf}^{inf} e^{-eta Y} f(y) dy, where f(y) is the pdf of Y.
Utility with a subsistence/death lower bound D: U(C;D) = (C^{1-eta} - D^{1-eta})/(1-eta) when C >= D > 0, and 0 otherwise (normalizing D to one relates it to the value of statistical life).
Newton's method is stated as the fixed-point iteration g(x) = x - f(x)/f'(x) with x_{n+1} = g(x_n); the Babylonian square-root iteration is f(x) = (1/2)(a/x + x).
Gradient descent iteration x_{n+1} = x_n - gamma * nabla f(x_n), with linear convergence bound |x_n - x*| <= q^n/(1-q) * |x_1 - x_0|.

Two-way fixed effects (TWFE) regression: when the distribution of the continuous treatment dose is symmetric and close to normal, TWFE weights are close or identical to weighting the average causal response ACR(d) parameters by the distribution of D; skewed dose distributions distort the TWFE weights.

Bradley-Terry model: P(Y_ij = i beats j) = gamma_i/(gamma_i+gamma_j); with u_i = log gamma_i this equals exp(u_i)/(exp(u_i)+exp(u_j)) = sigma(u_i - u_j), where sigma(x) = (1+exp(-x))^{-1} is the logistic sigmoid.

A fundamental open problem in Bradley-Terry statistical theory is a unified asymptotic theory (e.g., uniform consistency of the MLE) that applies to heterogeneous comparison graphs; special cases exist but no systematic framework for general graph structures is established, in the regime where both object count and comparison volume tend to infinity.

L-RAPM (Lineup Regularized Adjusted Plus-Minus) is an NBA lineup-regularized adjusted plus-minus method; it cites the empirical finding that offensive performance of a lineup/team stabilizes faster than defensive performance (Partnow 2021).

The L-RAPM paper's reference set includes Deshpande & Jensen (2016) on estimating an NBA player's impact on team win probability and Lopez, Matthews & Baumer (2018) on how often the best team wins (a unified approach to randomness in North American sport).

Applying conformal prediction to time series is challenged because temporal dependencies violate the exchangeability assumption underlying standard CP guarantees; the survey benchmarks fixes including relaxing exchangeability, redefining the data unit as collections of independent series, and modeling residual dynamics.

For modular multi-horizon forecasting pipelines, horizon-specific split conformal prediction (MSCP) was found the most robust and efficient distribution-free uncertainty quantification approach, because horizon-specific calibration accounts for temporal dependencies; online controllers ACI and AcMCP remain competitive and adaptable to non-stationary environments.

Live win-probability forecast sequences can be modeled as the Doob martingale of conditional win probabilities for a binary terminal outcome: p_k = P(Y=1|F_k) for k=0..N, enabling sharp distributional laws for the path maximum (the 'blown lead' statistic).

For a binary Doob martingale's running maximum M_N, the discrete-time CDF satisfies F_{M_N}(x) >= 1 - p_0/x for x in [p_0,1), with equality when P(tau_x = N)=0 and p_{tau_x}=x a.s. on {tau_x < N}; under continuous-path regularity the correction terms (last-step crossings, overshoots) disappear yielding exact identities.

The Blown Lead Paradox paper derives closed-form distributions for two extensions: the maximal win probability attained by the eventual loser in a two-player game, and the minimal win probability attained by the eventual winner — converting subjective 'collapse' narratives into objective, testable claims about model calibration.

A DeepHit neural network was tested for time-to-injury forecasting from longitudinal athlete monitoring data, using the public SoccerMon dataset (two seasons of training, match, and wellness records from elite female footballers), with cleaning, feature engineering, and three imputation strategies; baselines were Random Forest, XGBoost, and Logistic Regression optimized via grid search.

An agent-based model of a prediction market populates bettors with heterogeneous expertise, noisy private information, and variable learning rates to study how high-budget agents introduce price distortions, how those distortions persist under herding or stubborn agents, and how agent expertise affects market-price variance.

As an empirical benchmark, the prediction-market manipulation study compares PredictIt daily closing share prices to Economist weekly state-level presidential election forecasts in 2016 (May 10-Nov 8) and 2020 (Mar 1-Nov 3), finding price-vs-forecast differences of 5-30 percentage points, indicating stark variability in predictive accuracy.

ProSkill is the first benchmark dataset for action-level skill assessment in procedural videos, providing both absolute and pairwise skill annotations through a scalable ELO-based annotation protocol that combines crowdsourcing efficiency with tournament-style comparison reliability.

On ProSkill, existing state-of-the-art skill-assessment methods from more constrained or domain-specific settings underperform, particularly on global ranking tasks; pairwise methods generally yield better results, but overall performance shows skill assessment remains hard.

A calibrated probabilistic aggregation framework converts site-level probabilistic forecasts into reliable fleet-level (system) forecasts for renewable energy by combining copula-based dependence modeling of cross-site correlations with a Context-Aware Conformal Prediction (CACP) calibration step at the aggregated level, in settings where centralized fleet-level models cannot be trained or maintained.

BPASGM (Best-Path Algorithm Sparse Graphical Model) extends the Best-Path Algorithm to portfolio construction: it represents linear and nonlinear dependencies among many assets as a sparse graphical model with a structural Markov property, then filters out positively or redundantly connected assets to isolate conditionally independent or negatively correlated subsets for diversification.

BPASGM targets practical limitations of sample-based mean-variance optimization in high-dimensional problems (estimation error); it explicitly does not claim to improve on the theoretical mean-variance optimum defined under known population parameters.

Learning with abstention is formalized for multi-horizon time-series forecasting (simultaneous predictions for a consecutive sequence of future steps), where existing single-prediction abstention strategies are ill-suited; three instantiations are proposed: full abstention, partial abstention, and interval abstention, with progressively more flexibility to selectively predict.

Any differentiable nonconformity score induces a deterministic flow on the output space whose trajectories converge to the boundary of the corresponding conformal prediction set, giving a computationally efficient training-free method for sampling conformal boundaries in arbitrary dimensions; boundary samples can be reconformalized into pointwise prediction sets with controlled risk and repulsed along the boundary to improve geometric coverage.

Kelly Betting as Bayesian Model Evaluation treats each time-updating probabilistic forecast model (e.g., an in-game win probability model or election forecast) as a canonical Kelly bettor and pits models against each other in an iterative contest; each model's bankroll growth/decline serves as the evaluation metric, updating market consensus probabilities and implied model credibilities in real time without waiting for final outcomes.

Via simulation, the Kelly-betting model-evaluation method is shown to be generally more accurate than traditional average log-loss and Brier score methods at distinguishing a correct model from an incorrect model; it has a direct mathematical and conceptual link to Bayesian model evaluation.

A statistical framework forecasts American football defensive coverage schemes (man vs zone) from player tracking data, integrating supervised and unsupervised learning: elastic net logistic regression and gradient-boosted decision trees on incrementally derived features (pre-motion features, then motion trajectories, then features from a non-homogeneous HMM that infers latent defensive assignments between offensive and defensive players during motion).

Neural ordinary differential equations can model the time evolution of non-cyclic full-body baseball pitching motion as a low-dimensional latent dynamical system, accurately predicting the motion (R^2 > 0.45); approximately 50% of the variance in the latter half of the pitching motion was explained using only the initial ~8% of the movement sequence, suggesting complex non-cyclic movements evolve from their initial state according to the ODE-defined latent flow.

An inference-based probabilistic framework built on expected goals (xG) converts shot-level event data into season-level simulations of points, rankings, and outcome probabilities; applied to the English Premier League 2015/16 season, it captures the overall league-table structure, correctly identifies top-four contenders and relegation candidates, and explains a significant portion of variance in final points and ranks — providing a quantitative lens on Leicester City's title as a rare result differing greatly from expectations.

In distribution-free sequential prediction with abstentions (semi-adversarial setting where an adversary injects arbitrarily many corrupted instances but the learner may abstain penalty-free on corrupted ones), sublinear abstention and misclassification errors are achievable for general VC classes without knowing the clean-sample distribution mu, against oblivious adversaries; a finite 'reduction dimension' structural property of the function class enables learning against adaptive adversaries, with a polynomial-form tradeoff between abstention and misclassification errors.

STATS X is a latent contribution index quantifying a player's involvement in favorable dominance intervals identified by a T-process: a continuous dominance indicator (T-score) mapping final scores to real values consistent with win/lose outcomes, formulated as a time-evolving stochastic representation driven by standardized cumulative box-score statistics, enabling sequential analytically tractable in-game win probability updates and decomposition of competitive advantage into interpretable components.
The T-score satisfies |T(a,b)-1| = |a-b|/max(a,b) for the c=1 form, and an alternative form T(a,b) = log((a+kappa)/(b+kappa)) with kappa>0, c=0.

Case study of the Chiba Jets (basketball): their strong T-process is driven by extremely high baseline strength (large alpha_0), scoring ability, and defensive rebounds; |alpha_5| approx |alpha_1| quantitatively suggests defensive control, not only offense, supports their top win rate, while the offensive-rebound coefficient is negative but not significant (p=0.648).

Using 292 million trades across 327,000 binary contracts on Kalshi and Polymarket, prediction-market calibration decomposes into four components (a universal horizon effect, domain-specific biases, domain-by-horizon interactions, and a trade-size scale effect) that together explain 87.3% of calibration variance on Kalshi.

The dominant calibration pattern in prediction markets is persistent underconfidence in political markets, where prices are chronically compressed toward 50% — a bias that generalizes across both Kalshi and Polymarket; all crowds show a favourite-longshot bias at long horizons with prices compressed toward 50%, understating favoured outcomes' probability, but political-event traders exhibit this compression at nearly every horizon.

Bayesian Parametric Portfolio Policies: because portfolio weights are linear in policy parameters and utility is concave, parametric portfolio policies systematically overstate achievable expected utility by an amount proportional to parameter uncertainty and signal scale; the correction follows from Jensen's inequality applied to the posterior distribution of policy parameters, and the Bayesian rule integrates expected utility over that posterior.

AdaSpot is a precise-event-spotting framework for video that processes low-resolution video for global task-relevant features while adaptively selecting, via an unsupervised mechanism, the most informative region-of-interest in each frame for high-resolution processing — preserving fine-grained visual cues for precise temporal localization of fast-paced actions at lower compute than uniformly raising baseline resolution.

BRIDGE is a system that detects and tracks players from broadcast video to generate 3D play sequences and translates stand-up basketball demonstrations into wheelchair-based representations, using an embodiment-aware visualization framework that decomposes head, trunk, and wheelchair base orientations to represent attention, intent, and mobility.

In controlled studies with 20 participants (10 national wheelchair basketball team players, 10 amateurs), BRIDGE significantly enhanced perceived naturalness of player postures, made tactical intentions easier to understand, supported functional classification by conveying players' capabilities, and enhanced learners' self-efficacy and vividness of mental imagery.

An augmented Glicko-based rating system for Test cricket incorporates home advantage and toss impact into the expected-score formulation via logistic marginals and a bivariate copula, plus an interpretable Margin-of-Victory scaling of rating updates; it demonstrates improved expected score estimation and predictive accuracy over the ICC system, with rating stability confirmed by bootstrap resampling against scheduling imbalances.

For Test cricket, the optimal Elo/Glicko scaling factor is d=85, substantially smaller than the chess default d=400; the Glicko expected score is E_A = 1/(1+10^{-(R_A-R_B)g(RD_B)/400}) with g(RD) = 1/sqrt(1+3 RD^2/pi^2).
Glicko rating deviation updates: updated RD_A' = 1/sqrt(1/RD_A^2 + 1/d^2) with d^2 = 1/(g(RD_B)^2 E_A (1-E_A)); updated rating r_A' = r_A + (RD_A')^2 g(RD_B)(S_A - E_A).

A monocular video pipeline recovers 18 clinically relevant pitching biomechanics metrics from broadcast baseball footage (estimates 3D pose then applies a refinement stack: global lifting, bone-length enforcement, constrained IK, smoothing, symmetry), validated against professional tracking data across 13 professional pitchers, positioning pose-derived kinematics as a scalable injury-risk screening tool where stadium multi-camera systems are unavailable.

A Dual-Transformer-Cascaded (DTC) architecture with environmental priors predicts tennis ball landing points from a single 2D industrial camera + YOLO detection + ball launch machine: module 1 extracts prior information (critical prior points), module 2 classifies trajectories 'in' vs 'out' relative to court boundaries, module 3 predicts landing point coordinates; first-level transformer classifies the trajectory while the second level handles landing prediction.

The flying-trajectory framework uses normalized Gaussian kernels: Kernel(x,y) = 1/(2 pi sigma^2) e^{-(x^2+y^2)/(2 sigma^2)}, normalized over the frame grid, for prior-point heatmap construction via convolution I_p(i,j) = sum_{u,v} I_0(u,v) Kernel_n(i-u, j-v).

Tabular foundation models (TabPFN, TabICL) produce full predictive distributions but are benchmarked almost exclusively on point metrics (RMSE, R^2), which rewards a good conditional mean while ignoring distribution quality; the paper supplements point metrics with proper scoring rules (CRPS, CRLS, Interval Score) in a head-to-head comparison of realTabPFNv2.5 vs TabICLv2 across 20 OpenML regression datasets.

Analytically and empirically, different proper scoring rules induce different model rankings and different inductive biases during training — each rule is individually minimized by the true distribution in the population sense, but they exhibit different finite-sample regularization effects and differ substantially in computational tractability; choosing a scoring rule for tabular foundation model pretraining remains open.

Transfer-Informed Betting (TIB) warm-starts the WSR wealth process using a source domain's risk profile for selective prediction with risk control; the paper proves the TIB wealth process remains a valid supermartingale under all source-target divergences, TIB dominates standard WSR when domains match, and no data-independent warm-start can achieve better convergence (source-informed initialization is optimal among plug-in priors).

Across an ablation of nine finite-sample bound families (Hoeffding, Empirical Bernstein, Clopper-Pearson, Wasserstein DRO, CVaR; union bound, Learn-Then-Test fixed-sequence; WSR betting confidence sequences) on four benchmarks, the practical recipe is: large calibration sets (n >= 500) use WSR Betting + LTT or LTT + Empirical Bernstein — on MASSIVE both achieve 94.0% coverage.

The Confidence Gate Theorem: confidence-based abstention monotonically improves ranked decision quality if and only if the confidence function contains no inversion zones (C2), with pointwise rank-accuracy alignment (C1) as a practically verifiable sufficient condition; the key determinant is uncertainty type — structural uncertainty (cold-start, data sparsity) satisfies both conditions and yields monotonic gains, while contextual uncertainty (temporal drift) breaks them.

The confidence-gating distinction was validated across three domains — collaborative filtering (MovieLens, 3 distribution shifts), e-commerce intent detection (RetailRocket, Criteo, Yoochoose), and clinical pathway triage (MIMIC-IV): structural uncertainty produces near-monotonic abstention gains in all domains, while contextual uncertainty causes structurally grounded confidence signals to produce no fewer violations than random abstention.

Brenier isotonic regression extends shape-constrained isotonic regression to multi-output settings by requiring the regression function to be cyclically monotone (the gradient of a convex potential); since Kantorovich optimal transport always yields a cyclically monotone coupling, the regression function and convex potential can be interpreted as a link function in generalized linear models and Brenier's OT potential respectively, with demonstrated applications to probabilistic recalibration.

Brenier isotonic regression as a recalibrator was compared against Bin, Dir, IRP, IR, MS, OI, TS baselines by confidence calibration error (lower better, averaged over 10 trials, Mann-Whitney U at 5% significance), e.g., on balance-scale it achieves 0.012-0.023 vs baselines 0.010-0.062 depending on k.

Across nine diverse credit risk benchmark datasets, predictive multiplicity (conflicting outcomes for the same applicant from multiple near-optimal models in the Rashomon set) concentrates in regions of low predictive confidence, and minority class observations bear a disproportionate multiplicity burden; post-hoc calibration mitigates this algorithmic arbitrariness and yields more consistent final predictions and more stable confidence behavior.

TennisVL is a large-scale tennis benchmark with over 200 professional matches (471.9 hours) and 40,000+ rally-level clips annotated with expert analytical commentary (tactical reasoning, player decisions, match momentum) rather than descriptive play-by-play; TennisExpert is a fine-grained context-aware framework built on a video semantic parser and hierarchical memory that outperforms leading open-source and proprietary MLLMs while remaining efficient for real-time deployment.

TennisExpert's frame-level modeling: commentary C_t = MLLM(V_t, M_t, H_t); short-term context S_t = {(V_i, M_i, C_i) | i = t-K,...,t-1}; autoregressive objective log p(C_t | V_t, M_t, H_t) = sum_{j=1..L} log p_theta(w_j | w_{<j}, Z_v^{(t)}, Z_s^{(t)}).

For a single event with finitely many mutually exclusive outcomes, the full Kelly problem (maximize expected log wealth over nonnegative stakes plus optional cash) admits a short state-price derivation: a cash fraction c acts as an implicit position in every outcome, equivalent to a baseline stake c*q_i on outcome i (q_i = state price); on any active support, explicit bets only top up favorable outcomes from baseline c*q_i to the optimal total stake p_i, giving x_i = (p_i - c*q_i)_+ with threshold rule p_i/q_i > c and, after sorting by p_i/q_i, one-pass greedy support selection.

Distributionally robust quantile regression under type-p Wasserstein ambiguity sets has a closed-form worst-case quantile regression loss, yielding transparent convex regularized reformulations; the check loss is (for p>1) the only class of convex loss functions for which such additive Wasserstein regularization holds, and finite-sample out-of-sample risk guarantees of order O(N^{-1/2}) hold under mild moment conditions.

Wasserstein DR quantile regression shows sharp qualitative differences between p=1 and p>1 regimes: for p>1, slope coefficients coincide with the regularized formulation while the intercept undergoes a radius-dependent adjustment; the order p affects only this intercept correction, whereas the choice of transport norm influences both intercept and slope.

A generic spatio-temporal graph-based model for team sports represents attacking play as a directed path containing absolute and relative ball-carrier-centered spatial information, temporal information, and semantic information; applied to six-player union rugby from French clubs, preliminary results indicate notable effects of coaching pedagogy and initial defensive positioning on team coordination, though tiny data size allows only general trends, not strong assertions.

Horizon-aware anytime-valid tests and confidence sequences for bounded means under a strict deadline N cast horizon-aware betting as a finite-horizon optimal control problem with state (t, log W_t); when on schedule, substantial deviations from Kelly betting are provably suboptimal while Kelly reaches the threshold with high probability; when behind schedule, aggressive bets can increase the probability of crossing by N; when ahead, defensive bets mitigate unrecoverable drawdowns.

For diversity-aware multi-armed bandits over generative models (where a non-degenerate mixture of generators can outperform any individual model), the UCB exploration bonus consistently slows convergence and often reduces sample efficiency; a simple Mixture-Greedy strategy without explicit UCB-type optimism converges faster and achieves better performance, particularly for FID and Vendi metrics — i.e., exploration comes for free.

Mixture-Greedy's advantage is robust to feature representation: across three feature spaces, RKE increases and KID decreases over training with unchanged method ranking (Mixture Oracle best, Mixture Greedy very close, Mixture UCB worst), demonstrating stable convergence not tied to a particular feature extractor.

CRPS-Optimal Binning: non-parametric conditional distribution estimation by partitioning covariate-sorted observations into contiguous bins and using the within-bin empirical CDF as the predictive distribution; bin boundaries minimize total leave-one-out CRPS with closed-form cost cost(S) = mW/(m-1)^2 (a single pairwise-dispersion scalar), recoverable exactly by dynamic programming in O(n^2 K) time after O(n^2 log n) precomputation.

Minimizing within-sample LOO-CRPS is inappropriate for selecting the bin count K (in-sample optimism); instead K is selected by evaluating test CRPS on an alternating held-out split, which yields a U-shaped criterion with a well-defined minimum; the fitted full-data partition then feeds conformal prediction using the within-bin ECDF as both predictive distribution and nonconformity score.

ParlayMarket is the first automated market-making design supporting parlay-style joint contracts within a unified liquidity pool with coherent pricing across base markets and their combinations; the joint distribution is represented by a pairwise exponential-family model compressing the 2^M outcome space into O(M^2) sufficient statistics.

The ParlayMarket historical-market replay models correlated base markets as dS_i(t) = sigma_i dW_i(t) with Cov(dW_i, dW_j) = rho_ij dt, so S_T | S_t ~ N(S_t, Sigma); in the full-market emulation, the signal extracted from each trade is its target price (informed traders move the market to the price implied by their information) and the AMM updates from that post-trade price.

In chain-reaction systems where components activate sequentially and upstream failures suppress downstream effects, the causal structure is uniquely identifiable from blocking interventions that prevent individual components from activating; the paper proposes a minimal estimator with finite-sample guarantees achieving exponential error decay and logarithmic sample complexity.

Experiments on synthetic models and diverse chain-reaction environments show reliable causal recovery from a few blocking interventions, while purely observational heuristics fail in regimes with delayed or overlapping causal effects.

A basketball shot-chart modeling study (STAMP) comparing model specifications by estimated expected log predictive density found conclusions robust across PC prior scale choices (U_sd=1.5, U_slope=1.0) passing prior predictive checks, with the richest models ranking at or near the top; adding team-level slopes for lay_up, floater, rim_finishes, and fade_turn gave only modest incremental improvements in elpd_post^MC, suggesting the simpler slope structure retains most predictive and explanatory power.

TacSIm is the first large-scale dataset and benchmark for multi-agent tactical style imitation in football: it imitates the actions of all 11 players of one team from single-view Premier League broadcast footage, projecting all 22 players' beginning positions and actions onto a standard pitch coordinate system under offensive or defensive phases, with a structured tactical phase taxonomy and phase-aware evaluation protocol.

Tactical style imitation in TacSIm is measured by spatial occupancy similarity and movement vector similarity over defined time windows, supporting evaluation of spatial and temporal similarities for coordinated team behaviors; experiments show TacSIm distinguishes models that merely extrapolate motion from those that capture collective tactical organization.

A factorized attention-based transformer applied to NFL multi-agent play tracking data predicts individual coverage assignments, receiver-defender matchups, and the targeted defender on every pass play; the factorized attention mechanism separates temporal and agent dimensions to model player movement patterns and inter-player relationships independently, trained on randomly truncated trajectories with frame-by-frame prediction.

The NFL coverage model achieves approximately 89%+ accuracy across target defender identification, receiver-defender matchup prediction, and coverage assignment classification; true accuracy may be higher given human labeling ambiguity, with model predictions consistently defensible and often preferable to human annotations in gray-area situations.

The Load Management Paradox: naive survival models on NBA game-log data yield the paradoxical finding that players with recent heavy minutes appear less likely to get injured; the paper demonstrates this is an artifact of the healthy-worker survivor effect — conditioning on game participation induces severe collider bias driven by unobserved latent fitness — and a simulation confirms this selection mechanism is mathematically sufficient to entirely reverse the sign of the workload-injury relationship.

To correct the healthy-worker survivor effect in NBA injury modeling, the paper develops a Marginal Structural Piecewise Exponential Model (MS-PEM) unifying inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) with flexible piecewise-exponential additive models and weighted cumulative exposure (WCE); player archetypes were built from five summary-statistic domains (volume, availability, usage, playmaking, defense/physicality, efficiency), standardized, PCA-reduced (85% variance), and K-means clustered over k in {3,...,7} selecting max silhouette score.

A semiparametric framework for paired comparisons with covariates (e.g., home-field advantage) models item merits and covariate effects via latent random variables with unspecified distributions, relaxing parametric assumptions; a kernel-based least squares approach estimates all unknown parameters with explicit expressions, extendable to many items, and model averaging over candidate special regressors (averaging estimates from looping over each) is proposed for robustness.

Using 2021 NFL regular-season Hudl tracking data, two ridge-regularized Bradley-Terry paired-comparison models evaluate NFL pass blocking and pass rushing at the player level: a binary win/loss model aligned with the 2.5-second pass block win-rate definition and a four-class severity model over loss/win/hit/sack, both with a double-team indicator; the dataset contains 153,138 interactions across 33,283 pass plays in 266 games.

On an ordered 80/20 holdout split (n_test=30,628), both NFL pass-block BT models improve on global baselines and modestly outperform stronger matchup baselines under log-loss evaluation; the severity formulation shows the strongest external alignment with All-Pro selections.

PolySwarm is a multi-agent LLM framework for real-time prediction market trading and latency arbitrage on decentralized platforms like Polymarket: a swarm of 50 diverse LLM personas concurrently evaluates binary outcome markets, aggregating probability estimates through confidence-weighted Bayesian combination of swarm consensus with market-implied probabilities, with quarter-Kelly position sizing and an information-theoretic engine (KL/JS divergence) detecting cross-market inefficiencies and negation-pair mispricings.
PolySwarm's latency arbitrage module exploits stale Polymarket prices by deriving CEX-implied probabilities from a log-normal pricing model and executing trades within the latency window.

For fixed prior scales, the Bayes decision rule induced by deep fully-connected feedforward ReLU Bayesian neural networks in the normal location model under quadratic loss is NOT minimax, because the prior predictive density has stretched-exponential tails that apply overly conservative shrinkage to large signals.

A Beta-Prime hyperprior on the effective output variance of a BNN prior induces a superharmonic square-root marginal density with sufficiently heavy tails — strong shrinkage toward the origin for weak signals, rapidly reduced shrinkage for large signals — yielding a decision rule that is simultaneously admissible and minimax; results extend to predictive density estimation under KL loss.

Tracking 5,467 pre-match slips (~$4.8M in tracked bets) from three prominent Nigerian sports tipsters on X/Telegram and verifying outcomes against official Stake.com records to bypass survivorship bias, the study finds the influencers collectively lost 25.24% on their promoted bets, and following their public predictions was consistently associated with systemic capital loss across all four tested staking strategies (Flat, Inverse, Square Root, Fixed Return) — a sharp contrast with their displayed wealth.

A score-driven rating system generalizes Elo by using the score (gradient of the log-likelihood of game outcomes) as the rating update mechanism, accommodating win/draw/loss, point differences, and complete rankings; the score has zero expected value, sums to zero across players, and decreases with the player's own rating, ensuring internal consistency, fairness, and a reversion property toward unobserved true skills over time.

The classical Elo update recovered within the score-driven framework: r_t^{(A)} = r_t^{(A)} + 16 (y_t^{(A)} - 1/(1+10^{-(r_t^{(A)}-r_t^{(B)})/400})), with E[Y_t^{(A)}|r_t^{(A)},r_t^{(B)}] = 1/(1+10^{-(r_t^{(A)}-r_t^{(B)})/400}).

A research blueprint for studying institutional liquidity entering prediction markets separates market-quality channels (spreads, price discovery, forecast quality, internal consistency, trader-level welfare) and the distinct empirical objects of maker designation, incentive design, automation intensity, and participant-composition shifts; the synthetic microstructure proof-of-concept shows market-maker coverage, liquidity incentives, and automation need not work through the same channels.

A deployed DFS match recommendation engine adapts the Deep Interest Network (DIN) architecture by injecting temporality at two levels: real-time urgency features per candidate match (e.g., time-to-round-lock) and temporal positional encodings representing the time-gap between each historical interaction and the current request, so the model dynamically weighs recency of past actions for the time-critical pre-game window.

An unsupervised decision-support framework for multivariate biomarker analysis in athlete monitoring operates directly in the joint biomarker space, overcoming univariate and binary risk models to enable etiological differentiation between mechanical and metabolic stress responses; meaningful physiological phenotypes — including a latent 'silent risk' phenotype — were identified even under the small-sample conditions typical of real-world sports environments.

A geospatial framework for climate risk stress testing in California integrates physical hazard mapping (wildfires, drought, flooding, extreme heat), sector-specific exposure analysis (banking, agriculture, real estate, tourism), and scenario-based financial risk assessment; its central argument is that climate stress testing in finance becomes substantially more informative by mapping local hazard intensity into expected loss, repricing, and capital vulnerability rather than relying on generic disclosure.

The Odds-Only-Equal-Profitability-Confidence (OO-EPC) method converts betting odds to outcome probabilities without historical data, aligning with bookmakers' pricing objective of having equal confidence in profitability for each outcome; on a dataset of 90,014 football matches across five bookmakers it outperforms existing odds-only methods (Multiplicative, Shin, Power) in accuracy for the majority of bookmakers, and both Shin-method variants are shown to make assumptions unsupported by the data.

The paper also proposes a generalised linear model approach for converting betting odds into accurate outcome probabilities when historical data are available, providing a foundation for using odds as a benchmark for sports forecasting models under different data-availability situations.

A model-quality study of the Expected Threat (xT) model in football — which generalizes xG by describing the probability of scoring a goal in subsequent play from the current state — warns that increased data availability has increased the risk of incorrect use of data-driven models: conclusions based on insignificant differences are pitfalls, so xT/xG models must be accompanied by validation guidelines on how and when to use them.

A tick-level Polymarket order-book archive (30 billion events over 52 days) joined to the authoritative on-chain trade record, on a pre-registered stratified panel of 600 markets, reports eight stylized facts: a longshot spread premium; depth concentrated closer to a uniform geometric grid than the assumed top-of-book pattern; null block-clock alignment effect; broad maker-wallet diversity with a concentrated tail; category-conditional effective spread differences; sub-50ms median archive-ingestion delay with a multi-second tail; and self-counterparty wash share with median 1% and 22% upper tail.

The Polymarket microstructure study finds maker liquidity broadly decentralised with a thin tail dominated by a few wallets, and self-counterparty wash activity low under a direct-detection lower bound — benchmarks compared against Cong et al. (2023) network-classifier results on unregulated cryptocurrency token exchanges.

Prior-agnostic robust forecast aggregation assumes the aggregator observes only experts' reports while being ignorant of both the joint information structure and the full prior, including the state space; allowing unknown binary state values to be arbitrary numbers in [0,1] (so the same reported probability may correspond to very different realized outcome frequencies across environments), the paper derives a simple explicit closed-form log-odds aggregator that linearly pools forecasts, with rounded regret bounds (baselines to 4 decimals, results to 6).

For simultaneous bets (multivariate Kelly), the naive formulation scales as O(2^N) in time and memory; for independent bets, an integral-transform formulation eliminates explicit outcome enumeration, reducing objective evaluation to O(N) per function evaluation and enabling accurate solutions for hundreds of simultaneous bets; a decomposition-based approach additionally constructs tractable subproblems with computable lower and upper bounds.
Efficient multivariate Kelly optimization at scale reveals sigmoidal scaling laws in the multivariate Kelly problem's behavior.

Conformal prediction is applied to conflict forecasting: given a country's conflict history, CP on temporally-dependent data (assumed discrete-state Markov process) yields prediction sets of possible future conflict state-sequences that are finite-sample valid for any prespecified confidence level and robust to model misspecification; beyond achieving nominal coverage, CP's advantage over likelihood-based simulation grows as misspecification increases.

ConformaDecompose is an uncertainty-aware explainability framework for conformal regression that decomposes predictive uncertainty into calibration-induced epistemic (reducible) and irreducible components via progressive calibration localization: it explains how conformal intervals contract and stabilize as calibration support is localized around a test instance, giving a four-part explanation (uncertainty localization trajectory; global vs localized interval widths; evolution of calibration support; whether interval width is reducible).

ForesightFlow is an information-theoretic framework for quantifying informed flow on prediction markets: the Information Leakage Score (ILS) is a label generator quantifying how much of a market's terminal information move was priced in before the corresponding public news event, admitting a Murphy-decomposition reading connecting ILS to the proper-scoring-rule literature; the task is reformulated from post-hoc forensics to real-time inference, requiring all inference-time features to be causal in the available information.

The ForesightFlow paper notes recent empirical work documented hundreds of millions of dollars in anomalous profits on Polymarket between 2024 and 2026, while existing detection approaches are almost exclusively post-hoc and offer no actionable signal during the window when informed flow is moving prices.

April 2026 saw methodological convergence in studying informed trading on decentralized prediction markets: two approaches applied a composite statistical screen to over 210,000 wallet-market pairs estimating $143 million in aggregate anomalous profit; one applied event-level sign-randomization to the platform's complete transaction history, classifying 3.14% of accounts as 'skilled winners' driving most price discovery and flagging 1,950 accounts as 'insiders' via a single-event lifecycle-and-conviction heuristic; and the ILS framework quantifies per-market information front-loading.

Selective Prediction from Agreement: in the fixed-pool (transductive) setting, given queried labels and Lipschitz margin constraints in an embedding space, the version space of Lipschitz-consistent classification heads is well defined; upper and lower Lipschitz margin bounds define per-pool-point certified valid label sets, and the model predicts only when all consistent heads agree (label is forced), abstaining otherwise; forced pseudo-labels can be reused via a closure property without changing version-space semantics.
For budgeted querying in the fixed-pool setting, a monotone submodular geometric proxy is proposed for which a greedy algorithm retains the standard (1-1/e) approximation factor.

Cross-individual generalizability of ML models for ball-speed prediction in baseball pitching (50 pitchers, leave-one-subject-out CV): predictive performance was markedly lower cross-individual than within-individual, with R^2 decreasing from 0.91 to 0.38; ML models tend to overestimate Intermediate pitchers' performance relative to Experts; trunk and pivot leg show high generalizability, with the pivot leg retaining R^2 > 0.25 even during the weight-shift initiation phase.

Aggregating Elo Ratings axiomatization: under three conditions — same-scale normalization, recursive consistency, and marginal Elo-strength consistency (for two equally weighted coordinates, the ratio of marginal contributions to the combined rating equals the ordinary Elo odds) — the unique aggregation rule converts each component to its Elo strength, takes a weighted aggregation, and converts back, yielding a single scalar rating on the Elo scale.

An in-play football forecasting model extending the Weibull accelerated failure time model — half-specific hazard parameters, post-shot expected goals as a time-varying covariate, and team-strength parameters jointly calibrated to Betfair Exchange 1X2 and over/under prices at kick-off via squared-error minimization — almost matches Betfair's classification accuracy across 140 English Premier League matches at minute intervals (70.2% vs 70.6%) while retaining interpretable team-level parameters.

The Weibull goal-arrival model uses Weibull(gamma, lambda_H) and Weibull(gamma, lambda_A) waiting times for home/away goals; the calibration approach (jointly fitting team strengths to 1X2 and over/under markets) applies to any intensity-based goal arrival model and was confirmed against a Bayesian birth process and a Cox process calibrated to the same pre-match odds.

Entrywise error bounds for spectral Bradley-Terry-Luce ranking under a semi-random adversary that can arbitrarily boost sampling probabilities of certain edges: the unweighted spectral method's performance depends heavily on the spectral properties of the generated graph, but asymptotic performance approaching uniformly-sampled graphs can be recovered by appropriately reweighting observed edges to counteract the adversary.

Chernoff-type matrix concentration bounds are established for the largest eigenvalue of sums of Hermitian random matrices generated by a time-inhomogeneous Markov chain, assuming compact state space and contractivity of each kernel in Wasserstein distance (positive Ollivier-Ricci curvature) — satisfied by chains like SGD on strongly convex smooth objectives; analogous bounds hold for noncompact state spaces under an inhomogeneous spectral gap notion.

The matrix concentration results are illustrated through an analysis of the Elo rating system under a dynamic version of the Bradley-Terry-Luce model, demonstrating utility for sports ranking dynamics.

Trajectory Proper Score (TPS): a predictor-agnostic family of strictly proper trajectory-level scoring rules for LM agents' per-step uncertainty signals calibrated into probabilities of eventual success; TPS strictly elicits the prefix-conditioned success-probability process q_t = P^pi(Y=1|H_t) under complete observation, whereas AUROC, AUPRC, risk-coverage, Trajectory ECE, and scalarized trajectory scores only evaluate discrimination, binwise calibration, or collapsed summaries.

Low Rank for Rank: for task-specific LLM ranking under sparse pairwise comparisons (e.g., Chatbot Arena), the task-by-model ability matrix is modeled as low rank so information is shared across related tasks while preserving task-specific differences; a max-norm accurate estimator of the latent score matrix yields task-wise top-K recovery guarantees under sparse sampling, plus an uncertainty quantification framework with debiased estimates beyond point estimation.

Pluralistic leaderboards address heterogeneous LLM user preferences that a single Bradley-Terry global ranking misrepresents: adapting local stability from social choice theory, the leaderboard requires that no model outside the top-k is collectively preferred to the top-k set by more than O(1/k) fraction of users, yielding stability with respect to heterogeneous user populations.

Regularization in paired comparison models via pseudo-games: two data-augmentation perspectives — (1) fractional pseudo-games between every pair of competitors, (2) a fixed-strength phantom player against whom each real competitor gets a weighted pseudo-win and pseudo-loss — both yield finite shrunken ability estimates; the phantom-player construction also resolves location nonidentifiability without an arbitrary sum-to-zero constraint.

The pseudo-game regularization extends to Thurstone-Mosteller models via the probit link in augmented binomial regression, and to replacing the single zero-strength phantom player with several fixed-strength phantom opponents; covariates like home-field advantage can be included without changing the regularization structure, and disagreement between tuned and untuned estimates is a useful diagnostic of comparison-graph or tuning issues.

HPRO is an LLM-based discriminative framework for sales lead scoring in long-chain funnels (e.g., automotive): it transforms sparse binary supervision into dense, funnel-aware preference signals via a margin-aware Bradley-Terry objective, jointly modeling structured CRM features and unstructured customer interactions; on large-scale NEV retail data it achieved AUC 0.8161 and +39.7% P@0.1%, and a 132-day online A/B test validated 9.5% sales volume uplift.

To improve sharpness of neural-network-based parametric ensemble post-processing (DRN), the mean-CRPS loss is supplemented with a penalty term that is a scalar multiple of the width of the predicted distribution's central prediction interval at the confidence level determined by ensemble member count; the width depends only on variance, but the penalization is assumed to force the optimizer to find a better-located mean as well; demonstrated on 2m temperature ensemble forecasts from ECMWF via EUPPBench.

In real-time prediction markets with precisely observed public signals, prices become more accurate as resolution approaches and respond rapidly in the expected direction, but updating is incomplete: a one-minute change in the out-of-sample benchmark probability is associated with only about a 0.64-for-one contemporaneous change in market prices, and the missing adjustment predicts future price drift over the following minutes — interpreted as gradual price discovery under trading frictions, not frictionless arbitrage.

Bradley-Terry Rankings for Recommender Systems: ranking recommendation algorithms by BT over pairwise performance comparisons is more robust than naive metric averaging (e.g., averaging NDCG); rankings depend on dataset statistics like sparsity, sequential structure, and scale; a transitive-triplets metric assesses ranking consistency and robustness to incomplete data; BT trees and covariate-adjusted BT enable dataset-aware algorithm selection for unseen datasets without running the models.
equation: \mathrm{Pr}(i\succ j)=\frac{p_{i}}{p_{i}+p_{j}},\qquad \ell(p)=\ln\prod_{1\leq i,j\leq n}[\mathrm{Pr}(i\succ j)]^{W_{ij}}=\sum_{1\leq i,j\leq n}[W_{ij}(\ln(p_{i})-\ln(p_{i}+p_{j}))]

claim: For the SoccerNet 2026 Player-Centric Ball-Action Spotting challenge (predicting who performs which action and when, across eight classes in broadcast soccer), extensions to the FOOTPASS baselines (TAAD, TAAD+GNN, TAAD+DST) — gradient checkpointing for full-backbone fine-tuning on a single GPU, fusion of GNN logits into the DST encoder, square-root frequency class weighting for the 213:1 pass-to-tackle imbalance, and a post-processing pipeline (per-class logit gating, temporal frame refinement, jersey re-assignment, two-model ensemble) — achieved 0.548 Macro F1 on the test set and 0.446 on the challenge set.

A stochastic weather generator for high-frequency (minute-scale) surface wind vectors at Lamont, Oklahoma, built on 30+ years of measurements restricted to June to minimize seasonality, uses time vector-quantized variational autoencoders; evaluation uses day-level energy score differences (100*(Synth-Train)/Train) across 185 test days under independent vs consecutive sampling and embedded/features/no-weather generator variants.

Minute-scale wind data show complex diurnal structures in both wind speed and direction that challenge standard time series models; the generator is intended as input to wind energy, wildfire spread, and aviation models.

Mult-DPO generalizes Direct Preference Optimization from pairwise to set-wise preferences in recommender systems (multiple positives that must outrank unobserved/negative items, no prescribed order within positives or negatives): a multinomial surrogate event likelihood yields a tractable closed-form DPO-style loss that is a provable upper bound on the otherwise intractable marginalized Plackett-Luce loss, with tightness characterized by the number of positives and cumulative policy-induced weights of selected negatives; Mult-DPO and Mult^2-DPO outperform DPO-based baselines on general and conversational recommendation benchmarks.

Soft-Elo estimates human Elo ratings from LLM-judged battles: at the local level it replaces discrete win/loss/tie targets with calibrated preference probabilities derived from judge score differences (propagating calibrated win probabilities rather than hard labels into the BT procedure), bringing LLM-derived ratings within 17.9 Elo MAE of human-derived ones averaged over 55 held-out models on LMArena; at the global level, split conformal prediction on the residual gap between LLM-derived and human-derived Elo ratings yields conformal intervals for new models' human Elo ratings.

SA-MSCP (Simulation-Augmented Multi-Step Split Conformal Prediction) targets uncertainty quantification for aggregated forecasts (annual totals, year-over-year growth rates): it generates future paths from cross-validated residuals using a block bootstrap and constructs prediction intervals from empirical quantiles; experiments show SA-MSCP improves empirical coverage over a simulated-path baseline for aggregated and growth-rate targets, at the cost of wider intervals — a fundamental trade-off in conformal prediction under dependence and aggregation.

Raw ensemble forecasts of several AI weather models are generally overly narrow, yielding lower statistical coverage than desired — especially on extreme events — despite being considered well-calibrated; online conformal prediction corrects the coverage deficiency at all target coverage levels, endowing outputs with a statistical guarantee without sacrificing skill on CRPS or SSR, with the online adjustments c_t reacting to distributional changes like seasonal differences.

Quantile-Adaptive Temperature Scaling (QaTS) adapts the temperature as a function of a prediction's empirical confidence quantile, mapping confidences into quantile space to normalize the calibration problem; it outperforms standard temperature scaling and baselines (HFE, FeatClip) across corruption types (elastic transform, gaussian blur/noise, jpeg compression, zoom blur) at every severity level without needing additional OOD samples, addressing the largest correctness-confidence discrepancies that uniform rescaling leaves uncorrected.

A selective time-series forecasting framework decouples abstention from the training domain by modeling the empirical percentile of forecasting errors — a scale-invariant statistic — from structural characteristics extracted from recent lags via metalearning, rather than relying on domain-tied proxies like prediction-interval width or learned confidence scores; this enables generalization of the reject option across forecasting domains.

For the 2026 FIFA World Cup (first 48-team edition with an added Round of 32), team strength is described not only by current Elo but by a six-month lagged Elo-difference vector, reduced via categorical sufficient dimension reduction (SIR/SAVE) and fed into a Poisson double-regression model for home and away goals; in out-of-sample backtests on the 2018 and 2022 World Cups, SDR-based Poisson models beat non-SDR baselines, with SIR (M9) and SAVE (M11) with two directions strongest — combined RPS about 0.127 and accuracy around 68%.

Eleven models were compared for World Cup forecasting (logistic regression, standard Poisson, ARIMA, neural-network Elo forecasts, gradient boosting, an ensemble, and four categorical SDR variants based on sliced inverse regression and sliced average variance estimation), evaluated out of sample with the ranked probability score.

For model selection among probabilistic forecasting models evaluated on datasets of multiple time series, discrepancies between mean scaled score, mean ranks, and win rates arise from skewness of the score distribution (pronounced with short test sets); skewness can cause non-mean criteria (mean rank, median, win rate) to select misspecified models, while the mean score is immune — hence prefer the mean scaled score.

DD-Elo (Drift-Diffusion-Enhanced Elo) addresses outcome-centric rating lag by integrating move-level chess data, modeling skill expression as a drift-diffusion decision process from cognitive neuroscience; a rigorous derivation proves DD-Elo maintains bounded deviation from traditional Elo, and large-scale real-world chess experiments show it adapts to non-stationary skill changes significantly faster than Elo while preserving directional accuracy and long-term alignment.

The proper scoring ensemble filter (PSEF) is an ensemble data assimilation method that trains a permutation-invariant transformer-based analysis map — taking a forecast ensemble and observations as input, producing an analysis ensemble — to approximate the Bayesian filtering distribution using only synthetic state-observation trajectories, with training based on strictly proper scoring rules; it outperforms classical benchmarks even under favorable tuning protocols for the benchmarks.

BetXplain is an explanation-annotated dataset of betting advertisements from Instagram and Reddit, manually annotated for manipulative and deceptive advertising practices with human-provided explanations of the reasoning behind each annotation, enabling research into explainable detection of manipulative ads.

The BetXplain authors characterize gambling content in the dataset as operating as a high-risk psychological system — a 'Dual-Diagnosis Trigger' simultaneously promoting social inadequacy via sports comparison and severe addiction via gambling predation, with a 'Trojan Horse Effect' where juxtaposition of safe entertainment with high-risk financial triggers normalizes gambling and lowers psychological defenses.

Bayesian fixed-budget best-arm identification with abstention exhibits a polynomial-to-exponential phase transition: without abstention the error probability decays polynomially in budget T, but introducing any small positive abstention budget alpha shifts undetected-error decay to exponential; for Gaussian priors/rewards, exact matching information-theoretic lower and algorithmic upper bounds give optimal error exponent exp(-alpha^2 T / (8 kappa_nu^2)), where kappa_nu is a hardness parameter.

Calibrated Probability Forecast Sequences and Measure-Valued Martingales: the paper considers calibrated probability forecast sequences through measure-valued martingales, building on score-based calibration testing for multivariate forecast distributions (Knueppel, Krueger & Pohle 2023) and density forecast revisions/efficiency literature.

RL with verifiable rewards can train a calibrated probabilistic forecaster (NFL in-game win probability testbed, betting market as reference) without human labels or supervised fine-tuning: rewarding the realized per-play outcome fails because the single outcome is a noisy target and the policy gradient corrupts the chain of thought; instead a verifiable label-free reward — a state-conditioned empirical win rate estimated from past outcomes — turns a proper scoring rule into a usable training signal for events with no correct answer, calibrating the forecaster to betting-market level.

Latent Maps of Performance: a framework for counterfactual path generation in StarCraft II that models player improvement as algorithmic recourse within a learned representation, bridging representational learning and feedback generation by extracting actionable, counterfactual improvement trajectories from latent space — shifting the paradigm from predicting game outcomes to giving players tangible guidance on what to do differently.

For lab-to-track thermal transfer in EV motorsport powertrains, Ensemble Batch Prediction Intervals (EnbPI) calibrated on real CALCE lithium-ion cycler data (A123 SP20 cells, FUDS profile) achieved its nominal 95% coverage in-distribution (measured 95.00%) but degraded to 70.13% empirical coverage under a genuine measured covariate shift (second CALCE test condition: US06 Highway Driving Schedule at 45 degC); weighted conformal prediction is studied to recover bounds under this shift.

WALLA (advantage-aligned wagering mechanisms for LLM aggregation): each LLM reports a prediction and a learned wager, and predictions are aggregated using wagers as weights; a leave-one-out baseline in the net payout function yields dominant-strategy incentive compatibility of prediction under arbitrary belief structures, advantage-wager alignment (optimal wager proportional to the model's expected score advantage), and decoupling of prediction and wager learning; empirically WALLA matches centralized baselines in aggregated prediction performance.

Attention Limited Reward Learning: under a reduced-form model motivated by Shannon rational inattention, each pairwise label is generated by a low-capacity evaluation channel that scales reward differences by query-dependent attention and adds defaults that do not scale with reward; raw comparison log-odds need not form a potential field, the Bradley-Terry pseudo-true reward can reverse the deliberative ranking, and reward is not separately identified from attention or defaults — a near 50/50 label may reflect true closeness or merely limited attention.

A formal equivalence between predictive accuracy and trading profitability on prediction markets: for any strictly proper scoring rule S, a 'proper' betting strategy depending only on the forecaster's prediction p and the market price q earns positive expected profit whenever p outperforms q under S and the market has sufficient liquidity; this strategy strictly generalizes the canonical strategy applicable only to specific AMM designs, is essentially the only robustly profitable strategy, and has a deep connection to proper scoring rules.

The paper resolves the puzzle that informed forecasters routinely lose money on central limit order book prediction markets while uninformed heuristic strategies profit, even though classical theory ties accuracy to profit only for specific AMM designs.

Pitwall is a production system generating faithful trilingual (English, Spanish, Portuguese) Formula 1 race-strategy briefings from a calibrated real-time Monte Carlo engine: every published sentence is decomposed into typed factual claims (positions, gaps, tyres, pace, overtakes, race control) and each claim is verified against the probabilistic race state that prompted it; of 3,045 model-written fine-tuning targets, only the 81.9% whose every claim was state-supported were retained, with the rest falling back to a provably faithful template.

Pitwall models lap time as l(t,a) = f_0^{(t)} + delta^{(t)} a + 1[a>k^{(t)}] s^{(t)}(a-k^{(t)}) + epsilon with epsilon ~ N(0, sigma_lap^2), pass probability as P(pass) = sigma(A_GP + k_p Delta_pace + k_t Delta_age), safety-car probability as p_SC = lambda_SC / L_rem, and a calibration correction b-hat_c = b_c - b-bar + c-bar minimizing ||c-b||^2 subject to g_min <= c_{t+1}-c_t <= g_max.

The first framework generating professional-level, ITTF rule-compliant table tennis serve motion plans for a robot arm combines motion primitives, Model Predictive Control, and Bayesian Optimization; evaluated against elite and professional players, the robot's serves showed comparable or higher velocity and especially spin — a key component in the first robot win in fair Best-of-3 matches against multiple professional table tennis players.

The SoccerNet 2026 challenges (sixth annual edition) spanned five vision tasks: Ball Action Anticipation, Player-Centric Ball Action Spotting, Novel View Synthesis, Spiideo SoccerNet Synloc (single-image athlete localization in pitch coordinates), and Visual Question Answering; leading submissions improved over baselines with recurring gains from higher input resolution, larger or ensembled models, careful calibration, and explicit domain structure (camera geometry, tactical features).

A structural volatility model tailored to binary prediction markets combines a Wright-Fisher deadline-resolution component (capturing how remaining binary uncertainty is forced to resolve over time) with a Glosten-Milgrom order-flow component (capturing volatility from informed trading as reflected in spreads and volume); prediction-market state variables explain a large share of volatility, and the best dynamic model adds residual GARCH dynamics on top of the structural deadline-resolution/asymmetric-information baseline.

A survey of 3D human pose estimation for sports/biomechanics use notes that video-based markerless motion capture reports lower-limb joint angle mean absolute errors of 4-6 degrees and ground-reaction-force errors around 6% of body weight (Auer et al. 2024), and AI-smartphone markerless capture of hip/knee/ankle angles during countermovement jumps has been validated against Vicon (Barzyk et al. 2024).

Objective and subjective entropy measures of portfolio suboptimality: the paper develops entropy-based measures of how far a portfolio is from optimal, situated in the Kelly betting / portfolio choice literature (Latane 1959, Merton 1969, Platen).

Temporal Feature Distillation: a semi-supervised objective for label-efficient precise event spotting that aligns temporally informative backbone features (rather than projection-head outputs) across augmented views to preserve motion-sensitive, boundary-aware cues, since directly applying DINO-style self-distillation to PES suppresses subtle motion cues as noise; a supervised warm-up with ramp-up schedule stabilizes training, and experiments on fine-grained sports datasets show consistent improvements across annotation ratios with especially strong gains in low-label settings.

Preference-based RL is generalized to allow the expert to label trajectory pairs as incomparable (neither dominates the other); the paper introduces a Bradley-Terry-inspired rationality model capturing incomparabilities and inferring a multi-dimensional reward function, provides sample complexity analysis for learning its parameters, and evaluates its ability to reconstruct an expert-aligned reward function and recover the Pareto frontier of policies in simulated environments.

Training-free off-screen player imputation for football: broadcast main-camera viewports show only 10-16 of 22 players at any moment, and ignoring off-screen players inflates hidden-zone pitch-control error to 25.1-26.9 percentage points with mean absolute control-share error of 11.1-13.4 points across three matches (Metrica Sports open tracking data, simulated broadcast viewport, one match held out).

Hindcast evaluates LLM forecasters at a chosen past time t_0, replaying resolved Polymarket markets against a frozen snapshot of public Reddit and letting the model read only posts written before t_0, scored against both the resolved outcome and the matched-time price; retrieval lowers Brier on eight of nine models (up to 23%), but the effect splits by topic — retrieval helps Sports, Awards, and Trading (fact-anchored pre-event discussion) and regresses on Entertainment (speculative hype reads as evidence).

RENEW/Dynamics Learning from Human Feedback (DLHF): repairs world-model exploitation by training latent dynamics from binary human preferences over imagined rollouts via a Bradley-Terry preference loss over trajectory log-likelihoods, l_theta(sigma) = sum_t log T-hat_theta(s_{t+1}|s_t,a_t), with P(sigma^0 > sigma^1) = logistic(l_theta(sigma^0) - l_theta(sigma^1)); RENEW directs preference queries by epistemic uncertainty toward transitions most vulnerable to exploitation, improving sample efficiency over naive DLHF and avoiding catastrophic forgetting of pretrained dynamics.

KellyBench is an open-access benchmark (openreward.ai/GeneralReasoning/KellyBench) for long-horizon sequential decision-making: agents are placed in a sequential simulation of the 2023-24 English Premier League season and tasked with maximizing long-term bankroll growth, given historical data including advanced statistics, lineups, and public odds.

On KellyBench, all frontier language models evaluated lose money on average over the full season across five seeds; the best-performing model achieves an average return of -8%, many experience ruin across seeds, and the benchmark exposes failures in machine-learning modeling (struggling to outperform bookmaker-implied probabilities) and in closed-loop reasoning (failing to execute strategies, monitor performance, or adapt).

KellyBench strategy-sophistication grading via a human-expert rubric found models' approaches unsophisticated compared to human baselines (Claude Opus 4.6 scored 26.5%): rich player-level data was almost universally ignored in favour of simpler team-level features, and the non-stationarity challenge of newly promoted teams proved universally problematic with no model implementing a general solution despite several explicitly diagnosing the problem.

KellyBench's theoretical core uses the Kelly growth framework: log-wealth growth rate W(b) = sum_{x,y} p(x,y) log(b(x|y) o(x)); growth advantage g(p;p*,q) = sum_x p*(x) log(p(x)/q(x)) = D_KL(p*||q) - D_KL(p*||p); and the classical Kelly fraction f* = (rp-(1-p))/r.

Paper arXiv 2607.15483v1 ('Risk-Aware Preference Learning for Stochastic Outcomes') compares expected utility (EU) with Cumulative Prospect Theory (CPT) inside a Bradley-Terry preference-learning framework for social robot navigation: when preferences are generated by risk-sensitive users, CPT-based learners recover reward functions better than EU learners that assume humans aggregate outcome utilities linearly with probabilities.

Method claim from arXiv 2607.15483v1: model human evaluators as systematically risk-sensitive (overweighting rare negative events, exhibiting loss aversion) rather than expected-utility maximizers; the mismatch matters most for safety-critical rare outcomes such as collisions in robot navigation.

Paper arXiv 2607.15766v1 introduces Prospective Hypothesis Discovery (PHD): LLMs autonomously construct grounded, discriminative, testable hypothesis spaces from inconclusive evidence (anomalous observations, fragmented records). Evaluation testbed HypoArena = HypoData (988 cases across six domains) + HypoEval (bidirectional pairwise judgments plus Bradley-Terry-style aggregation for open-ended hypotheses).

Method claim from arXiv 2607.15766v1: HypoData is built via Retrospective Context Regression, a pipeline that reconstructs pre-conclusion contexts from expert documents by removing explicit conclusions while preserving the factual substrate.

Paper arXiv 2607.16675 ('Isotonic Conformal Prediction'): Self-Calibrating Conformal Prediction (SC-CP) attains both self-calibration (a point prediction unbiased conditional on its own value) and prediction-conditional validity (prediction intervals attaining nominal coverage conditional on the prediction) exactly in finite samples, but requires refitting its calibrator for every candidate outcome, which is computationally prohibitive for continuous outcomes.

Method claim from arXiv 2607.16675: Isotonic Conformal Prediction (ICP) decouples calibration from prediction-set construction by fitting a single isotonic recalibration map and constructing prediction intervals within strata, avoiding per-candidate refits.

Paper arXiv 2607.17953 ('Dynamical system for PageRank with a time-dependent memory', Flores, Primo, Rodriguez et al.): a continuous-time PageRank model in which the personalization vector evolves as a weighted average of its past values with weights from a memory function, formulated as an initial-value problem for an integro-differential equation whose initial condition is a probability vector.

Theorem claim from arXiv 2607.17953: for strongly connected networks, broad classes of memory functions make the PageRank vector converge toward a stationary state that is independent of the initial condition.
In arXiv 2607.17953 the contrasting case is the exponential-oscillatory memory function, stated in the paper as omega(t) = e^{at} cos(bt) for t >= 0 with a,b > 0. Formula: see equation field.

Paper arXiv 2607.17991 ('Optimal Market Making in Prediction Markets'): stochastic control framework where the market price is modeled as a conditional probability of the binary outcome generated by a transformed latent belief diffusion; the market maker chooses bid/ask quotes to maximize expected terminal wealth while controlling both mark-to-market inventory risk and the settlement risk of remaining positions at resolution.

Result claim from arXiv 2607.17991: the authors derive the associated Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation for optimal prediction-market market making and characterize the unique viscosity solution; the binary settlement structure makes the optimization fundamentally different from classical market-making settings.

Paper arXiv 2607.18009v1 proposes a Bayesian framework for modeling under- and over-dispersion in football goal counts by combining a Conway-Maxwell-Poisson (CMP) likelihood with a spike-and-slab prior on the dispersion structure, as an alternative to Poisson-only goal models.

Modeling claim from arXiv 2607.18009v1: the CMP distribution's extra dispersion parameter lets one likelihood family cover both under-dispersed and over-dispersed goal counts, and the spike-and-slab prior performs selection over which dispersion effects are active.

Paper arXiv 2607.18084 ('WorldCupArena') presents a dynamic benchmark for language models and deep-research agents on football forecasting: the 2026 FIFA World Cup (104 matches) is the first evaluation; before each match a model receives a common evidence package or searches itself, then predicts result, score, likely players/events, match statistics, and competition outcome, scored after the match against recorded results.

Metric claim from arXiv 2607.18084: WorldCupArena reports result accuracy, exact-score accuracy, and a scoreline score that gives partial credit when a predicted score is close but not exact, plus scores for the auxiliary prediction tasks.

Paper arXiv 2607.18269 ('Wisdom of LLM Crowds'): probability estimates elicited from 15 LLMs on 254 binary prediction-market questions; learned aggregators (a multilayer perceptron and a logistic regression) achieved lower Brier scores than all individual models and all classical aggregation methods.

Finding from arXiv 2607.18269: the logistic regression performed comparably to the neural network, implying the gain from learned aggregation comes from learning a linear combination of diverse model outputs rather than from nonlinear interactions; symbolic regression was also applied to the aggregation problem.

Paper arXiv 2607.18461 ('The triumphs and tragedies of fandom: Emotional arcs in NFL tweets', Kolak et al.): using a corpus of game-referencing tweets from the 2011-2014 NFL seasons, the authors estimate a fandom radius per team, identifying regions where engagement exceeds background discussion levels, and measure sentiment variation driven by geography, game outcomes, and team performance.

Finding from arXiv 2607.18461: sentiment toward both winning and losing NFL teams is positive immediately before games, drops at kickoff, and rebounds slightly during halftime; after halftime the trajectories diverge (winning-team sentiment rises toward the end, losing-team sentiment stays low), and both end below their start-of-game levels.
Finding from arXiv 2607.18461: comparing measured fan sentiment against win percentage reveals only a weak positive relationship, suggesting sentiment is driven by more than team quality.

Paper arXiv 2607.19783v2 ('Do In-Match Hydration Breaks Alter Match Momentum?'): the 2026 FIFA World Cup was the first to mandate hydration breaks near the 22nd minute of each half in every match; the authors test the claim that breaks blunt the dominant side's momentum with a within-match case-crossover design using non-break minutes of the same match as self-matched controls (adjusting only for game time, scoreline, pre-break momentum).

Finding from arXiv 2607.19783v2: the apparent post-break fade is not caused by the break - the dominant side's momentum decays at essentially the same rate whether or not a break occurs; what the break removes is only the continuation of pressure during the stopped minutes, leaving no trace in net expected goals (average effect approximately zero).

Paper arXiv 2607.22221v1 ('Convergence analysis of a family of Zermelo-type iterations for the Bradley-Terry model'): the Bradley-Terry model states the probability i beats j as pi_i/(pi_i+pi_j) under the normalization that the product of all strengths equals 1. Formula: see equation field.

In arXiv 2607.22221v1 the Bradley-Terry log-likelihood over pairwise win counts w_ij is l(pi) = sum_{i,j} w_ij log(pi_i/(pi_i+pi_j)), and the MLE is the argmax of l over positive strength vectors with product 1. Formula: see equation field.
In arXiv 2607.22221v1, Zermelo's classical fixed-point iteration for the Bradley-Terry MLE is pi_i = (sum_j w_ij) / (sum_j (w_ji+w_ij)/(pi_i+pi_j)) for i=1..n. Formula: see equation field.

In arXiv 2607.22221v1, Newman's accelerated family of Zermelo-type fixed-point iterations parameterized by alpha is pi_i = [sum_j w_ij (alpha pi_i + pi_j)/(pi_i+pi_j)] / [sum_j (alpha w_ij + w_ji)/(pi_i+pi_j)], which recovers Zermelo's algorithm at alpha = 1; the paper analyzes its convergence to speed up Bradley-Terry MLE computation. Formula: see equation field.

Paper arXiv 2607.23165 (ABF-T-GLCP): a model-agnostic framework for forecasting and uncertainty quantification in nonstationary multivariate time series; the forecasting module combines horizon-specific temporal experts through a learned gate and refines predictions with sparse predictive transfer across related series, and the same learned adaptive predictive state representation is reused for conformal calibration.

Method claim from arXiv 2607.23165: Gate-Localized Conformal Prediction (GLCP) uses the learned gate state together with temporal recency to select locally relevant calibration residuals, coupling uncertainty calibration to the predictive regimes used by the forecasting model so point forecasts and intervals adapt consistently under evolving dynamics.

Paper arXiv 2607.24875 (FinAbstain): a research framework for uncertainty-calibrated multimodal retrieval-augmented generation with selective prediction in finance; a point-in-time retriever admits only information public at the forecast timestamp and supplies modality-specific evidence to fundamental, news, technical, risk, and verification agents.

Method claim from arXiv 2607.24875: agents' probabilistic assessments are aggregated with retrieval relevance, evidence contradiction, repeated-sample consistency, and historical calibration statistics; temperature scaling, isotonic regression, conformal prediction, and a proposed hybrid uncertainty score are evaluated for the abstention decision.

Paper arXiv 2607.26061v1 (Sim2Win): a team-agnostic, event-based pre-match tactical recommendation framework; using StatsBomb open event data from 11 competitions (178 teams, 1,411 team-match records), it builds five-match rolling tactical profiles, engineers four interpretable tactical feature ratios, clusters team behaviors into eight playstyles via K-Means, and trains thirteen classifiers to estimate win/draw/loss probabilities from tactical matchup representations.

Method claim from arXiv 2607.26061v1: Sim2Win operates without team names or identity features, enabling generalization to teams never seen during training, and is validated with a rigorous Leave-One-Competition-Out protocol.

Paper arXiv 2607.27143 ('Cost-Sensitive Conformal Prediction and Human-in-the-Loop Abstention', Singh et al.): benchmark of conformal prediction on 15 imbalanced high-stakes datasets (credit scoring, fraud detection, etc.); marginal conformal prediction fails minority coverage (as low as below 1%), while Mondrian (class-conditional) conformal prediction restores minority coverage with a +61.7% gain over marginal CP.
Finding from arXiv 2607.27143: cost-controlled abstention reduces expected cost under human review, and the paper quantifies dataset-specific cost break-even thresholds for the deferral decision.

Paper arXiv 2607.28178 introduces the Interval-Score Receiver Operating Characteristic (IS-ROC) Curve: a graphical framework representing the complete family of interval forecasts generated by varying prediction tightness; the IS-ROC curve induced by the data-generating process is shown to be Pareto optimal and convex, giving a geometric characterization of the optimal forecasting frontier.

Method claim from arXiv 2607.28178: a geometry-based calibration procedure using tangent optimization and convexification, plus an ensemble strategy that combines competing forecasters through convex hull construction on the IS-ROC frontier.

Paper arXiv 2608.01494 ('Conformal Kelly'): combines conformal prediction intervals with fractional Kelly to size portfolio positions, using a 75% interval - as the range widens the position shrinks, as it narrows the position grows; on a fixed six-year development window (2016-2021) with trading costs, a one-day execution lag, and strict leverage caps, the strategy compounds at 28.5% annualised net log growth with Sharpe ratio 1.34 and 27.7% maximum drawdown, versus 15.9% for holding the S&P 500 and 21-22% for passive portfolios at the same leverage.

Calibration finding from arXiv 2608.01494: the 75% conformal intervals hit their target rate, containing the realised return 74.8% of the time against the 75% target; the paper's main design principle runs against the existing literature's advice for conformal prediction in this use.
